items.title: Integrating behavioral and molecular biomarkers reveals neurotoxic effects of common insecticide in big brown bats.
items.abstract: While foraging in croplands, bats are exposed to pesticides that can be neurotoxic even at low concentrations, affecting their physiology and behavior. These sublethal effects are often assessed using molecular biomarkers in isolation, with limited insights into ecological consequences. Here, we used an integrative approach to assess the sublethal effects of chlorpyrifos, a common neurotoxic insecticide, on big brown bats (Eptesicus fuscus). We combined behavioral experiments with molecular biomarkers that could reveal the mechanisms underlying observed changes. We orally exposed bats to chlorpyrifos and evaluated their associative memory in a crawling Y-maze, and their stereotyped flight trajectories. To understand the mechanisms behind these behavioral changes, we quantified brain cholinesterase (ChE) activity and used non-targeted proteomics to identify cellular and molecular biomarkers of neurotoxicity. Exposed bats did not change their flight consistency, but were less explorative, had a slower reflex response, and made more incorrect choices in the Y-maze. Exposed bats had a significant reduction in their ChE activity and showed dysregulation of proteins involved in neurological processes like memory, learning, and sound perception. Our results not only provide a comprehensive understanding of the different ways in which pesticides affect individual performance, they also provide a broad description of the underlying cellular and molecular processes, increasing our mechanistic understanding of these effects. Moreover, our results support the sensitivity of behavior as an ecologically relevant biomarker of toxicity and the importance of considering multiple levels of organization to elucidate the mechanisms underlying altered behavior in wildlife due to human activities.

items.title: The relationship between regularity of nighttime rest behavior and depressive symptoms in everyday home-life using smartphone-based sensor data.
items.abstract: Depression is associated with disruptions in circadian and behavioral rhythms. Beyond sleep duration, temporal consistency of sleep-related behavior may represent a relevant aspect of behavioral rhythms. We examine nighttime rest regularity derived from passive smartphone activity data and its association with depressive symptom severity. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) scores and self-reported sleep duration were collected via smartphones from 234 individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD; n = 95) or healthy controls (HC; n = 139). Step counts from a 15-day window surrounding BDI assessment were analysed for nighttime intervals (10 pm-8 am), requiring at least seven valid nights. Group differences and associations between nighttime rest regularity, sleep duration, and depressive symptom severity were examined. No significant MDD-HC differences in rest regularity emerged (all p ≥ .058), although estimates descriptively suggested lower nighttime consistency (NCI: β = -0.083) and greater rest-duration variability (LRI-SD: β = 0.118) in MDD. Within MDD, lower regularity corresponded descriptively to higher BDI scores, but no associations survived correction (all p-BH ≥ 0.154). LRI-SD showed the largest positive estimate (β = 0.086, p-BH = 0.154). Self-reported sleep duration was not significantly associated with BDI scores in MDD (β = 0.045, p = .662) or rest regularity variables (|β| ≤ 0.043, all p ≥ .236). Smartphone step count data enable multi-day characterization of nighttime rest regularity. No significant associations with self-reported sleep duration emerged, suggesting distinct behavioral characteristics. Associations with depressive symptom severity showed small descriptive tendencies but remained nonsignificant after correction, warranting investigation.

items.title: Longitudinal contributions of mother-toddler neural synchrony and maternal depression to children's neural reward response.
items.abstract: Healthy reward processing during early childhood is important for emotional development. Identifying factors that promote the development of reward processing is clinically important, given its relation to risk for depression. Parent-toddler dyadic interactions may support the development of healthy reward function in the prefrontal cortex, a region involved in reward processing, which is accessible during naturalistic social tasks via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). The current study aimed to evaluate whether mother-toddler prefrontal synchrony during dyadic play and the presence of maternal depression may predict child reward function. At baseline, 63 toddlers (49% female; Mage=30.6 months) and their biological mothers (21 with depression) engaged in a dyadic play task while undergoing fNIRS hyperscanning. One year later, child prefrontal response to reward was assessed via fNIRS. Greater mother-toddler left prefrontal oxyhemoglobin synchrony during positive dyadic play at baseline was associated with greater child left and right prefrontal oxyhemoglobin response to winning reward one year later. Children with a maternal history of depression had greater left prefrontal deoxyhemoglobin response to reward (i.e., greater prefrontal deactivation) when compared with children without this maternal history, although this finding did not hold after controlling for maternal antidepressant use. Our findings suggest that positive mother-toddler dyadic interactions may support, via co-regulation of prefrontal reward regions, the emergence of children's own prefrontal reward response during the preschool years. Further, our findings demonstrate that clinically observable maternal depression may be related to greater prefrontal deactivation in response to reward as early as age three.

items.title: Brain variation underlying genetic factors linked to psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
items.abstract: Psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions have both shared and distinct symptomatology, but the brain mechanisms underlying diagnostic similarities and differences remain unclear. Using genome-wide association data, we analyzed 12 psychiatric disorders and four neurodegenerative diseases, assessing polygenic overlap, shared loci, and genetic causal relationships linking their genetic latent factors with 3,935 brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDP). Using genomic structural equation modeling, we identified an internalizing factor (F1), an addiction factor (F2), a factor related to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (F3), a neurodevelopmental factor (F4), and a factor related to Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (F5). These showed shared transcriptomic enrichments for frontal and anterior cingulate cortical regions, while F1-specific depletion in substantia nigra and F3-specific enrichment in nucleus accumbens appeared to be specific. Fine-mapping identified 99 variants, including shared loci (e.g., VRK2: F1, F2, F3; TSHZ3: F1, F2; TCF4: F1, F3) and factor-specific loci (e.g., DRD2-F2; SCN2A-F3; FOXP2-F4; TNIP1-F5). The brain-wide analysis of fine-mapped loci identified 1,480 IDP associations (false discovery rate q 400 brain IDPs (mostly related to cortical area, cortical grey-white contrast, cortical thickness, and regional and tissue volume). Similarly, MOBP rs1768190 related to F5 was associated with >200 brain IDPs, with about half of them related to cortical thickness. The present study provides new insights into cross-diagnostic mechanisms linking genetic variation and molecular changes to the brain structural and functional variation across psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions.

items.title: The Association between Physical Activity and Higher Corticolimbic Synaptic Density is Independent of Body Mass Index.
items.abstract: Regular physical exercise has been linked to biomarkers of slowed biological aging, including brain aging, though the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. Exercise may enhance neuroplasticity and attenuate synaptic decline; however, evidence supporting these effects has largely been limited to animal and postmortem studies. Whether physical activity is associated with synaptic density in the living human brain remains unknown. We used positron emission tomography (PET) with the radiotracer [18F]SynVesT-1 to quantify synaptic density in vivo in 51 individuals (61% female). Participants were classified as physically active or insufficiently active, and group differences in synaptic density across corticolimbic regions were examined. Additional regression and mediation analyses assessed associations among physical activity, synaptic density, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptom severity. Physically active individuals exhibited significantly higher synaptic density across corticolimbic regions compared to insufficiently active individuals (F6,44=2.41, p=0.042). These effects remained marginally significant after adjusting for BMI and depressive symptom severity (F6,42=2.33, p=0.050). Region-specific regression analyses further demonstrated positive associations between physical activity and synaptic density. Mediation analyses indicated that BMI did not account for the observed relationships. These findings provide the first known in vivo evidence that physical activity is associated with higher synaptic density in the living human brain, particularly within prefrontal circuits. Results suggest that exercise may support synaptic integrity through mechanisms partially independent of BMI. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine causality, characterize temporal dynamics, and evaluate whether physical activity may serve as a scalable intervention to preserve synaptic health.

items.title: Flow-induced endothelial lipid dysregulation in ischemic stroke: from mechanotransduction to therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) induces significant and sustained alterations in cerebral hemodynamics, which extend beyond the acute phase and actively contribute to post-stroke cerebrovascular remodeling. Accumulating evidence suggests that endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis is a critical determinant of vascular integrity, whereas its dysregulation may promote endothelial inflammation, and vascular remodeling. Abnormal shear stress, particularly low and oscillatory shear stress, may connect post-stroke hemodynamic changes to endothelial lipid dysregulation by regulating lipid uptake, intracellular lipid processing, cholesterol efflux, and lipid storage through mechanotransduction pathways. Although direct evidence demonstrating that altered shear stress drives endothelial lipid accumulation in the cerebral vasculature remains limited, findings from endothelial studies and mechanobiology suggest a functional "flow-lipid axis" implicated in post-stroke vascular pathology. In this review, we summarize the hemodynamic alterations following IS and how abnormal shear stress may regulate endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis through mechanosensors and downstream pathways, including AMPK, mTOR, SREBP, and lipophagy. We further identify the existing gap in causal evidence connecting post-stroke hemodynamics to cerebral endothelial lipid accumulation, and propose targeted translational research avenues aimed at facilitating the development of hemodynamic- and metabolism-based therapeutic strategies for IS.

items.title: Brain-Computer Interfaces for Traumatic Brain Injury and Spinal Cord Injury: Lesion-Pattern Matching, Functional Restoration, and Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment. In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication. Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.

items.title: Reactive, subjective and executive agents: How survival circuits underlie the expansion of subjective experience and felt motivation in humans and other vertebrates.
items.abstract: We review the evolution of agency in vertebrates from the Cambrian explosion to humans. Active locomotion sparked evolution of efficient decision-making in arthropods, vertebrates and later in cephalopods. Isolated neural pathways-ancient control architectures for fitness-effective action-became interconnected survival circuits: evolutionarily conserved, functionally integrated neural pathways responding to specific classes of stimuli and that compete for control, with their own set of specific responses. Computational complexity was reduced by constraining inputs, processing and outputs. We hypothesize that three evolutionary transitions deepened the subjective experience by extending the survival circuits: (i) Associative and social learning implied non-genetic information acquisition; (ii) A simulated reality where episodic-like memory and internal simulation resulted in prediction-based action-selection; (iii) Setting and executing one's own wellbeing goals based on future expectations produced a felt experience of short-term personal goals. This subjective agency in vertebrates and some arthropods and cephalopods evolved from reactive agency. Key to this transition was the mighty quadruple-subjective experience, social learning, simulation-based prediction and felt goals-paving the way for nonverbal rationality and consciousness, again reinforcing each other. The emergence of culture, social bonding and the beginning of friendship started in early vertebrates. In humans and partly in some other lineages, the mighty quadruple coevolved with language-based culture under adaptation to social games into executive agency, enhancing the capacities for friendship and sociability and the impact of personalised and conscious norms, values and purpose in the survival circuits, further strengthening the feeling of free will.

items.title: Transdiagnostic effects of medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS): A systematic review and meta-analysis of sham-controlled trials.
items.abstract: There is a growing body of evidence to support the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) as having a central role in a variety of psychiatric disorders. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been investigated over the mPFC in multiple recent sham-controlled trials. However, no meta-analysis of transdiagnostic symptoms across psychiatric disorders has been undertaken. This systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD42022354346) examined the transdiagnostic symptoms of rTMS to the mPFC for a number of psychiatric diagnoses. The analysis included randomised, sham-controlled trials of rTMS to the mPFC for psychiatric disorders. The key outcomes were change in clinical symptoms, quality of life, and cognition measures from pre- to post- treatment, in symptom domains including depression, anxiety, obsessive compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, craving, and consumption. We retrieved 3,901 records, 176 were screened at full text, and 30 were included. Seventeen symptom domains and 1,083 participants were analysed. rTMS to the mPFC produced moderate to large effects for obsessive compulsive symptoms, moderate effects for negative symptoms and craving, and small effects for depressive symptoms. Effects for anxiety, cognition, consumption and impulsivity were non-significant. Interpretation was limited by the overall small number of studies, high heterogeneity in findings and some concerns of risk of bias. This systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that rTMS over the mPFC may have therapeutic potential for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, and craving, with modest effects for depressive symptoms. Further high-quality, adequately-powered trials are needed to confirm effects and clarify optimal stimulation protocols.

items.title: Anticoagulants compared with aspirin in patients with embolic strokes of undetermined source: an individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials.
items.abstract: Direct-acting oral anticoagulation did not reduce recurrent stroke compared with aspirin in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), and subgroup benefits suggested by analyses of individual RCTs were inconsistent across trials. We aimed to evaluate the effect of anticoagulation on the risks of recurrent stroke and major bleeding in patients with ESUS, overall and in prespecified subgroups using individual participant data from RCTs. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE and Scopus for RCTs published between April 1, 2014, and March 1, 2025, without language restriction, comparing anticoagulants with aspirin in patients with ESUS. Non-randomised studies and studies not enrolling patients with ESUS were excluded. We requested individual participant data from the principal investigators of all eligible trials. The primary outcomes were recurrent stroke and major bleeding. For each outcome of interest, we estimated the treatment effect for the overall trial population separately within each trial and the resulting overall treatment estimates were subsequently pooled across trials. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2.0) for the primary efficacy outcome of stroke recurrence. Hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% CIs were estimated following adjustment for prespecified covariates and pooled by use of the random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025644724). Our systematic database search identified 1170 records. Of these studies, four were eligible for inclusion in the analysis, including a total of 13 970 participants. Mean age of participants was 66 years (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participants were female and 8484 (60·7%) were male. Across all trials, 6989 patients were assigned to receive a direct-acting oral anticoagulant and 6981 were assigned to receive aspirin. The hazard for recurrent stroke was similar between participants allocated to anticoagulant or aspirin (399 of 6989 patients [4·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 417 of 6981 [4·8 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·78-1·14), without evidence of heterogeneity across studies (I2=5%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·37). The hazard for major bleeding was also similar between the two groups (149 of 6989 patients [1·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 106 of 6981 [1·1 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 1·19, 95% CI 0·52-2·73), but heterogeneity was present across studies (I2=79%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·0023). Anticoagulation did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke after ESUS when compared with aspirin, and the risk of major bleeding did not differ significantly between the two treatments. A possible benefit from anticoagulation in patients with ESUS and left atrial enlargement, as shown in a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis, should be investigated in future trials. items.title: DNA methylation profiling of human brain in posttraumatic stress and major depressive disorders indicate specific molecular features.
items.abstract: Molecular analyses of brain regions implicated in risk are essential to providing insights into the antecedents and consequences of psychiatric disorder. In the current study, we contrast the genome-wide DNA methylation levels in the postmortem brains of individuals with a primary diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD; N = 101), major depressive disorder (MDD; N = 101), and controls (N = 100). We demonstrate: (1) the potential role of adult trauma in PTSD-associated oligodendrocyte reductions in the amygdala, (2) an association of MDD with differential methylation within the amygdala that may be accounted for by cell type enrichment, (3) sex- and diagnosis-specific multi-omics factors within the methylome that differentiate the immune and other biological pathways involved in PTSD, and (4) illustrate the lack of concordance in DNA methylation across brain regions in PTSD compared to MDD. We also find a brain-based biological aging factor that may provide insights into the biological pathways of brain aging.

items.title: Something's gotta give: Reward-induced effort modulation in task-switching reveals a flexibility-stability trade-off.
items.abstract: Everyday behavior requires balancing two control modes: flexibility, for switching between tasks, and stability, for maintaining goals in the face of interference. One influential account posits that these modes trade off, such that increased flexibility comes at the cost of reduced stability. However, empirical support for this trade-off remains equivocal. We propose that it arises from reward-induced effortful control modulations during tasks that require both modes simultaneously. Across two experiments (N = 80 and N = 87), participants completed a task-switching paradigm in which cued reward incentives were manipulated over varying timescales. Large rewards increased flexibility, evinced by reduced task switch costs, but reduced stability, evinced by increased incongruence costs. In Experiment 1, this trade-off also emerged across blocks, with fluctuations in stability and flexibility inversely related under reward. Overall, these findings provide evidence for a reward-driven flexibility-stability trade-off, in which higher incentives promote flexibility at the cost of stability.

items.title: Emotion recognition training across sensory modalities: Comparing the effects of multisensory and unisensory training.
items.abstract: Emotion-recognition training is widely used to improve emotion recognition and, by extension, social competence, yet few studies compare unisensory and multisensory training. We randomly assigned adults to auditory, visual, audiovisual, or control training using a validated protocol adapted across modalities, and assessed emotion recognition with auditory, visual, and audiovisual tests. The primary analysis used first-response accuracy, analysed by ANCOVA with pre-test as a covariate; a similarity-based scoring method and a normalized-gain index served as robustness checks. All trained groups improved reliably from pre- to post-test across modalities, but the untrained control group also improved, indicating that part of this within-group change reflects task exposure. On the primary measure, no trained group reliably exceeded control, audiovisual training did not outperform unisensory training, and no trained-modality advantage emerged. In secondary comparisons using the more sensitive similarity-based metric, the trained groups exceeded control on overall recognition, and the audiovisual and auditory groups also exceeded control on their trained modality. Improvement in the trained groups extended to untrained modalities. Audiovisual stimuli were also recognized more accurately than unisensory stimuli at baseline and in the control group at post-test, a perceptual rather than training effect. Consistent with a preregistered prediction, basic emotions were recognized more accurately than social emotions, with no reliable differences by training condition. Overall, brief training improved emotion recognition on the similarity-based measure, and improvement extended to untrained modalities. We found no evidence that any single training modality, including audiovisual, was superior. Its value likely lies in matching the nature of everyday emotion.

items.title: Antiplatelet prophylaxis with low dose prasugrel in patients undergoing endovascular treatment of cerebral aneurysms; an Australian study.
items.abstract: Low-dose prasugrel is increasingly used for antiplatelet premedication before endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms, but regimens vary and the optimal dose is unclear. We describe platelet reactivity and periprocedural outcomes with a uniform regimen of aspirin 100 mg and prasugrel 5 mg daily. We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing endovascular treatments of unruptured intracranial aneurysms between January 2020 and September 2025. We included patients premedicated with aspirin 100 mg and prasugrel 5 mg daily for seven days. P2Y12 reaction units (PRU) were measured with the VerifyNow assay on the day of the procedure. Thromboembolic and haemorrhagic complications within 60 days were recorded. Ninety procedures in 87 patients were included. Median PRU was 74.5 (interquartile range 42-105.25); PRU was <194 in 89 procedures (98.9%) and <60 (hyperresponse) in 33 (36.7%). Hyperresponse was more frequent in patients weighing <60 kg (61.1% vs 30.6%; p = 0.027). Symptomatic thromboembolic events occurred in 6 procedures (6.7%; 95% CI 2.5-13.9), all after stent or flow diverter placement, and were associated with larger aneurysms (median 11.7 vs 6.0 mm; p = 0.003) and longer procedures (181 vs 118 min; p = 0.003), whereas PRU was not lower in this group. No intracranial haemorrhage occurred; minor extracranial bleeding occurred in 13 of 90 procedures (14.4%). Prasugrel 5 mg daily for seven days produced measurable P2Y12 inhibition in almost all procedures but frequent hyperresponse, particularly in patients weighing <60 kg. Prospective comparative studies incorporating PRU- or weight-guided dosing are required.

items.title: Correlation study between pre-stroke sleep characteristics and early neurological prognosis in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the association between pre-stroke sleep conditions and 3-month functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Consecutive AIS patients admitted between March 2022 and August 2024 were enrolled. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and Berlin Questionnaire were administered within 7 days after stroke onset to evaluate pre-stroke sleep characteristics. Poor functional outcome was defined as a 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score >2. Binary logistic regression was used to identify prognostic factors. Of 782 patients completing follow-up, 18.0% had poor functional recovery. Compared with the good-prognosis group, patients with poor prognosis had a higher rate of pre-stroke excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and more frequent in-hospital sedative-hypnotic use (both P 65 years, female sex, prior stroke history, higher admission NIHSS score, and pre-stroke EDS were independent risk factors for poor prognosis. Small-artery occlusion was protective relative to large-artery atherosclerosis (OR = 0.36, P = 0.002). Pre-stroke EDS appeared to be independently associated with unfavourable three-month functional outcome, apart from established clinical risk factors. Small-artery occlusion predicts better functional recovery compared with large-artery atherosclerosis.

items.title: The effects of perioperative intravenous balanced crystalloids versus normal saline on outcomes in patients undergoing craniotomy: A meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
items.abstract: Perioperative fluid therapy in craniotomy requires balancing intracranial and systemic physiology. Normal saline (NS) is associated with hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. While balanced crystalloids (BC) provide physiological buffering, their effects on cerebral relaxation remain unclear. This meta-analysis compares the effects of BC versus NS on metabolic parameters, intraoperative brain relaxation, and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing craniotomy. Medline, Embase, Scopus and Cochrane databases were searched up to 20 August 2026. Outcomes were meta-analysed with random-effects inverse-variance models, reporting mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The GRADE framework was used to assess the certainty of evidence. Twelve RCTs (n = 803) were analysed. BC and NS had no statistically significant differences in intraoperative brain relaxation (RR 0.94 95% CI: 0.83 to 1.08) (GRADE: +++), good neurological outcome at discharge (RR 1.08 95% CI 0.92 to 1.25) (GRADE: +), or mortality (RR 0.60 95% CI: 0.20 to 1.78) (GRADE + ). BC was associated with a reduced incidence of hyperchloremic acidosis (RR 0.15 95% CI 0.03 to 0.78) (GRADE: +++). At 24 h postoperatively, BC patients had higher arterial pH (MD 0.03 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.05) (GRADE: +) and increased bicarbonate (MD 2.24 mEq/L 95% CI: 0.54 to 3.93 mEq/L) (GRADE: +). Balanced crystalloids improved acid-base and electrolyte profiles without significant differences in brain relaxation, neurological outcomes, or mortality. However, the certainty and clinical significance of these findings remain uncertain, highlighting the need for further adequately powered trials.

items.title: Do we have an appropriate cut-off for the kappa free light chain index in multiple sclerosis diagnosis? a real-world single-center comparison with oligoclonal bands.
items.abstract: The kappa free light chain (KFLC) index has emerged as a quantitative marker of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis and is increasingly used in the diagnostic evaluation of multiple sclerosis (MS). However, the optimal diagnostic threshold remains uncertain and may vary across clinical populations. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the KFLC index in a real-world neurological cohort, compare it with oligoclonal bands (OCBs), and determine a locally optimal cut-off value. We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 140 patients who underwent lumbar puncture during routine neurological diagnostic work-up. Sixty-four patients were diagnosed with MS and 76 with other neurological disorders. Demographic and cerebrospinal fluid parameters, including OCB status and KFLC index, were analyzed. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and the optimal KFLC cut-off was determined using Youden's index alongside the established 6.1 consensus cut-off, with 9.3 selected to maximize diagnostic specificity. Agreement between dichotomized KFLC results and OCB status was evaluated using Cohen's kappa. The KFLC index was significantly higher in patients with MS than in non-MS patients [median 43.4 (IQR 16.6-88.1) vs. 1.8 (IQR 1.4-2.8), p<0.001]. ROC analysis showed high diagnostic accuracy for the KFLC index, with an AUC of 0.954 (95% CI 0.919-0.990), compared with 0.831 (95% CI 0.756-0.905) for OCB status. A locally optimal KFLC index cut-off of 9.3 yielded 89.1% sensitivity, 96.0% specificity, a positive predictive value of 95.0%, a negative predictive value of 91.3%, and an overall accuracy of 92.9%. OCB positivity was observed in 68.8% of MS patients and 2.6% of non-MS patients. KFLC and OCB results were concordant in 122 of 140 patients (87.1%), with substantial agreement (Cohen's κ=0.73). Among 16 OCB-negative patients with KFLC index values above the selected threshold, 13 were ultimately diagnosed with MS. The KFLC index showed high diagnostic accuracy for MS in a heterogeneous real-world neurological cohort. The locally derived cut-off of 9.3 provided a favorable balance between sensitivity and specificity and identified a clinically relevant subgroup of OCB-negative patients with MS. These findings support further evaluation of the study-derived threshold in independent cohorts and contextual interpretation of KFLC and OCB within the overall diagnostic assessment.

items.title: Validation and reliability of the Epilepsy Self-Stigma Scale (ESSS) in Italian.
items.abstract: Self-stigma is the interiorization and acceptance of prejudicial beliefs of one person's culture of origin. Higher levels of self-stigma in epilepsy negatively affect quality of life and outcome. We investigated self-stigma in people with epilepsy (PwE) in Italy, by translating, culturally adapting and validating the Italian version of the Epilepsy Self-Stigma Scale (ESSS). For psychometric validation, the scale (together with GAD7, NDDI-E, QOLIE31 and RSES) was filled-in by 87 adult PwE anonymously and voluntarily participating to an online survey broadcasted on "Fondazione Epilessia LICE ETS" social media. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Internal consistency was good (Cronbach's α = 0.74). Reliability was high (Omega Total = 0.87). Higher stigma scores were moderately associated with greater anxiety (GAD-7; ρ = 0.43, p < 0.001) and depressive symptoms (NDDI-E; ρ = 0.39, p < 0.001). Negative correlations were observed with self-esteem (RSES; r = -0.45, p < 0.001) and quality of life (QOLIE-31; ρ = -0.42, p < 0.001). Individuals with lower levels of independence showed higher stigma scores. The 8-item Italian version of ESSS is valid and reliable. The findings suggest self-stigma is closely associated with quality of life through psychological factors, particularly self-esteem, although relationships should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design.

items.title: Prevalence and prognosis of gait dysfunction in patients operated on for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a Spine CORe™ analysis of QOD data.
items.abstract: Among patients undergoing surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), the prevalence of gait disturbance and the likelihood of gait improvement remain unclear. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and prognosis of gait disturbance in CSM and identify factors associated with gait improvement postoperatively. This was a retrospective analysis of the CSM cohort of the prospectively collected 14-site Spine CORe™ Study Group Quality Outcomes Database (QOD) registry. Outcomes of interest included postoperative ambulatory function at 24 months defined by lower extremity score on the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale and predictors of improved ambulation. The p values for descriptive statistics were obtained using paired and unpaired t-tests and chi-square tests as appropriate. For multivariable analysis, a logistic regression model was fit for improvement in gait in the subset of patients with baseline gait impairment. Of the 1141 patients meeting prespecified inclusion criteria, 1135 had baseline gait data; of these, 877 (77.3%) had baseline gait dysfunction and 258 (22.7%) did not. At baseline, patients with gait dysfunction were older (61.5 ± 11.6 vs 57.2 ± 11.7 years, p < 0.001), had higher BMI (30.4 ± 6.6 vs 29.3 ± 6.0 kg/m2, p = 0.008), were less likely to have private insurance (46.0% vs 67.4%, p < 0.001), and had more comorbidities. Preoperatively, patients with gait dysfunction had worse neck disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI], 41.0 ± 20.8 vs 30.2 ± 18.4, p < 0.001) and quality of life (EQ-VAS, 56.2 ± 21.4 vs 70.0 ± 18.9, p < 0.001; and EQ-5D, 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 0.7 ± 0.2, p < 0.001). Patients with impaired ambulation at baseline were less satisfied with surgery at 24 months (North American Spine Society satisfaction questionnaire [NASS] score 1, 51.4% vs 60.9%, p = 0.004). Among 596 patients with gait dysfunction who received follow-up postoperatively at 24 months, 304 (51.0%) showed improvement and 292 (49.0%) did not. Patients who improved also demonstrated greater improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) neck pain (-3.3 ± 3.2 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) and arm pain (-3.2 ± 3.9 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) scores, as well as better NDI (16.5 ± 17.4 vs 26.8 ± 20.9, p < 0.001), EQ-VAS (74.1 ± 20.0 vs 60.2 ± 23.2, p < 0.001), EQ-5D (0.8 ± 0.2 vs 0.6 ± 0.2, p < 0.001), and NASS (score 1, 74.0% vs 53.8%, p < 0.001) scores. Multivariable analyses revealed that lower BMI (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02, p = 0.01) and lower American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (for ASA class I or II, OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.04-2.80, p = 0.04) were associated with gait improvement. In this cohort, 77.3% of patients who underwent surgery for CSM demonstrated gait dysfunction preoperatively. Of these patients, 51% had gait improvement after cervical spine surgery. Lower BMI and ASA class were associated with improved gait postoperatively. Patients who improved reported superior quality of life, satisfaction with surgery, and decreased pain and disability.

items.title: Intelligent chemical production mode occupational health risk identification, assessment and intervention study.
items.abstract: The intelligent transformation of the chemical industry has reshaped petrochemical production workflows and altered occupational-health risk landscapes. This paper delineates four typical operating scenarios for intelligent chemical manufacturing and develops a four-tier hierarchical risk indicator system covering objectives, criteria, factors, and measurable indicators. A hybrid entropy-weighted Bayesian-network evaluation model is established, where entropy weights calibrate prior probabilities of root-node inputs while conditional-probability tables are retained to characterize risk-coupling behaviors. Model performance is validated via time-series partitioning, multi-model benchmark comparisons, and cross-validation using Monte-Carlo simulations. An entropy-weighted TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making method is adopted to rank intervention-target priorities, and discrete time-series analysis quantifies outcomes from a six-month closed-loop intervention program. Results demonstrate that human-machine interaction, psychological, and managerial risks dominate occupational-health hazards within intelligent chemical-production contexts. Three highly sensitive critical drivers are identified: operating-instruction error rate, risk-monitoring gap duration, and information-overload frequency. Multi-criteria decision analysis further reveals that high-sensitivity risk factors do not inherently represent optimal intervention targets. The proposed model achieves 88.2% prediction accuracy on time-series test datasets, and statistically significant overall-risk reduction is observed post-intervention. This work offers theoretical support for risk identification, equipment retrofitting, and worker-health protection for smart petrochemical sites, facilitating the synergistic advancement of chemical-industry intelligent modernization, operational safety, and employee occupational-health outcomes.

items.title: Metonymic reconstruction and cognitive compensation in English-to-Chinese idiom translation: A corpus-informed study.
items.abstract: Idiom translation can preserve figurative meaning while changing the imagery and contextual cues through which it is conveyed. A central analytical challenge is to identify how a translation preserves or reorganizes access to an idiom's figurative meaning and which semantic, pragmatic, or cultural aspect of meaning it primarily maintains in context. We developed a product-level framework separating metonymic reconstruction from cognitive compensation, with the latter classified as semantic, pragmatic, or cultural. Retrieval from the CCL Corpus yielded 152 English-to-Chinese records for six source idioms after deduplication and eligibility screening. The analysis combined inter-coder reliability assessment using pre-adjudication labels, descriptive summaries and association analyses of final labels, and contextual examination of selected corpus examples and coding disagreements. Coding agreement was high, and shift and compression were the most frequent reconstruction strategies. The final reconstruction and compensation labels showed pronounced within-sample association (bias-corrected Cramér's V = 0.760): shift occurred mainly with cultural compensation, compression with pragmatic compensation, and retention with semantic compensation. These pairings were not one-to-one, and five of the nine compensation disagreements concerned the semantic-pragmatic boundary. This association describes the selected records under the coding scheme; it does not provide direct evidence of translators' cognitive processes or benefits to reader comprehension. The framework provides a systematic, textually grounded approach to analysing how idiom translations preserve or reorganize access to figurative meaning and to identifying their primary semantic, pragmatic, or cultural compensation functions in context.

items.title: Relationships between participation in leisure activities and mortality risk among adults aged 65 years and older in China: A propensity score-weighted cohort study.
items.abstract: Leisure activities have been recognized as significant determinants of health among older adults; however, evidence of their association with mortality among Chinese elderly people remains limited. To examine the dose-response association between leisure activity participation and all-cause mortality risk among adults aged 65 years and older. Using data from the 2008-2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS), we investigated the association of leisure activity participation with all-cause mortality in older adults aged ≥65 years. Multinomial propensity score-based inverse probability weighting (IPW) was used to balance the measured covariates, and time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to estimate hazard ratios (HRs)with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Stratified subgroup analyses were performed by age and sex. Among adults aged 65 years and older, an inverse dose-response association was observed between leisure activity count and mortality risk: each additional activity was associated with a 10% lower all-cause mortality risk (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.87-0.92). Compared with never participants, almost daily engagement in housework, outdoor activities, garden work, reading newspapers or books, playing board/card games,, raising domestic animals or pets, watching TV or listening to the radio, and organized social activities was associated with a lower mortality risk. No significant age or sex interaction was observed for total leisure activity count (all P values for interactions>0.05). A significant age interaction was detected for board/card games (P for interaction=0.025). Participation in leisure activities was associated with lower all-cause mortality among Chinese adults aged 65 years and older. Encouraging older adults to engage in a diverse range of leisure activities may enhance their quality of life and support China's long-term goal of healthy aging.

items.title: Restorative plein-air environments and academic self-efficacy among fine arts students:A PLS-SEM-fsQCA study.
items.abstract: Plein-air painting is a core component of fine arts education, yet its educational value is often framed primarily in terms of artistic skill development rather than students' psychological learning outcomes. Drawing on Attention Restoration Theory, this cross-sectional survey examined associations between four perceived restorative qualities of plein-air environments and fine arts students' academic self-efficacy, including statistical indirect associations through fine-arts involvement. Data from 386 fine arts students with plein-air painting experience were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). The PLS-SEM results showed that Being Away and fine-arts involvement were positively associated with academic self-efficacy, whereas Fascination, Compatibility, and Extent had no statistically significant direct associations with the outcome. All four restorative qualities were positively associated with fine-arts involvement, and each showed a significant positive indirect association with academic self-efficacy through fine-arts involvement. The fsQCA identified five equifinal configurations associated with high academic self-efficacy. Taken together, the findings position restorative plein-air environments as conditional learning resources while not establishing temporal or causal relationships.

items.title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA) for Indian children.
items.abstract: Narrative comprehension requires children to understand explicitly presented information and integrate events to derive implicit meanings. Despite its developmental and educational importance, English-language narrative assessments developed within the Indian cultural context remain limited. This study developed and conducted a preliminary psychometric evaluation of the Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA), a picture-based assessment for Indian children aged 4-8 years. The NCA was developed across three phases. An initial set of 27 comprehension questions was refined through expert review to 20 items comprising 9 literal and 11 inferential questions. The final assessment used two wordless picture narratives and four sequential components: Picture Walk, Retelling, Prompted Comprehension, and Guided Story Narration. Preliminary evaluation was conducted with 80 typically developing children, equally distributed across four age groups from 4-5-7-8 years. Content validity was high (S-CVI/Ave = 0.93), and internal consistency was high for both narratives (α = 0.97 and 0.96). Significant age-group differences were observed across major NCA components for both narratives (p < .001), with large effect sizes. Literal comprehension exceeded inferential comprehension across all age groups (p < 0.001). Guided Story Narration yielded higher overall scores than Prompted Comprehension for both narratives (p < 0.001). Three-week test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.89 and 0.91). The findings provide preliminary evidence for the NCA's content relevance, internal consistency, developmental differentiation, and temporal stability. Larger and more diverse samples are required to further establish broader psychometric, cultural, and clinical validity and to support future normative development.

items.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions.
items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in CDKL5 cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain-binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

items.title: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics.
items.abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin and ketamine are attracting renewed attention as rapid-acting therapeutics, yet how they reshape cognitive computations remains poorly understood. To address this, we trained mice on a free-response perceptual decision-making task that disentangles bias-driven from sensory-guided strategies. Acute administration of psilocybin or ketamine slowed decision times while improving accuracy. Behavioral modeling combining drift diffusion and GLM-HMM approaches revealed that these effects were driven by increased decision thresholds and a shift toward sensory-engaged states. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping identified modulation of distributed task-related networks, including the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). Calcium imaging showed that OFC population dynamics were reorganized under psychedelic conditions, with preserved task selectivity but altered temporal structure and shifted population correlations. Together, these findings indicate that psychedelics shift decision-making toward greater reliance on sensory evidence while reshaping cortical population dynamics, providing a system-level account of their effects on perceptual decisions.

items.title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation.
items.abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

items.title: Diagnostic cues and users' privacy attitudes: Evidence from an ERP experiment.
items.abstract: Although digital and intelligent technologies generate substantial digital benefits for users, they simultaneously exacerbate the risk of privacy breaches, making the mitigation of privacy concerns and the reconciliation of economic gains with privacy protection a critical challenge. Based on Cue Diagnosticity Theory (CDT) and the Associative-Propositional Evaluation (APE) framework, this study examines how contextual cues with varying scopes affect the real-time formation of user privacy attitudes and employs event-related potentials (ERPs) to uncover the associated cognitive-neural mechanisms. In terms of methodology, platform popularity and platform evaluation were operationalized as high-range diagnostic cues, while privacy explanation was operationalized as a low-range diagnostic cues. A 2 × 2 × 2 factorial experimental design was employed to measure participants' behavioral responses and neural activities in the privacy disclosure willingness task. Based on the Cue Diagnosticity Theory (CDT) and the Associative-Propositional Evaluation (APE) model, privacy attitude formation is proposed to involve an initial stage of rapid affective responses to diagnostic cues, followed by cognitive evaluations of information congruence and conflict monitoring. Compared with later ERP components associated with emotional evaluation (LPP), attentional allocation (P300), and semantic integration (N400), P2 and N2 provide more sensitive neural indicators for uncovering the mechanisms underlying immediate privacy attitude formation. Specifically, P2 reflects early affective arousal elicited by potential privacy risks, whereas N2 indexes subsequent cognitive conflict monitoring during propositional evaluation. The findings demonstrate that: (1) both high-range and low-range diagnostic cues exert significant effects on privacy disclosure willingness. Under conditions of low platform popularity, low platform evaluation, and the absence of privacy explanation, users' privacy disclosure willingness was significantly reduced, while larger P2 and N2 amplitudes were elicited, indicating stronger early emotional responses to risk and higher levels of cognitive conflict in later stages. (2) when the valence of high-range diagnostic cues was inconsistent, providing privacy explanation, compared with providing no privacy explanation, significantly increased users' privacy disclosure willingness and reduced P2 and N2 amplitudes. (3) when the valence of high-range diagnostic cues was consistent, the effect of privacy explanation was not significant. The study contributes theoretically by uncovering the temporal dynamics and underlying mechanisms through which multiple diagnostic cues shape privacy attitude formation at the cognitive-neural level, thereby broadening the application of Cue Diagnosticity Theory and the Associative-Propositional Evaluation Model within privacy disclosure willingness settings. Practically, the findings provide guidance for digital platforms to optimize the presentation of privacy information and interface design, thereby helping users make more rational privacy decisions.

items.title: Exploring barriers and facilitators to Hepatitis C virus treatment access in Los Angeles County: A mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Diagnosed but untreated chronic Hepatitis C virus infection remains an important public health problem in Los Angeles County, particularly affecting underserved and minority groups. This mixed-methods study (October 2024-January 2025) aimed to identify and describe the barriers and facilitators to accessing Hepatitis C virus treatment among Los Angeles County residents. The study used de-identified programmatic data from 344 case-residents in a linkage-to-cure program and conducted thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with ten participants (seven untreated, three treated) from the linkage-to-cure program. Overall, 54% of case-residents reported experiencing barriers. Among those reporting specific barriers (n = 91), personal barriers were most common (43%), followed by provider-related barriers (31%), insurance barriers (13%), and inadequate access to medical care (13%). Interviews provided further context. Themes identified included homelessness, incarceration, and drug addiction as key personal barriers. Provider-related barriers included language barriers, expressed frustration in navigating the healthcare system, long wait times to see a provider, and participants' lack of HCV information. Insurance barriers were characterized by cost barriers and inadequate access to medical care due to a lack of transportation. Facilitators of treatment access included personal motivation to seek treatment, family and community-based support systems, trust in their medical provider, adequate insurance coverage, understanding the benefits of HCV treatment, and the desire to avoid stigmatization. Local efforts to eliminate Hepatitis C should consider equitable interventions that address individual and system-level barriers. Potential strategies include implementing language support services, leveraging patient navigation and care coordination services, utilizing mobile clinics for the unhoused, ensuring treatment continuity for people re-entering the community from incarceration, and removing insurance restrictions, such as prior authorization requirements.

items.title: An enhanced U-shape architecture network with cross-scale attention and frequency-domain perception for robust colorectal polyp segmentation.
items.abstract: The early detection and removal of colorectal polyps can help reduce colorectal cancer and mortality rates. The segmentation of colorectal polyps in colonoscopy images is difficult due to multi-scale morphology, blurred boundaries, and complex background interference.To solve this problem, we propose a network of cross-scale attention and frequency domain perception of encoder-decoder architecture.The network has two new modules: first, Scale-Aware Cross Attention Skip Connection (SCAS) uses multi-head attention mechanism and multi-scale pyramid fusion to fuse multi-scale features from encoder and decoder to enhance the model to capture polyp features of different sizes.Secondly, Dual-domain fusion (D2F) separates and assigns weights of low-frequency global information and high-frequency detail information of the feature map at bottleneck stage, improving the model to analyze spatial and frequency domains and improve polyp boundaries.Multiple public colorectal polyp segmentation datasets show that our method is competitive and performs better than existing mainstream approaches in terms of mIoU and mDice: On the CVC-ClinicDB dataset our model produces mDice of 0.922 and mIoU of 0.863, outperforming UNet, UNet++, PraNet, ACSNet, DCSAU-Net, HarDNet-CPS, ProMamba, FoBS. These results validate its strong segmentation capability and effectiveness in accurately delineating polyp regions with blurred boundaries, large size variations, and complex background interference. The proposed method provides a reliable and promising tool for clinical endoscopic assistant diagnosis. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/si-yuan20/Robust-segmentation-of-colon-polyps-Unet.

items.title: Modulating BCL11A levels and DNA binding to control fetal hemoglobin production in adult-like HUDEP-2 cells.
items.abstract: BCL11A is a pleiotropic transcription factor required for neurodevelopment, hematopoiesis, and the fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switch. Its erythroid-specific activity is a major therapeutic target for sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia. We investigate BCL11A function and regulation through three complementary approaches. First, we show that BCL11A ZF2-3 and ZF4-6 zinc-finger arrays recognize related 6-bp TGnCCA motifs through distinct strand-specific interactions, supporting a model in which BCL11A oligomers engage multiple DNA motifs. Second, we demonstrate that small-molecule inhibitors targeting DNA methylation, H3K9 methylation, or H3K27 methylation increase fetal hemoglobin (HbF) expression in HUDEP-2 cells, with low-dose combinations producing synergistic effects. The H3K27 methylation inhibitor FTX6058 also reduces BCL11A expression, potentially through LIN28B activation. Third, screening 213 molecular glue degraders identifies compounds that promote degradation of the zinc-finger proteins IKZF1 and ZFP91 and induce HbF expression. Together, these findings define multiple regulatory mechanisms and complementary pharmacological strategies for HbF reactivation.

items.title: The Benefits of Physical Exercise on Epilepsy Treatment: Possible Mechanisms via Neurotransmitters Modulation.
items.abstract: This narrative review aims to critically explored current preclinical and clinical evidence on the therapeutic benefits of physical exercise in epilepsy management, with particular emphasis on the underlying mechanisms mediated by modulation of key neurotransmitter systems, including GABAergic, glutamatergic, monoaminergic, and neurotrophic pathways. It seeks to reframe exercise from a historically perceived risk factor to a promising non-pharmacological adjunct capable of reducing seizure susceptibility and improving comorbid outcomes. A comprehensive narrative synthesis of the literature was conducted by searching major databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science) for peer-reviewed English-language studies examining physical exercise or activity in experimental epilepsy models and people with epilepsy. Inclusion prioritized investigations of neurotransmitter alterations (GABA, glutamate, dopamine, serotonin, noradrenaline), BDNF signaling, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and related clinical endpoints such as seizure frequency, cognition, and quality of life. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that regular moderate-to-vigorous aerobic and resistance exercise reduces seizure frequency and severity in animal models and selected clinical cohorts, while concurrently ameliorating depression, anxiety, cognitive deficits, and overall quality of life. Mechanistically, exercise elevates brain GABA levels and GABAergic neurosteroids, restores excitatory-inhibitory balance by modulating glutamate, enhances monoaminergic transmission (dopamine, serotonin, noradrenaline), and robustly upregulates hippocampal BDNF and downstream plasticity pathways (ERK/mTOR). Physical exercise emerges as a safe, accessible, and multifaceted complementary strategy in epilepsy treatment, exerting anticonvulsant and neuroprotective actions principally through neurotransmitter modulation and neurotrophic support. Integration of structured exercise into multidisciplinary care is warranted, although larger randomized trials are needed to optimize intensity, modality, and patient stratification, particularly in drug-resistant epilepsy.

items.title: Long-term radiographic marginal bone level changes around implants placed in periodontally healthy and periodontally compromised patients: A retrospective case series with 17-27 years of follow-up.
items.abstract: The aim of this retrospective radiographic case series analysis was to assess the marginal bone loss (mBL) of implants placed in periodontally healthy (PHP) and periodontally compromised (PCP) patients after an observation period of at least 17 years. A total of 32 patients (16 PHP and 16 PCP) rehabilitated with 57 implants (16 transmucosal and 41 submerged) with a mean follow-up of 19.5 years were selected for the analysis. All data were retrospectively extracted from the Department of Periodontology, University of Naples Federico II, Naples, Italy, and from a Private Practice in Piacenza, Italy. Marginal bone loss (mBL) was set as primary outcome. mBL was calculated by subtracting the radiographic vertical distance from the implant shoulder to the most apical point of crestal bone (IS-CB) at the time of crown insertion from the IS-CB at the follow-up. In addition, setting, implant location, smoking habit, sex, type of prostheses, emergence angle (EA), healing modality (transmucosal/submerged) and presence of marginal misfit were also collected. After a mean follow-up of 19.5 years, implants placed in PHP showed a mean mBL of 0.04 ± 0.69 mm, while around implants placed in PCP the mean mBL was 1.02 ± 1.96 mm. No statistically significant differences between PHP and PCP were found (p > 0.05). On the contrary, the frequency distribution of implants with mBL ≥ 3 mm was significantly different between groups (p < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis did not show a significant correlation between estimated variables and BL ≥ 3 mm. Within the limitations of present study, the results indicate that past history of periodontitis in patients adhering to SPC may not affect the mBL around implants placed in PCP. However, the limited number of patients at each time point and the low statistical power do not allow for strong conclusions to be drawn. Dental implants are considered effective for the rehabilitation of edentulous patients in both PHP and PCP with high percentage of survival rate after an observation period up to 17 years. However, limited evidence on mBL around dental implants in PHP and PCP after a mean observation period greater than 15 years was noted. Hence, the objective of the study was to assess the mBL around implants after at least 17 years of follow-up. At different time points a few implants yielded a mBL ≥ 3 mm.

items.title: The Role of U.S.-Based Professional Societies in Advancing and Creating Space for Global Psychological Science.
items.abstract: With growing recognition that psychological science has primarily focused on White Euro-American samples, constructs, theories, and methods, there is an urgent need to broaden the scope and inclusiveness of the discipline. Although journals, funding agencies, and individual scientists each play important roles in advancing this shift, U.S.-based professional societies are particularly well positioned to promote globally engaged psychological science. Recognizing this potential, the U.S. National Committee for Psychological Science, with assistance from the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences, undertook an effort to gather and compile information about what U.S.-based professional societies are doing to enhance global engagement. Representatives of 24 professional societies across clinical, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology; statistics; behavioral medicine; neuroscience; and general psychology completed an online survey. Our analysis indicated that international focus was very important or important to more than 70% of the society representatives surveyed, and various activities to promote global engagement were described, although membership of Majority World scientists remained low, with limited integration of these scientists in leadership structures. On the basis of these findings and prior scholarship, we outline key approaches for inclusive, strategic, and scaffolded efforts to promote global psychological science.

items.title: Rituximab-responsive epilepsia partialis continua in autoimmune Polyendocrine syndrome: A video-EEG-EMG polygraphic study.
items.abstract: Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC) is a rare and challenging form of focal motor status epilepticus. Its occurrence strictly in systemic autoimmune disorders without overt encephalitis is exceptional. Corticosteroids are first-line therapy but may be limited by significant side effects and poor metabolic tolerability. We report a 54-year-old woman with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome (APS), including autoimmune hepatitis, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults, celiac disease, and hypothyroidism, presenting with continuous jerks of right III-V fingers. Neurological examination showed continuous, irregular jerks confined to the right III, IV, and V fingers. Extensive serum and CSF screenings, including neuronal antibodies, and MRI were unremarkable. Ictal HMPAO-SPECT revealed a focal hyperperfusion in the left hand-knob area of the primary motor cortex. Brain FDG-PET revealed focal hypometabolism in the same region. Video-EEG-EMG polygraphy showed intermittent spikes and polyspikes over the left central region preceding EMG bursts of the right V finger's abductor muscle with a latency of approximately 30-40 ms. These findings were consistent with EPC. Corticosteroids induced marked improvement but were discontinued due to severe glycemic worsening. Subsequent treatment with oral steroids, IVIG, and multiple antiseizure medications were ineffective. Administration of Rituximab led to complete and sustained clinical and electrophysiological remission, which persisted at the 18-month follow-up. EPC can be a severe, focal manifestation of systemic autoimmunity even without encephalitis. Rituximab represents an effective steroid-sparing option for refractory autoimmune EPC, particularly in metabolically vulnerable patients.

items.title: Clinical outcomes and EEG monitoring in absence epilepsy trials: A narrative review.
items.abstract: Absence epilepsy is characterized by typical absence seizures with distinct electroclinical signatures. The main semiological feature is sudden behavioral arrest associated with brief impairment of consciousness, and the electroencephalographic (EEG) hallmark pattern is generalized, symmetric 2.5-4 Hz spike-and-wave discharges (GSW). Absence epilepsy diagnosis relies on correlating GSW with observable clinical manifestations. Monitoring therapeutic effects based solely on reported symptoms may be misleading, as behavioral arrest can be difficult to identify. Patients often do not recall most seizures, and observable motor/behavioral signs may be subtle, such as minimal twitches or transient lapses in responsiveness, which may go unnoticed. In clinical trials for absence epilepsies, quantification of GSW activity by EEG offers an objective and accurate measure of electrical burden and therapeutic efficacy. Despite technological limitations, GSW remains a robust neurophysiological endpoint. Increasing evidence indicates that the timing and burden of GSW correlate with epilepsy comorbidities, including attention, cognition, behavior, and sleep. We reviewed the published literature regarding GSW as an outcome measure in absence epilepsy, including nonseizure outcomes and comorbidities. Our review highlights (1) nearly 100% of clinical absence seizures exhibit sustained GSW discharges on EEG; (2) >49% of electrographic seizures are asymptomatic, indicating that reliance on seizure diaries without EEG monitoring underestimates seizure frequency and burden; (3) Genetic Generalized Epilepsy is not a benign condition and is associated with a high prevalence of cognitive and behavioral comorbidities, supporting evaluation beyond clinically observable seizures and the use of prolonged (≥24-h) EEG monitoring; (4) circadian and multidien cycles further emphasize the need for prolonged EEG recordings to reduce timing-related bias; and (5) antiseizure medications effective in absence epilepsy reduce GSW, supporting EEG monitoring as an objective treatment outcome measure. We therefore recommend incorporating ≥24-h EEG in future clinical trials, especially in (young) adults, and exploring comorbidities as important outcome measures. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Absence epilepsy causes brief episodes in which a person suddenly stops what they are doing and may not be aware of their surroundings. Many of these seizures have no obvious signs and are often missed or forgotten, meaning seizure diaries alone do not show the full picture. Our review shows that brain recordings (electroencephalographic, EEG), especially when done over 24 h or longer, detect many unrecognized seizures and better measure how well treatments work. EEG findings are also linked to problems with attention, thinking, behavior, and sleep, highlighting the need to look beyond visible seizures when evaluating treatments in clinical trials.

items.title: Brivaracetam in Genetic Generalized Epilepsies and Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy, retention, safety, and tolerability of brivaracetam (BRV) in patients with genetic generalized epilepsies (GGEs) and developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). We systematically searched the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases for studies published up to October 19, 2026. Methods followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions were performed to estimate pooled proportions of patients achieving ≥ 50% reduction in seizure frequency, seizure freedom, retention rates, and safety and tolerability. Subgroup analyses were performed separately for juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) and DEEs. Twenty studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled ≥ 50% responder rate was 50% (95% confidence interval [CI] 35-66%), while the pooled seizure-freedom rate was 22% (95% CI 11-39%). In the GGE subgroup, pooled ≥ 50% responder and seizure-freedom rates were 61% (95% CI 41-78%) and 38% (95% CI 17-65%), respectively. In the JME subgroup, pooled ≥ 50% responder and seizure-freedom rates were 77% (95% CI 45-93%) and 67% (95% CI 57-75%), respectively. In patients with DEEs, the pooled ≥ 50% responder rate was 44% (95% CI 24-66%). The pooled 12-month retention rate was 62% (95% CI 42-79%). The pooled proportion of patients experiencing any treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) was 37% (95% CI 19-60%), while 7% (95% CI 3-19%) discontinued BRV due to TEAEs. BRV appears to provide clinically meaningful seizure control with favorable retention and tolerability in GGEs, particularly in JME. Although the available evidence also suggests potential benefit in DEEs, conclusions remain limited by small, predominantly retrospective studies and substantial clinical heterogeneity.

items.title: Parkin Modulates PFOS Induced Apoptosis via Bax Ubiquitination in Rat Dopaminergic Neuronal Cells.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a group of synthetic compounds known for their high chemical stability and resistance to degradation. Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) is one such PFAS that has been found to produce mitochondrial stress and neurotoxicity, although the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Parkin, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, is a critical regulator of mitochondrial quality control, and its dysfunction is associated with neuronal vulnerability. Here, we investigated the involvement of parkin and Bax ubiquitination in PFOS-induced apoptotic signaling. Using N27 dopaminergic cells, we assessed dose- and time-dependent effects of PFOS exposure. Early exposure induced an adaptive response characterized by increased parkin expression and enhanced ubiquitination of Bax, accompanied by reduced pro-apoptotic signaling. In contrast, prolonged or higher-dose exposure led to a decline in parkin levels, increased Bax expression, cytochrome c release, and activation of caspase-3/7, consistent with engagement of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway and mitochondrial dysfunction. Furthermore, PRKN knockdown exacerbated PFOS-induced cytotoxicity, supporting a protective role for parkin under PFOS-induced cellular stress. These findings suggest that alterations in parkin-associated Bax ubiquitination may contribute to the regulation of apoptotic signaling following PFOS exposure, shifting the balance toward cell death. Collectively, our results provide mechanistic insight into how environmental toxicants impair mitochondrial surveillance pathways and may contribute to dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

items.title: MOG-IgG in the cerebrospinal fluid: a narrative review.
items.abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a recently described inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) associated with antibodies against MOG (MOG-Abs). MOG-Abs are mostly synthesized in the peripheral compartment, but recent studies reported paired/isolated MOG-Abs cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) positivity, suggesting the possible occurrence of intrathecal synthesis. Nonetheless, this is of unclear diagnostic and prognostic significance, with concerns on the specificity and overall clinical relevance of isolated CSF MOG-Abs positivity. Consequently, current diagnostic criteria emphasize MOG-Abs seropositivity, while requiring additional clinical/radiological supportive features to diagnose MOGAD in patients with isolated CSF positivity. The aim of this narrative review is to clarify the diagnostic and prognostic significance of MOG-Abs CSF positivity.

items.title: From localisation to network modulation: how instruments reshaped the structure-function question in clinical neuroscience.
items.abstract: How function is organised in the brain remains an open question for neuroscience as a whole; its history, clinical neuroscience included, is largely the history of its instruments and of the limits they impose on interpretation. That relation is visible from the outset: under the light microscope, Golgi's black reaction was compatible with both the reticular theory and the neuron doctrine, a dispute settled only in the 1950s, by electron microscopy. This contribution traces that pattern along the axis of neurostimulation, from Fritsch and Hitzig's experiments and Penfield's intraoperative mapping to contemporary therapeutic neuromodulation, and argues that the shift from the discrete locus to the distributed network, made conceivable by functional neuroimaging and connectomics, found its causal and clinical proving ground in stimulation rather than in observation. Mood disorders furnish the exemplary case. Explanation moved from a diffuse neurochemical model of monoamine depletion, through the humoral model of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal dysregulation, to a limbic-cortical circuit account that specified a place to intervene: the subgenual cingulate. What followed is instructive precisely because it disappointed. Encouraging open-label results gave way to a multicentre controlled trial halted for futility; connectivity-guided targeting, developed in parallel, is only now undergoing sham-controlled pivotal testing. Replication failures in connectivity-based subtyping, and the sample sizes now known to be required for stable brain-behaviour associations, suggest that the point is general rather than anecdotal. The sequence recurs: the instrument defines the target, the target generates conviction, and reproducibility is established last, when it is the criterion that should come first.
