items.title: Mapping Mesoscale Cardiac Architecture With Axially Swept Dithered Light-Sheet Microscopy.
items.abstract: Comprehensive characterization of cardiac microstructure and vascular networks is critical for assessing cardiovascular development, disease progression, and therapeutic interventions. While volumetric imaging combined with tissue clearing enables high-resolution organ-level analysis, the densely organized cardiac microenvironment, characterized by compacted and trabeculated myocardium, remains technically challenging to resolve in its entirety. To address these limitations, we exploit the temporal dynamics of illumination-detection interplay to create a time-averaged beam profile, thereby maximizing system throughput across multi-scale specimens. Our dithered light-sheet (DiLS) approach extends the confocal region by over 40% and improves the space-bandwidth product while largely preserving optical sectioning capability. Building on this, the axially swept dithered light-sheet (AS-DiLS) employs a dual-actuator strategy that combines rapid beam dithering and axial sweeping to further accelerate imaging speed while achieving micrometer-scale resolution across centimeter-scale scanning ranges, enabling detailed cardiovascular morphological and topological assessment from embryonic to adult stages. We anticipate that this scalable imaging scheme will advance in-depth investigations of organ morphogenesis and disease pathogenesis across a broad spectrum of models.

items.title: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a Biomarker for Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy Tau Tangle Neuropathology.
items.abstract: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease that cannot accurately be diagnosed during life due to the absence of in vivo biomarkers for CTE neuropathology. To evaluate plasma endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau (eMTBR-tau) as a candidate biomarker for CTE tau tangle neuropathology. This case series included 21 former American-style football players who completed a blood draw as part of participation in clinical research at Boston University beginning April 17, 2008, and who subsequently died, donated their brain, and had completed autopsy by October 9, 2026. Plasma eMTBR-tau nucleic acid-linked immunosandwich assay single-plex immunoassay and plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) (SP-X n = 20; Elecsys n = 1). CTE status and stage. Cumulative neuropathologic tau burden scores ranged from 0 to 33 (higher scores indicate tau burden; 0, no tau burden). Among 21 male brain donors (median age at blood draw, CTE positive: 68 years [IQR, 61-77]; CTE negative: 49 years [IQR, 47-56]), 18 had a neuropathologic diagnosis of CTE. Of these participants, 16 had a diagnosis of high-stage CTE (stage IV = 8, stage III = 8); and 2, of low-stage CTE (stage II = 1, stage I = 1). Five CTE-positive participants had intermediate or high Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in CTE-positive participants (median, 0.019 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.030]) compared with CTE-negative participants (0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.61 [95% CI, 0.51-2.70]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentrations were highest among CTE-positive participants with comorbid ADNC (0.082 pg/mL [IQR, 0.059-0.131]) and intermediate among those with high-stage CTE without ADNC (n = 11; median, 0.009 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.021]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in high-stage CTE (median, 0.021 pg/mL [IQR, 0.006-0.038]) compared with low-stage CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.002]; β = 1.79 [95% CI, 0.45-3.13]) or no CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.78 [95% CI, 0.85-2.71]). Differences remained significant after exclusion of 5 cases with comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was associated with higher cumulative neuropathologic tau burden score across 11 brain regions (β = 0.71 [95% CI, 0.38-1.05]). Plasma p-tau217 concentration was positively associated with eMTBR-tau (β = 0.68 [95% CI, 0.32-1.04]) but was not associated with CTE. P-tau217 concentrations were in the negative range (n = 11) or intermediate range (n = 5) for participants without ADNC copathology. Four participants with ADNC had p-tau217 concentrations in the positive range; and 1, in the intermediate range. Participants with high-stage CTE had higher concentrations of plasma eMTBR-tau than those with low-stage or no CTE; concentrations were highest among those with CTE and comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau may represent a feasible biomarker candidate for high-stage CTE tau tangle neuropathology. Larger autopsy and clinical validation studies are needed to establish overall diagnostic accuracy and specificity of plasma eMTBR-tau for CTE neuropathology, in addition to the associated prognostic and clinical implications.

items.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke's area.
items.abstract: Wernicke's area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke's area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

items.title: Statin use is associated with reduced negative symptoms in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: A longitudinal observational study.
items.abstract: Inflammation has been implicated in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), suggesting that anti-inflammatory strategies might offer therapeutic potential. While statins exert anti-inflammatory effects and may reduce negative symptoms, findings on their efficacy remain inconsistent. We investigated whether statin use is associated with changes in symptom severity in SSD. This longitudinal cohort study used real-world data from the Pharmacotherapy Monitoring and Outcome Survey (PHAMOUS), an annual routine outcome monitoring program in the Netherlands. Data were collected from 2013 to 2024. Participants with SSD who were not using statins at baseline and had no recorded substance-related disorders other than cannabis or alcohol were included. Individuals who initiated statin therapy during the observational period were classified as statin users, all others were classified as non-users. Outcomes were changes in log-transformed Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) negative subscale scores and, secondarily, total and other subscale scores over time. Among the included participants, 264 initiated statin therapy, whereas 2,952 participants did not use statins during the study period. After one year, statin use was associated with a credible reduction in PANSS negative subscale scores (adjusted posterior mean = -0.358, 95% CI [-0.533, -0.174], PD = 1), corresponding to an approximately 3.6- point lower score when using the baseline median score of 11 as a reference. No credible evidence of mediation by C-reactive protein, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, or blood pressure was observed. The association with lower negative symptom scores was also observed among patients with continued statin use over three years. Statin use was associated with reduced negative symptom severity in individuals with SSD. Beyond their established cardiometabolic benefits, statins may also have therapeutic potential for negative symptoms in SSD.

items.title: Deep Clustering of fMRI with Global-Local Feature Extraction for Functional Brain Activity Analysis.
items.abstract: Clustering is essential for identifying patterns in data. In neuroscience, it is widely used on functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data to uncover brain activity patterns during cognitive tasks and rest. However, traditional methods like K-means struggle with the high dimensionality and temporal complexity of fMRI data, and often fail to capture spatial or contextual structures in image data, limiting their effectiveness. To address these challenges, we propose a deep clustering model that leverages the complementary strengths of Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) and Masked Autoencoder (MAE) for comprehensive feature extraction. The SAE captures global features and reduces data dimensionality while preserving overall structure. In parallel, the MAE reconstructs masked input patches to learn local contextual features-temporal for sequential data like fMRI, and spatial for imagedata. The combination of global and local features yields a more informative representation of the data. These fused features are then fed into a Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) module, which iteratively refines cluster centers and feature representations using Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence loss, improving clustering accuracy and robust ness. Experimental results show that our model effectively identifies functional brain activity patterns in task based fMRI and differentiates hippocampal subregions in resting-state fMRI. Overall, our approach offers a unified and versatile deep clustering framework capable of handling various data modalities, enabling more accurate and interpretable analysis in both neuroimaging and general high-dimensional data applications. The proposed framework explicitly decomposes global and local feature learning, overcoming limitations of single path deep clustering methods and providing physiologically meaningful clustering patterns.

items.title: Reinforced hippocampus-accumbens pathway marks a shift toward cognitive decline in aging.
items.abstract: Aging triggers early functional alterations in brain circuits preceding cognitive impairment, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unaddressed. Spatial navigation and memory, among the earliest affected, depend on the hippocampus and downstream targets such as the nucleus accumbens (NAc), which integrates spatial and motivational information to guide goal-directed behaviors. Here we identify age-related, sex-dependent changes in the dorsal hippocampus-NAc (dHPC→NAc) pathway. Combining optogenetics with electrophysiology, chemogenetics, and behavioral analyses in mice, we show that aging shifts the excitation-inhibition balance in dorsal CA1 toward pyramidal neuron hyperactivity, strengthening hippocampal outputs. This selectively enhances synaptic drive onto D1 receptor-expressing medium spiny neurons and involves a previously unrecognized long-range parvalbumin-expressing projection. Chemogenetically reducing the dHPC→NAc activity improves memory in aged mice. In humans, fMRI reveals heightened posterior hippocampal activity and stronger posterior HPC-NAc coupling during navigation. Together, we uncover a targetable pathway acting in an intervention-sensitive window of aging to correct negative cognitive trajectories.

items.title: OSTM1 restrains B-cell lymphomagenesis by promoting PDE3B degradation and activating cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling.
items.abstract: Through a genome-wide forward CRISPR/Cas9 screen in interleukin-3 (IL3)-dependent Ba/F3 cells, we identified osteoclastogenesis-associated transmembrane protein 1 (OSTM1) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor. Analysis of patient datasets revealed that OSTM1 is frequently deleted or downregulated in human B-cell malignancies (BCM). In mice, Cd19-Cre-driven B cell-specific monoallelic or biallelic deletion of Ostm1 cooperated with Cdkn2a loss to drive lymphomagenesis with near-complete penetrance. Mechanistically, OSTM1 directly interacts with phosphodiesterase 3B (PDE3B) and promotes its proteasomal degradation. Because PDE3B hydrolyzes cyclic AMP (cAMP), loss of OSTM1 stabilizes PDE3B, leading to suppression of tumor-suppressive cAMP-dependent PKA/CREB signaling and promotion of oncogenic transformation. Consistent with this mechanism, PDE3B is frequently amplified or upregulated in BCM, and expression of CREB/CREBBP transcriptional targets correlates positively with OSTM1 expression but inversely with PDE3B across BCM cohorts. Importantly, silencing Pde3b reverses oncogenic transformation driven by Ostm1 loss. Together, these findings establish OSTM1 as a tumor suppressor and uncover an OSTM1/PDE3B/cAMP signaling axis that restrains B-cell lymphomagenesis and may represent a therapeutically actionable vulnerability.

items.title: Believing is feeling? Emotion malleability beliefs in both at-risk for and clinically diagnosed bipolar disorders.
items.abstract: Despite the centrality of emotion dysregulation within bipolar disorders (BDs) and the severe and chronic nature of these conditions, limited research has examined how beliefs about emotion relate to mood health dimensions in this population. The present two-study investigation examined how emotion malleability beliefs (EMBs)-that is, whether emotions are viewed as more or less malleable-are related to mood symptomatology, BD risk and diagnosis, and life functioning. Study 1 (data collected between 2019 and 2020) assessed EMBs, symptom severity, and BD risk, in a multisite sample of emerging adults (N = 1,263). Study 2 (data collected between 2010 and 2014) compared EMBs in a community sample of adults diagnosed with bipolar I disorder (n = 100) with nonpsychiatric controls (n = 85) and assessed longitudinal associations between EMBs and mood symptoms, mood episode occurrence, and functioning in the BD group. In Study 1, lower EMBs were associated with greater depressive but not mania symptoms. In Study 2, individuals with BD reported lower EMBs than the control group. Furthermore, lower EMBs within the BD group were associated with greater mania severity and depressive episode frequency at a 12-month follow-up. Participants in both studies were majority White and educated, highlighting the need for greater demographic diversity in future research. The current findings suggest that EMBs may play a role in emotional disorders that involve positive mood symptomatology and may be associated with diagnosis of BD. items.title: Racial trauma and criterion a: On the nature of discrimination, threat, and danger.
items.abstract: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, fifth edition, text revision, Criterion A for posttraumatic stress disorder describes potential traumatic events as actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence. On its face, racial discrimination, particularly when individual discriminatory experiences, does not meet conventional trauma criteria. This commentary considers whether racial discrimination could be a source of perceived threat and considers how this might be relevant regarding the trauma diagnosis. Drawing on research in psychoneuroimmunology, neuroscience, and social rejection, this commentary examines the physiological mechanisms through which perceived discrimination activates the body's threat-response systems. Evidence suggests that racial discrimination activates neurobiological threat pathways involving the amygdala, anterior cingulate cortex, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and inflammatory response system. Studies have linked perceived discrimination to elevated inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and interleukin-6, as well as adverse cardiovascular, metabolic, and reproductive outcomes. Research on social rejection provides a theoretical framework for understanding why seemingly minor discriminatory experiences may cumulatively signal danger and activate physiological defense mechanisms. Racial discrimination can function as a biologically meaningful threat even when individual experiences fall outside current Criterion A definitions. Incorporating evidence of physiological threat activation into trauma research and reconsidering how subjective and cumulative threats are addressed in posttraumatic stress disorder diagnostic criteria may provide a more comprehensive understanding of racial trauma and its health consequences. items.title: miR-34a-5p, miR-340-3p, CCL22, and CXCL16 in Parkinson's disease: peripheral expression patterns and transcriptomic insights.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with peripheral immune alterations, in which chemokines and potentially regulatory microRNAs (miRNAs) may contribute to peripheral inflammatory alterations. This study, therefore, investigated the expression of miR-34a-5p/CCL22 and miR-340-3p/CXCL16 Axes in peripheral blood and explored their relationships with transcriptomic and immune-cell patterns in PD. The candidate miRNAs miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p were selected based on target prediction, with previous experimental evidence additionally supporting the miR-34a-5p/CCL22 interaction, and their corresponding chemokine targets, CCL22 and CXCL16, were evaluated using RT-qPCR in peripheral blood from 34 patients with PD and 34 healthy controls (HCs). Anindependent transcriptomic cohort (GSE99039; 205 patients with idiopathic PD and 233 controls) was analyzed using machine-learning approaches, differential expression, functional enrichment, and CIBERSORTx-based immune-cell estimation. miR-34a-5p expression was significantly higher in patients with PD than in controls (β = 0.62, 95% CrI 0.13-1.11, P = 0.011), whereas CXCL16, CCL22, and miR-340-3p did not differ significantly between groups. In patients with PD, CXCL16 was inversely correlated with miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p. Our findings also revealed a significant positive correlation between miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p in both the PD and HC groups. In GSE99039, CXCL16 was consistently prioritized among 60 chemokine-related genes and showed a positive association with estimated neutrophil abundance and inverse associations with several T-cell populations. CCL22 showed weaker and more heterogeneous associations with immune-cell populations. Although CXCL16 and CCL22 were not differentially expressed between PD and controls, CXCL16 showed consistent associations with peripheral immune-cell composition in an independent transcriptomic cohort. Together with the increased expression of miR-34a-5p and its association with CXCL16, these findings support further investigation of chemokine-miRNA relationships in the peripheral immune alterations associated with PD.

items.title: Clean sport in childhood: a paediatric call for doping prevention and early clinical recognition.
items.abstract: Physical activity is essential to child health, yet its potential adverse aspects, particularly doping, remain largely overlooked in paediatric populations. Emerging data indicate that doping behaviours are not anecdotal among youth in a context of increasingly intensive and widespread competitive youth sports. Children and adolescents represent a uniquely vulnerable population due to neurological, endocrine and musculoskeletal immaturity, identity construction, and strong social influences, including those from elite sports, peers, parents, and coaches. These factors may favour risk-taking behaviours and the normalisation of doping, with potentially serious and multisystem health consequences. Despite this, doping remains a blind spot in paediatric clinical practice. This narrative review aims to raise awareness of this underestimated issue, highlight key mechanisms of vulnerability, and emphasise the critical role paediatricians can play in early identification and prevention. Promoting proactive education, identification and multidisciplinary care is essential to safeguard young athletes in the evolving sporting environment. • Doping may cause significant physical and psychological harm during growth and development, yet it remains under-recognised in paediatric practice. • This narrative review highlights the specific vulnerability of children and adolescents to doping, summarises key warning signs for early clinical recognition, and proposes a practical prevention framework for paediatricians, emphasising their central role in prevention in line with international recommendations.

items.title: [Therapeutic drug monitoring in the clinical application-Part 1 : Why it is difficult to infer the drug concentration from the dose].
items.abstract: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) incorporates the measurement and interpretation of drug concentrations for optimization of (psycho)pharmacotherapy. The TDM group of the AGNP (Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Neuropsychopharmakologie und Pharmakopsychiatrie) has already published consensus guidelines for the optimal application of TDM in 2004, 2011 and 2018. The updated version of the consensus guidelines, which will be presented in the second part of this CME series, provides a fundamental methodological revision of the procedures to establish therapeutic- and dose-related reference ranges.The present part 1 of this two-part series on TDM provides the fundamental basics in order to show why it is rarely possible to infer the drug concentration from the administered dose. Part 2 then shows how a consistent application of TDM in combination with pharmacogenetic recommendations can help to optimize the psychopharmacological treatment in order to improve the treatment outcome.

items.title: Face adaptation to artificial filter characteristics: implications for face representations.
items.abstract: Successful recognition of familiar faces despite continuous changes, such as aging or varying lighting conditions, requires a flexible face memory system that continuously updates existing representations based on new visual input. These processes can be studied using the face adaptation paradigm, in which prior exposure to manipulated faces (adaptors) biases the perception of subsequently presented faces: veridical faces are perceived as shifted in the direction opposite to the adaptor, whereas faces resembling the adaptor appear more "normal." Such effects provide a useful tool for investigating how facial information is represented in memory. On social media, users are routinely exposed to artificially filtered faces that smooth skin, homogenize features, or enhance contours. However, it remains unclear whether such exposure updates face representations in memory, as reflected in face adaptation effects. If so, filter characteristics such as blurring or sharpening, may systematically influence face perception and recognition. We therefore investigated adaptation to artificial filter characteristics using blurring and sharpening manipulations. Our results provide evidence for adaptation effects (Experiment 1). These effects remained stable over a five-minute interval (Experiment 3) but were not observed at an intermediate interval of 3,000 ms (Experiment 4), indicating a non-linear time course. Furthermore, adaptation was not specific to upright face processing (Experiment 2) and did transfer across images or identities. Together, these findings suggest that the observed effects reflect general visual and non-identity specific face processing mechanisms, while there is no substantial evidence that the artificial filter information is robustly represented in face memory.

items.title: Perspectives of parents of children with monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders on research involving patient-derived neuronal models.
items.abstract: Patient-derived stem cell-based neuronal models hold great promise for advancing research into monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (mNDDs). These neuronal models are generated using induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technologies, and are perceived as "ethically sensitive". To date, ethical discussions on the use of neuronal models have predominantly focused on three-dimensional (3D) neuronal models, such as brain organoids, while two-dimensional (2D) neuronal models - which are widely used in current research settings - remain underexplored. A better understanding of the perspectives of parents of children with mNDDs on ethical issues - including the moral status of 2D models, informed consent, autonomy, privacy and misuse - is needed. We report the results of a semi-structured interview study among parents of children with mNDDs (n = 28) investigating their perspectives on the ethically responsible use of 2D patient-derived neuronal models in research. Respondents ascribed limited intrinsic value to neuronal models, often viewing them as ethically comparable to other somatic cells. They were highly motivated to enroll their child in iPSC research, but suggested that researchers: (1) restrict the use of their child's donated material to purposes benefiting the mNDD community, (2) protect their child's privacy, (3) communicate about research findings and reuse of donated material, and (4) minimize risks and burdens of research procedures for their (vulnerable) child. Based on these findings, we provide recommendations to research groups for informed consent and engagement processes to support responsible inclusion of children with mNDDs and their families in research using iPSC-based neuronal models.

items.title: Microstructural disruption of the forceps minor in schizophrenia: a potential clinical imaging biomarker using translational DTI.
items.abstract: Schizophrenia is one of the most complex brain disorders, arising from multidimensional pathophysiological processes that span genetic vulnerability, neurotransmitter dysregulation, structural brain damage, and large-scale brain network dysfunction. Large-scale neuroimaging studies have consistently demonstrated the critical role of frontal brain regions in schizophrenia. Despite substantial progress, the precise localization of structural damage within these regions and the neurobiological mechanisms linking such alterations to disease pathology remain poorly understood. In this study, we included a total of 115 subjects from two sites of the B-SNIP dataset, comprising 60 healthy controls and 55 individuals with schizophrenia. We employed diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to precisely characterize specific structural alterations in the frontal brain regions associated with schizophrenia. Our findings reveal significant microstructural abnormalities in the forceps minor, a major commissural white-matter tract that serves as a critical interhemispheric bridge between the bilateral frontal lobes. Network-level mapping further demonstrates that the forceps minor is closely integrated with large-scale brain networks, particularly the default mode network, and maintains strong structural connectivity with orbitofrontal regions-both of which are known to exhibit dysfunction in schizophrenia. Moreover, converging evidence suggests that the forceps minor plays an important role in the regulation of social behavior, a core domain of impairment in schizophrenia. Collectively, these findings identify the forceps minor as a promising structural imaging biomarker for schizophrenia and provide novel insights into the microstructural mechanisms underlying the disorder.

items.title: Intercellular Mitochondrial Transfer in Parkinson's Disease: Cargo Quality, Cell State Vulnerability, and Therapeutic Selectivity.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a defining feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), but it is still often framed as a neuron-autonomous defect of vulnerable dopaminergic neurons. This view misses an intercellular layer of mitochondrial quality control in which glia, extracellular vesicles, tunnelling nanotubes, and mitochondrial extrusion pathways influence whether mitochondrial material is retained, degraded, transferred, or released. In acute CNS injury, mitochondrial transfer can restore bioenergetic capacity in stressed cells. In PD, the same process is unlikely to be uniformly protective. PINK1/Parkin, LRRK2, GBA1, and α-synuclein affect mitochondrial quality control, organelle trafficking, vesicle biology, lysosomal clearance, and innate immune activation. These changes create conditions in which transferred cargo may be beneficial, disposable, or harmful. Here, we distinguish direct PD evidence from mechanisms inferred from other CNS disorders and general cell biology. We interpret mitochondrial transfer in PD through two linked variables: cargo quality and recipient cell state. Functional mitochondria may support metabolic repair; damaged organelles may be routed for disposal; and α-synuclein- or mtDNA-associated cargo may propagate proteopathic stress and inflammation. Therapeutic strategies should therefore focus less on increasing mitochondrial movement per se than on enriching competent cargo, preserving donor cell fitness, and preventing transfer routes from amplifying pathology.

items.title: Transplantation of Lhx8/KDM7A/FGF4-induced OM-MSCs-derived neuron-like cells improves neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in Aβ1-42-induced mouse model.
items.abstract: Cell-based therapies have emerged as a promising therapeutic avenue for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Prior studies have demonstrated the beneficial effects of neuronal-like cells differentiated from human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in mitigating AD pathology. This study investigates the therapeutic efficacy and molecular mechanisms of neuronal-like cells derived from olfactory mucosa MSCs (OM-MSCs) in Aβ1-42-induced acute neurotoxicity. Neuronal differentiation of OM-MSCs was induced using tricyclodecan-9-yl-xanthogenate (D609). An in vivo model was constructed by intrahippocampal injection of Aβ1-42 and treated by transplantation of OM-MSC-derived neuronal cells (OM-MSCs-NCs). In this study, we demonstrated that LIM homeobox protein 8 (Lhx8) expression was upregulated during OM-MSCs-NCs neuronal differentiation. Functional analyses revealed that Lhx8 overexpression enhanced neuronal differentiation of OM-MSCs, whereas Lhx8 knockdown impaired this process. In Aβ1-42-induced mouse models, transplantation of OM-MSCs-NCs ameliorated cognitive deficits, and neuroinflammation while promoting M2-like microglial polarization. Notably, Lhx8-overexpressing OM-MSCs-NCs exhibited amplified therapeutic efficacy, whereas Lhx8-knockdown cells showed diminished effects. Mechanistically, Lhx8 transcriptionally activates lysine demethylase 7 A (KDM7A) by binding to its promoter, thereby regulating the KDM7A/fibroblast growth factor 4 (FGF4) axis. Knockdown of either KDM7A or FGF4 abolished both the pro-differentiation effects of Lhx8 overexpression in vitro and its therapeutic benefits in an Aβ1-42-induced acute toxicity model. In conclusion, Lhx8 promotes neuronal-like differentiation of OM-MSCs by activating the KDM7A/FGF4 axis, thereby alleviating neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in an Aβ1-42-induced mouse model.

items.title: Goals of Care Conversations with Patients Living with Brain Tumors for Neurologists.
items.abstract: This article outlines the importance of goals-of-care (GOC) conversations in people living with brain tumors (PLWBTs) and why this population demands a disease-specific approach, proposing optimal timing of these conversations, and suggesting communication frameworks neurologists can use. Given progressive functional neurologic decline, cognitive impairment, and aphasia, PLWBTs should have GOC earlier in their disease course. Recent research reflects that early GOC conversations can improve quality-of-life. Emerging qualitative work suggests that having initial GOC conversations during chemo-radiation to the first few cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy may be preferable for patients with high-grade primary brain tumors and their care-partners. Early GOC conversations are essential given the guarded prognosis and progressive nature of decline for PLWBTs. This article serves as a resource for general neurologists leading these conversations, outlining important considerations and practical frameworks for effective discussions with patients and their loved ones.

items.title: Whey Protein Hydrolysate Attenuates Spatial Memory Deficits and Alters Hippocampal Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 in an STZ-Induced Rat Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
items.abstract: Alzheimers disease, known as a primary contributor to dementia, is characterized by cognitive deterioration and the buildup of beta-amyloid plaques along with tau tangles. Oxidative stress is a major contributor to the pathology, and Nrf2 enhances antioxidant responses by activating the HO-1 gene. Whey protein, exhibits antioxidant properties and can activate the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. This study evaluated the effects of whey protein hydrolysate (WPH) administration on hippocampal-dependent spatial memory, Keap1 and Nrf2 protein expression in hippocampal subregions, HO-1 mRNA expression in whole hippocampal tissue, and hippocampal neuronal integrity in a rat model of STZ-induced Alzheimer's disease.Thirty Wistar rats were assigned to three groups to study Alzheimer's disease induced by a single intracerebroventricular injection of streptozotocin (3 mg/kg). After one week of recovery, the rats received 100 mg/kg of whey protein hydrolysate (WPH) daily via gavage for four weeks. To assess spatial memory, the Barnes Maze test was used. Keap1 and Nrf2 proteins were visualized through immunofluorescent staining; HO-1 gene expression was measured using real-time PCR; and the number of intact hippocampal neurons was counted with cresyl-violet staining. In the WPH group, both latency time and the number of errors decreased, while the duration of stay in the target area increased compared with the STZ group. Also, in the WPH group in the CA1, CA3, and DG regions of the hippocampus, the fluorescence intensity of Keap1 protein decreased, whereas Nrf2 protein levels increased. Additionally, the number of intact neurons in these regions also increased. Our findings reveal that WPH not only alleviates STZ-induced memory impairment but also suppresses oxidative stress by modulating the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Additionally, it increases the number of intact neurons in the hippocampus.

items.title: A nonsense variant in KCNH7 (c.1324 C>T) is associated with a variable phenotypic spectrum of epilepsy.
items.abstract: KCNH7 is a voltage-gated potassium (K+) channel (Kv) that regulates membrane excitability and K+ flux across tissues. Studies using mouse models have suggested that Kcnh7 may play an important role in epilepsy susceptibility and pathogenesis. However, clinical and experimental evidence implicating KCNH7 variants in human epilepsy, as well as the genotype-phenotype association, remains unclear. Here, we aimed to refine the clinical, genetic, and functional electrophysiological features of a p.R442* variant identified in three individuals to elucidate potential genotype-phenotype association that may guide anticipatory management. We generated Kcnh7 mutants​ using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Heterozygous mutants exhibited increased neuronal hyperexcitability and increased seizure susceptibility due to reduced Kcnh7-encoded protein levels. Functional analyses established the KCNH7 p.R442* variant as a loss-of-function allele, with haploinsufficiency identified as a primary pathogenic mechanism. Our results underscore the significance of functional characterization for the KCNH7 p.R442* variant within the context of clinical interpretation, although larger cohorts are required to further validate these observations.

items.title: Maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy and child internalising and externalising problems over time.
items.abstract: Adequate gestational thyroid function is important for offspring neurodevelopment, yet behavioural implications of variation within the normal range are unclear. We examined associations with externalising and internalising problems across repeated assessments in childhood and adolescence. 2,606 mother-child dyads from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort with maternal free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurements in the first half of pregnancy and at least one child SDQ assessment. Primary analysis excluded women with overt thyroid disease or thyroid medication use and children born < 32 weeks or < 1500 g. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) scores at 5-6, 11-12 and 15-16 years, via mother-, teacher-, and self-report. Secondary analyses included logistic regression for borderline SDQ cut-offs, sex interactions, and effect modification by TSH. FT4 showed a U-shaped association with teacher-reported externalising problems (quadratic β = 9.49, FDR-adjusted p = 0.03), with higher scores at both low and high FT4. Higher FT4 was associated with lower child-reported internalising problems (β = -0.17, FDR-adjusted p = 0.04). For both primary associations, there was no evidence of FT4-by-age interaction, suggesting differences in problem levels rather than thyroid-related differences in symptom change over time. At age 5-6, FT4 showed a non-linear association with teacher-reported hyperactivity/inattention above the threshold, with a negative linear term (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.97) and a positive quadratic term (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.20). At age 11-12, higher FT4 was associated with fewer self-reported peer problems (OR = 0.84, 95% CI:0.71-0.99). In exploratory analyses, curvature of the FT4-externalising association varied by maternal TSH; no sex modification was detected. Within a cohort free of overt thyroid disease, maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy was associated with domain- and rater-specific differences in child internalising and externalising problems. We found no evidence that these associations changed across the available repeated assessments, suggesting differences in average problem scores rather than differences in how symptoms changed with age.

items.title: Failure of a device-aided therapy in Parkinson's disease, what's next?
items.abstract: Advanced Parkinson's disease (PD) frequently progresses to disabling motor fluctuations, dyskinesias, and impaired quality of life despite optimized oral or transdermal therapy. Device-aided therapies (DAT), including deep brain stimulation (DBS), levodopa-carbidopa intestinal gel (LCIG), levodopa-entacapone-carbidopa intestinal gel (LECIG), continuous subcutaneous apomorphine infusion (CSAI), continuous subcutaneous levodopa-carbidopa infusion (SCLC), and foslevodopa-foscarbidopa infusion (FLFC), provide effective management options for advanced PD. This narrative review discusses discontinuation rates, causes of treatment cessation, and switching between DATs. DBS consistently demonstrates the lowest discontinuation rates, while pump-based therapies, particularly subcutaneous infusions, show higher early dropout rates related to adverse events, device complications, neuropsychiatric symptoms, skin reactions, or insufficient efficacy. Intestinal levodopa therapies generally show intermediate persistence rates, although device-related complications remain common. Emerging evidence suggests that education, clinical experience, and structured patient support may reduce discontinuation from newer subcutaneous levodopa as well as apomorphine therapies. Patients who discontinue one DAT remain eligible for another. Shared decision-making and multidisciplinary evaluation remain essential to optimize long-term outcomes and treatment persistence in advanced PD. Future prospective comparative studies are needed to standardize DAT selection, clarify optimal switching strategies, and improve long-term treatment retention rates in patients.

items.title: Epistemic Challenges in the Interpretation of Brain Data: A Roadmap for Aligning Divergent Inferences.
items.abstract: Advances in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and artificial intelligence enable the identification of neural signatures-patterns of brain activity linked to thoughts, emotions, and mental states. Next-generation BCIs, including adaptive deep brain stimulation, promise personalized treatment for movement and psychiatric conditions. However, their effectiveness depends on whether neural signatures accurately reflect individuals' experiences and clinical states. Because neural signatures are abstract, they require meaningful correlations with behavior, symptoms, and clinical outcomes. Ethical challenges arise when brain data, behavioral observations, and patient self-reports conflict, raising questions about whose knowledge matters and how to determine clinical "ground truth." We argue that neural signature research needs epistemic duty-the responsibility to make well-reasoned decisions using the best available evidence-and propose three strategies to address these challenges: contextual, dimensional approaches to integrate diverse data; involving patients in decisions about data use; and stress-testing neural models to assess their robustness under uncertainty and conflicting evidence.

items.title: Global threats and conservation strategies for temporary ponds based on expert opinion and scientific evidence.
items.abstract: Temporary ponds are dynamic aquatic habitats found in all global biomes. Because they seasonally or intermittently dry out, they often support specialist flora and fauna including many endemic species. Although numerous studies report their decline, there is little consensus on their primary threats or effective mitigation strategies. Through a literature review and a global questionnaire survey of 137 pond experts, we identified agricultural intensification and urbanization as the leading threats, followed by habitat modification and climate change. The limited regulation of ecologically damaging human activities such as resource extraction or pollution and weak enforcement of conservation laws were also seen as significant barriers to effective protection. Although pond creation for ecological restoration emerged as the most common intervention, achieving desired conservation outcomes was found to be challenging because new ponds often are too permanent or too ephemeral to support many temporary pond specialists. We therefore identified the key challenges, considerations, and emerging guidelines needed to improve pond creation outcomes. A widespread lack of awareness among policymakers, researchers, land managers, and the general public was cited by most experts as a key driver of neglect. Our findings highlight the need to raise awareness and engage a broader range of stakeholders in the conservation of these ecologically valuable, yet often overlooked, habitats.

items.title: Using resource selection functions (RSFs) to model the movement ecology of invasive predators in the last remaining habitat of the endangered Atlantic whitefish.
items.abstract: Aquatic invasive species are among the top threats to freshwater fishes globally, causing declines in freshwater biodiversity and altering ecosystem functioning. Within Nova Scotia, Canada, invasive chain pickerel (Esox niger) and smallmouth bass (Micropterus dolomieu) have been found to reduce the abundance and diversity of native fishes. The invasive range of both species threatens and overlaps with the critical habitat of one of Canada's most endangered fishes, the Atlantic whitefish (Coregonus huntsmani). Here, we examine the seasonal space and depth use of adult chain pickerel and smallmouth bass using acoustic telemetry in Milipsigate Lake, Nova Scotia. High-resolution positions were calculated and analyzed using resource selection functions (RSFs) and generalized additive models (GAMs) to determine the relative space use and predicted depth of both species within the lake. Areas with the highest relative probability of use (>0.7) differed between species, and seasonal changes in space use were only significant for smallmouth bass (p < 0.001). Chain pickerel had the highest relative probability of space use in shallow areas of Milipsigate Lake (<4 m), whereas areas with the highest relative probability of space use for smallmouth bass were concentrated around four distinct overwintering sites. Chain pickerel were predicted to occupy a narrow range (~2 m) of relatively shallow depths year-round. Smallmouth bass were predicted to occupy depths that were on average three times deeper than chain pickerel, including a broad range of depths from spring to fall (0-15 m) that contracted during the winter months (2-6 m). Here, we showed that the combined occupancy of the lake by both species is extensive, with limited overlap in space or depth use year-round. Ultimately, the methodologies and results presented in this study could help inform the development of management strategies for invasive freshwater fish species.

items.title: Tick vectors and exposure of dogs (Canis lupus familiaris) to spotted fever group rickettsiae in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
items.abstract: Tick-borne rickettsioses remain a public health concern in Brazil, where their distribution is determined by the ecology of vector tick species. In Minas Gerais, human cases of Rickettsia rickettsii infection are recurrent. In contrast, Atlantic Forest spotted fever caused by Rickettsia parkeri strain Atlantic rainforest (ARF) has not yet been documented in the state, despite favorable environmental conditions and records of its vector, Amblyomma ovale. This study aimed to investigate the presence of R. parkeri ARF in A. ovale ticks infesting domestic dogs across ten municipalities representing nine mesoregions of Minas Gerais and to assess their exposure to spotted fever group (SFG) Rickettsia. A total of 300 dogs were examined, yielding 1,284 ticks from eight species. Rhipicephalus sanguineus sensu lato, Amblyomma sculptum, and A. ovale were the most prevalent species, with marked geographic variation in species composition and infestation indices. Serological analysis by indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) revealed a prevalence of SFG Rickettsia exposure above 50% in dogs from eight of the ten municipalities, with varying geometric mean titers, some as high as 4,096. Rickettsia parkeri ARF DNA was detected in only 1.5% of A. ovale ticks. These findings demonstrate widespread exposure of dogs to SFG Rickettsia and heterogeneous tick assemblages across Minas Gerais and confirm for the first time R. parkeri ARF circulation in the state of Minas Gerais State. This study is also the first statewide systematic survey of canine ticks in Minas Gerais and provides data to improve the understanding of the eco-epidemiology of tick-borne diseases and supports targeted surveillance strategies for human rickettsioses in the region.

items.title: CD47-dependent myeloid reprogramming drives IL-10-mediated T-cell suppression in heatstroke.
items.abstract: Heatstroke can trigger immune dysregulation, yet the mechanisms driving progression to critical illness remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing with functional studies to characterize heatstroke-associated immunosuppression. Transcriptomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from heatstroke patients revealed a transition from enhanced innate immune responses in mild heatstroke to marked adaptive immune suppression in critical disease. Disease progression was associated with increased S100A8/A12 and IL-10 expression and reduced T-cell- and HLA-associated gene expression. Myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) signatures correlated inversely with CD8⁺ T-cell abundance and cytotoxicity and positively with IL-10 levels and disease severity. Single-cell analyses revealed depletion of T and NK cells, myeloid expansion, MDSC accumulation, and reduced T-cell clonality. Pseudotime and RNA velocity analyses further indicated that heatstroke redirects myeloid differentiation towards an immunosuppressive MDSC state. In mice, CD47 blockade restrained MDSC expansion and IL-10 production, restored T-cell function, reduced organ injury, and improved survival. These findings identify myeloid reprogramming and MDSC-mediated T-cell suppression as mechanisms of heatstroke-associated immune dysfunction and support CD47 blockade as a potential therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium.
items.abstract: Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF-MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.

items.title: Migration strategy and colonization: the disproportionate role of partial migration.
items.abstract: Colonization drives diversification and determines how species shift their ranges, making it central to ecology and evolution. As both seasonal migration and dispersal depend on locomotor capacity, migration could be a major yet overlooked route to colonization. Here, we present evidence that partially migratory species are disproportionately successful in founding new populations, whereas strict migrants establish more rarely despite routinely reaching potentially suitable habitat in novel areas. Building on the threshold model of migration, we propose that partial migrants' liability to migrate lies closer to the threshold and/or is more environmentally sensitive, allowing displaced individuals to settle. This mechanism can help explain species distributions and diversification and predict which species might colonize newly suitable areas under global environmental change.

items.title: Microbial hazards and contamination dynamics in warm marine seafood supply chains: From detection to predictive risk management.
items.abstract: Warm marine seafood systems face distinctive microbial safety challenges arising from elevated environmental temperatures, climate-sensitive Vibrio ecology, cold-chain vulnerability, and heterogeneous supply chains. This review critically examines how environmental drivers of indigenous marine pathogens interact with post-harvest contamination and microbial amplification from harvest to retail, and evaluates the implications for HACCP verification, microbial risk assessment (MRA), molecular surveillance, traceability, and preventive control. The evidence indicates that seafood microbial risk is cumulative and stage-dependent: environmental baseline hazards are modified by time-temperature history, water and ice quality, sanitation, handling, processing, and cross-contamination. Reliance on endpoint and predominantly qualitative microbiological sampling limits source attribution, obscures contamination and amplification points, and constrains quantitative exposure assessment. We therefore propose an integrated environment-to-consumer framework linking stage-specific quantitative microbiology with environmental monitoring, predictive microbiology, molecular source attribution, HACCP verification, traceability, and quantitative MRA. Particular emphasis is placed on pathogenic Vibrio spp. as climate-sensitive hazards and on the complementary roles of culture-based and genomic methods in determining viable hazards and contamination pathways. Oman and the Gulf Cooperation Council are considered as a regional case within the broader context of tropical and subtropical seafood systems. The central priority is a transition from endpoint pathogen detection toward longitudinal, quantitative, and predictive microbial risk management capable of identifying where hazards originate, where they are amplified, and which interventions most effectively reduce consumer exposure.

items.title: Genome-resolved multi-omics reveals microbiome reorganization and carbon-flow regulation driven by functional bioaugmentation in thermophilic anaerobic digestion.
items.abstract: Bioaugmentation has emerged as a promising strategy for manipulating complex microbial ecosystems. However, the ecological mechanisms determining whether introduced microorganisms can functionally integrate into indigenous communities remain poorly understood. Here, genome-resolved metagenomics and metabolomics were combined to investigate how B. thermoamylovorans Y25 influenced microbial succession and ecosystem-level carbon transformation. Y25 successfully established within the thermophilic anaerobic microbiome and promoted a 12.69% (472.00 ± 27.69 NmL g -1 VS, p < 0.05) increase in cumulative methane yield without compromising reactor stability. This improvement occurred without significant changes in methanogenesis-related genes. Instead, Y25 bioaugmentation induced pronounced shifts in microorganisms associated with hydrolysis and fermentation and enhanced pathways related to substrate transport and intermediate carbon metabolism, accompanied by coordinated metabolite changes. These findings support a transition from strain-centered bioaugmentation strategies toward an ecosystem-level perspective, highlighting that successful microbial engineering depends on ecological integration and functional coordination within indigenous microbial networks.

items.title: Triclosan exposure alters calcium homeostasis and impairs shell biomineralization in Mytilus edulis.
items.abstract: Triclosan (TCS) is a persistent antimicrobial contaminant in wastewater-impacted aquatic environments, yet its sublethal effects on shell-forming systems in bivalves remain insufficiently understood. One-year-old Mytilus edulis were exposed for 21 days to nominal TCS levels of 0.5, 5.0, and 50 μg/L under semi-static renewal. Aqueous measurements, 24 h time-weighted average concentrations, and tissue burdens supported exposure interpretation. TCS exposure was associated with divergent changes in measured total Ca 2+ pools in hemocytes and serum, accompanied by altered mineralization-related enzyme activities, hemocyte-associated Raman signals, and remodeling of Ca 2+ -responsive pathways. Exposed mussels also showed reduced shell growth and thickness, altered polymorph-associated Raman signatures, and disrupted shell microstructure. Larger detached shells showed no consistent treatment-related change under the tested conditions, but the size mismatch limits comparison with the live-exposure cohort. Under an acute 5 μM ex vivo challenge, BAPTA-AM attenuated selected hemocyte responses. Exploratory structural equation modeling summarized associations without statistically supported mediation; neither analysis validates a causal pathway to shell impairment. The results show that recurrent TCS exposure impairs shell biomineralization and is associated with altered Ca 2+ homeostasis and hemocyte responses.

items.title: Combined effects of sulfoxaflor, microplastics, and Nosema ceranae on honeybee physiology and midgut transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Honeybees in agricultural ecosystems frequently encounter pesticides, microplastics (MPs), and pathogens, yet the combined effects of these stressors remain poorly understood. Here, honeybees (Apis mellifera L.) were exposed to sulfoxaflor (SFX, 10 μg/L), polystyrene nano- and microplastics (PS-NMPs, 0.08 μm and 5 μm, 25 mg/L), and Nosema ceranae (Nc, 1×10 6 spores/mL), either alone or in combination. Survival rate, sucrose consumption, midgut weight, histological structure, midgut transcriptomics, stress-related gene expression, and enzyme activities were assessed. Among the single stressors, SFX caused the strongest reduction in survival, whereas Nc more prominently reduced sucrose consumption and induced midgut epithelial thickening. In contrast, SFX and PS-NMPs were more strongly associated with reductions in midgut weight and epithelial thickness. Although combined exposure did not consistently increase mortality relative to single stressor exposure, it induced marked transcriptomic disturbances. Lysosome pathway changes were observed across most treatment groups, whereas combined exposure involving Nc showed the strongest transcriptomic perturbation, characterized by suppression of ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Representative gene expressions and enzyme activities further revealed stressor-specific immune, detoxification, and lysosome associated responses. These findings provide new insights into the complex interactions among multiple stressors in honeybees and highlight the potential ecological risks associated with multi-stressor exposure in honeybees.

items.title: Population-scale identification of gut commensals that antagonize antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat, yet microbiome-encoded defenses against antibiotic resistance gene (ARG)-associated pathogens remain poorly defined. Here, we analyze 12,238 human gut metagenomes and prioritize 159 commensal species ("coexcluders") that show inverse associations with ARG-associated pathogenic taxa. These taxa carry low ARG burdens and encode candidate antimicrobial peptide repertoires. For Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, deep learning-guided mining of 2,053 genomes reveals 6,737 peptides prevalent in the human gut that inversely associate with ARG-associated pathogens. In antibiotic-perturbed mice, F. prausnitzii reduces the resistance burden and restores ecological stability, with peptide enrichment. These peptides show preferential activity against antibiotic-resistant E. coli derivatives while sparing commensals, which is consistent with a kill-the-winner dynamic. Anaerobic coculture reveals resistance-dependent peptide induction, linking the resistance phenotype to competitive suppression. This work establishes a scalable, resistance-guided framework that links population-level ecological signatures to strain-resolved microbial and molecular candidates, providing a basis for mechanistic and therapeutic development.

items.title: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
items.abstract: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim -5kb ) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim +/ -5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

items.title: Mineral-microbe interactions in stratified dam reservoirs.
items.abstract: Mineral-microbe interactions are core interfacial processes regulating elemental cycling in aquatic sediments. Dam construction converts free-flowing rivers into sediment-retaining and often stratified reservoirs, thereby altering hydrodynamic energy, particle sorting, residence time, oxygen delivery and redox zonation at the sediment-water interface. Although extensive studies have documented dam effects on hydrology, sediment delivery, water quality and greenhouse gas emissions, less attention has been given to how reservoir formation reorganizes established mineral-microbe processes at oxygen-limited interfaces that persist during periods of stable thermal stratification. Here, we synthesize recent progress on mineral-microbe interactions in stratified dam reservoirs. We first examine how flow attenuation and sediment trapping create fine-grained, organic-rich depositional zones, and how thermal stratification promotes hypolimnetic anoxia, redox gradients and reactive sediment-water interfaces. Against this environmental background, we focus on three closely related modes of mineral-microbe coupling: microbial colonization on mineral surfaces, electron transfer between microorganisms and redox-active phases, and microbially mediated mineral transformation. We then summarize how these mechanisms operate in natural aquatic systems, including extracellular polymeric substances (EPS)-mediated colonization, direct and shuttle-mediated electron transfer, and microbial mineral dissolution, precipitation and transformation. Building on this baseline, we discuss how reservoir stratification and redox conditions reorganize these same processes and their consequences for Fe/Mn mineral cycling, organic matter stabilization, nutrient release, pollutant mobility and greenhouse gas production. Because stratification, anoxia and early diagenetic redox reactions also occur in natural deep lakes, we distinguish these shared limnological and diagenetic mechanisms from dam-specific controls, including sediment retention, regulated residence time, water-level fluctuation, selective withdrawal and downstream sediment discontinuity. This review provides a focused conceptual framework for linking dam-induced environmental transition with mineral-microbe coupling, and highlights implications for reservoir water-quality management, internal loading control, contaminant risk and carbon-cycle regulation.

items.title: Drivers of biodiversity in mineral extraction sites - a cross-taxa analysis with implications for management and restoration.
items.abstract: Extraction sites are often considered sources of environmental damage. However, in intensively used and nutrient-enriched landscapes they may also provide exceptional secondary habitats, shaped by disturbance and nutrient depletion. Their contribution to biodiversity across taxonomic groups remains insufficiently understood, and integrated guidelines for managing biodiversity during active extraction are needed. We examined terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity across twelve active German extraction sites of limestone, gypsum, sand and gravel. Data on vascular plants, soil parameters and six insect groups were collected via vegetation relevés, soil samples, DNA metabarcoding from trap samples and transect walks on 103 terrestrial plots. Aquatic diversity (Amphibia and Odonata) was assessed at 75 water bodies using transect walks and eDNA metabarcoding. Across all sites, we recorded 2054 species, including 168 threatened in Germany. Species composition varied strongly across substrate types and between plots. Terrestrial insect diversity increased with plant species richness, while higher latitude, which was correlated with sampling year, and the proportion of shrubs had negative effects. The respective insect groups showed group-specific responses to plot age, the proportions of open soil, active extraction area and surrounding grassland. To maximise conservation value, particularly for terrestrial insects, site management should promote habitat heterogeneity and allow the formation of temporary habitats through natural succession. Increasing vascular plant richness boosts local insect diversity. Embedding biodiversity management into the regional context can create networks of valuable secondary habitats. Extraction sites thus bear a high but so far underused potential to advance restoration targets beyond existing protected areas.

items.title: Effects of sampling methods on recovery of introduced emerald ash borer parasitoids: a Bayesian integrated nested Laplace approximation analysis of the mapBioControl dataset.
items.abstract: Since 2007 and 2015, respectively, the parasitoids Tetrastichus planipennisi Yang (Hymenoptera: Eulophidae) and Spathius galinae Belokobylskij and Strazanac (Hymenoptera: Braconidae) have been introduced to the United States for biological control of the emerald ash borer Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire (Coleoptera: Buprestidae). A web-enabled geospatial database, mapBioControl, has also been developed to support monitoring, management, and evaluation of these biological control efforts. We applied Bayesian binomial models and discrete-time hazard models to mapBioControl data to assess how sampling method, sampling effort, and release year influenced recovery probabilities for T. planipennisi and S. galinae across the United States and Canada. For both species, best-fit Bayesian binomial models indicated that recovery method was an important predictor of parasitoid detection, although method-specific patterns differed between species. Discrete-time hazard models indicated higher first-detection hazards for targeted recovery methods relative to yellow pan traps, including tree debarking for S. galinae (HR = 3.48 [95% CrI: 1.88 to 6.47]) and T. planipennisi (HR = 9.81 [95% CrI: 5.42 to 17.76]). Detection probabilities also increased with a greater number of sampling days for targeted recovery methods. While little evidence of residual spatial autocorrelation for T. planipennisi was detected, there were strong indications of spatial autocorrelation for S. galinae. Our results indicate that post-release monitoring is influenced by sampling method and sampling effort, and targeted recovery methods like tree debarking and larval sentinel logs may provide higher probabilities of parasitoid detection. When resources are limited, trade-offs among cost, labor, and monitoring objectives should guide the choice of sampling method.

items.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans.
items.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year -1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year -1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year -1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

items.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects.
items.abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

items.title: Applications of computer vision in mosquito-borne diseases: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs) remain a major global health challenge. Vector surveillance, pathogen detection, and clinical diagnosis are central to control efforts but are limited by labor-intensive workflows and shortages of trained personnel. Computer vision (CV) offers opportunities for scalable automation throughout the MBD management pipeline. We aimed to systematically characterize the applications of computer vision in mosquito-borne diseases research, summarize methodological developments, and identify opportunities and barriers to translating these advances into public health practice. We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, that applied computer vision to any aspect of MBD research or control. A total of 1,521 records were screened, and 650 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies were categorized by computer vision application area, data types, algorithmic approaches, and data acquisition methods. Descriptive quantitative analysis and qualitative thematic synthesis were performed. The use of computer vision in MBD research increased significantly over the review period. Most studies focused on diagnostic applications, particularly Plasmodium detection in malaria microscopy. More recent work incorporated deep learning models for mosquito species classification, UAV- and satellite-based habitat mapping, and smartphone-based non-invasive diagnostic imaging. Emerging areas included 3D mosquito behavioral analysis and Internet of Things-enabled surveillance. Algorithmic approaches evolved from traditional image processing to convolutional neural networks, You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based object detectors, and transformer architectures. However, most models were developed using small, geographically-limited datasets, lacked external or prospective validation, and were rarely evaluated in operational settings, limiting their translational readiness.

items.title: Absence of hydraulic segmentation in tropical and subtropical woody plants.
items.abstract: The stem-leaf segmentation hypothesis proposes that leaves act as safety valves to protect stem hydraulic function under drought, which involves two specific mechanisms, i.e., hydraulic segmentation hypothesis (HSH; higher hydraulic resistance in leaves than in stems) and vulnerability segmentation hypothesis (VSH; lower embolism resistance in leaves than in stems). However, relative to the VSH, the HSH remains poorly understood. In this study, we measured sapwood specific hydraulic conductivity (ks), leaf hydraulic conductance (${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$), embolism resistance (P50), and maximum stomatal conductance (gs) of 118 woody species from six tropical and subtropical forests. To test the HSH, we examined the relationships between stem and leaf hydraulic conductivity, and between hydraulic function and gas exchange. It is hypothesized that these tropical-subtropical species exhibiting distinct hydraulic segmentation (leaves as a hydraulic bottleneck) showed negative ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship and stronger ${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$-gs relationship (than ks-gs). We found that there were no significant ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationships across all the studied species and in any forest type or functional group. In addition, gs was positively related with ks, but not with ${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$. Our results thus did not support HSH in tropical-subtropical woody species. Furthermore, we analyzed ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship under different degree of vulnerability segmentation (the difference in P50 between stem and leaf; P50leaf-stem). Specifically, the ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship was absent under weak P50leaf-stem ( 2 MPa), revealing that the degree of P50leaf-stem influences the stem-leaf hydraulic relationship. This study deepens our understanding of the stem-leaf hydraulic framework coping with drought stress.

items.title: Carbon allocation under elevated CO2 shapes the fate of phytoplankton-derived ocean carbon.
items.abstract: Phytoplankton carbon allocation is a major pathway regulating atmospheric CO2 transfer into exportable particulate organic carbon (POC) and long-lived dissolved organic carbon (DOC) reservoirs. Yet, how elevated CO2 restructures taxon-specific carbon allocation remains poorly constrained. Here, we integrated growth experiments, operational carbon fractionation, FT-ICR MS molecular characterization, microbial degradation assays, and scenario-based global projections to investigate how elevated CO2 alters carbon fate across major phytoplankton taxa. We found that rising CO2 promoted phytoplankton carbon allocation toward residual POC (r-POC) in most phytoplankton groups, with r-POC allocation increasing by an average of 39.3% across non-diatom groups at 1370 ppm CO2. This shift was accompanied by pronounced carbohydrate enrichment within cell-associated extracellular organic carbon. Concurrently, elevated CO2 enhanced the accumulation of persistence-associated compounds, with carboxyl-rich alicyclic molecules increasing by 1.29 ± 0.22-fold. These molecules were accompanied by increases in the nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC). Microbial degradation experiments further demonstrated a negative relationship between NOSC and microbial carbon removal (R2 = 0.48). Scenario-based projections indicated that carbon-pool reallocation contributed more strongly than biomass enhancement to the projected r-POC response: under highest CO2, r-POC increased by 46.6%, of which approximately 67% was attributable to carbon reallocation compared with only 18% from biomass enhancement. Finally, incorporating global phytoplankton functional-type distributions revealed that Haptophyta was the dominant contributor to projected r-POC pool. These findings suggest that elevated CO2 may reshape future ocean carbon sequestration through carbon-pool reallocation, with Haptophyta contributing substantially to projected r-POC responses and the formation of potentially persistent organic compounds.

items.title: Population genetics of white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) across the United States based on mitochondrial DNA control region sequences.
items.abstract: White-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) experienced a severe population decline due to unregulated harvest during the late 1800s. Conservation efforts, including widespread deer translocations, facilitated the recovery of populations but also influenced patterns of genetic variation. Consequently, both historical management and natural processes have shaped the present-day population structure of white-tailed deer. To examine genetic diversity, population differentiation, and nationwide population structure, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) control region sequences of 598-601 bp were generated from 1035 white-tailed deer samples across 30 U.S. states representing 11 subspecies. We identified 202 unique control-region haplotypes and generated a network and phylogeny that resolved several geographically widespread haplogroups. A state-specific haplogroup was detected in South Carolina, and population-specific haplotypes were detected in two white-tailed deer subspecies of conservation concern, the Columbian white-tailed deer (O. v. leucurus) and the Florida Key deer (O. v. clavium). High genetic diversity was detected, particularly in deer populations from Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and mainland Florida. Identical haplotype sequences for deer in Georgia and Wisconsin may reflect historical translocations. Beyond the primary objective of characterizing population diversity and structure, we discuss these findings in light of refugial distribution during the Last Glacial Maximum and of the nominally recognized subspecies. Together, these findings provide a nationwide framework for understanding white-tailed deer population history and identify genetically differentiated populations for future conservation genetics and chronic wasting disease research.

items.title: Surveillance bias and the hidden ecology of Enterovirus coxsackiepol: implications for global risk assessment of vaccine-derived poliovirus emergence.
items.abstract: Global enterovirus (EV) surveillance has long relied on RD/L20B cell culture systems optimized for poliovirus (PV) detection. This systematically under-detected Enterovirus coxsackiepol (EV-C) while over-representing Enterovirus betacoxsackie (EV-B). This bias created a fundamental paradox: circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses (cVDPVs), including those of novel oral polio vaccine type 2 origin, have genomic regions of non-polio EV-C origin, suggesting frequent recombination with viruses rarely detected in surveillance datasets. Here, we show that EV-C viruses might be more prevalent and widely distributed than recognized. We further show that regions considered low risk for cVDPV emergence (especially those using only inactivated PV vaccine and acute flaccid paralysis surveillance) may harbor undetected non-polio EV-C circulation and silent PV transmission. We propose integrating wastewater (WW) surveillance, long-range reverse transcription-PCR (amplifying the complete or coding-complete genome as a single contig), and long-read sequencing to capture full EV diversity, improve cVDPV emergence risk assessment, and strengthen PV-eradication efforts. Expanding this framework to other viruses can facilitate the 100-day mission by enabling the acquisition of actionable intelligence for all such viruses directly from WW. Furthermore, this creates an opportunity to harmonize PV surveillance with broader pandemic preparedness frameworks, allowing investments in PV genomic surveillance to generate cross-pathogen benefits.
