items.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
items.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host-microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

items.title: Tracking the trajectory of individual conjugative plasmids in bacterial communities using CRISPR acquisition-based recording
items.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer mediated by conjugative plasmids is a primary driver of bacterial evolution and the spread of adaptive traits, including antibiotic resistance determinants. Tracking how these plasmids disseminate through complex microbial communities remains a major challenge. Current methodologies often yield static, endpoint snapshots of host identity, overlooking transient transfer events and plasmid encounters with the co-resident mobilome. To overcome these limitations, we introduce SPacer Integration (SPI) plasmids, which turn the mobile element itself into a recorder of its own transfer history. We engineered conjugative and mobilizable plasmids to carry a CRISPR-Cas adaptation cassette (cas1-cas2 and a minimal CRISPR array) and maintain tight repression of cas1-cas2 expression in the donor cell, so that upon transfer they capture spacers from the chromosome and plasmids of new hosts and store them permanently in their own array. Subsequent PCR amplification and sequencing of these expanded arrays provide a molecular record of both the bacterial hosts and the co-resident plasmids encountered. We created SPI plasmids using the backbones of well-characterized mobilizable and conjugative plasmids RSF1010, RP4, F, and R100-1. We tested SPI plasmids in defined laboratory matings and in complex wastewater communities. The analysis of the acquired spacers successfully mapped permissive host ranges and profiled the co-resident plasmids in situ. Requiring only standard cloning, PCR and sequencing, this accessible and cost-effective strategy establishes a new framework for studying plasmid ecology. Because spacers are integrated chronologically, it further offers the potential to reconstruct multi-step transfer trajectories across natural microbial networks.

items.title: Terminological variation in ecological connectivity terms in Europe
items.abstract: Abstract Ecological connectivity has become a major policy concern in Europe, but the language used to describe connected green–blue interventions is still fragmented. We analysed 3,868 articles with first authors based in Europe, published between 1956 and 2025, to examine how 15 related terms have been used across time, contexts, disciplines and keyword networks. Green infrastructure clearly dominates the literature, followed by ecological network, while corridor-, belt- and pathway-related terms occupy a smaller but diverse space. Since the early 2000s, the field has moved away from a mainly conservation-focused vocabulary towards broader concepts linked to urban planning, climate adaptation and ecosystem services. We show that broad terms connect debates across planning, ecology and climate, whereas more specific terms remain narrowly used. To improve comparable monitoring and policy alignment, we propose a pragmatic ‘umbrella + mechanism + scale’ heuristic for naming connected green-blue interventions.

items.title: Community perspectives on the health information ecosystem
items.abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 infodemic highlighted how misinformation, inconsistent guidance, and barriers to reliable information undermined vaccine confidence, particularly in underserved communities. This qualitative study examined barriers to vaccination, as well as communication and information challenges experienced by community residents and stakeholders in areas of high social vulnerability in a mid-sized Midwestern city. Focus groups and interviews with community residents, community leaders, and healthcare providers (N = 31) were thematically analysed and interpreted through the Social Ecology of Health Beliefs and Misinformation Framework. Findings identified two primary themes: (1) barriers to vaccination and (2) communication and information challenges, including language barriers and a lack of reliable information. These challenges emerged across individual, interpersonal, community, and structural/systemic levels. Community-informed solutions included micro-communication through trusted community messengers, culturally congruent communication, and partnerships with faith organisations. Importantly, these findings have implications for future public health crises, highlighting the need for coordinated strategies that operate across ecological levels and emphasise clear, culturally relevant, and trusted health messaging. Strengthening trusted messenger networks, fostering community partnerships, and implementing policies that address inequities may improve preparedness for future public health crises.

items.title: The ZebHLH35-ZeTIFY9-ZeSWEET12 module regulates susceptibility to soft rot caused by Pectobacterium carotovorum in coloured calla lily.
items.abstract: The ornamental and commercial value of coloured calla lily (Zantedeschia elliottiana) is severely reduced by soft rot. Previous studies have demonstrated that Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporters (SWEETs) are involved in plant-pathogen interactions. While, the role of SWEETs in coloured calla lily infected with soft rot remains unclear. In this study, transcriptome sequencing and RT-qPCR were used to analyze SWEETs in coloured calla lily infected with Pectobacterium carotovorum (Pc), identifying 17 ZeSWEETs. Among them, ZeSWEET12 markedly responds to Pc infection. Functional characterization revealed that ZeSWEET12 is localized in the plasma membrane and possesses sucrose transport activity, and overexpression of ZeSWEET12 increases the susceptibility of Z. elliottiana to soft rot, whereas silencing ZeSWEET12 enhances plant resistance. Furthermore, yeast one-hybrid screening revealed that ZeTIFY9, a transcription factor related to jasmonic acid (JA) regulation, directly interacts with the promoter of ZeSWEET12 and negatively regulates its expression, whereas ZebHLH35 directly binds to the G-box element in the ZeSWEET12 promoter and positively regulates its expression. Additionally, we confirmed that ZeTIFY9 can interact with ZebHLH35. Our study elucidated a mechanism by which the ZebHLH35-ZeTIFY9-ZeSWEET12 module regulates susceptibility to soft rot in Z. elliottiana, providing new insights and precise genetic targets for future molecular breeding for disease resistance in coloured calla lily.

items.title: The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.
items.abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and biogeographic analyses, while links to MicrobeAtlas provide further insight into global taxon distributions. The web interface has new features for interactive exploration of samples, studies, and taxon abundances on a map. The integrated mOTUs command-line tool enables taxonomic profiling of metagenomes, comparison of user genomes with marker gene-based operational species-level taxonomic units (mOTUs) represented in the database, and retrieval of genomes based on identifiers, taxonomic labels, and functional annotations. A new API enables high-throughput programmatic retrieval of user-tailored subsets. Taken together, mOTUs provides a foundation for advancing microbial ecology through systematic integration of taxonomic composition, functional potential, and environmental distribution of taxa within one framework. The database is available at https://motus-db.org.

items.title: Chromosome-level assembly and population-scale genomics in an intensively monitored wild bird, the Seychelles warbler.
items.abstract: Understanding evolutionary processes is greatly facilitated by high-quality data on genetic variation. We report the development of a genomic toolkit for a recently bottlenecked, long-term studied species, the Seychelles warbler (Ptimerl dezil; Acrocephalus sechellensis). This toolkit comprises a reference genome assembled into 31 chromosomes, together with functional annotations and reference-panel-free imputation of whole-genome sequences from 1,935 individuals. The genomic data have been used to assign the sequenced individuals into a genetic pedigree. Individual genomic data are associated with a suite of phenotypic metadata, amassed from three decades of fieldwork in this closed, long-term monitored population. We compared sex and parentage assigned using the genomic data with the previously recorded sex and parentage metadata to identify and correct 41 sample DNA samples labelled with the wrong identity. This population resource enables a wide range of analyses, that include, but are not limited to phylogenetics, metabarcoding, recombination rates, linkage patterns, adaptation, heritability, demographic history, selection, and inbreeding estimates. We wish to encourage interest from researchers seeking to collaborate on future analyses and data collection. Overall, our methods demonstrate the potential of next generation sequencing and statistical tools to provide dense genomic datasets at large sample sizes for wild populations.

items.title: Long-term effects of olfactory training on odor identification and depressive severity in older adults: an exploratory follow-up study.
items.abstract: Objective The beneficial effects of olfactory training (OT) have been well established, recently also in older adults. Meta-analyses indicate that in this age group, benefits from OT may extend beyond changes in olfactory function and include improved cognitive function and amelioration of depressive symptoms. However, the duration of these beneficial effects remains unclear. The present exploratory study investigated the persistence of OT-related benefits approximately 42 weeks after completion of OT. Results Thirty-eight older adults from the original OT study (aged 50-85 years; M = 69.7, SD = 7) returned for follow-up assessment, including psychophysical olfactory testing (Sniffin' Sticks), depression severity measures (PHQ-9), affective evaluation, and verbal fluency testing. Odor identification performance decreased significantly from post-training to follow-up, although it did not differ from baseline. Depression severity increased markedly from post-training to follow-up and was also higher than at baseline. In contrast, the improvement in verbal fluency observed after OT was maintained at follow-up. Conclusions These findings in this subgroup of participants in the original study suggest that some beneficial effects of OT may persist over time, whereas others, particularly those related to depressive symptoms and odor identification, may diminish within approximately ten months after cessation of OT. Additional analyses restricted to participants who received OT largely supported these findings. Given the exploratory nature of the study and the absence of a concurrent control group at follow-up, further controlled longitudinal studies are needed to determine the long-term effects of OT in older adults. items.title: Injectable Peptide Use and Associated Harms Among Boys and Men: Findings From the International IPED Survey.
items.abstract: Illicit injectable peptides are increasingly promoted to young men through social media. However, limited research has examined harms associated with injectable peptides. This study examined age-related differences in psychosocial and physical harms among cisgender men reporting injectable peptide use. Data were drawn from timepoint 1 (N = 1000) of the International Image and Performance Enhancing Drug Survey (October 2025-March 2026). Analyses were restricted to cisgender men reporting lifetime injectable peptide use (N = 294). Participants were stratified into younger (<25 years) and older (25+ years) groups. Outcomes included self-reported harms, depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), anxiety symptoms (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7), problematic social media use (Social Media Addiction Questionnaire) and body image concerns (Muscle Dysmorphic Disorder Inventory). Age-related differences in harms were examined using chi-square tests. Follow-up regression analyses modelled age continuously. Younger men reported significantly higher anxiety scores than older men (P = .023). Younger men were also more likely to report skin conditions such as acne (32.4% vs 18.7%, P = .009) and hair loss from the head (24.5% vs 15.0%, P = .045). No significant age differences were observed for depressive symptoms, social media addiction, body image concerns or most psychosocial harms. Regression analyses similarly demonstrated limited continuous age effects across psychosocial outcomes. Young men who use injectable peptides appear more vulnerable to anxiety symptoms and selected physical effects than older men; however, most other psychosocial harms were broadly comparable. Peptide-related harms may not be confined to younger populations and reinforce the need for clinician awareness and harm reduction responses.

items.title: How Do Sexual and Gender Minority Populations Experience the Diagnostic Process in Primary and Emergency Care: An Integrative Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Background Sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals face healthcare disparities, affecting health outcomes including diagnostic safety. Diagnostic vulnerabilities can be especially pronounced in primary and emergency care settings. While previous reviews explored general healthcare disparities, the experiences of SGM populations during the diagnostic process remain unexplored. We conducted an integrative systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42024608397, unfunded) to examine how SGM patients, their care partners, and healthcare providers experience the diagnostic process in primary and emergency care and how provider communication shapes these experiences. Methods We systematically searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and LLBA (2015-November 2025) and included English-language, empirical studies on diagnostic process experiences for SGM patients, their care partners, or providers in primary and emergency care. A qualitative integrative synthesis combined inductive thematic and deductive content analysis, mapping onto diagnostic process stages, and the approachability features communication framework. We appraised risk of bias with the QATSDD quality assessment tool. Results From 2207 identified studies, 43 met inclusion criteria. Most involved SGM patients (67%), with fewer provider (28%) or mixed samples. Studies spanned diagnostic stages, predominantly information gathering (n = 39, especially diagnostic testing (n = 29)); fewer addressed access (n = 15); and diagnosis communication (n = 9). Diagnostic experiences were shaped by structural barriers, provider competency, and healthcare interactions. Providers' affirming communication and SGM-specific knowledge supported trust, identity disclosure, appropriate care, and diagnostic safety, whereas non-affirming communication, cisheteronormativity, provider bias, and knowledge gaps contributed to avoidance or refusal of care, missed screening, and diagnostic delays. Discussion This is the first review to systematically map experiences of SGM patients, their care partners, and providers against diagnostic process stages. Experiences were limited to high-income Western settings, underrepresenting care partners, and asexual and intersex populations. Diagnostic inequities among SGM patients intersect across structural, competency, and interactional factors, highlighting communication and system-level interventions as key to improving diagnostic safety and equity for this vulnerable population.

items.title: How Indigenous Psychologies Resemble Mathematics: The Epistemic Role of Conceptual Innovation.
items.abstract: This paper argues that indigenous psychologies and mathematics share an important methodological feature: both advance understanding by refining conceptual systems and terminology. Throughout the history of mathematics, the reformulation of concepts has often enabled mathematicians to solve problems that had remained unresolved for centuries. Similarly, indigenous psychologies emerged from the recognition that the concepts of mainstream psychology do not always adequately capture the psychological realities of indigenous populations. They therefore develop culturally grounded concepts and terminology that improve the understanding of psychological phenomena within specific cultural contexts. Most indigenous psychology concepts belong to the field of social psychology. If the primary goal of social psychology is to understand human social behavior and experience, then indigenous psychologies pursue this goal through conceptual innovation in much the same way that mathematics advances through the refinement of its own conceptual framework. The paper also identifies important limits to this analogy: unlike mathematical concepts, the usefulness of indigenous psychological concepts may be difficult to appreciate without experience of the relevant cultural environment. The paper therefore discusses cultural experience and social success as possible ways of assessing the value of indigenous psychological concepts.

items.title: Assortative mating can mask non-additive genetic contributions to individual differences.
items.abstract: Assortative mating impacts trait variation and covariation among individuals within populations. Here, we examine how direct and indirect assortative mating influence additive and non-additive genetic contributions to individual differences. In an extended twin design, we show by simulations that correlations between mating partners can mask non-additive genetic influences. Accounting for assortative mating can unmask non-additive genetic contributions, revealing upward biases in additive genetic estimates. We applied our approach to anthropometric (height), personality (openness to experience), and psychiatric (borderline personality disorder features) traits in a large dataset of 9000 Dutch families of twins, siblings, and spouses of twins. Our results demonstrate that accounting for partner correlations (r = 0.21-0.29) unmasks non-additive genetic influences (13-19% of trait variation), leading to additive genetic estimates that are 14-39% smaller than those obtained from models ignoring assortment. Our findings clarify the impacts of assortative mating on both additive and non-additive genetic variance components, contributing to a better understanding of the heritability gap between twin and molecular-based studies, and highlight a refined framework for modelling the genetic transmission of behavioural and psychiatric traits.

items.title: Natural environments and sleep during pregnancy: Associations of green and blue spaces with prenatal sleep outcomes in a Canadian cohort.
items.abstract: Objectives Sleep quality during pregnancy is critical for maternal and child health, yet environmental determinants of prenatal sleep remain understudied. Green and blue spaces have demonstrated positive effects on mental health, which is robustly associated with sleep, but direct impacts of green and blue spaces on sleep among pregnant individuals are unclear. This study examined associations between green and blue spaces and sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment during pregnancy. Methods Data from the pan-Canadian Pregnancy during the Covid-19 Pandemic (PdP, n = 8583) were linked with green (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), tree canopy) and blue space (distance from the nearest water body) data from Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE). Sleep outcomes included self-reported sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment. Multiple linear regression models adjusted for age, ethnicity, neighborhood deprivation, socioeconomic status, population density, COVID-19 restriction severity, season, physical activity, and trimester. Results Greater tree canopy cover and NDVI were significantly associated with longer sleep duration. Contrary to our hypothesis, greater distance from water bodies was also associated with longer sleep duration and lower sleep disturbance. After additional adjustments, only the associations with sleep duration remained significant. No associations were observed for sleep-related impairment. Conclusions Green spaces, particularly tree canopy, may positively influence prenatal sleep duration, whereas the effects of blue spaces may depend more on the type of interaction with these environments and additional contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental factors, particularly tree-rich environment, into maternal health strategies and urban planning to support perinatal well-being.

items.title: Home-based pulmonary rehabilitation early after hospitalisation in COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Rationale COPD is characterised by respiratory exacerbations, often requiring hospitalisation. Post-hospitalisation pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) can reduce risk of readmission, but very few people attend PR post exacerbation. Objective To compare hospital readmission rates between people with COPD who undertake a home-based PR program commenced early (≤2 weeks) after hospital discharge (ePR) with usual care. Methods Assessor blinded, multi-centre RCT. Participants randomised 1:1 to ePR or usual care. ePR was 8 weeks (1 physiotherapy home-visit, plus 7x weekly phone calls). The primary outcome was all-cause, non-elective hospitalisation at 12 months after rehabilitation completion. Results From Jan 2020-Jun 2024 157 participants were randomised to ePR (n=77) or usual care (n=80). The ITT analysis included 151 participants (n=73 ePR, n=78 usual care; n=6 excluded: n=5 deceased, n=1 transplant). Rate of all-cause non-elective hospitalisation was not different between groups at 12-month follow-up (ePR 60.3%, usual care 64.1%; RR 0.94 [95%CI 0.73, 1.21]). There was no difference between groups for improvements in quality of life and breathlessness at either time point. There was a clinically and statistically significant reduction in anxiety favouring ePR (10-weeks post-discharge MD -2.1 [95%CI -3.4, -0.8]; 12-months MD -1.6 [95%CI -3.0, -0.2]). ePR completion rate (≥70% sessions) was high (n=57, 74%). When compared to no rehabilitation (per protocol), ePR completers demonstrated significant improvements in breathlessness, quality of life, anxiety/depression and self-efficacy. There was one intervention-related adverse event. Conclusion ePR delivered directly to patients in their homes, commenced within 2 weeks of hospital discharge, did not reduce hospital readmissions over 12 months compared to usual care but did support high program completion. When compared to no rehabilitation, improved clinical outcomes favoured ePR in those who completed the program.

items.title: Sensory eye dominance following theta-burst stimulation of right hMT.
items.abstract: We examined sensory eye dominance (SED) following theta-burst stimulation (TBS) of the right human middle temporal complex (hMT + ). Experiment 1 included 40 participants who completed dichoptic motion and orientation tasks to index SED before and after receiving intermittent TBS (iTBS) or continuous TBS (cTBS) stimulation. Experiment 2 included an independent group of 20 participants assessed at multiple time points with the dichoptic motion task following TBS. We found a significant reduction in SED following iTBS but not cTBS over hMT + . Additional comparisons with a supplemental group who received TBS over Cz (10 iTBS, 10 cTBS) revealed that the two groups did not differ depending on stimulation protocol. Compared with TBS over Cz, iTBS over hMT + produced greater reductions in SED in both the Motion and Orientation tasks. cTBS over hMT + did not produce SED changes that were any different from those with TBS over Cz. Together, these findings provide behavioral evidence for short-term modulation of binocular balance following iTBS over right hMT+, while the underlying physiological mechanisms and precise temporal characteristics require further empirical investigation.

items.title: Weekly intensive longitudinal assessment as a therapeutic adjunct for adolescent suicide risk: An observational study.
items.abstract: Adolescent suicide is a leading cause of death, highlighting the need for scalable prevention strategies. Intensive longitudinal assessment (ILA) is commonly used in suicide research to track fluctuations in suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB), though its therapeutic potential remains unclear. This study examined whether weekly app-based ILA engagement during outpatient treatment was associated with improved STB outcomes among high-risk adolescents and explored possible psychological mechanisms underlying these effects. Participants were 362 adolescents receiving outpatient care for STB (M age = 14.80 years, SD = 1.85) who were followed for 6 months. Adolescents were grouped by treatment condition (brief interpersonal psychotherapy-based suicide crisis intervention [IPT-A-SCI] vs. active control) and ILA engagement (ILA vs. no ILA). ILA participants completed one app-based assessment per week concerning the preceding week. STB were assessed using clinician-administered and self-report measures at baseline and follow-up. An ILA × Time × Treatment interaction indicated that the association between ILA and reduced SI presence was significantly stronger among adolescents receiving IPT-A-SCI than among those in the active control condition at one-month follow-up. Within the IPT-A-SCI arm, ILA engagement was also associated with greater reductions in SI severity over time. ILA was associated with reduced suicidal behavior at six-month follow-up in the active control arm. Mediation analyses showed that perceived connectedness and emotional awareness were associated with STB outcomes, though neither significantly mediated the relationship between ILA and STB. Findings suggest that weekly ILA paired with clinician-monitored safety follow-up may serve as an adjunct to outpatient care for high-risk adolescents.

items.title: Healthcare Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
items.abstract: Objective Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among healthcare providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed healthcare team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations. Study design A cross‑sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary NICU team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple‑choice questions, Likert‑scale statements, and open‑ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open‑ended responses. Results A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety. Conclusions Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

items.title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
items.abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

items.title: Not all food avoidance is the same: a latent profile analysis informed by the Appetite Self-Regulation model.
items.abstract: Food avoidance is a common problem for some children and negatively affects their dietary quality. The Appetite Self-Regulation (ASR) model proposes that food avoidance phenotypes arise in children due to interactions between bottom-up and top-down processes. However, it is unknown how these factors combine within children to produce distinct food avoidant profiles. This study aimed to better understand different types of food avoidance by identifying food avoidant profiles in middle childhood and examining their neurodevelopmental correlates. Participants were 517 parents of children aged 5-12 years. Latent profile analysis was conducted using multiple ASR domains, including appetitive traits (satiety responsiveness, slowness in eating, food responsiveness, enjoyment of food and food fussiness), temperament traits (fear, shyness, inhibitory control, impulsivity), food avoidance behaviours (food avoidance, texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity) and liking of low- and high-energy-density foods (vegetable and snack liking). Multinomial logistic regression examined associations between profile membership and neurodevelopmental disorders. Five profiles were identified, including two food avoidant profiles. Multi-Domain Food Avoidant profile (n = 114, 22%) was characterised by a multi-domain form of avoidance, particularly showing higher levels of fear and shyness, suggesting greater bottom-up emotional reactivity to foods. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile (n = 66, 13%) showed the highest texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity, indicating a sensory-driven pathway to food avoidance. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile was also characterised by the lowest inhibitory control, reflecting reduced top-down regulatory capacity. Children with neurodevelopmental disorders were disproportionately represented in the food avoidant profiles. Food avoidance in middle childhood reflects heterogeneous behavioural patterns shaped by different combinations of bottom-up avoidance processes and top-down regulatory control. Identifying distinct avoidant profiles may improve understanding of the processes underlying children's food avoidance and inform more targeted approaches to supporting children with persistent avoidant eating behaviours.

items.title: Psychological, lifestyle, and self-management profiles among Indonesian adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia family life survey.
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus requires continued psychological adjustment, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and ongoing disease management. This study examined heterogeneity in psychological functioning, well-being, lifestyle behaviors, and diabetes care indicators among adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS-5). The analysis included 685 respondents with a self-reported diagnosis of diabetes by a health professional and 14 binary indicators in six domains: psychological distress (depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, neuroticism), subjective well-being (life satisfaction, general happiness), lifestyle behaviors (smoking behavior, physical activity, sweet food consumption), diabetes self-management (medication use, health monitoring), comorbidity and functional burden (comorbid chronic conditions, functional limitation), and healthcare service utilization (outpatient health service utilization, inpatient hospitalization history). A three-class solution was retained because BIC and CAIC were lowest at three classes, the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test did not support a fourth class, the smallest class comprised 16.2% of the sample, and the classes were interpretable; class separation was moderate (entropy = 0.719). The classes were Low-Distress Low-Engagement (61.1%), with low distress, high well-being, and comparatively low medication use and monitoring; High-Engagement High-Comorbidity (22.7%), with a high probability of current medication use and health monitoring and the heaviest comorbidity and functional burden; and High-Distress Low-Engagement (16.2%), with elevated depressive symptoms, lower well-being, and the lowest probabilities of medication use and monitoring. The three-class structure was reproduced when seven indicators kept their original scales, although membership in the distress class was less stable. The same three classes were obtained without the Neuroticism indicator, whose internal consistency was low, and adjusting the standard errors for household and enumeration-area clustering changed them only slightly. These co-occurring patterns require longitudinal and external validation.

items.title: What are the relations between medical professionalism and burnout, empathy, personality traits, and socio-educational measures? A network perspective.
items.abstract: Medical professionalism (MP) is a multidimensional construct that underpins physicians' ethical conduct, responsibility, and relationships with patients and colleagues. No study to date has conceptualized MP and related psychosocial constructs as an interconnected relational system. This study applied network analysis to examine the complex interrelations operating simultaneously among MP, burnout, empathy, personality traits, and socio-educational variables in 325 Spanish medical residents (mean age = 29.24 years; 70.8% female). Partial correlation networks were estimated using regularization techniques that shrink small coefficients toward zero, with accuracy assessed through bootstrap resampling. MP-comprising Professional Responsibility, Ethical Commitment, and Fellowship-emerged as the most central construct, with Ethical Commitment showing particularly strong connectivity. Personal Accomplishment and Taking the Patient's Perspective were the most central non-MP nodes. Professional Responsibility was positively associated with Personal Accomplishment and Conscientiousness; Ethical Commitment was positively linked to Taking the Patient's Perspective and negatively to Depersonalization; and Fellowship was associated with Extraversion. Network structure was invariant across gender and specialty groups. These findings position MP as a structurally central component within a broader psychosocial system, with implications for both physician well-being and the quality of patient care.

items.title: Why purpose matters for first-year psychology students: Examining an autonomy-based pathway to study-related positive affect and intellectual risk taking.
items.abstract: The transition to higher education often challenges students' motivation and wellbeing. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and the Dualistic Model of Passion, this research examined whether academic self-concordance and harmonious passion (HP) statistically mediated the association between purpose in life (PIL) and two outcomes central to first-year adjustment: study-related positive affect (Study 1) and intellectual risk taking (IRT; Study 2). Two cross-sectional studies were conducted with independent cohorts of first-semester psychology students from a university in the Netherlands, with each cohort recruited in a consecutive academic year. In both studies, serial mediation analyses using PROCESS Model 6 (Hayes, 2022) showed that higher PIL was associated with greater academic self-concordance, which was, in turn, associated with higher HP for study. In Study 1, the indirect association between PIL and study-related positive affect through academic self-concordance and HP was significant. In Study 2, the same indirect association was significant for IRT. Overall, these findings are consistent with the proposed theoretical model linking purpose in life with more autonomous, value-aligned academic motivation and adaptive academic outcomes during the transition to university.

items.title: Public evaluation of environmentalinformationdisclosure materials for waste-to-energy incineration facilities: Effects of information quantity and comprehensibility support.
items.abstract: Environmental information disclosure is an important governance tool for reducing controversy and improving communication during the siting and operation of waste-to-energy incineration facilities. Drawing on cognitive load theory, this study examines whether key design features of disclosure materials affect the public's evaluations of the quality of these materials. Using environmental impact assessment reports as representative disclosure materials, the study conducts a survey experiment with nearby residents (N = 577), develops five experimental versions that vary in information quantity and the presence of comprehensibility support, and tests the effects using one-way and two-way ANOVA. The results show significant differences in evaluations across information quantity conditions, with the medium quantity version receiving the highest ratings. Adding comprehensibility support significantly improves public evaluation, with a significant interaction between information quantity and comprehensibility support. These findings contribute to environmental psychology research by deepening our understanding of public responses to environmental information disclosure, while offering practical guidance for government agencies and project developers seeking to improve environmental information disclosure and risk communication.

items.title: Evidence for a dissociation between subjective working memory experience and objective task performance.
items.abstract: Visual working memory (vWM) supports the temporary maintenance of visual information, yet subjective memory experience and objective performance may not depend on the same aspects of the memorized content. Here, we examined whether these processes are differentially sensitive to group-level properties of visual memories. A total of 216 participants performed a change-detection task in which they rated their perceptual awareness of the memory display during the maintenance interval. We manipulated the mean size and size variability of the items to examine how group-level properties relate to subjective experience and objective performance. Subjective and objective measures showed divergent sensitivity to group-level display properties. Although subjective experience showed a relatively consistent positive relationship with these properties, objective accuracy showed a negative/nonlinear relationship that was additionally moderated by target-level factors. Individual differences in visual imagery vividness (VVIQ) were associated with subjective awareness, but not with objective performance metrics. Subjective awareness nevertheless predicted objective performance, indicating that the two measures were related despite their divergent sensitivity to group-level properties. Together, these findings demonstrate that subjective and objective measures of vWM can be differentially influenced by properties of a memory display. This dissociation highlights the importance of distinguishing subjective memory experience from objective performance when characterizing vWM. The findings may reflect differences in the availability or use of group-level and item-specific information, but the present design cannot distinguish between representational, task-related, or metacognitive explanations.

items.title: Inferring basic and complex emotions across the lifespan: The influence of face masks and autistic traits.
items.abstract: Since Covid-19, wearing face masks has been more commonplace. Mixed findings exist regarding the impact of face masks on emotion recognition. This study investigated the recognition of basic and complex emotions from dynamic facial expressions portrayed with and without a face mask across the life-span whilst also examining the influence of autistic traits. 376 participants (112 children, aged 6-11, 74 males, 38 females; 101 adolescents, aged 12-15, 62 males, 34 females; 163 adults, aged 16-87, 44 males, 119 females) completed an online facial expression recognition task with newly created and validated stimuli of five basic and five complex emotions. Findings revealed that participants had lower recognition accuracy for masked compared to unmasked faces overall, [Formula: see text] = .18. Children and adolescents with a higher number of autistic traits were generally less accurate in both conditions, r = -.22 and -.30 respectively. Moreover, higher levels of autistic traits were linked to lower accuracy for masked faces in children, [Formula: see text] = .07, but not in adolescents, [Formula: see text] = .02, or adults, [Formula: see text] < .001. These findings highlight the challenges face masks pose to emotion recognition, particularly for children with higher levels of autistic traits.

items.title: Caregiver-Informed Safety and System Requirements for Real-Time Feedback During Pediatric Inhaler Use: Qualitative Concept-Elicitation Study.
items.abstract: Correct use of a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI), usually with a valved holding chamber, depends on use-related conditions that caregivers may not observe directly, including inhalation pattern, actuation-inhalation timing, mask seal, and device orientation. Many digital inhaler systems emphasize actuation or adherence. Systems that infer technique-related conditions from proxy signals may add real-time feedback but also create false reassurance if a positive state is displayed when evidence is inadequate. Caregiver expectations for such feedback and its failure states remain poorly characterized before prototype development. This study aimed to characterize caregivers' experiences of pediatric inhaler administration and translate responses to a proposed sensor concept into traceable candidate safety, system, and validation requirements. We conducted 23 semistructured concept-elicitation sessions through Zoom videoconference with 27 caregivers of children who currently or previously used a pMDI. Interviews consisted of 19 individual and 4 dyadic sessions pairing 2 caregivers from different households. Sessions were conducted remotely between April and July 2026 from the University of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Recruitment originated in Calgary and was not geographically restricted. A 6-phase guide examined current practices, difficulties, prior digital-tool use, and responses to a screen-shared clip-on concept incorporating airflow-, timing-, seal-, and orientation-related sensing; on-device feedback; an optional child-facing app; and a caregiver dashboard. No working prototype was evaluated. Approximately 86,000 transcript words underwent hybrid directed and conventional qualitative content analysis using an 18-category codebook. Two researchers independently coded the complete 27×18 matrix (486 paired decisions) across 2 rounds. Consensus categories were translated into candidate requirements and assigned an earliest verification or evaluation locus. Counts are descriptive caregiver-voice tallies, not prevalence estimates. Persistent uncertainty about whether administration conditions were adequate was the dominant lived experience (19/27); for 5 caregivers, existing passive cues had not resolved it. A simple, real-time on-device signal was endorsed by 25 caregivers, but willingness to consider the concept was conditional on reliability (9 caregivers named reasons for abandonment, notably a "false green"), low-friction operation during acute symptoms (12/27), minimal added bulk and technique change, and one or more of clinical validation, clinician recommendation, or a trial pathway (composite category; 23/27). Stances on gamification (20/27), dashboard cadence (18/27), aesthetics (24/27), and privacy (18/27) supported an optional, configurable software layer. Intercoder agreement was 94% (Cohen κ=0.88). The analytic synthesis yielded a conceptual architecture separating observable proxy signals, an inference and data-quality gate, and positive, corrective, or uncertain feedback states. Participating caregivers prioritized immediate and interpretable feedback about use-related conditions. The findings support conservative state assignment, an explicit uncertain state for indeterminate signals, and app-independent acute-use feedback. These are candidate requirements rather than validated device specifications; subsequent work should proceed through bench verification, simulated-use human factors evaluation, and prospective clinical or field validation.

items.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
items.abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads. Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety. Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads. The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection. Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research. DERR1-10.2196/107879.

items.title: Perspectives from older adults with hearing loss on the link between hearing loss and dementia.
items.abstract: Research and public messaging increasingly highlight a potential link between hearing loss and cognitive decline. This study explores how older adults interpret, evaluate, and respond to messages linking hearing and cognition. Data was collected using semi-structured interviews and analysed using inductive thematic analysis. Twenty-five Canadians aged 56-97 with self-reported hearing difficulties were recruited through research databases and community advertisements. Four themes were identified. Participants constructed meaning about the hearing loss-dementia link through lived experience, personal theorising, and interpretations of scientific and professional information (Theme 1: Making Sense of the Message). They evaluated the need for action, the modifiability of hearing and cognition, and the link's personal relevance (Theme 2: Weighing the Need for Action). Some participants described the link as motivating initial help-seeking, persistence with hearing management, and/or reinforcement of past decisions (Theme 3: Perceived Impact on Hearing Health Behaviours). Certainty and trust in evidence, clinicians, and the hearing healthcare system shaped participants' interpretations and influenced their willingness to act (Theme 4: Certainty and Trust). Public messages about hearing and cognition are filtered through personal and experiential frameworks, underscoring the importance of clear, balanced, and patient-centred communication when discussing hearing health and cognition.

items.title: Downstream effects of emotion regulation tactics and acceptance in younger and older adults.
items.abstract: Older adults report higher emotional wellbeing than younger adults and report using more emotion regulation tactics that approach positive elements of a stimulus and acceptance. However, it remains unclear what drives these age differences in regulation behaviour. Are particular regulation behaviours preferred due to their downstream consequences (i.e. their immediate affect and later memory for the eliciting stimulus)? Little prior work has examined the affective and cognitive outcomes of different emotion regulation tactics across age groups. In the present study, younger (N = 77; ages 18-25) and older adults (N = 62, ages 55+) viewed negative images while implementing Valence × Direction emotion regulation tactics (classified by approaching or avoiding positive/negative elements of a stimulus, yielding: positive-approaching, negative-approaching and negative-receding) and acceptance. Participants also reported their subjective valence and arousal after each regulation attempt. Afterwards, they completed an incidental memory task. Positive-approaching was associated with the most positive self-reported valence and lowest arousal. Negative-receding was associated with the poorest memory performance, whereas positive-approaching was associated with the best. Age group did not significantly interact with tactic type for affective or memory outcomes. Overall, these results suggest that some forms of emotion regulation may simultaneously support emotional wellbeing and information processing.

items.title: Men's Engagement in and Enjoyment of Sex Toy Use with Female Partners: Exploring Differences in Masculinity, Sexism, Male Genital Image, and Sexual Esteem.
items.abstract: Despite growing prevalence of partnered sex toy use, limited research has examined the psychological factors that shape men's engagement with and enjoyment of sex toys. The present study investigated whether conformity to masculine norms, precarious manhood beliefs, hostile and benevolent sexism, male genital self-image, and sexual esteem differentiate men who use sex toys with female partners from those who do not, and men who enjoy such use from those who do not. Male-identified participants (N = 828; Mage = 39.63; SDage = 15.29) who had ever had at least one female sexual partner completed an online survey. Multivariate and discriminant function analyses revealed that sex toy users demonstrated less conformity to masculine norms, fewer precarious manhood beliefs, lower sexism, and greater genital self-image and sexual esteem than non-users. Among users, enjoyers exhibited lower masculine conformity, precarious manhood beliefs, and sexism, alongside greater sexual esteem, compared to non-enjoyers; genital self-image did not differ significantly between groups. Hierarchical logistic regressions further indicated that sexual esteem - but not genital self-image - predicted use of phallic-style toys. Findings suggest that masculine ideology and traditional sexual scripts may pose meaningful barriers to partnered sex toy engagement among men who have sex with women, with possible implications for sexual health education.

items.title: Multivariate cortical thickness-cognition covariance supports the criterion validity of the Riga Cognitive Screening Task.
items.abstract: There is a predicted increase in the prevalence of older adults presenting with mild to severe cognitive impairment. Screening tools with high sensitivity are the first frontier in identifying a cognitive pathology; however, to ensure that they are measuring the intended concept or criterion, thorough psychometric procedures should be followed. In this study, concurrent criterion validity of Riga Cognitive Screening Task was measured, using cortical thickness of regions of interest as the criterion. 106 older adults (Mage = 70.49, SD = 8.08, 35.8% male) with varying levels of cognitive functioning were involved in the study. All participants underwent cognitive assessment with the screening task and a 3T MRI. Cortical thickness of selected temporal and parietal regions was used as a brain measure. Behavioural Partial Least Squares Correlation was conducted and one latent variable was extracted. The results confirmed that Riga Cognitive Screening Task shows good criterion validity, suggesting successful use for screening.

items.title: Developing endpoints for the cognitive burden in myotonic dystrophy type 1: A workshop report.
items.abstract: Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 (DM1) is an autosomal dominant, repeat expansion, progressive multisystem disorder. While central nervous system (CNS) involvement has been well established, a consensus on a dedicated protocol to assess cognitive function and collect CNS biomarkers is still lacking in this disease. In the era of disease-modifying therapies that cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB), availability of mechanistically relevant neuropsychological probes and reliable biomarkers of DM1 pathology is no longer deferrable. Consequently, to better define and harmonize a CNS assessment pathway, the Myotonic Dystrophy Clinical Research Network (DMCRN) convened a workshop entitled ''Myotonic Dystrophy CNS Workshop'' in September 2024. Presenters described the protean manifestations of CNS involvement in DM1, shared data about neuropsychological assessments available with cross-fertilization from other neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and discussed existing data and future perspectives on CNS radiological biomarkers.

items.title: Seasonal cycles in basic human values: Evidence from over thirteen years of U.S. data on the Schwartz value survey.
items.abstract: Previous research revealed a bimodal seasonal cycle in Americans' endorsement of "binding" moral values (authority, loyalty, purity). We extended this work by examining seasonal patterns in human values more broadly, using Schwartz Value Survey data collected across more than 13 years from respondents in the United States (N = 31,981). Of the 10 values assessed, four values-pertaining to conformity, power, achievement, and benevolence-showed seasonal cycles that were consistent across years and robust across analytic strategies. These seasonal cycles were bimodal-characterized by two peaks (periods of strong endorsement) and two valleys (periods of lower endorsement) over the year-but the timing of those peaks and valleys differed across values. The bimodal seasonal cycle for conformity was similar to the seasonal cycle in binding moral values and is interpreted as a partial conceptual replication of those previous findings. The seasonal cycles for power, achievement, and benevolence resulted from exploratory analyses, and interpretations are cautiously speculative.

items.title: Genetic and Epigenetic Determinants of Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviors: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: A better understanding of the determinants of physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB) is needed to counter increasing inactivity. Twin and family studies indicate that these behaviors are shaped by biological factors, including genetic and epigenetic mechanisms. The number of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) on PA and SB that try to elucidate these mechanisms has been increasing, motivating a review on whether their findings point to overlapping or distinct biological mechanisms. In this preregistered systematic review, we synthesize GWAS and EWAS findings on PA and SB and identify replicated loci across studies. We included nine GWAS reporting 414 unique lead SNPs and seven EWAS reporting 437 significant CpG sites associated with PA and/or SB. Across all findings, 51 genomic loci and 93 SNPs met our replication criteria, defined as support from at least two different GWAS or EWAS studies. Five genomic loci (1p36.23, 1p13.3, 1q21.3, 6p22.2, and 6p21.31) including six lead SNPs (rs301799, rs8450, rs4845364, rs2393593, rs10947452, and rs6457816), showed convergence between PA/SB-associated GWAS variants and mQTLs for PA/SB-associated CpG sites, highlighting candidate regions for future functional follow-up. Functional annotation indicated that these loci are mostly enriched in genic and transcript-associated regions. Gene mapping and enrichment analyses highlighted biological pathways across neurobiological systems involved in motivation and exercise liking, as well as peripheral systems related to movement, exercise capacity, energy metabolism, and cardiometabolic functioning. PA/SB-associated SNPs also overlapped with variants linked to body composition, cardiometabolic markers, educational attainment, cognitive ability, and brain-size traits. Overall, PA and SB appear to be influenced by a complex, highly polygenic architecture, with consistent genetic influences but limited convergence yet in epigenetic influences. Further large-scale, multi-ancestry studies integrating genomic and epigenomic data with harmonized PA/SB measures are needed to inform functional genetic studies.

items.title: Preemptive solving of future problems: Multitask Preplay in humans and machines.
items.abstract: Humans can pursue a near-infinite variety of tasks, but typically can only pursue a small number at the same time. We hypothesize that humans leverage experience on one task to preemptively learn solutions to other tasks that were accessible but not pursued. We formalize this idea as "Multitask Preplay", an algorithm that replays experience on one task as the starting point for "preplay"-counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task. Preplay is used to learn a predictive representation that can support fast, adaptive task performance later on. When implemented within deep reinforcement learning, it predicts human generalization to novel tasks more accurately than traditional planning and predictive representation methods across grid-worlds and a 2D Minecraft domain. Additionally, Multitask Preplay improves an artificial agent's ability to generalize to new environments sharing task co-occurrence structure. These findings demonstrate that Multitask Preplay is a scalable theory of human counterfactual learning and generalization; endowing artificial agents with this capacity can significantly improve their performance in challenging multitask environments.

items.title: Morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment.
items.abstract: Modern western legal and criminal justice theories assume that punishment should deter criminalized behavior by introducing costs that reduce its expected utility, but, empirically, punishment often has weak effects on rates of crime and recidivism. Here, we hypothesize that when people are motivated to engage in criminalized behavior for moral reasons, they show diminished sensitivity to punishment. We demonstrate our hypothesis across 10 correlational, experimental, and economic game studies with participants drawn from the general population as well as participants with criminal backgrounds. Studies 1 to 3 draw on federal data of over 30,000 offenders and find that participants' estimates of moral motives for crime predict higher recidivism while estimates of material motives predict the opposite. Studies 4 to 8 use judgment studies and find that morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment across a diversity of crime types, when motives are manipulated but actions are kept constant, persist for different types of consequences, and are unique to moral motivation. Studies 9 and 10 employ economic games and find that when players take money from others for moral reasons, they are less deterred by the imposition of fines. Implications for systems of punishment, offender psychology, and restorative justice approaches are discussed.

items.title: Training the Future Public Health Workforce: Reflexive Insights From an Undergraduate Needs Assessment Experience.
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to examine how public health workforce capabilities develop through engagement in real-world research tasks. In this qualitative longitudinal autoethnographic study, 72 reflective journal entries were analyzed using reflexive analysis to explore the development of capability during applied research in public health. Five developmental processes were found to demonstrate that capability emerges through reconstructing understanding rather than through linear skill acquisition: 1) destabilizing prior knowledge, 2) engaging with uncertainty, 3) negotiating real-world constraints, 4) forming professional identity, and 5) developing reflexive judgement. Experiential research participation transforms knowledge into context-sensitive professional capability, highlighting the importance of uncertainty, responsibility, reflection, and practice beyond competency-based training.

items.title: Immersive Virtual Nature to Promote Mental Health and Nature Connectedness in Youth: Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Mental health disorders are increasing among adolescents and young adults. While contact with real nature provides mental health benefits, access to natural environments is not always possible. Immersive virtual nature (IVN) represents a potential alternative to promote mental health and nature connectedness. This scoping review aims to map and synthesize how IVN has been used to promote mental health and nature connectedness among adolescents and young adults (<24 years). A systematic search was conducted across 6 databases (PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) in November 2025 and updated in August 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and expert consultation. Inclusion criteria encompassed quantitative and qualitative studies examining IVN interventions with mental health and/or nature connectedness outcomes. Sixty-one studies were included (4630 participants). The majority involved young adults (n=55), almost all university students, while only 6 studies included adolescents. Overall, included studies reported improvements in mental health and nature connectedness outcomes following IVN. Single-session IVN studies (n=26) reported immediate improvements, multisession IVN interventions (n=11) reported short-term benefits, and environments characteristics comparisons (n=30) compared different virtual environments. This last category indicated that visual characteristics (brightness and vegetation density), auditory stimuli, and interactivity substantially influence outcomes. IVN shows promising potential to support mental health in youth populations. However, current evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity, the predominance of laboratory-based single-session interventions, and the scarcity of research in adolescents. Future research should prioritize rigorous multisession interventions in younger and more clinically diverse populations, while also exploring personalization strategies based on environmental characteristics.

items.title: Medication Management Strategies for People with Multiple Long-Term Conditions Approaching End of Life: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Despite the challenges of managing medication for people with multiple long-term conditions approaching end of life, guidance remains limited. The review aim was to evaluate the effectiveness of medication management strategies in this population and identify research gaps. Eligible studies examined medication management strategies in adults ages ≥ 50 years with multiple long-term conditions approaching end of life. Studies focusing on a single condition, early-stage multimorbidity, or non-pharmacological palliative care interventions were excluded. MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to September 2025. Study quality was assessed independently by two reviewers using recognized appraisal tools, with risk of bias rated as high, fair, or low. A narrative synthesis was conducted. From 14,945 records, six studies met inclusion criteria. All focused on deprescribing potentially inappropriate medications, with mixed effects on polypharmacy, regimen complexity, and clinical outcomes. The limited number of studies, all conducted in Europe, and the presence of high risk of bias in half of them, restrict generalizability. Findings suggest that deprescribing, supported by multidisciplinary and patient-centered approaches, is central to optimizing medication management at end of life in multimorbid populations. Further research is needed on broader strategies, including symptom control and anticipatory prescribing beyond deprescribing.

items.title: Intra-Visit and Retrospective Participant Experiences in Group Medical Visits for Chronic Pain in Rural Communities: A Qualitative Analysis.
items.abstract: IntroductionAs a leading cause of disability, chronic pain disproportionately impacts rural communities. Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines call for interdisciplinary, whole-person, non-pharmacological approaches as first-line treatment for chronic pain. Group Medical Visits (GMVs) are a promising approach; however, evidence on the patient experience remains limited. This manuscript describes the participants' experiences and the impact of a chronic pain GMV series for rural adults.MethodsTwo rural health systems implemented 4 series of an 8-week chronic pain GMV. Intra-visit shifts were assessed through a weekly progress sheet, administered at the start and end of each session. Thematic analysis was employed on the 250 weekly progress sheets collected. Semi-structured interviews (n = 29), conducted one month after the series, underwent rapid analysis.ResultsWeekly progress sheets showed trends towards improved intra-visit pain scores and improved mental and physical state across cohorts and sites. Semi-structured interviews yielded 34 themes throughout five categories (Skills Acquired, Group Experience, Materials, Instruction, and Improvement).ConclusionOutcomes analysis demonstrated positive impact of the curriculum and GMV environment. The use of both intra-visit assessment and retrospective interviews illustrates participants' weekly experiences, incremental changes, and overall positive experiences during and across a whole-person, chronic pain GMV series in two rural communities.

items.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
items.abstract: Dark chocolate (DC) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for exercise performance and recovery, but evidence in trained women remains limited. This exploratory secondary analysis examined selected lower-limb performance outcomes and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in female CrossFit® athletes. This secondary analysis included 15 trained female CrossFit® athletes from a randomized crossover trial. No separate a priori sample-size calculation was performed for these outcomes (minimum detectable paired effect, d_z = 0.78). DC (30 g/day, 85% cocoa), placebo chocolate (PLA), and an open-label control (CONN) were compared at four operationally defined menstrual-cycle assessments after three days of supplementation. DC-PLA allocation was blinded, but blinding success was not assessed. Outcomes were vertical jump height (VJH), knee isokinetic and isometric performance, and muscle-specific DOMS after the Cindy WOD. Condition effects survived FDR control for VJH and 19 of 22 dynamometry outcomes. Across assessments, VJH was 34.48 ± 5.09 cm with DC and 30.22 ± 2.34 cm with PLA (mean difference 4.27 cm, 95% CI 1.45 to 7.08; Holm-adjusted p = 0.017; g_av = 1.09). No condition-by-assessment interaction survived FDR control (all q ≥ 0.141). DOMS showed significant time effects for all three muscles, peaked at approximately 24 h, remained elevated at 48 h, and declined toward baseline by 72 h. A condition-by-time effect remained significant only for gastrocnemius soreness (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012; ηp2 = 0.212); no DOMS condition main effect or condition-by-assessment-by-time interaction was supported. DC was associated with higher values for selected lower-limb outcomes, but these exploratory findings do not establish phase-specific efficacy, equivalent effects across cycle assessments, or a consistent DOMS benefit. Unusually large performance estimates and unmodeled period and carryover effects warrant caution.

items.title: Sensorimotor dimensions of weight stigma among women with binge eating disorder and higher weight bodies: a phenomenologically framed body mapping study.
items.abstract: Weight stigma and binge eating disorder (BED) are connected phenomena related to body image. Body awareness and embodied distress are important targets for physiotherapeutic intervention on body image in this patient group. However, the influence of weight stigma on body image and specific treatment approaches are not included in clinical guidelines. Thus, a better understanding of the body's role in stigma management is needed to inform clinical practice. To explore sensorimotor experiences in situations perceived as weight‑stigmatizing among women with BED and higher weight. Seven patients who had participated in body-oriented group therapy in a specialized psychiatric outpatient unit were recruited. The art-based research method Body Mapping (BM) was applied, which facilitated closeness to the participants' bodily experiences and their visual and symbolic expressions. Phenomenological theory about embodiment informed the analysis of the body maps. Analysis revealed two interrelated experiential patterns: Vivid torso and vague limbs: confusing body presence, and Separation and withdrawal: limited agency. Participants experienced weight stigma through intense bodily sensations concentrated in the torso, while the extremities appeared absent, weakened, or unavailable for action. These experiences were accompanied by feelings of fragmentation, restriction, disconnection from the environment, and diminished agency in social situations. This study highlights the importance of understanding weight stigma as an embodied phenomenon and underscores the value of attending to lived bodily experience in BED. By demonstrating the utility of body mapping for accessing dimensions of experience that may be difficult to articulate verbally, the study expands current approaches to exploring weight stigma and body image. The findings support the integration of embodied perspectives into assessment and treatment and point to the potential value of interdisciplinary approaches in BED care. Further research is needed to examine the transferability and clinical relevance of these insights across diverse populations and contexts.

items.title: Who do children turn to for help regulating their emotions? Intrinsic interpersonal emotion regulation in late childhood.
items.abstract: Children often regulate their emotions with help from multiple people within their social networks, including parents, peers, and teachers. In late childhood, children are increasingly expected to take an active role in managing their emotions, making it important to understand how they seek interpersonal emotion regulation support. The present study examined who children turn to for emotion regulation support and whether the way this support is organized is linked to their emotion regulation strategies and emotional functioning. Participants included 180 children aged 9-12 years (M = 10.72, SD = 1.06; 57% female; 75% White) who nominated specific people they would turn to for help regulating sadness, nervousness, and excitement and reported characteristics of these relationships. Children also reported their use of cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, and generalized anxiety symptoms. Parents reported children's self-management skills. Children's emotion regulation support was organized primarily around family members and peers and embedded in close, long-standing relationships. Support across a wider range of emotions and reliance on different helpers for different emotion regulation goals were associated with greater cognitive reappraisal, even after accounting for the number and closeness of helpers. Greater relationship-type diversity was associated with lower parent-rated self-management. The organization of children's emotion regulation support was unrelated to expressive suppression and generalized anxiety symptoms. These findings provide an initial picture of children's interpersonal emotion regulation support across relationships in late childhood and suggest that some features may be relevant to specific aspects of children's emotion functioning.
