items.title: Tear Proteomics Reveals Metabolic Stress–Driven Ocular Surface Barrier Dysfunction in Myopia
items.abstract: Abstract Background The global prevalence of myopia is rapidly increasing and has become a major public health concern. Beyond axial elongation and refractive error, accumulating evidence suggests that myopia is associated with ocular surface dysfunction, including tear film instability, epithelial barrier impairment, and altered antimicrobial defense. However, the molecular basis underlying myopia-associated ocular surface imbalance, particularly in pediatric mild-to-moderate myopia, remains incompletely understood. Methods In this prospective case–control study, tear samples were collected from 20 children with mild-to-moderate myopia and 20 age- and sex-matched emmetropic controls. Label-free quantitative proteomic profiling was performed using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). Differential protein expression analysis, unsupervised clustering, and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) were conducted following quality control. Functional annotation included Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment, functional module scoring, correlation network analysis, and protein–protein interaction (PPI) network construction. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the discriminative performance of key metabolic signatures. Results Global tear proteomic profiling revealed a clear separation between mild-to-moderate myopia and control samples, indicating substantial molecular remodeling of the tear film. Myopia exhibited a bidirectional regulatory pattern characterized by upregulation of proteins involved in one-carbon metabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis, and redox homeostasis, together with downregulation of proteins related to corneal epithelial structural maintenance, lysosomal processing, antimicrobial immunity, and vesicular transport. Core enzymes of the one-carbon metabolic pathway, including SHMT1, MTHFD1, and MTHFS, were significantly elevated, accompanied by increased markers of endoplasmic reticulum stress, antioxidant responses, and activation of the STAT1/NF-κB signaling axis. A composite one-carbon metabolism score effectively distinguished myopia from controls (AUC = 0.772). Network analyses further demonstrated coordinated associations among one-carbon metabolism, oxidative stress regulation, interferon signaling, and epithelial structural proteins. Conclusions This study delineates a comprehensive tear proteomic landscape in pediatric mild-to-moderate myopia and identifies a metabolic stress–associated ocular surface imbalance characterized by activation of one-carbon metabolism, enhancement of inflammatory signaling, and remodeling of epithelial barrier structure. These findings provide mechanistic insights into ocular surface dysfunction in myopia and suggest potential metabolic biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

items.title: Nested cell-level voltage-window selection for partial-charge state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Estimating the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries from a short part of the charging curve is attractive for battery management systems, because vehicles and devices are rarely charged from empty to full. Published errors are often very low, but the voltage window and the data split are usually chosen by the authors, and the sensitivity to measurement conditions is seldom reported. We study a simple pipeline: five features from a voltage window of the constant-current charging phase feed a ridge regression, and the window is selected using only the training cells (nested leave-one-cell-out). On three public datasets of LCO/NMC-type cells (lithium cobalt oxide or nickel–manganese–cobalt oxide cathodes; NASA, 4 cells; CALCE, 6 cells; Oxford, 8 cells), the mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) of SOH is 3.01, 2.28 and 0.72 %, against 5.9, 2.8 and 2.3 % for a linear model that knows only the cycle index. Ridge regression is statistically indistinguishable from random forest, gradient boosting and support-vector regression (paired Wilcoxon \(\:p\approx\:0.42\), 18 cells) and is much cheaper. The best window differs between datasets; a window shift of 0.02 V increases the error by a factor of 1.6 to 3.3 on NASA and Oxford; 10 mV of voltage noise doubles the NASA error unless the voltage is filtered; and models do not transfer between datasets. On 119 lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells (Supplementary Material), ridge does not beat the cycle-index baseline, and tree ensembles are only moderately better.

items.title: Biosorption of Chromium Using Biochar Derived from Fruit Waste: Isotherm and Thermodynamic Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract In recent years, heavy metal contamination has become a major environmental and public health concern. Chromium is considered one of the most toxic heavy metals and is listed as a priority pollutant by the United States Environmental Protection Agency due to its high toxicity. Chromium is widely released from industries such as electroplating, tanning, textile processing, and mining. Hence, it is essential to develop simple, efficient, and sustainable methods for chromium removal from contaminated water. This study investigated the feasibility of using green biochar synthesized from orange peel waste through a simultaneous pyrolysis process for the adsorption of hexavalent chromium from synthetic wastewater. The biochar was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy to identify functional groups such as C–O and C–H bonds. Kinetic experiments were performed with contact times ranging from 0 to 330 minutes to determine the equilibrium time, which was found to be approximately 270 minutes. Adsorption behaviour at different chromium concentrations indicated that physisorption dominated at lower concentration (15 mg/L), whereas chemisorption was more prominent at higher concentration (65 mg/L). Batch adsorption studies showed chromium removal efficiencies in the range of approximately 36% to 87%. The maximum adsorption capacity was determined to be about 5.88–3.28 mg/g. The adsorption data were best fit described by the Langmuir isotherm model (R 2 is 0.955). Overall, the results demonstrate that orange peel–derived biochar is a promising, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly adsorbent for hexavalent chromium removal.

items.title: Immunometabolic Reversal of Long COVID and Inflammatory Memory via Host-Directed Antiviral and Metabolic Shielding
items.abstract: Abstract Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection provokes an intense acute inflammatory response (1, 16). However, in hundreds of millions of individuals surviving the acute phase, clinical presentation frequently diverges into persistent post-acute sequelae known as Long COVID, or Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) (1, 16). With global epidemiological estimates now surpassing 400 million affected patients worldwide, Long COVID has emerged as one of the most debilitating public health crises of the modern era (1, 16). Characterized by intractable chronic fatigue, post-exertional malaise (PEM), neuro-psychiatric cognitive impairment ("brain fog"), autonomic dysregulation, and accelerated biological aging (inflammaging) in the absence of active viral replication, the syndrome imposes an immense socioeconomic and healthcare burden (1, 16). Current clinical management remains severely bottlenecked by palliative symptom management, largely because existing therapeutic models fail to address the core drivers of disease persistence (1, 16). Here, we uncover the precise molecular circuitry coupling viral persistence and metabolic stress to chronic post-viral fatigue: the SARS-CoV-2 ORF7b-c-Myc-MALAT1/NEAT1-miR-22-3p-NLRP3 axis, integrated with the SIRT6-SIRT3-LCAD/SLC25A13-mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MIDAS) axis and the p53-FBXO22-NSP5 / RIG-I / MAVS feedforward antiviral loop (1, 9, 10, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21). Utilizing an expanded deterministic eight-variable non-linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) kinetic model and phase-space separatrix analysis, we establish a critical therapeutic separatrix threshold (S_"ImmunoShield" ≥2.85" a.u." ) and demonstrate how a host-directed p53/NRF2-metformin-taurine immunometabolic shield successfully dismantles pathological attractors, clears oxidized mitochondrial DNA, restores sirtuin-mediated deacetylation, and terminates inflammatory memory.

items.title: Protective and Cross-Protective Efficacies of Inactivated Recombinant H5N1 and H5N8 Vaccines Against Highly-Pathogenic Avian Influenza H5-Type Strains in Chickens
items.abstract: Abstract Background Co-circulation of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 and H5N8 viruses (clade 2.3.4.4b) threatens poultry production and public health, so vaccines that protect against both viruses are needed. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and cross-protective efficacy of inactivated recombinant (reverse genetics-derived) rgH5N1 and rgH5N8 vaccines (10 8.0 50% embryo infectious dose [EID 50 ]/dose) against homologous and heterologous HPAI H5-type challenge in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens. Vaccine strains were inactivated with 0.2% formalin and emulsified with Montanide ISA 71 VG adjuvant. SPF chickens (n = 10 per group) received rgH5N1 (G1), rgH5N8 (G2), or phosphate-buffered saline (G3, unvaccinated controls). Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers were measured at weeks 2, 3, and 4 post-vaccination. At week 4, birds were challenged intranasally with homologous or heterologous HPAI virus (10 6 EID 50 /0.1 mL) and monitored for 10 days for clinical signs and mortality; viral shedding was assessed by real-time RT-PCR. Both vaccines induced HI responses that peaked at weeks 3–4. The rgH5N1 vaccine elicited high cross-reactive titers against H5N8 (9.2–9.4 log 2 ), whereas the rgH5N8 vaccine elicited lower cross-reactive titers against H5N1 (7.25 log 2 ). Both vaccines conferred 100% survival and no detectable viral shedding (cycle threshold [Ct] > 38) after homologous and heterologous challenge. All unvaccinated controls died, with high viral loads detected from day 3. Both inactivated vaccines provided complete cross-protection against heterologous H5-type challenge under controlled conditions, preventing mortality and detectable viral shedding. This supports their potential for controlling co-circulating H5N1 and H5N8 viruses in poultry, although confirmation in larger groups under field conditions is needed.

items.title: Associations of Stromal Markers' Expression in Benign Breast Tissue With Subsequent Breast Cancer Risk.
items.abstract: Breast stroma may play an important role in carcinogenesis. We examined the associations of stromal markers alpha-smooth muscle actin (αSMA), tenascin-C (TNC), fibroblast activation protein (FAP), calcyclin (s100a6), and matrix metallo-proteinase (MMP14) in benign breast biopsy samples with subsequent breast cancer (BCa) risk. This study included women with biopsy-confirmed benign breast disease (BBD) from a nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study (NHS) and NHSII cohorts. The data on BCa risk factors were obtained from questionnaires updated biennially. Multiplex immunofluorescence (IF) of stromal markers was completed on tissue microarrays. For each core, the percent (%) positivity was quantified using inForm v2.6.0. Multivariate logistic regression was used to examine the associations of each marker's expression (continuous and binary with 1% cutoff) with BCa risk, while adjusting for BCa risk factors. Among the 370 women (82 cases/288 controls), 106 (28.7%) had non-proliferative BBD, 205 (55.4%) had proliferative BBD without atypia, and 59 (16.0%) had proliferative BBD with atypia. We found suggestive evidence of positive associations of FAP expression with BCa cancer risk (OR per 10% change in expression = 1.15, 95% CI: 0.98-1.35). The expression of αSMA, s100a6, TNC, and MMP14 was not associated with subsequent BCa risk. In secondary models adjusting for BBD subtype and % mammographic breast density, these results remained similar. Our findings suggest that increased stromal fibroblast activation (as captured by FAP expression) may be associated with greater subsequent BCa risk. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: The Association of Oral and Anogenital Human Papillomavirus Genotypes With Head and Neck Cancers in Brazil: A Nationwide Case-Control Study.
items.abstract: This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer-free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50-65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high-risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV-16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV-16/18-positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case-control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high-risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. 9%; p = 0.049). Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten-fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92-34.6). Oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52-26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site-specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV-16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

items.title: Search Interest in Alleged COVID-19 Treatments During the Pandemic and the Impact of Mass News Media Coverage Based on Google Trends and Media Cloud Data: Retrospective Analysis.
items.abstract: Background During a public health emergency, interest in unsafe or illegitimate medications can delay appropriate treatment and foster medical mistrust. Objective The aim of this study is to assess the relationship between search interest and media coverage of 3 purported COVID-19 treatments: hydroxychloroquine, ivermectin, and remdesivir. Methods The authors obtained daily US-based Google Trends and Media Cloud data from 2019 through 2022, conducted national-level anomaly detection, and assessed the state-level association of treatment-specific search interest and media coverage by regressing search interest against daily media coverage, and vice versa, for each treatment using a 2-stage process. This allowed us to explicitly model the questions: (1) does a state have any of the outcomes (search interest or media coverage), and (2) given a nonzero outcome, how much is it impacted by the exposure? Results Search interest and media coverage of all 3 treatments were significantly elevated during the study period. Anomaly detection identified several periods of higher-than-expected activity; anomalies in search interest and media coverage showed similar temporal patterns within treatments. There were distinct patterns of media source bias across treatments: while the plurality of top sources for all treatments were rated "Left" or "Left Leaning," ivermectin was covered by the highest number of "Right"-biased sources, and remdesivir had the highest coverage by "Center" or unbiased sources. Significant associations between media coverage and search interest were observed for all 3 treatments. Media coverage had the strongest impact on same-day search interest for hydroxychloroquine (21.3% increase, 95% CI 20.1%-22.5%) and ivermectin (18.3% increase, 95% CI 16.8%-19.7%), and a more modest impact for remdesivir (12.8% increase, 95% CI 11.8%-13.8%). For hydroxychloroquine and remdesivir, this same-day effect was more transient, while interest in ivermectin remained elevated at a comparable level 1 and 2 days after media coverage. When evaluating the separate impact of search interest on media coverage, the associations were much weaker for all 3 treatments and all lagged conditions. Conclusions During a public health emergency, the information accessed by populations can directly influence health-seeking behaviors, potentially resulting in life-threatening consequences. Given the observed associations between treatment-related news media coverage and public interest in those treatments, our results suggest that news media serve as a powerful mechanism for experts to inform the landscape of public opinion and to reach audiences during future public health emergencies.

items.title: Food Insecurity Patterns and Risk of Poor Glycemic Control, Acute Complications of Diabetes, and Ability to Obtain Diabetes Technologies in Youth and Young Adults With Youth-Onset Type 1 Diabetes.
items.abstract: Objective Household food insecurity (FI) is linked cross-sectionally to diabetes-related outcomes. However, prior studies have not fully considered temporal relationships or the evolving nature of FI. We explored the patterns of FI and associations with hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), severe hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), health care use, and the ability to obtain diabetes technologies among youth and young adults (YYAs) with youth-onset type 1 diabetes (T1D). Research design and methods Longitudinal data (2016-2022) from 956 YYAs with T1D were analyzed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Food security was measured thrice (t1, t2, and t3) with the Household Food Security Survey Module and patterned into persistent food security (PFS), intermittent FI (IFI), and persistent FI (PFI). We evaluated FI patterns derived from repeated assessments with follow-up diabetes-related outcomes. Results The prevalence of IFI was 20.8% and PFI was 7.7%. Compared with YYAs experiencing PFS, the odds of inability to obtain continuous glucose monitors were higher for IFI (1.9, 95% CI 1.1, 3.3) and PFI groups (2.3, 1.0, 5.2), independent of individual characteristics. PFI was additionally associated with higher HbA1c (β = 0.6, P 9.0%, 3.0-fold higher odds of diabetes-related emergency department visits, and 2.5-fold higher odds of inability to obtain an insulin pump. Conclusions Among YYAs with T1D, IFI and PFI over time both seem to be associated with severely impaired ability to maintain glycemic targets, increasing the risk of adverse outcomes.

items.title: Iron deficiency activates the GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1-TFEB axis to promote pexophagy.
items.abstract: Peroxisomes are dynamic metabolic organelles whose dysfunction results in severe diseases. The homeostasis of peroxisomes is also ensured through pexophagy, a type of selective autophagy targeting these organelles. Pexophagy can be activated by several stressors, such as starvation, mTOR inhibition, and iron deficiency. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying pexophagy are poorly characterized. Here, we identify a novel regulatory axis of iron deficiency-induced pexophagy, which preferentially engages GABARAP among the mATG8 family members. Comparative analysis of the mATG8 interactomes reveals that upon iron depletion, GABARAP selectively interacts with the tumor suppressor complex FLCN/FNIP1 triggering the activation of the autophagy and lysosome transcription factors TFEB and TFE3, thus promoting efficient cargo degradation. Our findings thus identify the GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 axis as a molecular sensor that bridges iron deficiency and TFEB/TFE3 activation to prime pexophagy execution.

items.title: Decision making around end-of-life: Focused ethnography in two intensive care units in Vietnam.
items.abstract: Literature on the quality of death and dying has predominantly drawn on high-income contexts, while much less is known about end-of-life care in low-middle-income settings. In Vietnam, policy and practice around palliative and end-of-life care has not kept pace with the ageing of the population. This study explores factors influencing end-of-life decision making in intensive care units (ICUs) where formal protocols are lacking. This analysis is a part of a larger ethnographic study examining vital sign monitoring in two ICUs in Vietnam, including observations, informal conversations and formal interviews with healthcare workers. In addition to learning about the care practices around vital sign monitoring, we noted the various complexities that influenced physicians and family members' end-of-life decision making in these contexts. Factors included patients' prognosis, family wishes, cultural practices surrounding death and financial considerations. Financial concerns were a significant factor in discontinuing treatment, particularly for uninsured patients. The lack of accessible out-of-hospital care made it difficult for patients to spend their final moments at home with their families, which is important in Vietnamese cultures. This paper sheds light on the preferences and practices of families and staff at the end-of-life with the longer-term goal of improving end-of-life care across Vietnam.

items.title: Pediatric Frostbite and Cold-Weather Injuries in the United States: A Multi-Database Retrospective Analysis.
items.abstract: Pediatric cold-weather injuries (frostbite and hypothermia) are uncommon but can lead to substantial morbidity, including amputation and long-term functional loss. National data on incidence, management, and outcomes are limited, particularly for fatalities outside healthcare settings. We conducted a retrospective analysis using three complementary data sources: an institutional registry at an American Burn Association-verified burn center (2018-2026), the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Readmission Database (NRD 2016-2021), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Storm Events Database (NOAA 2016-2023). Our institutional cohort included 16 patients (ages 1-17 years; 68.8% >13 years); treatments included rapid rewarming (43.8%), perfusion imaging (56.3%), thrombolytic therapy (18.8%), and hyperbaric oxygen therapy (31.3%). Two patients required amputation; both presented with hemorrhagic blisters, had delayed care, and did not receive thrombolytics. No thrombolytic-related complications were observed. Nationally, 2,155 pediatric cold weather injuries occurred; a national estimated hospitalization rate of 1.62 per 100,000. 79 pediatric frostbite admissions were identified, including 15 admissions designated as severe injury. NOAA data captured 16 pediatric deaths and 49 injuries across 30 states. Pediatric cold-weather injuries result in morbidity and mortality across diverse U.S. regions. Early aggressive management may reduce amputation and broader adoption of standardized protocols and public health prevention strategies are needed. Limitations of public health data emphasize the need for integrating diverse data sources to better understand the full impact of cold-weather injuries in the U.S.

items.title: IFT20 mediates trafficking of ciliary proteins to support mammalian motile ciliogenesis in testicular efferent ductules and respiratory tract.
items.abstract: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is essential for ciliary assembly and maintenance. IFT20, a component of the IFT-B complex, participates in cargo trafficking during primary cilium and sperm flagellum formation. However, its role in multiciliated cells (MCCs) remains unclear. Here, we investigated IFT20 function using mice with conditional deletion of Ift20 in FOXJ1-expressing cells. Most conditional knockout (cKO) mice survived to adulthood and exhibited reduced body weight without apparent left-right asymmetry defects or hydrocephalus. Adult cKO males were subfertile, with significantly shortened motile cilia and reduced ciliary beat frequency (CBF) in the efferent ductules (EDs). Ultrastructural analysis revealed abnormalities in peripheral doublet microtubules, inner and outer dynein arms, and the central pair apparatus. These defects were accompanied by ED luminal dilation and sperm aggregation, along with seminiferous tubule dilation, testicular atrophy, and increased germ cell degeneration. In contrast, tracheal cilia were only slightly shortened and exhibited reduced CBF without obvious ultrastructural abnormalities. Interestingly, immunofluorescence analysis revealed abnormal accumulation of the central apparatus proteins SPAG16 and SPAG17, outer dynein arm protein DNAI2, and inner dynein arm protein DNAH2 in the apical cytoplasm of ciliated cells in both EDs and trachea. Together, these findings demonstrate that IFT20 is critical for maintaining somatic motile cilia structure and function, with more pronounced defects in the EDs. The apical accumulation of axonemal proteins further suggests that IFT20 facilitates their trafficking from the cytoplasm into motile axonemes.

items.title: Sleep as a partial mediator of the association between residential greenness and biological ageing: A population-based study in China.
items.abstract: Residential greenness has been associated with healthier ageing, but its relationship with sleep behaviours and the role of sleep in this association remain unclear. This study examined associations among residential greenness, sleep indicators, and biological age in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. This population-based study included 8,527 Chinese adults aged 45 years and older. Residential greenness was assessed using city-level normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Sleep indicators included night-time sleep duration, nap duration, total sleep duration, and categorical sleep measures. Biological age was estimated from chronological age and eight blood-based or physiological biomarkers. Multivariable regression and mediation analyses were used to examine the associations and potential mediating role of sleep behaviours. Higher NDVI was associated with lower biological age, with each 0.1-unit increase linked to a 0.529-year reduction. Longer night-time sleep was associated with younger biological age, whereas longer nap duration was associated with older biological age. Higher NDVI was modestly associated with longer night-time sleep and shorter naps. Mediation analyses indicated that night-time sleep duration, nap duration, and long naps partially mediated the association between NDVI and biological age, accounting for 2.7%, 5.7%, and 3.3% of the total effect, respectively. Residential greenness was associated with younger biological age. Sleep behaviours may partly explain the link between greener environments and healthier biological ageing.

items.title: Structural basis of avian-to-human receptor-binding adaptation in H9Ny influenza A virus hemagglutinin.
items.abstract: The receptor-binding specificity of influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) is a major determinant for viral host tropism, enabling interspecies transmission. The molecular determinants for receptor-binding properties of HAs vary among different IAV subtypes. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis on the receptor-binding determinants of IAV subtype H9 HA and found that the receptor-binding characteristics of H9 subtype influenza viruses have exhibited temporal variations over decades. Q226L (hydrophobicity switch) substitution in the 220-loop is the key determinant for H9 subtype HA to acquire human receptor-binding preference. The amino acid residues of the 130-loop greatly affect the binding of HA protein to canonical receptors. Organoid infection models demonstrate that all three representative viral strains could infect human bronchial epithelial organoids. These findings increase our understanding of the molecular determinants of receptor-binding properties of different HA subtypes and call for the surveillance and response to potential influenza outbreaks, or even epidemics/pandemics.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) subtype H9 poses persistent zoonotic spillover risks due to its adaptive receptor-binding capacity, yet the molecular determinants remain incompletely defined. This study systematically characterizes the receptor-binding determinants of H9 hemagglutinin over decades of viral evolution and identifies two critical functional domains: the 220-loop residue Q226L substitution, which serves as the key mutation conferring human receptor-binding preference, and the 130-loop residues that predominantly modulate canonical receptor-binding affinity. Functional assays using human bronchial epithelial organoids further confirm the robust human infection ability of prevalent H9 viral strains. These findings clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying H9 IAV host tropism and adaptive evolution, provide critical theoretical evidence for targeted influenza surveillance and pandemic preparedness against emerging H9 influenza outbreaks.

items.title: Sheep or cattle fecal contamination? Using long-read amplicon sequencing for fecal source attribution and apportionment.
items.abstract: Fecal contamination of freshwater poses a risk to environmental and human health. Accurately attributing contamination to specific sources is critical for remediation. However, discriminating between closely related ruminants, sheep and cattle, remains a challenge. This study evaluated the use of f ast e xpectation m a ximization microbial s ource t racking (FEAST) and mitochondrial and microbial source tracking (MST) qPCR markers for fecal source identification. The focus was differentiation between cattle and sheep sources using a spiked laboratory experiment with known fecal inputs and field testing of samples from an agricultural stream. Sheep and cattle fecal samples were diluted into urban stream water, with spiked samples containing either single or mixed feces at varying ratios. Field samples were collected from a rural stream where adjacent sheep and cattle grazed. Full-length 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of spiked fecal and field samples was conducted, and the resulting taxonomies were used as input to FEAST; the results were also compared with those of MST analysis. Single cattle or sheep fecal sources could be identified by FEAST, but thresholds need to be established to avoid misattribution. FEAST results for field samples were consistent with ruminant and cattle MST markers, but the low sensitivity of cattle/sheep MST markers complicated comparisons. Using taxonomic groupings for FEAST analysis gave greater discrimination. However, apportionment of source contributions was not consistent within groupings. Inclusion of an aquatic source reduced misattribution of non-fecal microflora to animal sources. FEAST is a promising tool for source tracking but struggles to differentiate between mixed sources with similar fecal microflora and to produce accurate source apportionment.IMPORTANCEFecal contamination of freshwater is an issue for communities across the world because it has both environmental and health consequences. Therefore, differentiating between potential sources of contamination is important for both remediation and risk assessment. Microbes from fecal material are one of the main indicators used to track fecal contamination and identify its potential sources. In recent years, the use of the entire gut microflora to determine the origins of fecal contamination events has become a promising area of research and has the potential to overcome the low sensitivity of ruminant host-associated MST markers in field samples. The research demonstrated that an algorithm developed for this purpose could identify contamination from single sources. However, when applied to mixed-source scenarios, it struggled to differentiate between the similar microflora of livestock ruminants, cattle and sheep. Inclusion of an aquatic source was important for reducing misattribution of non-fecal microflora to animal sources.

items.title: The CD1d-iNKT Axis Modulates Allergic Responses to Alpha-Gal.
items.abstract: Background Amblyomma americanum (Aa or lone star tick) bites can induce alpha-gal syndrome (AGS)-allergic responses to mammal products linked to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose (alpha-gal or α-Gal)-specific (s)IgE. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells in AGS show increased CD4 + T cell-associated gene expression and expansion of CD1d-restricted invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells. Whether tick exposure activates these T cell subpopulations to promote α-Gal-sIgE and dietary α-Gal-specific hypersensitivity responses remains unclear. Methods We injected α-Gal-deficient (AGKO) mice on a C57BL/6J background with: (1) protein-rich Aa tick whole body extracts with or without anti-CD1d monoclonal antibody 19G11; (2) iNKT lipid activator α-galactosylceramide plus α-Gal glycoprotein (cetuximab) or (3) lipid-enriched Aa tick whole body extracts. We profiled circulating CD4 + T and/or iNKT cell subsets and measured serum cytokines and α-Gal-specific and total IgE and IgG1. We infested AGKO mice with adult Aa ticks to determine if AGS-associated tick bites altered CD4 + T and iNKT populations. We measured serum mast cell mediators after oral challenge with α-Gal-containing beef thyroglobulin to assess dietary α-Gal-induced mast cell activation. Results Tick extract injections induced α-Gal sIgG1, expanded circulating Th2 cells, promoted systemic type 2 (T2)-skewed cytokine responses, and primed for dietary alpha-gal-induced mast cell activation in AGKO mice. Activating iNKT cells with alpha-galactosylceramide concurrent with cutaneous α-Gal-glycoprotein injections, or with lipid-enriched tick extracts alone, induced α-Gal-sIgE. Disrupting CD1d-iNKT cell interactions blunted T2 cytokine-producing iNKT cell expansion induced by tick lipids; α-Gal-sIgE production; and α-Gal-induced mast cell activation. Importantly, infesting with adult Aa ticks increased circulating activated iNKT and Th2 cell frequencies and systemic IL-4, α-Gal sIgG1, and sIgE levels, priming mast cells for degranulation after dietary α-Gal challenge. Conclusions CD1d-iNKT cell interactions may enhance early T2 cytokine production induced by tick bite, supporting α-Gal sIgE production and amplifying α-gal-induced mast cell degranulation primed by tick-induced, systemic T2-skewing.

items.title: Partner Consultation to Inform Comparative Effectiveness Research on Frostbite Treatment: A Multi-Method Community Engagement Study.
items.abstract: Frostbite causes severe tissue injury frequently requiring amputation. Functional outcomes following frostbite injury are underreported, and no published literature describes a stakeholder-informed approach to frostbite research design incorporating patient, provider, or community perspectives. A multi-method stakeholder consultation was conducted to inform a Comparative Effectiveness Research (CER) grant proposal. The aim of this report is to share the community perspectives gathered during consultation, to support others designing frostbite research, and to demonstrate a replicable engagement process for rare, acute injury research. Sixteen participants were recruited through collaborative clinical sites, Healthcare for the Homeless, and the International Frostbite Resource Group. Eleven completed an online survey and eleven participated in virtual group meetings; persons with prior frostbite injury were offered optional 1:1 meetings. Survey data were analyzed descriptively; meeting transcripts were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. This report follows GRIPP2 and SRQR reporting guidelines. Reducing severe cases and amputations was the most endorsed outcome priority, though survivors identified cold sensitivity, fine motor function, grip strength, and return to activities as the outcomes with the greatest impact on daily life. Three qualitative themes emerged: barriers to care are multilayered and mutually reinforcing; patient-centered outcomes extend beyond amputation prevention; and important clinical questions and care needs remain unaddressed. This community partner consultation demonstrates that improving outcomes requires not only advances in treatment, but systems enabling timely access to care and addressing structural barriers for high-risk populations.

items.title: Periodontal Progression and Chronic-Condition Count in Older Adults: A Longitudinal Analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction Longitudinal evidence on whether periodontal progression is associated with chronic-condition count remains limited. This study investigated the longitudinal association between periodontal progression and chronic-condition count in older adults. Methods Data were obtained from the South Australian Dental Longitudinal Study (SADLS), a cohort study with up to 11 years of follow-up. Periodontal progression was defined as the proportion of sites exhibiting a ≥ 3 mm increase in clinical attachment loss (CAL) between baseline and the 5-year follow-up. Chronic-condition count was defined as the number of self-reported chronic conditions at each wave. A generalised estimating equation (GEE) with a Poisson distribution, a log link, and an exchangeable correlation was used to examine the association between periodontal progression and chronic-condition count. Models were adjusted for prior oral and chronic-condition count, socio-demographic factors, and behavioural factors. A sensitivity analysis using inverse probability-weighted GEE was conducted to account for loss to follow-up. Results Of 801 participants examined at baseline, 344 (42.9%) and 210 (26.2%) completed the 5-year and 11-year follow-ups, respectively. Periodontal progression was not associated with chronic-condition count across all three models, including the fully adjusted model (IRR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.89-1.08). The prevalence of cancers, osteoporosis, and cataracts increased over the 11-year follow-up, while the prevalence of several other chronic conditions declined over the same period. Conclusions In this selected dentate survivor cohort, periodontal progression, measured as CAL progression among retained teeth between baseline and 5 years, was not clearly associated with chronic-condition count at the 5-year and 11-year follow-ups, although the estimate was imprecise.

items.title: Incidence and risk factors of medical events in 1.4 million international leisure travellers.
items.abstract: Background Although health events during holidays are considered common, data on the number requiring care while overseas are scarce. This research aims to calculate the incidence and identify risk factors for medical events requiring professional assistance during international leisure travel of less than 365 days. Methods This retrospective observational study uses de-identified data from a large Australian travel insurer and medical assistance provider. Demographic and travel characteristics of insured travellers from 2018, 2019, 2022 and 2023 were supplied. Medical events counted were self-described unexpected illnesses, injuries or deaths, during the travel period, notified to the company whether or not a claim was made. We report descriptive characteristics, crude incidence, incidence rates and incidence risk ratios for all characteristics, before identifying significant independent risk factors with a multivariable Poisson regression model. Ad-hoc analysis of potential compounding effects was completed. Results 1,410,260 travellers were included. The median age was 38 years and median travel duration was 15 days. Medical events were notified at an overall cumulative incidence of 1.02%, a rate of 5.16 per 10,000 days of travel. Against a baseline of 0-17 years, destination New Zealand, the highest independent risk factors for medical events in this population were age over 65 years (aIRR=3.89, 95% CI 3.55-4.27, p 5 countries, and destinations in the Americas and Southern Asia. Conclusions Pre-travel discussion with leisure travellers from high-income countries should include the identified risk factors. All international leisure travellers should prepare a plan to access and pay for medical care, because at least 1 in 100 will require medical advice or support during their journey.

items.title: Understanding of Size and Scale and Order‐Of‐Magnitude Reasoning in Secondary Science: A Teaching Experiment With Worked Examples as Educational Scaffold
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding of size and scale (USS) and order‐of‐magnitude reasoning (OMR) are considered essential elements of scientific practice and literacy. This study combines intersecting strands of research to develop a rationale and conceptualization for OMR as an extension of USS from a broad body of research in science and math education. It also considers cognitive prerequisites essential for the development and mastery of USS and OMR. Based on this, the study presents an educational approach to enhance USS and OMR in high school science. Developing these abilities faces major barriers, involving complex procedural skills and strategies for coordinating multiple reasoning steps. Transfer of learning has also been found unsatisfactory in many studies. While there is work on individual activities that can improve this state of affairs, research on systematic approaches in full teaching sequences is scarce for USS and, to our knowledge, nonexistent for OMR. An educational approach for the acquisition of complex knowledge and development of strategies well investigated in the literature is worked examples (WEs). This strand of research found strong evidence for the usefulness of WEs in STEM education, in particular for supporting transfer. The quasi‐experimental repeated‐measurement investigation reported here compares a WE intervention group with a control group using conventional tasks (same content, lesson plan, and teacher). Conducted within regular high‐school science classrooms, the results reveal significant and practically relevant effects on students' procedural and conceptual knowledge regarding USS and OMR, including near and far transfer of learning.

items.title: Perceptual glimpses are locally accumulated and globally maintained at distinct processing levels
items.abstract: Making decisions often requires the integration of multiple pieces of information. An extensive body of research has investigated the neural architecture underpinning evidence accumulation in perceptual tasks where information is continuously present, but less is known about how this neural architecture operates in situations affording only intermittent glimpses of an evidence source. In two electroencephalography experiments, human participants judged the direction of up to two pulses of motion evidence separated by gaps of varying duration. Our behavioural analysis found that participants used both pulses but underutilised the second and showed no systematic decrease in accuracy as a function of gap duration. At the neural level, motor beta lateralisation tracked cumulative evidence across pulses, maintaining a sustained representation of the decision variable through the gap and until response. In contrast, the centroparietal positivity (CPP), a previously characterised signature of evidence accumulation, built up transiently to a peak that scaled with each pulse’s contribution to the decision variable (i.e. the absolute belief update it produced), falling back to baseline in between pulses. These patterns were recapitulated in a model where pulse-information transiently integrated at the CPP level is fed to and maintained at a bounded motor level. In this model, the evidence in the second pulse is only integrated to the extent that the evidence in the first pulse falls short of the bound, or not integrated at all if a bound has already been hit.

items.title: The characteristics of online gaming behaviors and psychosocial problems among Japanese adolescents: classification of gamers by latent profile analysis
items.abstract: Introduction This study aimed to investigate gaming disorder (GD) symptoms and psychosocial correlates among Japanese adolescents. It also sought to describe patterns of gaming behavior, depressive symptoms, and game-related social dysfunction using latent profile analysis (LPA). Methods A cross-sectional online questionnaire was administered to 9,699 adolescents aged 12–18 years (3,113 males and 6,586 females) recruited through a nationwide non-random panel between July and August 2022. Participants completed the Gaming Addiction Scale (GAS-7), Patient Health Questionnaire for Adolescents (PHQ-A), and five custom-developed items assessing game-related social difficulties. Additional variables included gaming time, in-game purchases, and demographic factors. Results A total of 2,093 participants (21.6%) screened positive using the GAS-7 criterion for probable GD; this was not a clinical diagnosis. Gaming duration, depressive symptoms, and reported difficulties were each associated with GAS-7 scores in this sample. Exploratory LPA among 8,015 adolescents reporting online gaming yielded nine descriptive groups. Some groups had similar gaming durations but differed in reported depressive symptoms and social difficulties. Discussion These findings describe heterogeneity in this online-panel sample. Representative, longitudinal, and experimental studies should assess generalizability and potential applications to prevention or harm reduction.

items.title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
items.abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

items.title: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
items.abstract: Undocumented and poorly known species spanning Linnean and Wallacean biodiversity shortfalls pose a major challenge to conservation due to the uncertainty they introduce. To address this, we developed a novel pluralistic approach that accounts for sampling gaps, spatial patterns, environmental associations, and varying conservation needs simultaneously, using amphibians as a case study. Using environment-based richness models and species accumulation curves (SACs), we identified areas with high biodiscovery needs for amphibians. These were concentrated primarily in humid tropical South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and East/Southeast Asia. While environmental models produced more reliable richness estimates than SACs overall, SAC-based estimates nonetheless added unique insights, especially in biodiverse, moderately well-sampled areas like Costa Rica and Panama. By integrating environmental models and SACs—thus leveraging combined strengths of previous approaches—our holistic scoring technique also proved consistent in estimating biodiscovery priorities across ecoregions, enabling robust recommendations for future sampling.

items.title: Methane and nitrous oxide concentrations and sea–air fluxes in western Long Island Sound, a eutrophic urban estuary: Hourly to seasonal variability
items.abstract: Western Long Island Sound is a seasonally hypoxic urban estuary undergoing anthropogenic change, which may influence concentrations and emissions of the potent greenhouse gases methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). To provide a benchmark of current gas distributions in this system, enabling detection of future changes and comparison with data from other estuaries worldwide, we obtained the first water column profiles of dissolved CH4 and N2O concentrations in western Long Island Sound. We collected samples at seven stations along an 18-km transect in August 2023, October 2023, and May 2024. CH4 concentrations and sea–air fluxes were highest in August (mean concentration of 101 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 154 μmol m−2 d−1) and lowest in May (mean concentration of 32 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 62 μmol m−2 d−1). Conversely, N2O concentrations and sea–air fluxes were highest in May (mean concentration of 12.0 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 4.8 μmol m−2 d−1) and lowest in August (mean concentration of 10.1 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 2.5 μmol m−2 d−1). Surface concentrations and sea–air fluxes of CH4 and N2O were highest at the westernmost station (closest to New York City) in all three seasons, suggesting that there is a persistent source of surface water to western Long Island Sound with high concentrations of CH4 and N2O. To investigate short-term variability in CH4, N2O, and oxygen (O2), we collected samples every 4 h over 28 h at the middle station of the transect, in all three months. We concluded that there is measurable short-term variability in all three gases, and that the drivers of variability in these dissolved gases are complex and not dominated by tidal advection or light levels alone.

items.title: Plasticity promotes persistence and evolution in novel environments
items.abstract: Abstract Phenotypic plasticity––the ability of organisms to adjust their traits in response to changes in their environment––has long been thought to prevent extinction in novel or changing environments. However, there are few tests linking plasticity to population persistence. Here, we show that plasticity promotes population persistence in replicate populations of rotifers. We experimentally exposed 33 clonal lines that varied in plasticity to over 20 novel environments for up to 40 overlapping generations. We found that clonal populations expressing plasticity in morphology and life history traits persisted longer and were less likely to go extinct in novel environments than populations not expressing such plasticity. These results directly link plasticity to population persistence in novel environments and suggest that plasticity can buy time for organisms in a changing world. Teaser A multigenerational experiment finds that environmentally induced traits allow populations to persist in novel environments.

items.title: Effects of Littoral Habitat Complexity on Trophic Structure
items.abstract: Abstract The functional importance of habitat complexity and heterogeneity has wide-ranging implications for the restoration and protection of wetland habitats. The loss of littoral complexity due to shoreline modifications, water level fluctuations or invasive species may have negative consequences not only for biodiversity but also for ecosystem processes; however, little is known about the role of macrophyte complexity and bathymetric heterogeneity in supporting diverse food webs. To address this knowledge gap, we used stable isotopes to characterize the trophic niche of macroinvertebrate predators across a gradient of macrophyte complexity. Our results show a wide range in individual isotopic signatures within what is commonly averaged as one minor trophic level of macroinvertebrate predators. Trophic position had a complex relationship with habitat attributes, but was not strongly correlated with macrophyte canopy cover, and deep and shallow vegetated areas only a few meters apart had distinctly different integrated food webs based on predator isotopic niches. Maximum trophic position and predator niche overlaps were not correlated with the coarse measures of habitat complexity, potentially because of the truncated complexity gradient due to the lack of predators in the lowest-complexity habitats. These findings underscore the need to consider more individuals to capture the intra-guild variation in food web studies and are potentially transformative for interpreting food​ webs constructed with the commonly used replication of three samples per guild (or major habitat). This study can also inform the design of future research aimed at advancing functional assessments of complex habitats increasingly threatened by anthropogenic stress.

items.title: Resiliomics: a systems-level and genetic framework for quantifying biological resilience
items.abstract: Biological systems are continuously exposed to internal and external perturbations, yet they maintain functionality through complex adaptive and regulatory mechanisms. While conventional omics approaches have substantially advanced our understanding of molecular responses to stress, they predominantly capture static states or peak responses, overlooking the dynamic processes governing recovery and long-term system stability. Here, we introduce resiliomics, a conceptual omics framework dedicated to the quantitative characterization of biological resilience. Resiliomics integrates time-resolved multi-omics data with systems biology and network-based approaches to quantify key parameters, including recovery kinetics, perturbation amplitude, and system robustness. Importantly, resiliomics incorporates genetic determinants of resilience, including gene regulatory mechanisms, genetic variation, and genotype-phenotype relationships, which shape system responses and recovery trajectories across biological contexts. By shifting the focus from response-centric to recovery-centric analyses, this framework enables the investigation of dynamic trajectories underlying adaptation and stability. Resiliomics provides a unifying perspective that bridges molecular biology, ecology, and engineering principles of resilience, offering new opportunities for predictive modeling and integrative analyses across biological scales. This approach has broad implications for understanding stress tolerance, disease dynamics, and ecosystem stability in a rapidly changing environment.

items.title: Sheep grazing within regenerative perennial systems accelerates soil carbon and nitrogen accrual
items.abstract: Abstract Background Global agricultural intensification and crop-livestock decoupling have reduced soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, weakening terrestrial carbon sinks and altering nutrient cycling. Integrating livestock into cropping systems is a cornerstone regenerative practice, with the potential to enhance carbon and nitrogen storage. However, on-farm research quantifying outcomes of stacked regenerative production models remains limited, and it is unclear how grazing, alone or combined with other practices, affects soil carbon and nitrogen accrual. We assessed carbon and nitrogen stocks (0–60 cm), including mineral-associated and particulate organic matter pools, microbial biomass and plant productivity across 49 California (USA) vineyards spanning conventional to regenerative management, with and without sheep grazing. We evaluated the relative contributions of management practices to carbon and nitrogen pools, accounting for spatial and edaphic predictors, and estimated accrual rates from vineyards with differing management histories (space-for-time substitution). Results Grazing emerged as the most influential management practice for increasing soil organic matter pool stocks, followed by reduced physical disturbance and permanent ground cover. Other regenerative practices, including organic amendments and avoidance of synthetic insecticides, showed positive but more variable associations with soil organic matter pool stocks. Grazing was strongly associated with approximately fivefold higher nitrogen accrual rates (+ 0.04 ± 0.01 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), including plant-available nitrogen (+ 0.94 ± 0.30 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), and more than threefold higher soil carbon accrual within regenerative management systems relative to conventional ungrazed systems (+ 0.38 ± 0.13 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹). Grazing was also associated with greater microbial biomass and plant productivity, consistent with enhanced carbon and nitrogen cycling. Conclusions Under grazing, greater nitrogen availability and more robust plant and microbial communities likely reduced microbial nitrogen limitation while enhancing carbon sequestration and stabilization. Geography and edaphic properties constrained soil carbon and nitrogen accumulation. These patterns proved robust across geographically independent farms, highlighting the value of multi-farm datasets for climate-mitigation assessments. These results demonstrate that integrating grazing within regenerative perennial systems can help meet mitigation targets while building nitrogen stocks and reducing synthetic fertilizer reliance. This underscores the importance of research on commercial operations for translating site-specific results into scalable, climate-smart farming strategies.

items.title: Plastic pollution reshapes snail intermediate host life history: implications for schistosomiasis transmission
items.abstract: Abstract Background Plastic debris is increasingly recognized as an ecological driver of mosquito-borne disease by creating freshwater breeding habitat, yet its consequences for snail hosts of human schistosomiasis transmission remain poorly understood. For these snail hosts, including Bulinus truncatus , plastic pollution may alter population dynamics by modifying life-history processes through surface biofilm-derived nutritional subsidies, habitat alteration, and toxicity-induced reproductive trade-offs. Methods We performed two laboratory experiments testing the effects of macro- and microplastics, individually and jointly, on B. truncatus’ life-history traits (survival, growth, egg mass production, and hatching) by using environmentally realistic sizes, polymers, concentrations, and biofouling status. To assess the potential demographic consequences of plastic pollution, we derived a measure of reproductive output under each plastic treatment, i.e., the expected number of cumulative viable offspring produced over the experiment. Results We found that macroplastic and its ecological changes boosted somatic growth, egg mass production, and hatching, consistently playing the most critical role in the demographic increase driven by observed biofilm-derived nutritional subsidies. Microplastics improved survival but had an overall undetectable effect on its expected reproductive output. Combined exposure elevated egg mass production and resulted in an increase in expected reproductive output comparable to biofouling macroplastic alone. Collectively, these results suggest that plastic and its ecological changes may shift snail population growth by altering life-history processes that scale to net reproductive output, with biofouling emerging as the primary driver of demographic response. Conclusions In laboratory experiments, macroplastic pollution increases B. truncatus expected reproductive output by altering key life-history traits. While schistosome infection and cercarial production were not measured in this experiment, these life history changes may translate into population growth, which prior work has linked to greater cercarial production with critical implications for human transmission risk. These findings identify plastic pollution as a previously unrecognized pathway and demonstrate that ecological transformation of plastic debris is the dominant determinant of host demographic response with potential implications for integrating environmental management into disease control strategies.

items.title: What two decades of environmental-economic accounting reveal about Guatemala's natural capital and governance
items.abstract: Guatemala is one of the few developing countries to have kept the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) running for more than two decades without interruption. This paper draws together what those two decades produced and what the experience teaches in terms of empirical findings and governance lessons, including the conditions in which SEEA informs policy in a developing country context. The SEEA revealed how much the economy depends on natural capital that conventional statistics fail to capture. Most indicators show that Guatemala has consumed its natural asset base rather than rebuilding it. The paper describes how a long partnership between government and academia turned these accounts into official statistics and put them to work in national planning and forest governance. Four conditions stand out as necessary for natural capital accounts to shape policy in a developing country: (i) the need for a stable institutional anchoring, (ii) a clear demand from live policy questions, (iii) a gradual build-up from simpler to more complex accounts, and (iv) capacity building within the institutions that produce the accounts. This path led the Central Bank of Guatemala to create a permanent environmental accounting unit inside its macroeconomic statistics department. Accounts will be published annually with a fully funded program within the Bank.

items.title: Charting the insect biodiversity of southern-central Crete: Insights from a pilot metabarcoding survey
items.abstract: Among eukaryotes, insects are by far the most diverse organisms on Earth, yet their global decline threatens ecosystem stability. Understanding local and regional biodiversity patterns is critical for conservation planning, ecosystem management, and predicting responses to environmental change, but traditional surveys for assessing insect diversity (e.g., manual collection, morphological identification, and counting) are highly labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often require rare or simply unavailable dedicated taxonomic expertise. DNA metabarcoding offers an efficient, high-resolution alternative to assess insect communities. Here, we report on the first insect metabarcoding survey on Crete, spanning two sampling periods (2021–2022 and 2022–2023) from a small area in Southern Central Crete in the context of a citizen science project. Samples collected during the two sampling periods were processed using different laboratory workflows, and the resulting datasets are therefore interpreted independently rather than as directly comparable datasets. A total of 29 samples yielded 10,865 Exact Sequence Variants (ESVs), 10,516 of which were assigned to insects, covering 988 species, 900 genera, and 227 families across 14 orders. A comparison with the existing observation records reveals 406 candidate new occurrence records and a rough approximation of 690 unclassified species, indicating substantial unresolved molecular diversity. Our results demonstrate that even small-scale sampling can unravel substantial insect diversity and highlight critical gaps in barcode reference databases. Our study demonstrates how DNA metabarcoding can accelerate biodiversity monitoring in understudied regions.

items.title: When does modelling dependence change the interpretation of biodiversity indicators?
items.abstract: Abstract Recent biodiversity trend analyses have modelled uncertainty arising from temporal, spatial and phylogenetic dependence. For primarily descriptive indicators such as the Living Planet Indices (LPIs) however, a prior question is whether dependence modelling improves estimation of a fixed quantity or actually changes the quantity being reported. Using the high‐profile case of Johnson et al., the current paper argues that covariance‐rich hierarchical models can make the relationship between a reported model coefficient and an intended estimand ambiguous. When aggregate trends are estimated from common coefficients in latent models with structured covariance, observations contribute unequal independent information to the estimator through assumed redundancy among related units. The reported collective trend is then a model‐based coefficient (e.g. a mean over a latent‐effect distribution) shaped by partial pooling and dependence; this is not automatically an average under declared estimand or ‘aggregation’ weights that indicator trend users may assume. A further ambiguity is whether the reported coefficient summarises the analysed sample or supports claims about a broader spatial, taxonomic or other policy‐relevant domain. One defensible reply, that the model is merely a more efficient estimator of a sample average, requires explicit statement of the estimand, weighting scheme, relationship between the model output and that estimand, and evidence of performance for that target; predictive success alone is not sufficient for this descriptive claim. Claims concerning broader generalisability require accompanying risk‐of‐bias assessments where evaluation against the true target (e.g. a time trend in some facet of global biodiversity) is unobtainable. The implication is that covariance‐rich hierarchical indicator analyses should state the estimand, the role of dependence modelling, missing data assumptions and domain of inference clearly before interpreting the resulting trend for scientific or policy applications.

items.title: MacroTraits: a global trait data and information system for marine benthic ecology
items.abstract: For a long time, biological trait data have been a bottleneck in biodiversity research. Constraints of data unavailability and challenging analytical implementation are still obstacles to the investigation of functional biodiversity patterns. This is especially true in marine zoobenthic ecology where the use of biological traits became common much later than in terrestrial and freshwater ecology. Additionally, most of trait-based marine studies have dominantly been conducted in European waters while large gaps remain in other areas of the world. Therefore, this paper offers a framework to fill this gap by providing the most comprehensive zoobenthic trait data compilation at the global scale. Based on more than 8000 references, 1893 species of marine macro- and megazoobenthos are fully documented for life history, dwelling mode, ecosystem function, habitat and biogeography through 41 traits. Next to this compilation, the paper brings clarifications on research directions by means of these data within the dominant paradigms of modern ecology. In particular, the dichotomous expression that contrasts response and effect traits (i.e. fitness components versus ecosystem function) is emphasised. The database is accessible through an R package in the repository https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24318255 (Beauchard and Soetaert, 2026b) and that facilitates data treatment such as trait selection, cross table construction and label handling.

items.title: 寄生虫对宿主的适应性操纵：从现象到因果框架
items.abstract: Parasite-induced alterations in host phenotypes are widespread across diverse taxa, yet their evolutionary significance remains difficult to establish. A central challenge in this field is not the scarcity of examples, but distinguishing adaptive parasite manipulation from host responses to infection or incidental pathological consequences. The adaptive manipulation hypothesis proposes that parasites modify host traits in ways that increase transmission or reproductive success, but empirical evidence for this interpretation remains largely correlative, with few studies establishing a direct causal relationship between altered host phenotypes and parasite fitness. In this review, we critically examine the evidence for adaptive host manipulation and develop a framework for distinguishing parasite adaptations from alternative explanations. We identify four criteria for evaluating putative manipulation: stage-specific temporal alignment, independence from host compensatory responses, demonstration of a net parasite fitness advantage, and evidence of mechanistic causality. These criteria provide a hierarchical basis for assessing the strength of evidence across host-parasite systems. Applying this framework to widely cited examples reveals that several canonical cases lack sufficient evidence to establish adaptive manipulation. We further examine the molecular processes implicated in host phenotypic modification, including neural interference, immune modulation, endocrine disruption, and gene regulatory changes, highlighting the limited functional evidence linking these processes to parasite-induced phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose an integrated research strategy combining spatially and temporally resolved transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, and targeted functional perturbations, to establish causal links among molecular mechanisms, host phenotypic changes, and parasite fitness. By emphasizing causal evidence rather than descriptive associations, this review provides a conceptual and methodological framework for critically evaluating adaptive host manipulation and clarifying its evolutionary significance in host-parasite interactions.

items.title: Vegetation cover shapes community structure and metabolic genetic potential of high-alpine soil microbiomes
items.abstract: Abstract Background Alpine permafrost-affected soils, particularly in the European Alps, remain poorly understood despite rapid warming and projected vegetation increase at higher elevations. We investigated how vegetation cover and physicochemical soil properties structure microbial communities across ten high-altitude alpine permafrost-affected sites. Results Soil parameters (pH, soil water content, temperature, and total C and N contents) varied significantly between sites and revealed pH and C: N ratio as key drivers modulated by vegetation cover, highlighting its indirect role in shaping soil environments. Microbial community composition differed significantly across sites, and functional gene profiles mirrored taxonomic patterns, indicating strong coupling between community structure and functional gene potential, with reduced functional redundancy. Microbial abundance increased with vegetation cover, whereas taxonomic and functional gene diversity plateaued at intermediate vegetation cover, suggesting that the presence of vegetation primarily enhances microbial abundance rather than diversity. Genome-resolved metagenomics revealed a shift from generalist-dominated communities in barren soils to increased prevalence of specialist taxa in vegetated soils. Functional gene abundances, particularly for C cycling, were higher in vegetated soils, while N and S cycling gene potentials were associated with soil temperature and water content. A microcosm experiment measuring ex situ CO₂ and CH₄ fluxes from incubated summer soils, identified vegetated soils as modest CO₂ sources. Vegetated soils exhibited lower, pH and C: N ratio, shaping a more abundant microbial community with more specialist members and higher C cycling gene potential. Conclusion Overall, our findings indicate that alpine greening is associated with microbial community turn-over via vegetation-mediated changes in soil properties, with implications for biogeochemical cycling and C emissions under climate warming.

items.title: Social processes as drivers for empowerment of sustainable fisheries management on Åland
items.abstract: Engagement of local communities and policy coherence across different sectors are essential to ensure that no one is left behind in the green transition. Coastal communities face many challenges that are difficult to adapt to, including those associated with blue growth. In this article, outcomes from two Horizon Europe projects were used to explore barriers to applying the Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principle. A policy coherence framework was applied to assess the level of coherence between policies identified to create conflicts and disempowerment in an Eastern Limassol case study. The coastal community is industrialised yet still supports a diversity of habitats and endangered species. The region is subject to multiple, overlapping EU policy streams, creating policy incoherence and local tensions. The article highlights the blue economy as a paradigm that inevitably will lead to conflicts between ecological, social, and economic priorities, and how the LNOB principle can be essential in bringing these together in a holistic approach. However, there are several limitations to the principle’s applicability in the current policy landscape. The main mechanism for equitable transition in the blue economy, the Just Transition, is not applicable under many circumstances, leaving no strict legal framework for implementation of equity and equality in the transition of coastal areas. The mainstream understanding of the blue economy is still dominated by the hope of win-win-win scenarios with limited transparency about the trade-offs and conflicts at stake, and few mechanisms that offer legal consequences.

items.title: Wild edible greens heritage in western Crete and across Greek islands: does it follow the flora or the tilled field?
items.abstract: Chorta (wild greens gathered and eaten as cooked or raw vegetables) is one of the most distinctive and resilient elements of the Greek, and particularly Cretan, Mediterranean Diet. However, the associated local ecological knowledge (LEK) is under increasing pressure across Greece. We report an ethnobotanical survey conducted in May 2026 in seven villages and at the weekly farmers’ market of the Chania prefecture (western Crete), documenting 37 botanical taxa used as wild vegetables by local communities, and we ask whether differences in Chorta knowledge across Greek islands follow the richness of the flora or the persistence of small-scale farming. Twenty-five study participants (15 women and 10 men, aged 34–79 years), chiefly rural farmers, shepherds and elderly women, were recruited through exponential discriminative snowball sampling and interviewed. The new data were set beside seven datasets recorded by our research group between 2022 and 2026 with the same field protocol: central Crete, the Lasithi Plateau (eastern Crete), Ikaria, Olympos (Karpathos), Corfu, Syros and Kasos. LEK richness was measured as the number of wild-vegetable genera quoted by at least 10% of participants, and was related, through rank correlations, to the share of the employed population working in agriculture, forestry and fishing recorded in the 2021 and 2011 censuses of the Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT), and to the number of native vascular taxa on each island. In Chania, Asteraceae dominated the repertoire, 19 genera were quoted by at least 10% of participants, and 21 of the 37 taxa were also sold at the market; the young flowering shoots of Hypochaeris radicata , eaten like wild asparagus, stood out as a local speciality. Across the eight units, LEK richness showed a positive but statistically non-significant association with agricultural employment (Spearman ρ = 0.52, p = 0.18) and a weaker one with native flora richness (ρ = 0.37, p = 0.47). Kasos was the clearest exception: the census attributes 17% of its employed residents to the primary sector, yet only eight wild-vegetable genera are still known there, and during fieldwork we counted five vegetable gardens on the whole island. The data do not support the idea that Chorta knowledge simply mirrors floristic diversity, and they are consistent with, though they cannot prove, the view that it is sustained by everyday work on tilled ground. Since most Chorta taxa are weeds of fields, gardens and terraces, what seems to matter is not agricultural employment as counted by the census but the actual cultivation of small plots. Safeguarding this biocultural heritage therefore means supporting small-scale, diversified farming together with the household and market settings in which knowledge of wild greens is learnt and handed on. items.title: Uso de GeoAI e Sensoriamento Remoto Multimodal no Monitoramento da Biodiversidade Amazônica: Uma Revisão Sistemática
items.abstract: A Amazônia desempenha papel fundamental na manutenção da biodiversidade global e na regulação climática, porém sofre crescentes pressões relacionadas ao desmatamento, degradação florestal e mudanças no uso da terra. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura científica sobre aplicações de GeoAI, sensoriamento remoto multimodal e inteligência artificial no monitoramento da biodiversidade amazônica. A revisão foi conduzida conforme as recomendações do protocolo PRISMA 2020, com buscas realizadas nas bases Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PubMed e IEEE Xplore. Após aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão, 35 estudos foram selecionados para análise. Os resultados evidenciaram predominância de aplicações voltadas ao monitoramento de desmatamento, biomassa, degradação florestal e estrutura da vegetação, utilizando principalmente redes neurais convolucionais, aprendizado profundo e integração entre sensores ópticos, LiDAR, SAR e drones/UAS. Observou-se crescimento expressivo das publicações após 2020, associado à ampliação de abordagens multimodais e plataformas geoespaciais em nuvem. Os estudos demonstraram elevado desempenho analítico na detecção de padrões ambientais complexos, embora persistam limitações relacionadas à heterogeneidade metodológica, disponibilidade de dados rotulados e validação externa dos modelos. Conclui-se que a GeoAI apresenta elevado potencial estratégico para fortalecer o monitoramento ambiental amazônico e subsidiar ações de conservação, manejo florestal e planejamento territorial.
