items.title: Baseline Diurnal Activity and Seasonal Patterns of the Critically Endangered Tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis Heude 1888) and Co-occurring Mammals in a Strict Protection Zone
items.abstract: Mammal activities are influenced by temperature and foraging opportunities particularly in the tropics which highlights the importance of understanding diel patterns and seasonal variations for evidence-based conservation. However, in the Philippines, behavioral studies on mammals remain scarce particularly for the critically endangered tamaraw Bubalus mindorensis (Heude, 1888). Hence, a targeted camera trap survey was conducted in the Tamaraw Strict Protection Zone of Mts. Iglit-Baco Natural Park to provide baseline information for the species. From the survey, a total of five medium-large sized mammal species (B. mindorensis, Sus oliveri Groves, 1997, Rusa marianna [Desmarest, 1822], Macaca fascicularis [Raffles, 1821], Viverra tangalunga (Gray, 1832) were captured across 3,556 camera trapping days from March 2016 to October 2018. Among the mammals, B. mindorensis, R. marianna and M. fascicularis were the most frequently detected species (>100). Among these, only M. fascicularis was observed to exhibit seasonal variations in detections (p = 0.026). Furthermore, observations reveal a predominantly diurnal pattern for the tamaraw, likely as foraging adaptations in a strictly protected habitat. These findings provide crucial baseline information for the conservation and monitoring of threatened Philippine mammals.

items.title: Green Global Value Chains for Sustainable Development: Environmental Upgrading in a Fragmented Spatial Economy
items.abstract: In a world facing environmental transformation, mobilising the capital, skills, and knowledge required for decarbonisation and wider sustainability remains a formidable challenge. We argue that Green Global Value Chains (GGVCs)-and the Green Foreign Direct Investment (GFDI) that helps to build and reconfigure them-are central to this shift and can support sustainable development across a fragmented spatial economy. We advance the concept of environmental upgrading, showing how participation in GGVCs can move firms, regions, and countries towards cleaner production and higher-value activities while reshaping natural capital. This work has three aims. First, it offers a unified conceptual perspective on how GVCs shape environmental and development outcomes, introducing the Green Smile Curve and a typology of green, brown, and ordinary value chains. Second, it provides new empirical evidence on the geography of GFDI. Third, it proposes a GGVCs-sensitive policy framework-centred on building, embedding, and reshaping value chains-to help governments leverage GGVCs. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

items.title: Vegetational diversity and dissimilarity shape the diversity and composition of tree-dwelling spiders in post-mining regeneration sites in Eastern Amazon
items.abstract: Abstract Ecological restoration in tropical forests is critical for recovering biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, particularly in landscapes degraded by intensive activities such as mining. Clarifying the relationships between plant community attributes and fauna reassembly is important for understanding regeneration processes in early successional stages. We evaluated how plant abundance, species richness, and compositional dissimilarity relate to the diversity and composition of arboreal spider assemblages in post-mining regeneration sites in the Eastern Amazon. Sampling was conducted across 14 sites, including seven five-year-old regeneration areas and seven forest remnants. Plant communities were characterised by abundance and species richness, and spiders were collected using canopy beating (2562 sampling events). We applied generalised linear models, PERMANOVA, and Mantel tests to assess diversity patterns and biotic tracking. A total of 2304 spider specimens representing 136 species were recorded. Forest remnants supported higher spider species richness and adult abundance per plant than regeneration sites. After accounting for sampling effort, plant abundance was not associated with spider abundance, whereas plant species richness was positively associated with total spider abundance per plant and with most diversity metrics, and was the only predictor associated with variation in species composition. Beta-diversity analyses revealed a positive correlation between plant and spider compositional dissimilarity, indicating that spatial variation in plant community is associated with turnover in spider assemblages. Plant species richness was associated not only with spider species richness but also with variation in spider assemblage composition. Restoration strategies may benefit from prioritising plant species richness to support diverse spider assemblages.

items.title: Strong meiofaunal differentiation despite weak links to vegetation patch structure in emerging dunes
items.abstract: Abstract Context Landscape studies often assume that visible habitat patches correspond to meaningful biological units, but this need not be the case. Young coastal dunes provide a useful test because pioneer vegetation forms discrete patches that contribute directly to dune development. Objectives We asked whether meiofaunal biodiversity follows this vegetation-defined landscape structure, and whether spatial patterns are consistent across major taxonomic groups. Methods We surveyed meiofaunal assemblages in standardized samples from 137 dune-grass patches across four geographically separated dune fields along the Dutch North Sea coast. We related local richness and community composition to patch area, vegetation-based connectivity, broader spatial context and measured habitat conditions. We also quantified how diversity accumulated across patches and dune fields and partitioned compositional differentiation into turnover and nestedness. Results Patch area and the surrounding vegetation network explained little additional variation in richness or community composition once broader spatial context and measured habitat conditions were accounted for. This result was similar across connectivity decay distances of 5–25 m. Broader spatial context was more strongly associated with community composition, particularly differences among dune fields. Assemblages nevertheless differed strongly among individual patches, and sampling additional patches and dune fields recovered substantial additional richness. Most compositional differentiation reflected taxon turnover. Annelids, arachnids and collembolans broadly followed the whole-community pattern, while nematodes showed weaker spatial structuring and collembolans a somewhat stronger association with the surrounding patch network. Conclusions Vegetation configuration is important for dune development, but corresponds only weakly to the spatial organization of sediment faunal diversity. The same landscape can therefore be structured differently by different ecological processes.

items.title: Shared traits underlie prehistoric bird extinctions on continents and islands
items.abstract: Vertebrate extinctions are one of the earliest and most conspicuous examples of human-driven environmental change. On continents, large mammals were the most obvious casualties, but many continental bird species went extinct during the same period. A far greater number of island birds disappeared as humans spread to more isolated landmasses. In this study, we analysed patterns in the traits of continental and island birds to determine the factors that influenced the incidence of extinction in both groups. To this end, we used a dataset of traits for 10 165 extant and 426 extinct (prehistoric) birds. Using phylogenetic regression, we determined that birds were more likely to go extinct if they had a large body mass, lived in areas with high extinction rates for megafauna or were scavengers. For island birds, extinction rate was also much higher among flightless species and, unexpectedly, for less morphologically unique birds. Given that the underlying traits that had the greatest effect on extinction patterns in both groups were similar between continental and island systems, we propose that the drivers of extinction patterns were also similar despite much higher extinction rates on islands.

items.title: Regional endemic species in conservation planning: a multi-taxon assessment of spatial priorities and protected-area gaps
items.abstract: Abstract Endemic species represent a distinctive component of biodiversity because their known distributions are geographically restricted. When endemicity is defined at the scale of an administrative territory with direct responsibilities for biodiversity conservation, identifying and conserving these species becomes particularly relevant for regional conservation planning. However, endemic species are often assessed within individual taxonomic groups, limiting the extent to which their overall contribution to regional biodiversity can be evaluated. Here, we provide a multi-taxon assessment of the endemic biota of the Region of Murcia, southeastern Spain, and evaluate its representation within the regional protected-area network. We compiled information for 47 taxa considered endemic to Murcia and retained 34 consolidated endemic taxa representing different taxonomic groups. Using a 5 × 5 km grid, we quantified endemic species richness and spatial rarity, identified the upper 5% of grid cells as endemism hotspots, and assessed their representation within protected areas. Endemic richness was strongly concentrated in southeastern Murcia, particularly in coastal and pre-coastal sectors. Twenty-six endemism hotspots were identified, six of which had less than 10% protected-area coverage. At the species level, nine endemic taxa had none of their known localities within protected areas, whereas eight were represented at all known localities. Our results show that even relatively small Mediterranean regions can harbour a spatially concentrated diversity of endemic taxa across multiple taxonomic groups, while important gaps remain in their representation within existing protected-area networks. Aligning the biogeographical scale at which endemicity is assessed with the governance scale at which conservation is implemented can therefore help translate geographical restriction into concrete conservation priorities and strengthen the capacity of biodiversity planning to safeguard geographically restricted taxa.

items.title: Taxonomic and functional reorganization of terrestrial mammal communities under anthropogenic influence in a tropical forest
items.abstract: Protected areas and national legislation are important tools for conserving biodiversity and maintaining ecosystem services. In Brazil, the 2012 Native Vegetation Protection Law no. 12.651, of 25 May 2012 requires rural landowners in the Amazon to maintain at least 80% of each property under native vegetation as legal reserves (LRs), including within settlement projects. We compared mammal community structure and trait-based responses between human-occupied LRs and a continuous protected forest (CPF) in the central Amazon. Using camera-traps, we assessed species richness, relative abundance, taxonomic composition, functional traits and ecological attributes in relation to anthropogenic variables. RLQ and fourth-corner analyses revealed similar species richness, but different taxonomic composition and relative abundance patterns between protection types. Herbivores and subsistence-hunted species were associated with the CPF, whereas carnivores, retaliation-hunted species and mammals with large home ranges were linked to LRs. Within LRs, relative abundance increased with forest cover and distance to water but declined farther from roads; in the CPF, species richness increased with distance to roads, while LR mammal communities exhibited compositional reorganization under multiple anthropogenic pressures. These findings indicate that LRs, despite being embedded in human-altered landscapes, can support diverse mammal assemblages and play a complementary role in biodiversity conservation.

items.title: Land use transitions and their impacts on carbon storage in the Yellow River Basin under different scenarios
items.abstract: Abstract Terrestrial carbon sequestration capacity is closely tied to land use patterns, with different land cover types exerting distinct effects on carbon pools. Strategic optimization of land use configurations offers a viable pathway to enhance ecosystem carbon storage (CS). This study focuses on three representative Yellow River Basin (YRB) segments, namely the Shanxi (Shanxi section of the Yellow River Basin, SYRB), Gansu (Gansu section of the Yellow River Basin, GYRB), and Shandong (Shandong section of the Yellow River Basin, SDYRB) sections, using an integrated PLUS‑InVEST approach with dynamic carbon density estimation to evaluate land use effects on CS from 2005 to 2023 and project 2035 trajectories under alternative scenarios. Results reveal: (1) CS increased by 0.85% in SYRB and 0.91% in GYRB from 2005 to 2023, while declining by 4.55% in SDYRB due to construction land expansion; changes in grassland and forest land (FL) were the primary drivers. (2) Multi‑scenario 2035 simulations show divergent optimal pathways: SYRB peaks under Urban Organic Renewal Scenario (UORS) (1.277 × 10⁹ t) and Territorial Spatial Planning Scenario (TSPS) (1.276 × 10⁹ t); GYRB under TSPS (2.379 × 10⁹ t), with Ecological Protection Scenario (EPS) lowest (2.343 × 10⁹ t); SDYRB under TSPS (0.99 × 10⁹ t), EPS worst (0.944 × 10⁹ t). Thus, differentiated policies are needed: SYRB requires coordinated urban renewal and spatial planning; GYRB needs TSPS‑oriented grassland management and unused land restoration; SDYRB should adopt TSPS to balance urbanization and cultivated land (CL) protection. (3) Driving mechanisms differ regionally: SYRB’s CL‑to‑forest gains are partially offset by energy development; GYRB faces precipitation decline and overgrazing, requiring ecological migration and grassland restoration; SDYRB must reconcile urbanization with agricultural intensification via a CL‑wetland system and improved compensation. We recommend differentiated “Three Zones and Three Lines” spatial controls, with SDYRB strictly protecting CL, GYRB restoring unused land, and SYRB coordinating forest conversion with new energy development, to jointly enhance YRB carbon sink function. This study provides theoretical support for ecological conservation in the Yellow River Basin.

items.title: UAV-based blow microbiome profiling reveals core respiratory signatures in wild bottlenose dolphins
items.abstract: Non-invasive approaches are increasingly important for monitoring wild cetaceans, particularly vulnerable populations inhabiting anthropogenically impacted ecosystems. Respiratory-associated microbial communities may provide insights into host health and interactions with the environment. This study aimed to characterize the blow microbiome of free-ranging bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncates ) from the Gulf of Ambracia, Greece, using uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), while assessing the influence of sampling matrices and environmental microbial signatures. Blow was collected during 27 sampling events using three collection and preservation matrices: DNA/RNA Shield, QIAcard FTA cards, and dry cellulose sponges. Seawater and air controls were used to identify and reduce environmental microbial contributions. Dry sponges yielded distinct, compositionally biased bacterial communities dominated by Sphingomonadales and Pseudomonadales and were therefore excluded from subsequent analyses. FTA cards and DNA/RNA Shield recovered broadly overlapping microbial profiles, although compositional differences remained detectable. Following environmental filtering, a limited number of recurrent core taxa accounted for a substantial proportion of the blow microbiome. These taxa mainly belonged to Bacteroidota, Proteobacteria/Pseudomonadota, and Actinobacteriota, including Flavobacteriales, Burkholderiales, Pseudomonadales, Rhizobiales, Alteromonadales, and Micrococcales. Predicted functional profiles highlighted pathways associated with central metabolism, biosynthesis, transport, environmental sensing, and bacterial interactions. Exploratory screening also identified potentially pathogenic or opportunistic bacterial signatures, generally at low relative abundance. Overall, this study identifies suitable approaches for UAV-based blow microbiome sampling and establishes an initial population-specific taxonomic and predicted functional baseline. These findings provide a foundation for future longitudinal investigations into respiratory microbiome variation, wildlife health, and conservation in this threatened dolphin population.

items.title: Digging deeper: Plant sedimentary ancient DNA in archaeobotanical studies
items.abstract: The analysis of plant sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) is increasingly being applied in paleoecology and is now gaining relevance in archaeobotany and archaeology. This review outlines the practices involved in sedaDNA sampling, extraction, and analysis, emphasising contamination prevention and methodological considerations. Various genetic methods (metagenomics, metabarcoding, and target enrichment) are discussed concerning their strengths, limitations, and suitability for specific research questions. This review also examines the methodological advances, applications, and challenges associated with plant sedaDNA research, especially highlighting its potential to refine paleoenvironmental reconstructions when combined with other traditional archaeobotanical and palaeoecological methods. SedaDNA can allow researchers to detect various plant species, including those that may not have left morphologically determinable remains, thereby offering a more comprehensive understanding of past ecosystems. The approach provides crucial evidence for analysing long-term vegetation changes, climate impacts, and the role of humans in shaping biodiversity. Moreover, sedaDNA may also allow the detection of species used or encountered by humans at the site level. As sequencing technologies and bioinformatic tools continue to advance, sedaDNA will further enhance interdisciplinary research by connecting traditional methods.

items.title: Deciphering the Physical Origin of GRB 240825A: A Long Gamma-Ray Burst Lacking a Bright Supernova
items.abstract: Abstract We present a comprehensive multiwavelength analysis of GRB 240825A, a bright gamma-ray burst (GRB) detected by Fermi and Swift, with a prompt duration ( T 90 ∼ 4 s in the 50–300 keV band measured by the Gamma-ray Burst Monitor) near the boundary separating short and long GRBs, prompting a detailed investigation into its classification and progenitor. We use classical prompt metrics (duration, minimum variability timescale, lag, and spectral hardness) and modern classification techniques (machine learning–based t-SNE, support vector machine, energy- hardness duration, and ε ≡ E γ , iso , 52 / E p , z , 2 5 / 3 ) and find most properties (prompt energetics, placement on the Amati relation, and spectral lag) of GRB 240825A consistent with a collapsar origin. However, extensive late-time optical and near-infrared follow-up with the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) telescope and the 8.4 m Large Binocular Telescope reveals no bright supernova (SN; like SN 1998bw) is detected down to stringent limits (e.g., m r > 25.0 mag at 17.59 days), despite a redshift of z = 0.659 measured from GTC spectroscopy. Host-galaxy spectral energy distribution modeling with Prospector indicates a massive, star-forming galaxy typical of collapsar GRB hosts, though with a large offset. We compare these findings with hybrid events like GRB 211211A, GRB 230307A, GRB 200826A, including supernovae-GRBs, and conclude that GRB 240825A most likely originated from a massive star collapse, possibly with the associated AN heavily obscured or intrinsically faint. This study emphasizes the need for multiwavelength follow-up and a multilayered classification to determine GRB progenitors.

items.title: Observability of Eccentricity in a Population of Merging Compact Binaries
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate the prospects of observing residual eccentricity in a population of compact binaries by calculating the power in the eccentric harmonics, following the methodology in B. G. Patterson et al. Although most observed compact binary coalescences are expected to circularize before entering the sensitivity band of the ground-based gravitational wave (GW) detectors, dynamical interactions in dense star clusters can lead to a fraction of these binaries with nonnegligible eccentricity at the time of detection. To quantify the observability of eccentricity, we simulate a population of merging compact binaries and identify those that have sufficient power in subdominant eccentric harmonics to be clearly distinguishable from quasi-circular systems. We consider a binary black hole (BBH) population derived from globular cluster (GC) simulations with residual eccentricity distribution obtained from Cluster Monte Carlo (CMC) catalogs as well as a fiducial log-uniform model. Assuming the LIGO-Virgo network of GW detectors with their sensitivities achieved during the fourth Observing Run (VK), we find that the BBH population with measurable eccentricity will have a significantly higher median eccentricity e 10Hz ∼ 0.3 (with 90% range: 0.1−0.6) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) ∼ 20 (90% range: 13−54) compared to the observable population of BBHs. We compare our predictions of the regions of parameter space where eccentricity is detectable with the claimed observations of eccentricity in GW events from the third Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-3).

items.title: Magnetic-field morphological diagnostics with ALMA in the G327.29 protocluster: The velocity gradient technique versus dust polarization
items.abstract: Magnetic fields and turbulence may play a key role in the evolution of protoclusters, influencing the formation of dense cores and stars. We examined the morphology of the magnetic fields in the G327.29 protocluster using both the velocity gradient technique (VGT) extracted from molecular line emissions and linear polarization in the dust-continuum emission. The VGT analysis was performed using four molecular tracers: DCN (3-2), C 18 O (2-1), HN^13C (3-2), and H^13CO^+ (3-2); these were observed with the ALMA 12 m array. Owing to its sensitivity to gas dynamics, a comparison between VGT and dust polarization provides a powerful probe of the evolutionary processes in massive star-forming regions. Our analysis reveals a complex magnetic-field structure shaped by the combined influence of turbulence and gravity, as evidenced by the distributions of both the alignment measure (AM$) and the relative orientation angle (þeta_ between the magnetic fields inferred from the VGT and dust polarization observations. The þeta_ distributions are clearly double-peaked for DCN and HN^13C, whereas C^18O and H^13CO$^+ predominantly exhibit a preferred perpendicular orientation. In addition, it also appears that there is a large-scale (beyond the core scale) gravitational infall from the surrounding medium onto the filament and the central densest region. Furthermore, we observe that cores are dominated by a mix of turbulence and gravity. Overall, this work presents, for the first time, the application of VGT to a massive protocluster, G327.29, using high-resolution ALMA observations.

items.title: Reionization bubbles from real-space cross correlations of line intensity maps
items.abstract: We propose a new way to reconstruct the ionized-bubble size distribution during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) through the real-space cross-correlation of 21-cm and star-forming line-intensity maps. Understanding the evolution and timing of the EoR is crucial for both astrophysics and cosmology, and a wealth of information on the first sources can be extracted from the study of ionized bubbles. Nevertheless, directly mapping bubbles is challenging due to the high redshifts involved, possible selection biases, and foregrounds in 21-cm maps. Here, we exploit the real-space cross-correlation ξ21,ν between 21-cm and line-intensity mapping (LIM) signals to reconstruct the evolution of bubble sizes during reionization. For the first time, we show that ξ21,ν (r) departs from a saturation level for each separation r when bubbles of size r begin to form, providing a handle for the onset of bubbles of each radius. Moreover, we demonstrate that ξ21,ν evolves from positive to negative as the EoR progresses, reaching a minimum (i.e. maximum anti-correlation) when bubbles of radius r reach peak abundance. We show that these results are robust to changes in the astrophysical model as well as the timing/topology of reionization. This real-space observable complements usual Fourier-space estimators by capturing the localized nature of bubbles, offering new insights into the sources driving cosmic reionization.

items.title: Two-parameter analytical model for paralyzable radiation detectors
items.abstract: Certain radiation detectors are 'paralyzed' with high input count rates. When applied to count rates close to the event discriminator working rate the one-parameter dead time model fails. Here we present a corrected paralyzable detector model accounting for the event discriminator's finite response time. This two-parameter analytical model, when compared to the experimental data from a commercial x-ray detector, gives an improved description of the input and output count rate relations. Furthermore, it can independently determine the discriminator response time and the pulse shaper dead time, critical parameters for understanding a detector's performance. Finally, this model also provides a post-acquisition pile-up correction that greatly reduces artifacts in high-throughput spectra. In some situations, applying this model to optimize the acquisition and post-acquisition correction allows a user to acquire data an order of magnitude faster without compromising accuracy.

items.title: The assembly and fate of a giant disc galaxy in a protocluster at z = 3
items.abstract: Abstract Recent JWST observations revealed two massive (M⋆ ≳ 1011 M⊙), unexpectedly large spiral galaxies at z ∼ 3, both in overdense environments. We focus on one of these, ADF22.A1 at z = 3.09, which hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN), exploiting its extended [CII] emission (∼30 kpc in diameter) with high-resolution observations from the Atacama Large Millimetre Array and JWST. We find a flat outer rotation curve reaching ∼530 km s−1, and perform, for the first time for a system of this type, a rotation-curve decomposition. We infer a dark-matter halo mass of $\log (M_{200}/M_{\odot })=12.9^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$, a baryon-to-halo mass ratio of $0.4^{+0.6}_{-0.3}$ in units of the cosmological baryon fraction, and a ratio between the baryonic and dark-matter halo specific angular momentum of $1.0^{+0.7}_{-0.5}$. Comparing these quantities with those of local galaxies, we find that ADF22.A1 is indistinguishable from z = 0 giant discs, pointing to the inefficiency of AGN feedback in halting disc growth. Using the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey, we identify potential z = 0 descendants of ADF22.A1, suggesting it will evolve into an extreme (in either mass or angular momentum) early-type galaxy. Finally, we argue that cold-stream accretion, invoked to explain disc formation at z > 1, is disfavoured as the primary formation channel: while not formally excluded, it struggles to account simultaneously for the observed morphology, size, dynamical properties, high specific angular momentum, and baryon-to-halo mass ratio. Instead, sustained accretion from the hot circumgalactic medium offers a plausible, and possibly favoured, alternative.

items.title: JWST and Keck observations of the off-nuclear tidal disruption event TDE 2025abcr: An evolving reprocessing layer
items.abstract: Off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a rare probe of massive black holes (MBHs) outside galactic nuclei. Only a handful are known, including five X-ray-selected candidates and three optically selected events. We present observations of TDE 2025abcr, the second optically selected off-nuclear TDE, discovered at a projected offset of 9.08 ± 0.02 kpc from the nucleus of its host galaxy. We analyze X-ray, UV, optical, and infrared (IR) data from Swift, Keck, ZTF, and JWST. Broad H and He emission lines in the optical and IR confirm a TDE-H-He classification. From luminosity scaling relations and MOSFiT modeling, we infer a BH mass of 10 6 - 10 7 M ⊙ , substantially smaller than the 10 8.38 ± 0.42 M ⊙ BH inferred for the host-galaxy nucleus. We observe velocity evolution in the N III + He II emission complex, shifting from − 100 km s at day − 7 to + 1000 km s by day + 29 , which we interpret as radiative transfer effects in an evolving reprocessing layer. The IR SED deviates from a thermal blackbody, with ν L ν ∝ λ − 2.13 ± 0.04 , significantly shallower than the Rayleigh-Jeans slope of λ − 3 . We rule out dust as the source of this IR excess. Two possibilities remain: free-free emission from reprocessing gas, or an unresolved stellar cluster at the TDE location. Reprocessed emission provides a natural explanation for the IR excess but an underlying stellar cluster of mass log ( M * / M ⊙ ) = 7.57 ± 0.02 and age <2 Gyr is also consistent with the data. If interpreted as a stellar cluster, the inferred mass suggests a stripped remnant of a satellite galaxy. The wandering MBH most likely originated in a minor merger with a smaller galaxy, although dynamical ejection from the host nucleus cannot yet be ruled out.

items.title: GRMHD accretion beyond the black hole paradigm: Light from within the shadow
items.abstract: We present the first three-dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulation of sustained accretion onto a horizonless singularity in which matter reaches the central object rather than being accumulated outside of it or expelled in outflows. We consider a Joshi-Malafarina-Narayan (JMN-1) spacetime, a well-motivated black hole mimicker that arises from gravitational collapse with anisotropic pressure in general relativity, and adopt a compactness parameter for which the central singularity is null. We find that the system evolves into a sustained magnetically arrested disk state. For parameters appropriate to the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus M87*, we obtain an accretion rate of $\sim(3.0 \pm 0.5)\times 10^{-6} \dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$, in full agreement with estimates based on black hole models and, in particular, comparable to that of our reference Schwarzschild black hole simulation. Synthetic ray-traced images at $230\,{\rm GHz}$, computed using polarized general relativistic radiative transfer, are broadly consistent with the Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87*. We identify a key observational discriminant between a black hole and JMN-1: the presence of detectable brightness inside of the ``observable" shadow of JMN-1. This emission originates very close to the central singularity, in a region that would be hidden behind the event horizon in a black hole spacetime. Although this signature is beyond the reach of current observations, it falls within the projected imaging dynamic range of next-generation radio interferometric instruments, offering a robust test of the black hole paradigm.

items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
items.abstract: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

items.title: Clustering constraints on super-early galaxy formation scenarios
items.abstract: The unexpectedly high abundance of bright, blue, super-early galaxies (z≳ 10) has challenged most pre-JWST models of early galaxy formation and motivated a wide range of proposed explanations. We systematically investigated whether galaxy clustering can distinguish among representative scenarios that reproduce the observed UV luminosity function. Using the Shin-Uchuu dark-matter-only simulation, we populated z≈ 11 halos with galaxies according to solutions based on the absence of dust attenuation, feedback-free bursts, bursty star formation, and primordial black hole models. For each model, we predicted the galaxy bias for flux-limited samples at different thresholds in the -20 < < -16 magnitude range. All models predict similar bias values (b≈ 7) for faint galaxies (̊m M_ i) ii) iii) iv) M_ UV ̊m UV ≈ -16), but diverge at ̊m M_ ̊m UV łesssim -18, as the underlying halo-mass to ̊m M_ ̊m UV relations differ significantly. In particular, the primordial black hole scenario predicts an almost luminosity-independent bias, whereas the other models generally predict an increasing bias with luminosity, reaching b≈ 13 for ̊m M_ ̊m UV ≈ -19. Current observational estimates of the bias cannot yet rule out any of the models with significant statistical confidence. More precise measurements from future JWST programs, together with improved theoretical predictions, will be required to break the current degeneracies. Ideally, constraints from a complete sample of galaxies with rm M_ UV <-18 would probe the knee of the b( ) function, taking advantage of the differences in model predictions and strengthening our analysis. Although requiring further refinement, galaxy clustering is confirmed to be a promising probe of the physical origin of the high-redshift luminosity function observed by JWST. M_ UV

items.title: The first 3D magnetohydrodynamic core-collapse progenitors. II. Rotation, magnetic-field amplification, and magnetic topology
items.abstract: The most energetic core-collapse supernovae are thought to arise from rapidly rotating, magnetised progenitors. However, the three-dimensional pre-collapse structure of their angular momentum and magnetic fields remains poorly constrained, limiting the realism of magnetorotational core-collapse simulations. We aim to investigate the angular-momentum distribution, magnetic-field amplification and magnetic topology of physically consistent three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic pre-supernova progenitors from the stellar core to the helium shell. This second paper focuses on the rotational and magnetic properties of the models introduced in . Griffiths2026PaperI We used to evolve two compact Wolf--Rayet progenitors, computed with the stellar-evolution codes and through the final minutes before core collapse. The initial magnetic-field strengths were derived from the one-dimensional stellar-evolution prescriptions in radiative regions and then evolved self-consistently in three dimensions. Our models suggest that the rotation profile near the inner core can depart from a purely shellular distribution and reorganise itself towards a more cylindrical structure. In convective regions, hydrodynamic Reynolds stresses drive the flow towards an approximately constant specific-angular-momentum profile, corresponding to an average rotation profile close to Ω∝ ̌arpi^ -2 (̌arpi denotes the cylindrical radius). Maxwell stresses oppose this tendency but are not strong enough in our models to restore rigid rotation. Convective regions amplify seed magnetic fields, transported from neighbouring radiative layers, producing saturated fields with comparable toroidal and poloidal components and a topology containing substantial small-scale power. As a result, regions that are magnetically disconnected in the original one-dimensional stellar-evolution description become magnetically linked in the multi-dimensional models. Together with , these models represent the first three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic pre-supernova progenitors of this kind, which are suitable for subsequent collapse and explosion calculations. Griffiths2026PaperI Multi-dimensional evolution can substantially modify both the angular-momentum distribution and magnetic topology of pre-collapse progenitors. They provide a physically motivated basis for constructing more realistic initial conditions for magnetorotational core-collapse simulations and for improving prescriptions of magneto-convective angular-momentum transport in late stellar evolution.

items.title: Forward Modeling of Spectral-line Polarization for Weak Magnetic Field Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract Measurements of interplanetary magnetic fields rely mainly on spacecraft observations that provide in situ sampling and cannot directly reveal global magnetic structures. In addition, the Zeeman effect is generally too weak to image weak interplanetary magnetic fields. Here, we investigate the suitability of spectral-line polarization for spatially resolved imaging of weak magnetic fields, focusing on the Na I D lines in Mercury’s magnetosphere. We calculate the spectral-line polarization produced by anisotropic solar radiation and modified by the magnetic field orientation. Using a three-dimensional forward-imaging model of Mercury’s magnetosphere, we generate synthetic maps of Na I D–line intensity and linear polarization. The resulting polarization maps trace the large-scale magnetospheric magnetic field geometry, demonstrating the potential of Na I D–line polarimetric imaging to constrain the spatial structure of Mercury’s magnetosphere. We further show that, with a 1.8 m telescope, Na I D–line linear-polarization imaging of Mercury’s magnetosphere at a spatial resolution of 2″ is feasible with an exposure time of approximately 10 minutes.

items.title: Matrix-free inversion framework for weak lensing mass mapping and its application to DES Y3 data
items.abstract: Weak gravitational lensing mass mapping offers a direct probe of the matter distribution. Accurate reconstruction of mass maps from masked shear catalogs remains challenging due to survey boundaries and spatially varying noise. In AKRA 2.0, we addressed the mask problem on the curved sky by constructing and inverting the normal-equation matrix $\mathbf{H}\ensuremath{\equiv}{\mathbf{A}}^{\mathrm{T}}{\mathbf{N}}^{\ensuremath{-}1}\mathbf{A}$ explicitly, necessitating a split-scale strategy that reconstructed different angular scales independently to reach high resolution. Here we present AKRA 3.0, in which $\mathbf{H}$ is treated as a linear operator and the normal equations are solved by the conjugate gradient method. This reformulation reduces the memory requirement from $\mathcal{O}({N}^{2})$ to $\mathcal{O}(N)$ and the inversion cost from $\mathcal{O}({N}^{3})$ to $\mathcal{O}({N}_{\mathrm{iter}}{N}^{3/2}),N\ensuremath{\sim}{\ensuremath{\ell}}_{\mathrm{max}}^{2}$ for full-sky (SHT-based) operations. Such optimizations render high-resolution full-sky reconstruction tractable for Stage III and Stage IV surveys. Applying AKRA 3.0 to the DES Y3 METACALIBRATION catalog, we produce the highest-resolution convergence map of this dataset to date at HEALPix ${N}_{\text{nside}}=2048$ without imposing a cosmological signal prior. We validate the map reconstruction and its auto and cross-power responses using end-to-end simulations with known input fields and present a preliminary power-spectrum analysis of the DES Y3 maps. The reconstructed $E$-mode convergence map will be made publicly available to facilitate future cosmological studies.

items.title: Detecting classical nova-like explosions with LISA
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves from close binary white dwarfs will form the bulk of measurements obtained by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Previous studies have highlighted the importance of including the effects of steady-state mass transfer in waveform models as many individually resolvable white dwarf binaries will be interacting during the LISA observation window. However, few studies have considered the effect of novae on gravitational wave observations and parameter estimations. We fill in this gap by analyzing the detectability of novae in these systems and the biases in physical parameters when these bursts are not considered. We model a nova burst as a rapid loss of mass from the accretor that suddenly shifts the gravitational wave frequency. We analytically predict the signal-to-noise ratios for direct detection of the nova and where bias from mismodeling becomes greater than the statistical uncertainty. We also consider comparison of two halves of future LISA data to detect bursts in a model agnostic way. Our work has implications for identifying and classifying individual nova events as well as constraining the galactic nova rate throughout the entire galaxy, a challenging task for optical surveys.

items.title: Statistical field theory for weak gravitational lensing
items.abstract: Standard weak-lensing calculations treat lensing as a linear remapping of the matter field along the line of sight. We instead formulate lensing as a stochastic field theory for the Sachs optical scalars, driven by random Ricci-focusing and Weyl-shearing fields. With convergence and shear expressed linearly in the Sachs-scalar fluctuations, the resulting path integral generates a diagrammatic expansion for their n -point correlation functions, organized into linear response, nonlinear propagation, and driving-field cumulants. The conventional calculation emerges as the lowest-order, linear-propagation limit. Beyond it, nonlinear Sachs evolution couples to driving-field non-Gaussianity, mixing the matter cumulant hierarchy into the lensing hierarchy. A selection rule governs the couplings: an n -point observable receives a direct contribution from the n -point driving-field cumulant, and its leading hierarchy-mixing correction from the ( n + 1 )-point cumulant via one nonlinear Sachs interaction, with higher cumulants entering only at higher order. The two-point function, for instance, receives corrections from three-point cumulants of Ricci focusing and Weyl shearing through nonlinear Sachs evolution. Rather than a restrictive approximation scheme, the formalism is a paradigm shift: a unified framework naturally accommodating path corrections, higher-order matter statistics, stochasticity, and small-scale effects.

items.title: Spatiotemporal evolution of the current filamentation instability in relativistic beam-plasma systems: Higher-order spatial correction and the role of the initial seed perturbation
items.abstract: The spatio-temporal evolution of the current filamentation instability in a relativistic beam--plasma system is studied analytically and with two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations. A partial differential equation for the transverse vector potential is derived for a sharp-front relativistic beam entering cold, unmagnetized plasma, including a second-order spatial derivative term that governs the spatial growth near the beam front. The equation is solved analytically for constant, linearly growing, and oscillatory initial noise when this term is neglected, and numerically when it is included, as no closed-form solution then exists. For constant initial noise, the numerical solution reproduces the simulated magnetic-field structure, unlike the analytical solution without the term. This shows that the longitudinal field modulation is intrinsic to the instability, present even for a noise with constant amplitudes. The noise profile as well can influence the spatial-temporal evolution of the instability, which we discuss further considering linearly growing and oscillatory noise. The field grows spatially behind the beam front and saturates at a length $L_{\mathrm{sat}}\propto(v_{0b}+2)v_{0b}/γ_{0b}^{3}$, where $v_{0b}$ and $γ_{0b}$ are the beam velocity and Lorentz factor, beyond which growth is purely temporal. The saturation length increases linearly in time at a constant rate $\mathrm{d}L_{\mathrm{sat}}/\mathrm{d}τ\approx0.42\,c$, matching the analytical estimate. The temporal growth rate remains unchanged, so the term modifies the spatial transport of the instability rather than its local amplification. For beam velocities above $0.6c$, the model deviates from the simulations as oblique modes and nonlinear filament dynamics outside the single-mode treatment become important.

items.title: Non-spherical cows: Introducing the asphericity parameter as a measure of accretion geometry
items.abstract: The outer regions of galactic haloes represent the bridge connecting internal processes within the galaxy to the larger surrounding cosmic web. The gas in this bridge region is shaped by the competing processes of cold inflows from the web and hot ejecta from feedback of supernovae or an active galactic nucleus. Similarly, the gas around galaxy clusters characterizes the balance between inflows and outflows. To study this connection, we introduce a new parameter for quantifying the geometrical configuration of the flow field connecting structures to the cosmic web, the asphericity parameter. This inflow asphericity is based on a spherical harmonics decomposition of the inflow at the virial boundary of the halo. It can be computed using both the linear and the logarithmic inflow field. To validate this parameter, we apply it to both an extensive toy model set and to simulated haloes from the Magneticum simulations. We find the linear asphericity to be a tracer of the total power of the non-spherical inflow and the total anisotropy. On the other hand, the logarithmic asphericity traces the covering fraction of inflows at the surface and is highly sensitive to regions with zero inflow (regions that are dominated by outflow). Thus the asphericity of the flow field is a powerful tool to simultaneously study the geometry of in- and outflows in numerical simulations.

items.title: Hybrid Simulations of Proton Acceleration at Oblique High- β Shocks
items.abstract: Abstract Collisionless shocks in the intracluster and intergalactic media (ICM/IGM) are expected to energize both electrons and ions. While electron acceleration is revealed by prominent radio emission, γ -ray emission from hadronic interactions remains undetected, suggesting that high- β (ratio of thermal to magnetic pressure), low-Mach-number shocks cannot accelerate protons efficiently. We present three-dimensional hybrid simulations of quasi-perpendicular shocks with sonic Mach numbers M s ∼ 3.4–17.5, focusing primarily on high- β conditions representative of cluster environments and including several lower- β comparison runs. We find that weak shocks with M s ≲ 5 are consistently inefficient, with ε CR ≲ 0.1%, while inefficient cases can persist to substantially higher M s depending on M A and β . In contrast, stronger shocks ( M s ≳ 10) develop clear power-law tails with slopes q ∼ 4.0 and reach ε CR ∼ 3%. These results suggest that weak, oblique ICM shocks are generally unlikely to accelerate protons efficiently. However, reducing ϑ B n to ∼45 ∘ leads to substantially higher acceleration efficiencies, indicating that magnetic obliquity plays a critical role in determining proton acceleration. Our findings provide a microphysical framework for interpreting radio relic observations, whose polarization suggests that electrons are accelerated at oblique shocks, and the absence of cluster γ -ray detections.

items.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum X Y model and the interacting disordered X X Z chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

items.title: Parameter estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a binary merger triggers with subsolar mass components
items.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

items.title: Black bounces to traversable wormholes from pure gravity in four and higher dimensions
items.abstract: Abstract This article derives generic static and spherically symmetric spacetimes --- most notably wormholes and black bounces --- as vacuum solutions of metric gravitational theories in four and higher dimensions. To this end, I extend previous results on quasi-topological gravities to encompass cases in which the metric depends on two arbitrary functions of one variable --- instead of the usual single function. I then explain how, given (almost) any spherically symmetric metric, one can reverse engineer a well-defined theory having such a metric as solution. I apply these results to three paradigmatic examples, including the Simpson--Visser black bounce, to showcase the versatility of this method, as well as its limitations. Moreover, I consider the coupling to a Vaidya-like matter source, so as to generate time-varying solutions and investigate what kind of dynamical evolution these theories can account for.

items.title: Astrophysical constraints on hadron-quark crossover in hybrid neutron stars
items.abstract: We investigate astrophysical constraints on hybrid neutron-star equations of state constructed by combining an extended linear sigma model description of quark matter with several representative hadronic equations of state through a smooth hadron-quark crossover. Four different hadronic models are examined in order to explore the model dependence of the resulting hybrid equations of state. After imposing stability, causality, perturbative QCD matching, tidal deformability, and maximum-mass constraints, only the eLSM+GMSR(BSK16) construction remains fully consistent with current astrophysical observations. The surviving parametrizations are further constrained using Bayesian inference based on NICER mass-radius measurements and the GW170817 gravitational-wave event. The posterior distributions favor a broad hadron-quark crossover occurring at relatively high baryon densities, while the formation of extended pure quark cores is strongly disfavored. Instead, the current observations favor neutron stars containing an extended mixed hadron-quark transition region. We also investigate the implications of the inferred maximum-mass distribution for the secondary object of GW190814 and find that, within the present model and adopted observational constraints, its interpretation as a neutron star is unlikely.

items.title: Dark energy in the w − c s 2 plane
items.abstract: We introduce a unified framework for dark energy diagnostics based on the joint phase space of the equation of state w and the sound speed c s 2 . This w - c s 2 plane provides a minimal extension beyond background cosmology, capturing both the expansion and perturbative properties within a single representation. Building on this, we then define the microphysical flow parameter ℱ = d c s 2 / d w , which encodes the dynamical relation between background evolution and perturbative response. We derive a direct connection between ℱ 0 (the present-day value of ℱ ), H 0 , and σ 8 . We show that the microphysical flow parameter enables a hierarchy of increasingly stringent consistency tests that significantly reduce the viable dark energy theory space. We further demonstrate how trajectories in the w - c s 2 plane distinguish models that are nearly degenerate at the level of w ( a ) , including canonical quintessence, Chaplygin gas models, and noncanonical scalar field realizations. This provides a compact phenomenological bridge between dark energy microphysics and future perturbation-sensitive observations, making ℱ 0 a useful discriminator of the kinetic structure which is underlying cosmic acceleration.

items.title: BilbyFlow : User-friendly Neural Posterior Estimation for Gravitational-wave Astronomy
items.abstract: Abstract Bayesian inference plays a central role in the new field of gravitational-wave astronomy. However, traditional Bayesian inference with stochastic samplers is computationally expensive, taking hours to days per event. Transformative changes are therefore required to enable the science of next-generation observatories whose event rates and signal-to-noise ratios will increase significantly over the current generation. Recent work has shown that neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a promising path forward. A neural net is trained to approximate the posterior distribution of gravitational-wave parameters, allowing generation of reweighted posterior samples in a fraction of the time required by stochastic samplers. In this work, we introduce BilbyFlow , which harnesses the power of NPE in the popular Bilby code suite. We use BilbyFlow to analyze a subset of 38 high-mass events from the third LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-3). For 29 events (76%), we obtained an importance-sampling efficiency > 1%, allowing us to produce reliable posterior distributions within 3 minutes to 1.5 hr. For the other events, with importance-sampling efficiency ≪ 1%, the runtime can be as long as 35 hr. We achieve a median importance-sampling efficiency of 7%, which is roughly comparable to the DINGO package. We aim to significantly improve this efficiency with further development to make the runtime more reliably O ( min ) . BilbyFlow is open source and pip installable.

items.title: Properties of neutron stars with hyperons within a generalized relativistic approach
items.abstract: In this work, we study the effects of $Λ$-hyperons on neutron star properties employing a generalized relativistic framework for the equation of state (EOS). Different choices for defining the hyperonic couplings with different levels of parametric freedom are discussed. In all models, the predicted NS maximum masses are reduced compared with the purely nucleonic composition as expected. In the case of relating hyperonic couplings via $SU(6)$-symmetry arguments to the nucleonic ones, we find that NS radii for intermediate mass stars are shifted to higher values compared with purely nucleonic stars, in agreement with the existing literature. However, allowing for more freedom for the hyperonic couplings, the effect is strongly reduced, and the distributions in the NS mass-radius plane of models with and without hyperons become very close. We have also investigated how different nucleonic density functionals influence the hyperon matter composition and neutron star properties.

items.title: Probing the details of relativistic electrons with multifrequency observations of M87 black hole
items.abstract: Abstract Beginning in March 2026, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) conducted a two-month observing campaign aimed at obtaining the first time-resolved sequence of images of the black hole M87* at the center of the Virgo A galaxy. The primary objectives of this campaign are to constrain black hole spin and investigate the temporal variability of the magnetic field and plasma properties within the horizon-scale jet-launching region. In this work, we present theoretical predictions for the spectral index maps expected from these observations. Our predictions are based on Magnetically Arrested Disk simulations performed with the EBHLIGHT code and post-processed using the IPOLE general relativistic ray-tracing code. We investigate the temporal evolution of the spectral index for a range of electron distribution models and five black hole spin values. The analysis includes both frequency bands currently present within the EHT and neighboring frequencies proposed for future array extensions. In addition to extending previous studies to a broader frequency range, our work systematically investigates the time variability of the predicted spectral index maps. In purely thermal electron models, temporal variability of the spectral index maps closely traces variations in magnetic field strength and electron temperature near the event horizon. By contrast, models incorporating a non-thermal electron population exhibit weaker spectral index variability, owing to the contribution of a power-law component with a fixed spectral slope. Our numerical results are consistent with theoretical expectations. Finally, a comparison with the recently measured integrated spectral index of M87* enables us to place preliminary constraints on model parameters.

items.title: A Multimission Detection Framework for High-energy Transients: Application to a 13 yr Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT Sample
items.abstract: Abstract The detection of faint high-energy transients is becoming increasingly important in time-domain and multimessenger astronomy, particularly for identifying electromagnetic counterparts to binary neutron star mergers, high-energy neutrino events, and other weak transient phenomena. At present, the sensitivity of gamma-ray and hard X-ray searches is often limited by the detection threshold of individual instruments, leaving a population of faint transients inaccessible to single-mission analyses. To address this limitation, we develop a joint detection framework that combines trigger information from multiple detectors and assigns each candidate a joint association probability, p joint , as a function of the individual detector signal-to-noise ratios. We apply this framework to archival Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT rates data from 2013 to 2025. The method effectively separates coincident signals from accidental background associations, suppressing inconsistent coincidences while enhancing the significance of faint events observed by both instruments. We find that, under optimal conditions, a two-mission search can increase the accessible volume for short gamma-ray bursts by up to 60%. This framework provides a practical foundation for generalized multimission searches, enabling more sensitive exploration of the faint high-energy transient sky and improving the prospects for future multimessenger discoveries.

items.title: PEARLS: NuSTAR and XMM-Newton Extragalactic Survey of the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-domain Field V: Unraveling X-Ray Spectral Variability
items.abstract: Abstract As one of the first deep time-domain surveys in the hard X-ray band, the NuSTAR campaign in the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time Domain Field (NEP-TDF) offers a prime opportunity to measure variability in a faint population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the medium- to high-redshift Universe. In the X-ray band, AGN variability is generally caused by changes in the brightness of the corona ( F int variability) or changes in the column density of obscuring material near the supermassive black hole (SMBH; N H variability). Broadband spectroscopy (∼0.5–24 keV) is required to reliably disentangle these two phenomena. With simultaneous NuSTAR and XMM-Newton coverage—as well as 1.8 Ms of Chandra monitoring—the X-ray surveys in the NEP-TDF are ideally situated for this purpose. This work presents the first spectral modeling of the 52 NuSTAR-identified sources discovered in the latter half of the campaign, as well as a spectroscopic variability study of the entire 112-source NuSTAR NEP-TDF catalog. Seven variable candidates are identified. We find that ≳1000 total counts split across many (≳10) epochs are needed in order to detect variability. Additionally, variable sources are compared to the survey sensitivity in order to inform population synthesis models of how variations can affect the detectability of faint AGN, which dominate the SMBH accretion history. Lastly, the timescale of N H variability is investigated as a probe for the obscurer location. Significant variability is slightly more common on >100 day timescales, suggesting that the torus may have only slight dominance in driving N H variability in faint AGN.

items.title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an Ultraslowly Rotating Neutron Star versus a White Dwarf
items.abstract: Abstract The source PSR J0901-4046 shows a very long rotational period of ≈75.88 s. In fact, its long period suggests that it could be a white dwarf. We examine the properties of the source and compare the outcomes under the hypotheses of the source being a highly magnetized white dwarf (B-WD) and neutron star. We find that assuming it to be a B-WD with a surface field ∼10 10 G explains many properties, including its storage/rotational energy, in turn, explaining luminosity. On the contrary, the neutron-star-based idea, particularly if examined under the conventional spin down mechanism, requires an unusually high surface magnetic field ≳10 14 G, even exceeding 10 16 G, depending on the obliquity angle and emission mechanism. The source also sits very close to AR Sco, a white dwarf pulsar, in the period and period-derivative plane. We suggest that the source is a B-WD. Along with AR Sco, the source being a B-WD constrains the death line model. The B-WD hypothesis alleviates the necessity of an unusually high magnetic field hindering pair production for PSR J0901-4046 under the neutron star hypothesis. We argue that some rotation-powered pulsars with extreme properties may possibly be white dwarfs rather than neutron stars.

items.title: Composition-controlled cut-off-resonance coupling and polarization-selective wave propagation in a four-component magnetized plasma
items.abstract: Abstract This study deals with the propagation of circularly polarized electromagnetic waves in magnetized multicomponent plasmas composed of electrons, deuterium positive ions (D + ), hydrogen negative ions (H − ), and oxygen negative ions (O − ). Based on the cold-fluid approach combined with Maxwell’s equations, the dielectric functions of right-hand circularly polarized (RCP) and left-hand circularly polarized (LCP) waves are obtained analytically. The numerical values of the cut-off frequencies, the reflection, transmission, and absorption coefficients for a finite multicomponent plasma slab are found using electromagnetic boundary conditions. Due to the presence of two kinds of negative ions, three cut-off frequencies of the RCP waves and the propagation and stop bands related to the negative-ion and electron cyclotron resonances are found. In turn, the LCP wave has only one cut-off-controlled propagation boundary. The effects of negative-ion concentrations of hydrogen and oxygen, magnetic field strength, slab thickness, and frequency are studied. Increase in the concentration of the H − ions leads to a shift in cut-off frequencies, changes in the widths of propagation and stop bands, decrease in the gap between the RCP and LCP cut-offs, and improvement of the low-frequency transparency when both RCP and LCP modes are propagating. A remarkable effect is a tendency of the second RCP cut-off towards the H − cyclotron resonance that results in the cut-off-resonance coincidence with an enhancement in absorption of the light negative ions. The cut-off-resonance proximity produces enhanced electromagnetic absorption associated with the resonant response of the light negative-ion population, indicating enhanced wave-ion coupling. The results provide a fluid-level basis for controlling frequency-selective electromagnetic energy deposition in multicomponent plasmas and show how negative-ion composition can tune polarization-dependent propagation and electromagnetic power deposition in the present model. It can be used in plasma diagnostics, ionospheric wave propagation, plasma electromagnetic filters, tunable polarization devices, and ion-selective heating.

items.title: Cultural invariance in music-evoked emotions
items.abstract: Worldwide, people produce and listen to music to induce, express, and regulate their own and others' emotions. To what extent culture influences the emotions evoked by music is, however, contested. The documented global variation in musical behaviours and emotion concepts suggests substantial cross-cultural differences in how listeners relate to music emotionally, while shared physiology and evolutionary history would predict broad global agreement on the emotional information extracted from music. Some evidence suggests shared processes but experiments on the subject do not represent global diversity in either music or participants. Here, we report a large citizen-science experiment wherein listeners (N = 124,394 in 189 countries; conducted in English) rated their emotional responses to popular Western music and to vocal music produced in mostly small-scale societies drawn from a globally representative corpus (i.e., songs assumed to be unfamiliar in style). We found strong similarity in listeners' emotional responses to music: Average agreement between pairs of countries' listeners was high. Furthermore, across both popular and unfamiliar types of music, emotional responses were shaped far more by individual listeners and the specific songs than by cultural background: Both between-person differences within a country and within-subject differences across songs explained substantially more variance in emotional responses than country-wise differences. Together, these results indicate that a listener's cultural background has only a marginal influence on the emotions they feel in response to music, raising the possibility of universal structure in emotional responses to music.

items.title: Persistence of Multifractal Dynamics at the Mammalian Neuromuscular Junction Across Extracellular Calcium Conditions
items.abstract: The neuromuscular junction represents a relevant experimental model for revealing important biophysical mechanisms underlying synaptic transmission. In this work, we revisited the time-series analysis of electrophysiological recordings obtained from mammalian diaphragm neuromuscular junctions. We applied multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) to assess whether intervals between spontaneous potentials exhibit multifractal behavior at physiological extracellular calcium concentrations and at hypocalcemic and hypercalcemic levels. Surprisingly, we observed a robust, stable multifractal profile across all electrophysiological recordings, regardless of calcium concentration. Therefore, our results provide support for a rich and complex scenario governing neurotransmitter release. Based on these findings, we discuss their biophysical significance and physiological implications.

items.title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
items.abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. These TZ planets in the overlap between the Habitable Zone and Venus Zone can test how incident stellar irradiation affects surface water retention and habitability. Observations of exoplanets in the TZ can probe not only the emergence and decline of exoplanet habitability but also test hypotheses about Venus' past, complementing upcoming Venus flagship missions. Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV). We examine their demographics and quantify their potential for follow-up observations. This list of rocky TZ and EV planets allows observers to optimize target selection and observing strategy for specific instruments. Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.

items.title: The SPACE Program IV: Atmospheric Features on the Cold Transiting Sub-Neptune TOI-6478 b
items.abstract: Among the current population of exoplanets there are very few sub-Neptunes that have their atmospheric composition identified. This is primarily due to sub-Neptunes having high metallicity, clouds, and/or hazes obscuring absorption features. This often produces a spectrum that presents itself as a featureless spectrum especially in the near-IR. However, there are tentative trends that suggest sub-Neptunes with the lowest equilibrium temperatures ($\mathrm{T_{eq} < 400\:K}$) have detectable features, perhaps due to inefficient haze production or cloud sedimentation. TOI-6478 b is a low-density sub-Neptune exoplanet ($\rm <\mathrm{9.9\:M_{\oplus}}$ and $\rm \sim 4.5R_{\oplus}$) with an equilibrium temperature $\mathrm{T_{eq} = 220 \:K}$ assuming zero albedo. In this study, we present the highest S/N spectral feature ($\sim$6) of any sub-Neptune detected using HST/WFC3. We detect this spectral feature using a robust analysis that incorporates the Transit Light Source Effect (TLSE) to rule out false detections due to stellar activity. With the narrow bandpass of HST we were unable to distinguish whether the spectral feature at 1.4$μ$m is from H$_2$O or CH$_4$ absorption. Meanwhile, self-consistent atmospheric models provide physical motivation for CH$_4$ to be the dominant absorber given that H$_2$O should condense or cold trap at higher pressures. Through our analysis we determine that HST/WFC3 alone cannot distinguish between major absorbers. However, a broader wavelength coverage by JWST will be able to measure the atmospheric composition in detail, due to the high S/N features for this target.

items.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
items.abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $λ=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.

items.title: On the High Eccentricity Orbit of 51 Eri b and Constraints on Interactions with a Second Companion
items.abstract: The eccentricity of an exoplanet's orbit is a key observational quantity that can be used to infer its dynamical past and predict its future orbital evolution. Planets are expected to emerge from their protoplanetary cradles with roughly circular eccentricities, and non-circular eccentricites to arise from subsequent dynamical processing in the absence of the gas disk. We present an updated orbit for 51 Eridani b based on 5 years of 0.2 mas precision optical interferometry from VLTI/GRAVITY(+). This planet is young (${\sim}20\,\mathrm{Myr}$ old), temperate ($T_{\rm eff}\sim650\,\mathrm{K}$), and on a wide orbit ($a{=}9.36\,\mathrm{au}$) with an uncertain mass ($M_{\rm b}\leq12\,M_{\rm J}$). We measured the planet's motion to an exceptionally high precision, confirming that its orbit is very eccentric ($e_b=0.574\pm0.003$). We observe residuals to the absolute astrometry of the host star based on a single planet orbit that could be attributable to reflex motion from a third body in the system. We construct a two companion orbit model that could explain the apparent reflex motion of 51 Eri A: this model predicts that the putative second companion has $M_c\in[1.0, 2900]_{95\%}\,M_{\rm Jup}$ and $a_c\in[0.3, 3.1]_{95\%}\,\mathrm{au}$. In this framework, a dynamical interaction between b and ``c" could have kicked the exterior, lower mass b out onto its present, eccentric orbit. If this signal is astrophysical, and not due to a systematic error, this candidate should be confirmable with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry in the near future.

items.title: Validation and Physical Characterization of Seven TESS Exoplanets: A Compact Multi-Planet System and Targets for Atmospheric Spectroscopy
items.abstract: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) continues to identify thousands of transit candidates that require statistical validation to rule out astrophysical false positives before atmospheric characterization can be pursued. We statistically validate and characterize seven TESS exoplanet candidates orbiting five host stars. As a consistency check of our automated vetting and Bayesian inference pipeline, we include TOI-2392.03, a sub-Neptune companion previously validated in the literature. Our framework combines automated signal retrieval, pixel-level centroid and Gaia DR3 contamination analysis, and false positive probability (FPP) computation with the TRICERATOPS vetting engine. Physical and orbital parameters are derived via nested sampling (juliet/Dynesty), complemented by an empirical mass-radius relation, since no dynamical mass measurements are available. Applying the same procedure to all candidates, we statistically validate six new exoplanets ($\mathrm{FPP} < 0.015$ and $\mathrm{NFPP} < 0.001$), one of which (TOI-7721.01) lies close to the FPP threshold. We report the period ratios of the three-planet system TOI-2392, and identify TOI-7721.01 and TOI-1277.02 as the candidates with the highest Transmission Spectroscopy Metrics (TSM) in our sample, making them targets of interest for atmospheric follow-up with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the upcoming Ariel mission.
