items.title: Competition Indices and Environmental Variables Weakly Improve Predictions of Natural Population Fluctuations on Independent Data
items.abstract: The debate about the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations has persisted in ecology for many decades. Ecologists face the challenge of determining the extent to which interspecific competition and environmental factors impact population growth rates. We assess the predictive ability of models with and without interspecific competition and environmental covariates to predict population size one year beyond the model-building data. For 11 of 14 datasets a model with interspecific competition and/or environmental factors make better mean ‘absolute’ prediction error. However, none of the models with interspecific competition and/or environmental variables make predictions that are statistically significantly superior to the random walk model. Overall, in about 60% of the sites, models with interspecific competition and environmental variables show performance worse than the random walk baseline model on independent data. We conclude that there is weak evidence that incorporating interspecific competition and/or environmental covariates leads to improved model predictive ability. A thorough assessment of the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations will require evaluating the predictive power of a broader range of models that incorporate ecology of species traits at each generational time.

items.title: Spatial distribution and uncertainty assessment of heavy metals in coastal groundwater of northern Hainan Island using sequential Gaussian simulation.
items.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in coastal aquifers has attracted increasing attention, yet probabilistic characterization of spatial uncertainty remains limited. This study investigated the coastal aquifer of northern Hainan Island using 315 sampling locations. Sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) was applied to characterize the spatial heterogeneity, prediction uncertainty, and threshold exceedance probabilities of Fe, Mn, As, and Pb, and was compared with ordinary kriging (OK). Mean concentrations followed the order Fe > Mn > As > Pb. Mn had the highest exceedance percentage among the measured samples (26.35%), followed by Fe (2.54%), As (1.59%), and Pb (1.59%). Spatially, Mn and Pb concentrations generally increased from coastal to inland areas. Mn formed an extensive high-concentration zone in the central-southern region, whereas As formed a relatively continuous high-concentration belt along the northern coast. OK and SGS produced highly consistent regional trends, but SGS better preserved local spatial variability and reduced the smoothing effect of OK. The SGS simulation standard deviations showed that uncertainty for Mn was concentrated in the southern region, whereas high uncertainty for As occurred in the northeastern coastal area. Threshold exceedance probability analysis identified a continuous high-risk belt for Mn in the southern region, where probabilities exceeded 0.6 and locally approached 1.0. Mn was therefore the contaminant requiring the highest management priority. Overall, SGS extends conventional concentration interpolation into a probabilistic risk-zoning approach and supports refined identification and management of heavy metal contamination risks in coastal groundwater.

items.title: No effect of post-meiotic sperm aging on male fertility in a species with finite sperm production.
items.abstract: Post-meiotic sperm aging occurs when mature sperm cells are stored in the male reproductive tract before mating. In most species, males produce sperm throughout their life, thereby partially mitigating sperm aging by replenishing their sperm supply. By contrast, sperm production is finite in some species, preventing aging sperm to be replaced by new gametes. Finite sperm production is therefore predicted to impose strong selective pressure to minimize post-meiotic sperm aging. In this study, we tested this prediction by investigating post-meiotic sperm aging in a species with finite sperm production and pre-mating sperm storage in males, the buff-tailed bumblebee (Bombus terrestris). We adopted an integrative multi-level approach combining high-throughput flow cytometry, dual-type DNA methylation profiling, and untargeted proteomics. We identified molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging in sperm cells during male storage, including reduced sperm viability, elevated oxidative stress, increased DNA damage, and altered DNA methylation and proteomic profiles. However, these changes were modest in magnitude. Accordingly, neither male fertility nor reproductive fitness declined with age: males (hence, sperm) of different ages achieved similar mating success and sired colonies that did not differ in foundation success, productivity, composition, or lifespan, indicating that post-meiotic sperm aging has no significant impact on male reproductive performance. Together, our results support the prediction that finite sperm production is associated with limited post-meiotic sperm aging. More broadly, they challenge the assumption that advancing paternal age inevitably compromises reproductive function and highlight the importance of life history in shaping reproductive aging.

items.title: The Curse of Dimensionality: How Does it Affect Dynamical Systems Research in Clinical Psychology?
items.abstract: The dynamical systems approach is gaining attention across many subfields of clinical psychology. Although the systems are assumed to involve many variables, theoretical and methodological work in this field often relies on low-dimensional stability landscapes, creating potential mismatches. In this article, I discuss how high-dimensional stability landscapes may challenge intuitions derived from low-dimensional landscapes, put forward a potential solution based on sufficient low-dimensional descriptions, and propose a future research agenda centered on dimensionality reduction approaches that emphasize preserving information about stability and transitions.

items.title: Estimating the replicability of psychology experiments after an initial failure to replicate
items.abstract: When a replication fails, scientists have to decide whether to make a second attempt or move on.Psychology researchers who attempt to replicate studies often face this decision, given the empiricalrate of replication success in psychology, which is lower than desired. Here, we report 17 re-replicationsof experiments for which an original replication had failed. In 5/17 of these “rescue” projects (29%),the “rescue” study mostly or fully replicated the original results, albeit with a smaller effect size;in the other 12, the second replication was also judged to have failed. We speculate that successfulrescue projects were due to larger sample sizes or methodological changes such as attention checks. Inthe absence of obvious weaknesses in a failed replication study’s sample or procedure, however, it maybe most efficient to stop pursuing an effect after a single failed replication.

items.title: Recipient-Focused Hallucinations in AI-Generated Professor Outreach Emails: A Pilot Factorial Evaluation of Grounding and Verification
items.abstract: Abstract Background : LLMs increasingly draft personalized academic outreach, which depends on describing a real professor's research. Unsupported claims about a recipient's topics, methods, or findings misrepresent their scholarly work. Methods : In an offline pilot, a 2 × 2 design varied whether the writer received a publication evidence packet during drafting and whether a verifier revised the draft afterwards (conditions A–D). We generated 96 emails for 12 professors across three fields, decomposed them into 360 atomic research claims, and labelled each against the professor's evidence packet with an automatic (LLM) evaluator. All primary estimates are pilot estimates from automatic labels, not human-verified measurements. Reliability was assessed against a blinded 36-claim human-labeled subset (10% of claims) and a second automatic evaluator from a third model family. Results : Under the primary evaluator, the closed-book baseline (A) had a Severe Error Rate (SER) of 0.344 (21/61 claims; exact 95% CI 0.227–0.477). Grounding the writer (B) produced no severe errors in 90 judged claims (0.000, CI 0.000–0.040) and raised Supported Personalization Density (SPD) from 0.65 to 1.71 supported claims per 100 words. Verify-only (C) left 1 severe error in 50 claims (0.020; SPD 1.04); grounded-plus-verified (D) produced none (0/87) at the highest specificity (1.76). Interpretation and limits: Primary-evaluator agreement with the human annotator was only fair (Cohen’s κ = 0.33, CI 0.16–0.49). The evaluator was too lenient in 14 of 16 disagreements, suggesting that the automatic severe-error rates may underestimate error prevalence. However, the small human-labelled subset does not establish the magnitude or direction of bias across the complete dataset. The zeros are evaluator-specific: a second evaluator relabelling the same claims found 10 severe errors in B and 4 in D, closed-book 0.455 - a large reduction under grounding, not elimination. And 17 of the 21 closed-book severe errors came from the four psychology professors; excluding that field, closed-book SER falls to 0.095. Both automatic evaluators reported lower pooled severe-error rates for grounded conditions than for ungrounded conditions. Grounding during drafting also showed a lower observed pooled SER than post-generation verification alone. Conclusion : Verified publication evidence sharply reduced severe misrepresentation - to zero under the primary evaluator, roughly four-fold under the second - while making emails more specific, and outperformed correcting drafts afterwards. Grounding, not correction alone, is the more promising safeguard; establishing the effect size needs human labelling at scale and a validated judge.

items.title: Behavior–emotion decoupling as micro-level spatial injustice: Why urban villages morphology fails to heal marginalised groups in China
items.abstract: Abstract Urban villages host tens of millions of rural-to-urban migrants in Chinese cities, yet their dense, fragmented morphology is widely assumed to erode residents' mental health (Wu, 2016). Drawing on spatial justice theory and environmental psychology, this study asks whether urban villages morphology shapes healing environments differently for marginalised groups versus indigenous residents.Using Kuidong Village (Xuzhou, China) as a case study, we integrate Baidu POI and heatmap data, SegNet-based street view segmentation, behavioral observation, and a seven-dimension emotion survey (N = 162) into a multi-group mediation framework linking spatial configuration, daily behavior, and emotional perception. We identify systematic behavior–emotion decoupling among migrants: their activity patterns respond to spatial form, yet no behavior produces emotional returns. All three mediation pathways (enclosure via necessity to depression, greenery via spontaneity to safety, and permeability via sociality to relaxation) fail for migrants while remaining significant for indigenous residents. Healing resources thereby remain visible yet unusable. We interpret this decoupling as a form of micro-level spatial injustice, extending spatial justice theory from the macro distribution of resources to micro psychological pathways. We accordingly propose differentiated spatial interventions to restore migrants' behavior–emotion linkage, transforming urban villages from mere dwelling spaces into healing places.

items.title: Sensitivity to Physical Activity Predicts Daily Physical Activity Levels in People with Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated whether Sensitivity to Physical Activity (SPA, a measure of changes in pain responses to standardized physical tasks) predicts self-report and objective physical activity levels in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. We also examined whether SPA offers predictive value in activity levels beyond psychological factors and quantitative sensory testing (QST). Methods Sixty-one participants with chronic MSK pain completed a standardized SPA lifting task, psychological questionnaires (Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale), and QST (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation of pain). Participants wore an accelerometer for up to nine days to objectively measure physical activity. Self-reported activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the predictive value of SPA, psychological, and QST measures on physical activity outcomes. Results SPA significantly predicted objectively measured daily physical activity levels, explaining unique variance in both average daily steps (ΔR²=11.6%, P=0.005) and time spent performing moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (ΔR²=6.1%, P=0.030), after controlling for age and pain levels. SPA was not associated with self-reported physical activity. Neither psychological factors nor QST measures significantly predicted objective or subjective activity levels. Discussion Lifting-based SPA emerged as a unique predictor of real-world physical activity in individuals with chronic MSK pain, outperforming traditional psychological and sensory predictors. These findings support the potential of SPA as a biopsychosocial marker for physical inactivity and the importance of objective activity monitoring in rehabilitation planning.

items.title: Burden and Trends of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Major Clinical Bacterial Pathogens in Bangladesh (2019–2024): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh, where factors such as unregulated antibiotic use, weak surveillance, and inadequate healthcare infrastructure exacerbate the problem. A unified, up-to-date assessment of recent resistance trends is crucial to guide effective public health interventions and optimize clinical decision-making. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance patterns of major clinical bacterial pathogens in Bangladesh between 2019 and 2024. The analysis followed PRISMA guidelines, with data sourced from PubMed, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, and DOAJ. A random-effects model was employed to synthesize data from 30 eligible studies encompassing over 270,000 clinical specimens, providing estimates for the pooled prevalence and resistance patterns of eight major bacterial pathogens. Median resistance (MR) and interquartile ranges (IQR) were also calculated to determine resistance levels for each pathogen–antibiotic pair. The findings revealed that Gram-negative bacteria were most prevalent, with Escherichia coli (12%), Klebsiella spp. (8%), and Pseudomonas spp. (7%) as the most common pathogens. Alarmingly high antibiotic resistance rates were observed across all species, particularly in Enterococcus spp. (70%), Pseudomonas spp. (56%), Acinetobacter spp. (53%), E. coli (46%), Proteus spp. (44%), Staphylococcus aureus (43%), Klebsiella spp. (41%), and Enterobacter spp. (40%). Resistance was notably high for conventional antibiotics such as β-lactams, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones, while concerning levels of resistance were also detected against last-resort antibiotics including carbapenems, colistin, and certain aminoglycosides. These findings highlight the urgent need for national antimicrobial stewardship programs, enhanced surveillance, and coordinated public health strategies to mitigate the escalating threat of AMR.

items.title: Awareness and knowledge of breast cancer risk factors, signs and symptoms, and prevention among in-school female adolescents in Ibadan North-West Local Government Area, Oyo State, Nigeria: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in Nigeria, and many women present late. Early breast health literacy may support lifelong preventive behaviour, but evidence on adolescents’ knowledge in Southwest Nigeria is limited. We assessed awareness and knowledge of breast cancer risk factors, signs and symptoms, and prevention among in-school female adolescents in Ibadan North-West Local Government Area (LGA), Oyo State, Nigeria. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study included 396 female students aged 11–18 years from four randomly selected public secondary schools, recruited by multistage sampling. A structured questionnaire, assessed socio-demographic characteristics, awareness, and 44 knowledge items (signs and symptoms, 9; risk factors, 20; prevention, 15). items.title: Nobody writes for the reader: Reading level in paediatric health guidance, real health queries and AI chatbot responses
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare the reading level of paediatric health guidance, parents' own questions and artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot responses to those questions, and to test whether chatbots adapt to the reading level of the person asking. Methods Cross-sectional study, reported following the Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool (CHART), of 18,392 guideline pages (17,516 family-facing, 876 clinician-facing) from 86 organisations, 1,000 parent-authored questions sampled from 23,477 public forum posts, and 5,000 responses to those questions from five commercially deployed chatbots. Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) was the primary outcome, with six secondary metrics. In a sub-study, 100 questions were resubmitted with an instruction to match the reader's level or to answer at sixth-grade level (1,500 responses). Results Median FKGL was 12.51 for clinician-facing guidance, 9.08 for family-facing guidance, 8.37 for chatbot responses and 6.15 for parents' questions. The American Medical Association sixth-grade standard was exceeded by 99.3% of clinician-facing pages, 92.6% of family-facing pages and 89.2% of chatbot responses. Every chatbot answered above the reading level of the question asked (median difference + 1.21 to + 3.57 grades). Given an explicit sixth-grade instruction, the median gap narrowed in every model and three of five answered below the reader's level. Conclusion Paediatric health information from institutions and chatbots alike is written above the level of its readers. Chatbots do not adapt to the reader by default, but can when instructed.

items.title: Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation Analysis Reveal Insights into the Molecular Mechanism of Schizandrin A in Treating Age-related Hearing Loss
items.abstract: Abstract Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is a bilateral, symmetrical, and progressive sensorineural disorder associated with aging and represents a major public health challenge in aging societies. Schisandrin A (SchA), a biphenylocyclooctene-type lignan monomer isolated from the dried fruits of Schisandra chinensis, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, regulates mitochondrial autophagy, and inhibits apoptosis. This study aimed to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of Sch A against ARHL using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Network pharmacology identified 137 potential targets. Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed that these genes mediate cellular signaling responses, ion balance, and physiological homeostasis through kinase cascade signaling, ion channel regulation, and synaptic signal transmission. Kyoto encyclopedia of genes and genomes pathway enrichment analysis identified calcium and cAMP signaling pathways, neuroactive ligand signaling, and neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions as major enriched pathways. Molecular docking and MD simulations were used to screen binding affinities. The binding energies for SRC, STAT3, EGFR, HSP90AA1, HIF1A, and PTGS2 were all lower than − 5.0 kcal/mol, indicating high binding affinity and stable binding modes. Among these, PTGS2 exhibited the lowest binding energy. MD simulation revealed that the PTGS-deoxyschizandrin complex had an overall average root mean square deviation (RMSD) of 0.18 nm, a protein backbone and ligand RMSD of 0.22 and 0.09 nm, respectively. The mean radius of gyration and solvent-accessible surface area were 3.16 and 443.21 nm, respectively, suggesting that the complex did not undergo significant expansion or contraction. The average root mean square fluctuation values for A and B chains of PTGS were 0.12 and 0.13 nm, respectively, indicating low overall flexibility and a relatively stable conformation. The complex formed strong hydrogen bonds, potentially exerting a neuroprotective effect. This study demonstrated the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch A against ARHL and provides a theoretical basis for its application and further drug development.

items.title: Postnatal Family Planning Service and Documentation Gaps in Ondo and Kebbi States, Nigeria: A Four-Year Retrospective Analysis of Counselling, Recorded Acceptance, and Method Mix, 2022–2025 Running head: Postnatal family planning counselling and acceptance gaps in Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract Background The postpartum period creates repeated opportunities to prevent unintended and closely spaced pregnancies, yet routine information systems often record counselling and contraceptive provision incompletely. We assessed postnatal family planning counselling, recorded contraceptive acceptance and method mix in public facilities in two contrasting Nigerian states. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of facility-month aggregate National Health Management Information System records from 23 public facilities in Ondo and Kebbi States, January 2022-December 2025. The primary counselling-to-acceptance ratio used months with both indicators recorded, more than zero women counselled, and acceptors not exceeding women counselled. Method mix was restricted to months in which all four recorded methods (IUD, Implant NXT, Jadelle and Depo-Provera) were present and their sum equalled the acceptor count. We reported counts, percentages, Wilson 95% confidence intervals and data-completeness indicators; no causal comparisons were undertaken. Results The analytic dataset contained 988 facility-months. Counselling was recorded in 902/988 (91.3%) and acceptors in 595/988 (60.2%). After excluding 10 internally inconsistent months and 117 paired zero/zero months from rate estimation, 456 months contributed 20,284 counselled women and 3,810 acceptors, a pooled ratio of 18.8% (95% CI 18.3–19.3). The ratio was 23.2% in Kebbi and 15.2% in Ondo, but acceptor reporting was substantially lower in Kebbi (219/556; 39.4%) than Ondo (376/432; 87.0%). Recorded annual ratios varied from 3.9% to 41.9% in Kebbi and from 7.4% to 19.4% in Ondo. Among reconciled complete method records, Ondo recorded 1,586 methods: IUD 35.8%, Implant NXT 32.0%, Jadelle 31.2% and Depo-Provera 1.0%. Kebbi contributed only 49 reconciled methods, precluding stable inference about its method mix. Conclusions Routine records indicate a substantial gap between documented counselling and recorded contraceptive acceptance, marked facility heterogeneity, and severe state- and level-specific incompleteness. The findings support integrating method provision with counselling, protecting contraceptive choice and commodity availability, and making completeness and internal consistency visible in routine dashboards.

items.title: From Reservoirs to Potential Vectors of Superbugs: Wild Birds Co-Harboring Extended- Spectrum Beta-Lactamases and Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone Resistance determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Pakistan
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a significant health issue of the 21st century. Wild birds are increasingly recognized as reservoirs of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. They are ecologically important because they have travelling ability across globe, and with no direct antimicrobial interaction making them an important part of One Health interface to predict environmental contamination of MDRs and its dissemination. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and co-occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the gut of wild birds in Islamabad region. Using standard bacterial characterization techniques in total, 342 Gram-negative Enterobacteriaceae isolates were obtained from fresh fecal droppings collected seasonally at eight locations with various types of facilities in Islamabad Pakistan including hospitals. zoo, parks and other public areas. Disk Diffusion test was performed to confer quinolones resistance and double-disk synergy test (DDST) was used to confirm ESBL production. Multiplex PCR was used to detect PMQR genes ( QnrA, QnrB, and QnrS ), whereas aac (6′)-Ib-cr was detected using conventional PCR. Statistical analysis was used to assess inter-variable associations. A total of 342 isolates were obtained, of which 118 (34.5%) were ESBL producers. Among ESBL-positive isolates that were phenotypically co-resistant to ciprofloxacin and/or nalidixic acid (Quinolones), 73 (61.8%) carried at least one gene of the PMQR family. The most common PMQR determinants were QnrS (76.7%) and aac (6′)-Ib-cr (47.9) %. The co-harboring isolates were dominated by Escherichia coli (82.2%). K. pneumoniae showed a high carriage of aac (6′)-Ib-cr (90%) and QnrB (60%) genes. The highest levels were observed in autumn and winter. Multi-gene co-carriage patterns, where ESBL and PMQR genes occur on a single plasmid, were inferred and were similar to those found in other major plasmid families, IncF, IncI, and IncHI. Wild birds are important reservoirs and active spreaders of MDR Enterobacteriaceae carrying ESBL and PMQR determinants on transferable plasmids in the urban environment of Islamabad. Based on these results, the need to involve wildlife surveillance in One Health-based AMR surveillance programs and increase antibiotic stewardship in Pakistan is highlighted.

items.title: A Sandwich-Structured Dual-Mode Fabric with Temperature-Adaptive Spectral Tunability for All-Season Outdoor Personal Thermal Management.
items.abstract: Owing to global warming, sudden temperature fluctuations are occurring with greater frequency, which exacerbates risks to public health. Passive radiative cooling and solar heating technologies have unique advantages of requiring no energy input, rendering them highly suitable for thermal management textiles. The operation of the dual-mode fabric with cooling and heating functions primarily relies on the contrast between the solar reflectance on the cooling side and solar absorption on the heating side. However, the regulation of infrared emissivity in both modes tends to be ignored. Here, we report a dual-mode woven fabric based on a sandwich structure that features temperature-adaptive spectral tunability for all-season outdoor personal thermal management. The combination of a polydimethylsiloxane/nano-zinc oxide (PDMS/nano-ZnO) radiative cooling layer with a polydopamine (PDA) solar heating layer constituted the basis of the dual-mode switchable fabric. More importantly, the introduction of eicosane into the porous fibers realized the spectral tunability in response to ambient temperature. The solar reflectance in the cooling mode showed an increase of nearly 6% at high temperature (>40 °C), while the infrared emissivity in the heating mode was reduced by 13.4% at low temperature (<10 °C). In addition, the introduction of eicosane also endowed the fabric with considerable latent heat to further improve thermal management performance. Its temperature range of response corresponds closely to the human thermal comfort zone. Under solar intensity (Isolar) of ∼500 W/m2, the resulting fabric achieved a temperature increase of ∼7.1 °C compared with bare skin in the heating mode and maintained the average temperature of the covered skin close to that of bare skin in the cooling mode. Thanks to the woven structure, the fabric exhibited desirable mechanical strength, waterproofness, washability, breathability, and moisture permeability. This dual-mode woven fabric was expected to provide further insight into developing responsive dual-mode personal thermal management textiles.

items.title: Association of dietary essential amino acid intake profiles with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality.
items.abstract: Dietary essential amino acids (EAAs) are crucial for metabolic health, but their association with long-term mortality remains unclear. Existing studies often focus on individual amino acids, failing to capture patterns of overall combined EAA intake.We analyzed data from two prospective cohort studies: the UK Biobank (UKB; n = 126,336) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES; n = 35,084). Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify distinct dietary EAA intake patterns. We examined the associations of these patterns with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality using Cox proportional hazards models and pooled the estimates via inverse-variance-weighted fixed-effects meta-analysis. Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 14,518 deaths were documented. Four distinct EAA intake profiles were identified: low, moderate, high, and very-high. Compared with the low-profile group, higher EAA intake profiles were associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality in the pooled analysis (Moderate-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.83-0.92; High-profile: HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.78-0.90; Very-high-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.77-0.97). Similar protective associations were observed for cardiovascular and cancer mortality. In exploratory stratified analysis within the UKB cohort, the protective association appeared more pronounced among older adults (≥65 years).Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 14,518 deaths were documented. Four distinct EAA intake profiles were identified: low, moderate, high, and very-high. items.title: Sex chromosome turnover as an evolutionary escape from mitonuclear conflict
items.abstract: Mitochondrial and nuclear genomes must remain coadapted to sustain oxidative phosphorylation, yet their distinct inheritance often fosters conflict. Sex chromosomes are a key arena for these dynamics: by biasing co-transmission between nuclear-encoded mitochondrial (N-mt) genes and maternally inherited mtDNA, they can amplify or suppress mitonuclear incompatibilities. Existing syntheses emphasize stable XY (mammals) and ZW (birds) systems, where genomic context is conserved. In contrast, many fishes and amphibians undergo frequent shifts among XY, ZW, and polygenic or environmental sex determination, repeatedly resetting the linkage backdrop for mitonuclear interaction. I propose a comparative framework in which sex-chromosome turnover acts as an evolutionary “escape hatch” from Y- or W-linked deleterious N-mt alleles by entrapping N-mt loci into, or releasing them from, non-recombining sex-linked strata, thereby altering the sex bias and intensity of conflict through time. This hypothesis predicts cyclical pulses of hybrid dysfunction and genomic “scars’’ that record historical entrapment, offering testable predictions for when turnover entrenches versus relieves mitonuclear conflict. By integrating evidence from stable and labile vertebrate systems, this article outlines how sex-chromosome dynamics shape mitonuclear coadaptation, postzygotic isolation, and ultimately lineage diversification.

items.title: Ecological and economic impacts of increasing landscape connectivity in highly threatened ecological corridors of Tanzania
items.abstract: Abstract Ecological corridors facilitate the flow of ecosystem goods (e.g., wildlife movements) and services (e.g., water regulation) between protected areas, benefiting farmers and governments. To enhance landscape connectivity, farmers within ecological corridors are often encouraged to make pro-conservation decisions, ideally in a coordinated manner. These decisions, however, come along with costs to farmers (e.g., opportunity and transaction costs) as well as governments (e.g., mobilization and enforcement costs). Yet, outcomes of conservation decisions may not be certain due to risks such as droughts and global market crises. This study estimates the ecological and economic impacts of conservation decisions under different levels of landscape connectivity in the Igando-Igawa Wildlife Corridor (IIWC) and the Baga-Kisima Gonja Forest Corridor (BKG) in Tanzania. Using a Decision Analysis approach, we evaluate ecological (forest stock and African savanna elephant populations) and economic (conservation costs, benefits and risks) outcomes under low, medium, and high landscape connectivity scenarios. Then we estimate the expected impact of increasing connectivity as the expected change in outcomes, using low connectivity as a counterfactual. Results from Monte Carlo simulations show that increasing landscape connectivity to medium or higher levels enhances forest stock in both corridors and African savanna elephant movement in IIWC. The expected annual conservation costs for households and the government are two to three times higher in IIWC than in BKG. While the government can benefit from increased landscape connectivity, this was limited for household-level estimates. The results indicate that payment-based policies are necessary to mitigate household losses. Nonetheless, government environmental benefits alone cannot fully bridge this gap.

items.title: Dietary ecology of introduced predators in a fragmented biodiversity hotspot
items.abstract: Introduced predators, such as red foxes (Vulpes vulpes) and feral cats (Felis catus), threaten biodiversity, particularly in fragmented landscapes where loss of structurally complex vegetation reduces refuge for native wildlife. Quantifying predator diets is essential for understanding the pressures they impose. This study morphologically analysed 76 fox and 75 cat stomachs collected from the Fitz-Stirling macro-corridor in southwest Western Australia to compare dietary overlap, identify predation on native and threatened fauna, and assess use of anthropogenic resources. Twenty-seven native species were detected. Cat diet was richer than fox diet (23 vs. 18 species), but fox diet was more diverse. Over half the species consumed were unique to each predator, resulting in limited niche overlap (Schoener’s index: 0.142; Pianka’s index: 0.135). Native mammals were important food for both predators (Frequency of Occurrence (FOO), where FOOfox = 60.5% and FOOcat = 48.5%), with foxes generally consuming larger species than cats. Four threatened species were identified: tammar wallaby (Notamacropus eugenii; FOOfox = 5.5%), western brush wallaby (Notamacropus irma; FOOfox = 22.5%, FOOcat = 2.5%), chuditch (Dasyurus geoffroii; FOOfox = 1.5%) and malleefowl (Leipoa ocellata; FOOcat = 2.5%). Foxes exploited canola crops and carcasses originating from kangaroo culling and from deceased livestock, while cats frequently consumed introduced rodents. These findings highlight shared and distinct predation pressures and reinforce the need for ongoing predator management.

items.title: Age-independent physiological shifts, but no faster life history, in an urban Neotropical frog
items.abstract: This repository contains the raw data, R and Python code, model summaries and figures needed to reproduce all analyses of the article below (main text and Online Resource 1). It does not contain the manuscript text. Associated publication Severgnini MR, Gonçalves SF, Fernandes CE, Bovo RP, Franco-Belussi L, Provete DB. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24294393 License Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) for data, figures and text, and MIT for code. Summary of the study We tested whether urban males of the Neotropical frog Leptodactylus podicipinus differ from rural males in escape behaviour, energy metabolism, immunity, reproduction, growth and skin traits, and whether these differences depend on age. Frogs were collected in 2024 in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, central Brazil, at one urban pond (Lagoa Itatiaia) and two rural ponds (Chácara Buritis and Morro do Ernesto). We dissected 35 males (18 from Chácara Buritis, 17 from the urban pond) and measured 16 morphophysiological traits: somatic indices (liver, heart, spleen, kidney, testes), blood glucose, red and white blood cell counts, leukocyte composition, hepatic melanin, testis locule area and percentage of spermatozoa, skin layer thickness (epidermis, Eberth-Kastschenko layer, total) and dorsal darkness. Six additional males from Morro do Ernesto provided blood cell counts and dorsal darkness. In a separate escape-behaviour experiment, we measured flight initiation distance (FID) and the distance of the first jump of 28 males (15 urban, 13 from Morro do Ernesto). The age of every frog (number of lines of arrested growth, LAGs) was estimated by skeletochronology of phalanges. Each trait was analysed with Bayesian multilevel models in brms (site — age, with frog-level random effects for repeated histological measurements), and a joint model with partial pooling across traits addressed multiplicity. The analysis report follows the Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines (BARG; Kruschke 2021, Nature Human Behaviour 5:1282-1291) and documents priors, convergence diagnostics, posterior predictive checks, cross-validation (PSIS-LOO and 10-fold) and prior sensitivity. items.title: Microscopic Neuromodulation with Locally Enhanced Electric Field
items.abstract: Implantable neural stimulation devices play an important role in fundamental neuroscience research, clinical applications, and emerging technologies such as neuroprosthetics and brain machine interfaces, with increasing demand for spatially precise neuromodulation at cellular and circuit levels. Microelectrode based electrical stimulation relies on charge injection into neural tissue, where irreversible electrochemical reactions at the electrode electrolyte interface may lead to electrode degradation and tissue damage. Although microscale magnetic stimulation provides an alternative, it typically requires sophisticated microcoil architectures and complex fabrication processes. In this work, we introduce a novel neural stimulation mechanism based on localized electric field enhancement. The proposed device employs an electrically insulated sharp metallic tip to concentrate the electric field and generate localized displacement currents capable of activating nearby neurons. Finite element simulations were performed to investigate the underlying stimulation mechanism and establish design guidelines for device fabrication. MEMS based neural probes were subsequently fabricated and experimentally evaluated through in vivo animal studies, with neuronal activation observed at distances of less than 200 micrometers from the probe tip using two-photon imaging. By avoiding Faradaic charge transfer at the tissue interface while offering high spatial localization, orientation selectivity, and a compact device architecture, the proposed approach provides a promising alternative to existing stimulation technologies for chronic and high-density neural interfaces.

items.title: Advances in Neuroscience in an Age of Rapid Technological and AI Innovation – Towards Integration Across Scales
items.abstract: Rapid technological innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed not only the resolution at which the brain can be observed, but also the questions that can be asked, shifting the field from description toward prediction, regulation and generation. Yet progress has largely advanced along parallel trajectories, and findings at one level rarely inform or constrain the next. Here, we review recent advances in three exemplary domains and propose a future-oriented framework for their integration. First, molecular and cellular neurotechnology, including synaptic proteomics, cryo-electron tomography, super-resolution microscopy, optoacoustic and ultrasound imaging, sonogenetics and molecular MRI, resolves neural processes with unprecedented specificity. Second, AI-based decoding of human brain activity yields precise signatures of complex, subjective conscious experiences in naturalistic contexts and is beginning to inform diagnosis, drug evaluation and individualized neuromodulation in mental disorders. Third, large-scale neural recordings, mechanistic whole-brain simulations, neural foundation models and AI surrogate brains are converging toward individualized digital twin brains. We argue that the next level of progress requires integrating these domains into a closed loop of reciprocal constraints, in which molecular measurements inform model parameters, human signatures define and evaluate what models must reproduce, and model predictions prioritize perturbations that can be tested across domains.

items.title: From Social Brain Modules to Dynamic Network Dysfunction: An Integrative Neuropsychological Framework for Social Cognition
items.abstract: Abstract Social cognition is commonly partitioned into emotion recognition, empathy, theory of mind, and social decision-making, yet these labels do not map clearly onto discrete neural modules. Recent taxonomic, meta-analytic, network-neuroscience, and clinical evidence instead indicates that adaptive social behavior depends on context-sensitive coordination of partially specialized and domain-general systems. We conducted a structured, search-informed integrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE-indexed literature updated on 6 September 2026, supplemented by citation chaining and targeted 2024–2026 searches. We synthesize evidence across social perception and action observation, interoception and affective salience, mentalizing and social-semantic knowledge, valuation and executive control, and large-scale network dynamics. The incremental contribution of this review is not to introduce node dysfunction, disconnection, or network dynamics as isolated concepts, but to integrate them into a cross-diagnostic neuropsychological framework that links task demands and component computations to distinct mechanisms of clinical dysfunction. The framework distinguishes two comparatively evidence-grounded mechanisms namely, (1) node dysfunction, affecting a computationally important region or subsystem, and (2) disconnection, impairing integration among otherwise viable components from (3) hypothesis-generating network-reconfiguration dysfunction, concerning context-appropriate transitions among network states. Frontotemporal dementia provides convergent evidence for node and disconnection mechanisms; Alzheimer disease and Parkinson disease illustrate the importance of general cognitive support and network state; acquired brain injury demonstrates the consequences of focal injury and long-range disconnection; and schizophrenia and autism emphasize mechanistic heterogeneity. Recent psychometric and ecological-validity syntheses further show that conventional task performance maps only incompletely onto everyday social behavior. The framework generates falsifiable predictions for dynamic imaging, electrophysiology, perturbation, lesion-network methods, and naturalistic assessment, with the aim of linking neuropsychological profiles more directly to mechanisms and real-world function.

items.title: Level of Personality Functioning as a Marker of Clinical Stage in Older Adults with Personality Disorders: A Proof-Of-Concept Study.
items.abstract: Objectives Clinical staging has been proposed to improve assessment and treatment planning for personality disorders (PDs) in older adults. This proof-of-concept study examined whether level of personality functioning, assessed with the clinician-rated Level of Personality Functioning Scale - Brief Form 2.0 (LPFS-BF 2.0), might serve as a marker for determining clinical stage in older adults with PDs. Methods Eighty-four patients aged > 60 years receiving specialized mental health care for PDs were included. Clinical stage was established by multidisciplinary consensus based on severity of personality dysfunction and life-course progression of personality pathology. Differences in LPFS-BF 2.0 scores were examined using non-parametric tests and pairwise comparisons. Results LPFS-BF 2.0 scores differed significantly between stages 2 and 4 ( r = .42), but not between adjacent stages. Similar patterns were observed for Self-Functioning and Interpersonal Functioning. Jonckheere-Terpstra tests for ordered trends indicated increasing scores across stages, including for the Total score ( p r = .37). Conclusions These findings provide preliminary evidence of an association between level of personality dysfunction and clinical stage in older adults with PDs. The pattern suggests a gradual increase in severity across stages, but further research is needed to establish the validity of the staging model.

items.title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Ischemic Stroke: Mechanisms of Neurovascular Injury and Repair.
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) disrupts intestinal homeostasis through autonomic, endocrine, hemodynamic, and immune pathways, allowing gut-derived signals to influence secondary brain injury and recovery. Gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs) are membrane-enclosed particles that protect and transport bacterial proteins, lipids, glycans, nucleic acids, and metabolites across biological barriers. This narrative review examines how GMEVs may connect post-stroke dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction with peripheral immune activation, blood-brain barrier injury, glial responses, and neurovascular repair. Pathobiont-derived vesicles may promote endothelial activation, complement and inflammasome signaling, oxidative stress, leukocyte recruitment, and regulated cell death. Conversely, vesicles from selected commensal or probiotic bacteria may support epithelial integrity, immune resolution, and restorative signaling. Engineered bacterial vesicles have also shown therapeutic potential as targeted carriers in preclinical ischemic stroke models, although these studies do not establish equivalent effects for endogenous gut-derived vesicles. Depending on microbial source, cargo, route, dose, host state, and timing, vesicle-associated signaling could contribute to worsening or improvement rather than necessarily producing both outcomes. Translation will require source-resolved tracing, rigorous vesicle characterization, physiologic dosing, clinically relevant models, and longitudinal human studies.

items.title: Who am I now? Experienced changes of occupational identity after spinal cord injury.
items.abstract: Purpose To explore the experiences of individuals in redeveloping their occupational identity following a spinal cord injury (SCI). Material and methods This qualitative interview study included six adults with SCI and used an inductive design. Data were analyzed using latent qualitative content analysis. Results The findings indicate uncertainty and a dynamic process in redeveloping occupational identity through engagement in altered daily activities shaped by environmental and contexts. This is captured in the theme: "Landing or not landing in a new identity." Participants' experiences are expressed in four categories: Loss of identity sparks the fighting spirit; Challenge to maintain hope and faith in the future; The person I was - who am I now?; and Searching for my future self. Together, these illustrate the tension between holding on to a pre-injury identity and allowing a new one to emerge while navigating facilitators, barriers, and expectations. Conclusions Following SCI, occupational identity undergoes a transformative process extending from rehabilitation into post-discharge life. Although individuals may initially strive to restore their pre-injury identity, redevelopment is influenced by self-worth and exploration of personal narratives. Findings highlight the importance of person-centered rehabilitation, coordinated interventions, lifelong follow-up, and further research to support occupational identity development following SCI.

items.title: WNK-SPAK/OSR1 signaling pathway facilitates ictal activity via reduced neuronal chloride extrusion rate.
items.abstract: Seizures upregulate Na + -K + -2Cl - (NKCC1)-mediated Cl - influx and downregulate K + -Cl - (KCC2)-mediated Cl - efflux via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 kinases, leading to cytoplasmic chloride ([Cl - ] i ) accumulation, reduced GABAergic inhibition, and anticonvulsant failure. Early studies found that inhibiting WNK-kinase reduced baseline [Cl - ] i (E Cl ) and seizures via increased KCC2 activity. However, increased KCC2 activity alone should not affect E Cl , whose determinants are more complex. We determined the net effects of the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway inhibitor WNK463 on E Cl and [Cl - ] i transients during spontaneous ictal-like discharges (ILDs) in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures from mice. We found that WNK463 reduced interictal [Cl - ] i , but did not change baseline [Cl - ] i measured in the presence of TTX. WNK463 enhanced neuronal Cl - extrusion during and after ILDs before abolishing ILDs. Pharmacological inhibition and targeted siRNA silencing demonstrated that the anti-ictal effects of WNK463 involved both NKCC1 and KCC2. Our data support a mechanism whereby mutual NKCC1 inhibition and KCC2 activation via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway exert powerful anti-ictal effects by facilitating [Cl - ] i extrusion during ILDs.

items.title: Hierarchical neural circuit theory of normalization and inter-areal communication.
items.abstract: The primate brain exhibits a hierarchical, modular architecture with conserved microcircuits executing canonical computations across reciprocally connected cortical areas. We present a hierarchical neural circuit theory with feedback connections that dynamically implements divisive normalization across its hierarchy. In a two-stage instantiation (V1 ↔ V2), increasing feedback from V2 to V1 amplifies responses in both areas. We analytically derive power spectra (V1) and coherence spectra (V1-V2) as functions of frequency ( f ) and compare them with experimental observations: peaks in both spectra shift to higher frequencies with increased stimulus contrast, and power decays as 1/ f 4 at high frequencies. The closed-form spectra are validated against direct stochastic simulation of the full nonlinear circuit across contrasts. The theory further predicts distinctive spectral signatures of feedback and input gain modulation. Crucially, the theory offers a unified view of inter-areal communication, defined as the ability to linearly predict neural activity in one brain area from neural activity in another, with emergent features consistent with empirical observations of both communication subspaces and inter-areal coherence. It admits a low-dimensional communication subspace, where inter-areal communication is lower-dimensional than within-area communication. It further predicts that: (1) increasing feedback strength enhances inter-areal communication and diminishes within-area communication, without altering the subspace dimensionality; (2) communication is strongest, and the subspace dimensionality lowest, at the frequencies at which V1-V2 coherence peaks; (3) normalization reduces the subspace dimensionality. Finally, a three-area (V1 ↔ V4 and V1 ↔ V5) instantiation of the theory demonstrates that differential feedback from higher to lower cortical areas dictates their dynamic functional connectivity. Altogether, our theory provides a robust and analytically tractable framework for generating experimentally testable predictions about normalization, inter-areal communication, and functional connectivity.

items.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Efficacy of a Novel Online Prevention Program Addressing Changes to First-Time Parent Couples' Sexual Well-Being.
items.abstract: The perinatal period brings persistent changes to couples' sexual and romantic relationships. Access to perinatal sexuality information benefits sexual well-being, yet sexual health remains neglected in perinatal care. We examined feasibility and preliminary efficacy of the first couple-based online prevention program ( S upporting the T ransition to Parenthood through O nline Sexual and R elationship K nowledge; STORK) targeting perinatal sexual challenges via psychoeducation and cognitive-behavioral skill-building. We examined feasibility (practicality, acceptability, demand) via adherence and self-reports, and preliminary efficacy by comparing primary (sexual satisfaction, desire, distress) and secondary (relationship satisfaction, relationship conflict, depressive symptoms) outcomes among expectant couples with STORK program access ( N = 45 woman-man dyads) and a matched control sample from mid-pregnancy/pre-program to three months postpartum/post-program. Feasibility was strong. Most couples adhered to the STORK program and rated it highly. Preliminary efficacy findings were small-to-moderate and positive for birthing parents but mixed for partners. Compared to controls, birthing parents reported smaller declines in sexual satisfaction and desire and smaller increases in conflict and depressive symptoms. Relationship satisfaction declined less for both parents. Unexpectedly, partners reported greater declines in desire and increases in sexual distress. STORK addresses a critical gap in perinatal care by offering an accessible program to support couples' adjustment, especially for birthing parents.

items.title: Progress in parabiotic mouse models: From origins to modern applications.
items.abstract: The parabiotic mouse model involves a surgical technique that connects the circulatory systems of two mice, enabling the sharing of peripheral circulatory system, immune cells, and various physiological factors. This review traces the historical development of the model from its initial establishment by Paul Bert in the 19th century to the present, summarizes technical improvements in surgical methods, animal adaptation, and model stability, and systematically outlines its cutting-edge applications in fields such as aging reversal, immune tolerance mechanisms, cancer biology, neuroscience, and metabolic diseases. Studies demonstrate that heterochronic parabiosis can reverse aging phenotypes in tissues of older mice and reveal the pivotal role of circulating factors in disease progression. Despite technical challenges and ethical considerations, the integration of this model with multi-omics technologies and organoid research holds promising prospects, providing essential tools for regenerative medicine and the elucidation of complex disease mechanisms. The model's irreplaceability stems from its ability to simulate systemic, whole-body physiological interactions, which cannot be fully replicated by in vitro systems like organ chips or organoids. Importantly, we provide critical synthesis of conflicting findings and highlight methodological caveats to guide future research.

items.title: Imagery Reprocessing in the Treatment of PTSD and Psychosis: A Case Illustration.
items.abstract: Traumatic experiences are strikingly elevated among people with psychosis, yet the post-traumatic stress symptoms they experience have historically been overlooked and undertreated. Concerns that addressing trauma may exacerbate psychotic symptoms have contributed to clinical hesitancy. Encouragingly, a growing body of evidence supports the safety and efficacy of trauma-focused interventions for people experiencing both post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and psychosis. This article demonstrates how imagery-based reprocessing techniques can be used to treat overlapping PTSD and psychosis symptoms. This article presents Hamid, a 22-year-old Kurdish refugee experiencing PTSD and psychosis symptoms, including flashbacks, nightmares, distressing voices, visions, and somatic intrusions, alongside pervasive fears of harm. Hamid was deeply distressed by these experiences, leading to social withdrawal and a diminished quality of life. Hamid attended 26 weekly sessions and 3 booster sessions of Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for psychosis (TF-CBTp), an integrative approach combining principles and techniques drawn from cognitive models of PTSD and psychosis. Early sessions focused on collaborative formulation, psychoeducation, and developing strategies to promote a sense of control through emotional regulation, to support readiness for trauma-focused work. The central phase employed imagery-based memory reprocessing techniques to address unhelpful meanings (cognitive appraisals), update traumatic memories, meet emotional needs, and reduce the emotional intensity of both PTSD- and psychosis-related symptoms. By the end of therapy, Hamid reported fewer trauma-related intrusions, reduced distress linked to his voices and somatic experiences, and a growing sense of safety in his daily life enabling him to begin re-engaging socially. A comprehensive Staying Well Plan was developed to maintain this progress and continue rebuilding his life.

items.title: TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons ameliorates amyloid-β pathology via coordinated enhancement of autophagy-lysosome and mitochondrial function.
items.abstract: The intraneuronal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) is an early pathogenic event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), initiating a pathological cascade that includes synaptic dysfunction, metabolic deficits, and eventual neuronal loss. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP) and mitochondrial homeostasis, represents a promising therapeutic target. However, its efficacy and mechanisms when specifically activated in neurons during the prodromal stage remain unclear. Here, we used an adeno-associated virus (AAV) under the control of the CaMKIIα promoter to achieve excitatory neuron-specific TFEB overexpression in the hippocampal CA1 region of 2 months-old 5×FAD mice. This intervention significantly reduced soluble Aβ levels at 3 months and attenuated amyloid plaque burden, dystrophic neurite formation, and glial activation at 6 months, accompanied by substantial improvements in spatial learning and memory. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that TFEB not only enhanced autophagic flux and lysosomal biogenesis but also promoted the expression of key mitochondrial genes and improved mitochondrial function. In APP695swe-N2a cells, TFEB overexpression increased levels of LC3B-II and LAMP1, enhanced mitochondrial activity and biogenesis (via PGC-1α upregulation), and effectively reduced intracellular Aβ accumulation. Our findings demonstrate that targeted TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons during early AD pathogenesis initiates a protective cascade by co-activating autophagy-lysosomal clearance and mitochondrial pathways, thereby reducing Aβ accumulation and mitigating downstream pathology. This study highlights the potential of neuron-specific TFEB activation as a cell-type-specific therapeutic approach for early AD intervention. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

items.title: Valence- and locus-specific attributional patterns across manic, depressive, and euthymic presentations of bipolar disorder: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Aim Attributional biases are relevant to social cognition in bipolar disorder (BD), but whether they vary across clinical presentations remains unclear. We examined attributional patterns during mania, depression, and euthymia relative to healthy controls (HCs). Methods In a two-site, cross-sectional study, 75 adults with DSM-5-defined BD-I/II were assessed during mania (n = 32), depression (n = 21), or euthymia (n = 22), alongside 22 HCs. Participants completed the Internal, Personal and Situational Attributions Questionnaire-Revised (IPSAQ-R), which assesses internal, personal, and situational attributions to positive and negative scenarios. Dominant causes were coded into counts by valence and causal locus and analyzed using adjusted negative binomial generalized estimating equations. Results The Group × Valence × Locus interaction was significant (Wald χ 2 (6) = 13.16, P = 0.041). Differences primarily involved negative events. Compared with HCs, mania was associated with fewer situational attributions (incidence rate ratios [IRR] = 0.39, 95% CI [0.23, 0.69]) and higher personal attributions (IRR = 1.34, 95% CI [1.05, 1.72]). Depression was also associated with fewer situational attributions (IRR = 0.60, 95% CI [0.36, 0.99]), without increased personal attributions. After Holm adjustment, only the reduced situational attribution in mania remained significant (pHolm = 0.009). Euthymia did not differ significantly from HCs. Conclusion Attributional patterns in BD differed across clinical presentations, with differences most evident in mania and depression and less evident in euthymia. Reduced situational attribution in mania was the most robust finding; findings in depression and higher personal attribution in mania were preliminary. These cross-sectional findings are consistent with possible presentation-related variation; longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether attributional patterns change within individuals over time.

items.title: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in the Drosophila brain.
items.abstract: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE-gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE-gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE-gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE-gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE-gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity and functional adaptability of the brain.

items.title: Synergistic mechanistic and deep learning approaches for modeling insect thermal responses and geographic distributions
items.abstract: Aim: The Hutchinsonian shortfall, the lack of knowledge about species' abiotic tolerance, limits our understanding of species responses to environmental change and consequently also the outlining of their distribution in space and time. Such environmental tolerance is commonly inferred with two distinct approaches: i) trait performance studies, which use lab experiments to model species' functional responses, often overlooking real-world complexity, and ii) species distribution models, which infer environmental suitability from occurrence data, but offer limited causal insights. In this paper, we argue that these two strategies bring complementary information that can be integrated to estimate species-environment relationships more robustly and accurately map species distributions. Location Global scale Time period 2000-2019 Major taxa studied Given their exceptional diversity and climatic sensitivity, insects provide a powerful system for studying these responses. We selected key insect species representing i) disease vectors: the yellow fever (Aedes aegypti) and Asian tiger (Aedes albopictus) mosquitoes; ii) agricultural pests: the cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) and the fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda); and iii) biocontrol agents: the green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) and the 14-spotted ladybug (Propylea quatuordecimpunctata). Methods We compared predicted insect thermal suitability and distributions derived from two complementary methodological approaches: mechanistic models based on experimentally derived thermal responses of ecological rates, and deep learning-based species distribution models based on occurrence data. We further tested hybrid frameworks integrating mechanistic and correlational information through model ensembling, mechanistic regularization, and mechanistically informed deep learning. We assessed the efficacy of these methods under increasing data scarcity by progressively removing up to 80% of species occurrence records using three strategies: removal from the warmest or coldest parts of species' thermal ranges, removal from the least-sampled locations based on geographic sampling bias, and random removal as a baseline. Results Our findings highlight that occurrence-derived thermal suitability closely reproduces the observed distributions of insects. Compared to the mechanistic estimates, these thermal response curves are consistently shifted towards lower temperatures, potentially reflecting niche underfilling. However, when challenged with progressive data removal, correlative methods fail to extrapolate reliably in data-deficient regimes, where mechanistic knowledge becomes increasingly more crucial. Hybrid approaches in turn leveraged complementary information, improving predictive performance and reducing the sensitivity of environmental suitability estimates to sampling biases. Main conclusions Ultimately, we show how the synergistic integration of experimental ecology with observational biogeography can lead to more accurate and ecologically robust predictions for species distributions and their environmental responses to climatic changes.

items.title: The everyday ecology of children’s emotional experience
items.abstract: Emotional experiences are fundamental inputs to human development, yet we know surprisingly little about their distribution in everyday life. Research typically characterizes children’s emotional environments using global reports or brief observations, obscuring the real-time contexts in which emotions arise. Here, we used artificial intelligence to automatically transcribe and annotate daylong audio recordings from three samples totaling N=159 families with children aged 5 months-8 years old (48.43% female). Our findings reveal the architecture of children’s everyday emotional environments: positive speech was concentrated during play and music, and 25% of speech segments conveyed frustration, concentrated during routine caregiving. Mothers’ mental health did not predict affective speech, but lower child effortful control predicted more frustration in our toddler sample. Frustration peaked in early toddlerhood, suggesting that children’s growing independence at this age may reorganize family emotional environments. Overall, emotional speech appears to emerge from everyday activity, with meaningful shifts across development.

items.title: A Narrowly Tuned Olfactory Receptor in the Sunda Pangolin Identifies 1-Octen-3-One as a Key Chemical Cue in Foraging Behavior.
items.abstract: The Sunda pangolin (Manis javanica) is considered a critically endangered species, partly due to its highly specialized diet, which consists mostly of ants and termites. Field observations have shown that pangolins rely on olfaction to locate ant and termite nests even from distances of several kilometers. However, the specific chemical signal used to locate food in the field remains unknown. Based on transcriptome sequencing, 1033 olfactory receptors (MjavORs) of M. javanica were identified and analyzed. Four MjavORs (OR118, OR171, OR215, and OR276) were functionally characterized using the Xenopus laevis oocyte system co-expressing CFTR, RTP1, and Gαolf. Notably, MjavOR215 showed a robust response to 1-octen-3-one, a compound released from termite nests. An odorant-binding protein, MjavOBP3, also demonstrated the highest binding affinity for 1-octen-3-one. Behavioral tracking assays confirmed that pangolins are significantly attracted to 1-octen-3-one, a volatile emitted from termite nests (p < 0.05), rather than to volatiles from termites themselves. These results clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying pangolin foraging, demonstrating that volatile from termite nests guide this behavior.

items.title: The Joint Impact of Deleterious Mutations, Dominance, and Gene Flow on Linked Neutral Variation in Structured Populations.
items.abstract: Most species are geographically structured, which leaves characteristic signatures in neutral genomic regions used to reconstruct demographic history. Yet, these signatures can be distorted by linked selection due to deleterious mutations. This can reduce genetic diversity through Background Selection, or increase diversity through Associative Overdominance. While their effects are well characterized in panmictic populations, they remain largely unexplored in structured populations. We investigated an Isolation-with-Migration model using simulations across a range of migration, selection, dominance, and recombination parameters. We quantified the effects of deleterious mutations on standard summary statistics by simulating either genotypes at neutral and deleterious mutations (genotype-based approach) or genealogies and deleterious mutations (Ancestral Recombination Graph-based approach). The latter recovered similar patterns, directly relating genomic patterns to underlying coalescent processes. For lower recombination rates, we found a Background Selection-driven regime for weakly codominant mutations, characterized by lower diversity and increased genetic differentiation. For recessive mutations, we identified an Associative Overdominance-driven regime, characterized by increased diversity and lower genetic differentiation. This is reflected in the genealogies: Background Selection shrunk coalescence times and led to lineage sorting topologies, while Associative Overdominance stretched coalescence times and led to incomplete lineage-sorting topologies. Migration strongly affected genetic differentiation and topology frequencies but had weaker effects on diversity and coalescence times. Our results provide evidence of a transition from Associative Overdominance to Background Selection for recessive deleterious mutations in an isolation-with-migration model. Importantly, these processes leave distinct signatures on genealogies, highlighting that Ancestral Recombination Graph-based approaches have the potential for inferring linked-selection in structured populations.

items.title: A Model-Specialist Predator Attacks a Batesian Ant Mimic as Readily as Its Model.
items.abstract: Batesian mimicry can protect palatable species when predators avoid their defended models, but resemblance to a model can also impose costs when predators actively target the model. We tested this potential cost using the ant-mimicking jumping spider Myrmaplata plataleoides (O. Pickard-Cambridge, 1869) and its model, the Asian weaver ant Oecophylla smaragdina (Fabricius, 1775), together with the aggressive ant-mimicking crab spider Amyciaea lineatipes O. Pickard-Cambridge, 1901, which routinely attacks O. smaragdina. We tested whether A. lineatipes differentially attacked the Batesian mimics and its model, and whether its responses differed when these prey were paired with less similar alternatives. In simultaneous-choice assays with living prey, A. lineatipes showed no differential attack probability between M. plataleoides and O. smaragdina. In contrast, A. lineatipes strongly preferred O. smaragdina over the non-ant-like salticid Thiania bhamoensis Thorell, 1887, M. plataleoides over the non-model ant Camponotus sp., and O. smaragdina over Camponotus sp. These controls show that the absence of a difference between M. plataleoides and O. smaragdina was not simply due to indiscriminate prey choice. We therefore interpret our main results as showing that the predator did not express differential attack preference between the Batesian mimic and its model under our experimental conditions; this could reflect limited discrimination or equivalent acceptance of both prey types. The findings indicate that model-specialist predation can impose a potential cost on Batesian ant mimicry, highlighting the importance of considering predator specialization when evaluating the fitness consequences of mimicry.

items.title: Seasonal Population Dynamics and Habitat Use of Dromiciops gliroides (Microbiotheriidae), an Endemic Marsupial of the Temperate Rainforest of Southern South America.
items.abstract: Dromiciops gliroides is an arboreal marsupial endemic to the temperate rainforests of South America, where it functions as a key seed disperser for several native plant species. To evaluate the ecological drivers shaping its activity patterns, we integrated demographic, spatial, and environmental data collected over three consecutive annual cycles in a forest stand of southern Chile. Population abundance, survival, and movement were estimated using capture-recapture analyses across five trapping grids (255 traps). We used Boosted Regression Trees to quantify the influence of microhabitat structure and climatic conditions on species detectability. Our results revealed pronounced seasonal dynamics: captures and recaptures peaked between late spring and early summer, and males were caught more frequently and moved farther than females during the reproductive season, a pattern compatible with a polygynous mating system but also with sex-specific detectability. Detection probability increased in areas characterized by a tall bamboo understory and the presence of key tree species (Eucryphia cordifolia, Lomatia dentata, and Nothofagus dombeyi), and captures were largely confined to periods when minimum temperatures exceeded ∼10°C, although seasonal timing and minimum temperature were weakly associated in our dataset. This study provides one of the first multi-year ecological datasets available for D. gliroides and provides new insights into its spatial ecology, seasonal dynamics, and habitat associations. Because these results derive from a single, structurally intact forest remnant, they should be read as a local demographic baseline rather than as range-wide values. Still, our findings highlight the importance of long-term monitoring to understand and conserve this ecologically pivotal and evolutionarily singular marsupial.

items.title: Resource Rich but Risky Patches: Primary Productivity Triggers Intraguild Predation of Insects by Livestock in Oak Savannas.
items.abstract: Theoretical models on intraguild predation (predation among organisms within the same trophic level, intraguild predation) assume a spatially heterogeneous primary productivity. Hence, resource-rich patches could attract both predators and prey, yet prey may suffer higher predation rates. This theoretical framework can be extended to antagonistic, size‑asymmetric interactions among herbivores in which negative effects arise not only from predation but also from other non‑trophic mechanisms. We analyzed antagonistic interactions driven by primary productivity among oak-defoliating Lepidoptera and livestock in Iberian oak savannas. Caterpillars defoliate oak canopies, but exclusion experiments have shown that free-range livestock predate/trample soil-pupating Lepidoptera. We used fine-scale multispectral imagery to assess the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) of oak canopies and surrounding pasture. Then, we tracked the visits of GPS-collared sheep in each tree of the study site, where we sampled oak-defoliating Lepidoptera caterpillars. NDVI of canopies and pasture were spatially correlated, and sheep grazed more often at more productive patches. Negative top-down effects (increased predation/trampling) outweighed positive bottom-up ones (increased food availability) in soil-pupating Lepidoptera, whose abundance was lower in productive pastures due to higher sheep activity. In contrast, species pupating in leaves/branches were more abundant in those trees, benefiting from increased productivity while avoiding predation, as their pupae were inaccessible to sheep. Irrespective of the underlying mechanisms (direct predation and/or trampling), our results show that assessments of antagonistic interactions between large herbivores and insects must incorporate landscape‑level variation in productivity and the movement abilities of both guilds.

items.title: An Attention Bias for Threat and a Safety-First Strategy: Trait Anxiety Selectively Facilitates Aversive Over Reward-Based Learning in Zebrafish (Danio rerio).
items.abstract: Trait anxiety reflects stable inter-individual differences in anxiety-like behavior and modulates an animal's assessment of risk-benefit trade-offs, thereby influencing its decisions in ecologically relevant contexts. Such decisions are often shaped by learning from both aversive and rewarding experiences. However, evidence on how anxiety affects these two types of learning remains inconsistent, suggesting that the effect may be task specific. Moreover, a direct comparison under a unified paradigm is lacking. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio) to address this gap, we screened for high- and low-anxiety individuals, characterized their food-shelter preference, personality traits, and baseline cortisol levels, then compared their cognitive performance across aversive (predator cue) and reward-based (social interaction) associative learning tasks. Our results demonstrate a clear task-specific effect: high-anxiety individuals performed better in aversive learning, but performed comparably to low-anxiety individuals in reward-based learning. Baseline cortisol levels did not differ between high- and low-anxiety individuals. The aversive-learning advantage in high-anxiety fish was partly explained by their personality, yet anxiety itself contributed unique variance, suggesting that the effect involves an interplay of personality co-variation, safety-first strategy, and sustained threat-related attentional bias. These findings suggest that a high-anxiety phenotype may confer greater survival fitness in high-risk environments. From a cognitive ecology perspective, this study provides insights into the potential evolutionary adaptive value of trait anxiety.
