items.title: Triggered electromyography-guided progressive fascicular subdivision to identify a bilaterally tEMG-silent interval in conjoined twin spinal cord separation: a dual-configuration case series.
items.abstract: Purpose Surgical separation of conjoined twins with fused caudal spinal cords requires identification of a safe neural cleavage plane, yet anatomical boundaries are often indistinct. Triggered electromyography (tEMG) has been used to determine nerve root ownership, and iterative subdivision with sequential stimulation has been reported in pygopagus twins, but the sequence and its endpoint have not been standardized. This study describes a tEMG-guided progressive fascicular subdivision approach to identify a bilaterally tEMG-silent interval in two conjoined twin configurations. Methods We monitored two cases (pygopagus and ischiopagus) using multimodal intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring, including tEMG, transcranial motor evoked potentials, somatosensory evoked potentials, and free-running electromyography. A dual-twin color-coded electrode configuration enabled simultaneous independent mapping of both nervous systems. Progressive fascicular subdivision with re-stimulation of each bundle was performed until a bilaterally tEMG-silent interval was identified. Results Case 1 involved pygopagus twins with a fused conus medullaris at S2. Case 2 involved ischiopagus twins with syringomyelia involving both spinal cords and an anterior sacral meningocele. In both cases, progressive fascicular subdivision identified a bilaterally tEMG-silent interval, which guided microsurgical separation. Motor function and anal tone were unchanged at 6-month follow-up. Conclusion Triggered electromyography-guided progressive fascicular subdivision identified a bilaterally tEMG-silent interval in both pygopagus and ischiopagus configurations, including one with complex intrinsic spinal cord pathology. This interval reflects absence of detectable somatic motor activation in the monitored muscles and does not exclude sensory or autonomic fibers; its value as an intraoperative reference requires validation in larger series.

items.title: Using binocular rivalry to assess cultural differences in spatial-frequency processing of faces.
items.abstract: Cultural experience shapes attention, memory, and some aspects of visual processing, but it remains unclear whether it influences perceptual selection when incompatible images compete for awareness. We preregistered a binocular rivalry study to test whether Eastern and Western observers differ in the relative weighting of low- versus high-spatial-frequency information during initial perceptual competition. Forty-nine Western participants (U.S.-born, ≤ 2 years abroad) and 43 Eastern participants (recent East Asian arrivals, ≤ 5 years in the U.S.) viewed dichoptic pairs of spatially filtered faces (Albert Einstein, Marilyn Monroe). Image size was varied across five levels to shift retinal spatial frequency content, allowing estimation of each observer's "balance point"-the size at which low-pass and high-pass filtered faces were equally dominant. In a second component of the study, a filtered image of one face was pitted against an unfiltered image of the other face to assess the competitive strength of isolated spatial-frequency bands against broadband-image rivals. Increasing retinal image size enhanced the dominance of high-pass information. However, mean balance points did not differ between cultural groups, and no reliable association emerged with measures of participants' levels of acculturation or cultural values. The results suggest that the initial outcome of perceptual competition in binocular rivalry is largely independent of cultural background and that the mechanisms governing this competition operate similarly across observers from different cultural backgrounds. OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The study was preregistered online ( https://osf.io/pgyqv ). Final analyses deviated from the plan in that we used the quickpsy Package in R (instead of fitting a 2nd-degree polynomial using MATLAB's curve fitting toolbox) to generate a cumulative normal curve which better characterized the relationship between image sizes and task performance. This also allowed us to use t tests rather than ANOVAs. In addition, sample sizes exceeded the original plan to allow for exclusions and for exploratory individual difference analyses. After reviewing the stereopsis test measure-but without comparing data from the two groups-the team decided that getting six of the nine circles correct (instead of the preregistered criterion requiring nine out of nine circles) would be sufficient to demonstrate stereopsis. We did not use response times as an exclusion criterion for individual trials, and our additional exploratory analyses focused on the self-report measures of culture rather than those included in the preregistration. We deemed these exploratory analyses to be more of interest, given the focus of the paper, than those originally planned or the sample characteristics did not support further follow-up analyses (e.g., uneven distributions of urban/rural background and gender). Data and code are available at https://osf.io/st473 and https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/ST473 .

items.title: Microglia mediate motor memory decay through activity-dependent phagocytosis of myelin sheaths.
items.abstract: Experience-dependent changes in myelination are important for motor learning, with newly generated oligodendrocytes contributing to the formation of new myelin. However, motor memories decay over time and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here we show that motor memory decay is linked to changes in memory-associated myelin sheaths resulting from microglial phagocytosis in mouse brain. Mechanistically, reduced activity of motor memory engram cells lowers oligodendrocyte expression of the 'don't eat me' signal from Cluster of differentiation 47 (CD47), facilitating microglial phagocytosis and driving myelin loss. Knockout of CD47 from motor memory-associated oligodendrocytes increased microglial phagocytosis of myelin sheaths and accelerated the decay of motor memory, whereas overexpression of CD47 showed opposite results. Moreover, microglia phagocytose myelin sheaths and synapses independently. Our findings reveal that microglial phagocytosis of motor memory-associated myelin sheaths leads to the decay of motor memory. Since various types of memory require myelination in the brain, this mechanism may contribute to the decay of other memory types.

items.title: Dietary interventions and stroke clinical outcomes: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Optimal nutrition is biologically essential for supporting neural repair mechanisms post-stroke, yet clinical guidelines provide limited and non-specific dietary recommendations that are largely extrapolated from primary cardiovascular prevention rather than stroke recovery populations. To systematically review and synthesise evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of food-based or whole-diet interventions on clinical outcomes in adults with stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), including disability, neurological function, cognition, mood, quality of life, and stroke recurrence. Following Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, four databases (Medline, Embase, CINAHL, CENTRAL) were searched to February 2026 for RCTs testing oral dietary interventions (≥4 weeks) in adult stroke/TIA survivors. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Eight RCTs (n=15,974) were included (1 low risk, 6 some concerns, 1 high risk). Quantitative meta-analysis was precluded by marked heterogeneity. Interventions included salt substitution (n=2), Mediterranean diets (n=2), ketogenic diet (n=1), partial meal replacement (n=1), Trigona honey (n=1), and soy milk (n=1). Reduced-sodium salt substitution decreased stroke recurrence (RR 0.86, 95%CI 0.77-0.95) and mortality (RR 0.88, 95%CI 0.82-0.96) in large Phase III trials, while Mediterranean diets improved quality of life (EQ-5D mean difference: 10.1, 95%CI 1.8-18.4). For functional recovery, small Phase I/II pilot trials yielded exploratory, domain-specific proof-of-concept signals (e.g., post-exercise soymilk enhancing walking performance; Trigona honey improving MoCA scores), but were constrained by high susceptibility to Type I errors and effect size overestimation. Ketogenic diet improved NIHSS (5±2 vs 7±2, p<0.01) and disability (mRS: 2±1 vs 3±1, p<0.05), but was accompanied by high adverse event rates (keto-flu 25%, GI distress 15%, hyperlipidemia 10%). Salt substitution and Mediterranean diets show clear promise for secondary prevention and recovery. Given the limited and heterogeneous evidence base, high-quality, phase-specific RCTs are urgently needed to establish stroke-specific nutrition strategies.

items.title: Beyond memory strengthening: noradrenergic control of memory specificity.
items.abstract: Emotionally significant events are typically remembered better and for longer than mundane experiences. This emotional memory enhancement critically depends on arousal-induced norepinephrine release within the brain. Beyond memory strengthening, recent work shows that noradrenergic activity also shapes the specificity, detailedness, and temporal precision of memories during both early consolidation and systems consolidation. In this review, we synthesize recent findings from human and animal research spanning molecular, circuit, systems, and behavioral mechanisms to propose an integrative framework for how emotional arousal-induced noradrenergic activity affects neural systems that regulate memory specificity and systems consolidation dynamics. The proposed framework refines current models of memory under emotional arousal and may have relevant implications for stress-related psychopathologies.

items.title: Intervening contexts reshape hippocampal-cortical retrieval states and later source attribution.
items.abstract: Memories are often reactivated in one context and only later judged with respect to where they originally occurred. We tested how an intervening retrieval context shapes neural representations and later source memory. In two fMRI tasks, participants (both male and female) encoded objects within contextual backgrounds, completed an immediate retrieval test in which object cues appeared against either the original background or a different background, and subsequently judged each object's original context on a neutral screen. Shifted cueing contexts reduced source accuracy and biased errors toward the intervening context, despite no detectable difference in immediate recognition or associative-memory performance. Representational similarity analyses showed that encoding patterns reflected original-context structure, whereas immediate-cue-period patterns were broadly organized by the cued (i.e., currently visible) context. On shifted trials, activity patterns showed greater similarity to encoding-derived templates for the cued context than for the original context. Across participants, greater differentiation of original-context similarity between consistent and shifted cueing in posterior hippocampus, parahippocampal cortex, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex was associated with better source memory after a contextual shift. Within participants, precuneus contextual engagement and dorsal anterior cingulate context alignment predicted later source choices, with similar relationships after adjustment for immediate recognition responses. Later source attribution therefore depended on the contextual state expressed when an item was re-encountered, not simply on reinstatement of the original event. Significance statement Remembering is often described as bringing up the past, but memories are frequently reactivated in new contexts before we judge where they came from. We show that this intervening context can bias later source attribution even when that context is no longer visible at final test. Using two fMRI tasks, representational similarity analysis and trial-level source-choice models, we found that cue-period activity was organized by the context present during cueing and that specific context-state signals predicted later memory choices, whereas item reinstatement did not. Source-memory errors can therefore reflect contextual information encountered after the original event, not only failures to recover the original context.

items.title: Phase-Structured Neuronal Recruitment in Motor Cortex during Skilled Movement Reorganized Early after Stroke.
items.abstract: Skilled forelimb movement engages both oscillatory and spiking activity in the motor cortex. However, how oscillatory phase organizes neuronal recruitment during behavior remains unclear. Here, we performed longitudinal bilateral recordings of local field potentials and single-unit activity in the rat (male) caudal forelimb area during a single-pellet retrieval task before and after stroke. Stroke altered spectral organization and redistributed neuronal recruitment across hemispheres. In the CFA contralateral to the reaching forelimb, which was the lesioned hemisphere, firing rates decreased and spike timing became more variable, whereas spike-LFP phase consistency increased in low-frequency bands. In contrast, the CFA ipsilateral to the reaching forelimb showed increased firing and reduced low-frequency phase consistency. These results demonstrate that early post-stroke motor cortical reorganization does not simply weaken neural activity but reshapes neuronal recruitment into a phase-structured form within ongoing oscillatory activity, providing insight into the dynamical principles underlying motor cortical reorganization during skilled movement. Significance Statement Skilled movement depends on coordinated interactions between populationlevel oscillations and neuronal spiking, but how this organization changes after cortical injury remains unclear. Using longitudinal bilateral recordings during skilled forelimb behavior, we show that early post-stroke reorganization is not characterized by a uniform loss of cortical activity. In the CFA contralateral to the reaching forelimb, firing was reduced and spike timing became more variable, yet low-frequency spike-LFP phase consistency increased. The ipsilateral CFA showed the opposite pattern, with increased firing and reduced low-frequency phase consistency. These findings demonstrate that firing output and spike-phase organization can reorganize independently after stroke, revealing a phase-structured dimension of motor cortical activity that is not captured by firing rate alone.

items.title: Multidimensional dynamics of object representations in the human visual system.
items.abstract: Natural image representations are distributed across many dimensions of visual cortex activity, but little is known about how the multidimensional structure of these representations evolves over time following stimulus onset. Herewe examined the temporal dynamics and latent dimensional structure of natural object representations in large-scale EEG and MEG data from male and female human participants. We also compared these datawith leading representational models derived from large-scale human similarity judgments and deep neural networks. Our findings reveal a rapid expansion of stimulus dimensionality in the brain, which peaks within 100 milliseconds and gradually decays over hundreds of milliseconds. The dynamics of these dimensionality changes tracked the decoding accuracy for both behavioral embeddings and neural network features, suggesting that dimensionality may be a general indicator of representational expressivity. Interestingly, the dimensionality of the neural representations could not be fully explained by a leading behavior-based model or deep neural network. Follow-up experiments showed that the remaining neural variance carried additional perceptually relevant information not yet explained by leading models. Together, these findings reveal previously unrecognized complexity in measurements of dynamic human brain responses to natural objects. Significance Statement When we look at an object, our brains rapidly construct a rich internal representation of what we see. Using large-scale, time-resolved brain recordings from people viewing thousands of natural images, we find that the brain rapidly expands its representational complexity within the first 100 milliseconds, sustaining this richness for hundreds of milliseconds thereafter. A leading behavioral model and a large-scale deep neural network do not fully account for this complexity - yet the unexplained brain activity is not noise: people can reliably use these residual neural patterns to judge image similarity. These findings challenge the assumption that such brain recordings are informationally limited and reveal structure in the human visual system that future models will need to explain.

items.title: Relative Contribution of Individual and Environmental Determinants of Sleep in a French Adult Population.
items.abstract: Insufficient sleep is a major public health concern. Many factors influence sleep, including light exposure, physical activity, and the bedroom environment. The objective of this observational study was to identify the main factors influencing sleep. A total of 195 healthy participants (61% female; 22-74 years) were monitored for eight consecutive days. Environmental, physiological and behavioural variables (light exposure, heart rate, physical activity, and bedroom conditions) and individual characteristics (age, sex, chronotype, and anxiety level) were collected. Regression tree models were used to identify the main determinants of sleep quality. Sleep efficiency was mainly influenced by sex, with women showing a higher efficiency (88% vs. 85%). In men, anxiety was associated with lower sleep efficiency (77% vs. 85%), whereas in women, nighttime noise ≥ 40 dB was associated with reduced sleep efficiency (85% vs. 89%). Slow wave sleep was determined by age and sleep timing, reaching 16% in individuals aged ≥ 50 years, 19% in those aged 34-50 years, and 23% in younger individuals with an earlier sleep midpoint. A later sleep midpoint (≥ 4.3 h) was associated with more nocturnal awakenings (57 vs. 38). Total sleep time was higher in women than men (414 vs. 382 min). This study suggests that both environmental and individual factors are associated with sleep quality and emerged as key determinants of sleep outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of considering both types of factors in sleep and support more personalized approaches to intervention. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and better characterize sleep determinants.

items.title: Coordinate-Based fMRI Meta-Analyses of Episodic Memory Encoding and Retrieval in Depression.
items.abstract: Background Depression is a mood disorder frequently associated with episodic memory impairment. However, it remains unclear whether functional brain activity differs between depressed and non-depressed individuals during encoding or retrieval of autobiographical or non-autobiographical memories. Clarifying these differences is important for refining theoretical models of memory impairment in depression and, potentially, for developing targeted interventions. Methods We conducted three coordinate-based meta-analyses examining encoding and retrieval of autobiographical and non-autobiographical memory in control participants and individuals with current, remitted, or subthreshold depression, or those at risk for depression. Studies were identified via database searches and analysed using Seed-based d Mapping. Results We included coordinates from 22 fMRI studies. During encoding, depression was associated with reduced activity in the caudate, and in regions associated with salience processing, frontoparietal control, and motor functions (11 studies, N = 542). During non-autobiographical retrieval, depression was associated with higher activity in the right inferior frontal gyrus (7 studies, N = 345). During autobiographical retrieval (10 studies, N = 433), depression was associated with reduced activity in the right insula and fusiform gyrus, alongside increased activity in the left anterior cingulate cortex and the left middle frontal gyrus. Between-study heterogeneity was low and no evidence for publication bias was found. Conclusions Our results indicate that depression may be associated with impaired salience integration during encoding and autobiographical retrieval. In contrast, during non-autobiographical retrieval, increased frontal activity suggests a more vigilant or self-monitoring retrieval mode. Functional brain activity changes in depression therefore appear stage- and content-specific.

items.title: Dietary Lutein, Vegetable and Nut Intake, and Open-Angle Glaucoma: The Maastricht Study.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate whether total dietary lutein intake, intake of lutein derived from major lutein-rich food groups, and consumption of those lutein-rich food groups themselves are associated with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) and related ocular parameters. Design Cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from The Maastricht Study. Participants Community-dwelling adults aged 40-75 years (N = 5,613), including 442 participants with OAG. Methods Dietary intake over the preceding year was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire to estimate total dietary lutein intake, source-specific lutein intake (from vegetables, fruit, eggs, and nuts), and consumption of these foods. Glaucoma was classified from standard automated perimetry (Heidelberg Edge Perimeter) with independent specialist review. Intraocular pressure (IOP) was measured by non-contact tonometry, and retinal structural parameters (peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer and ganglion cell complex) were obtained by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT). Eye-level generalized and linear mixed-effects models with participant-level random intercepts were used, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and metabolic covariates. Main outcome measures Open-angle glaucoma, IOP, and OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses. Results Total dietary lutein intake was not significantly associated with OAG prevalence (odds ratio [OR] per standard deviation [SD] increase, 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.87-1.09). Among source-specific lutein analyses, only lutein derived from nuts was associated with lower odds of OAG (OR, 0.86; 95%CI, 0.75-0.98 per SD increase), whereas lutein derived from vegetables, fruit, and eggs was not. In the analyses of lutein-rich food group consumption, higher vegetable intake (OR, 0.84; 95%CI, 0.75-0.95 per SD increase) and higher nut intake (OR, 0.86; 95%CI, 0.75-0.98 per SD increase) were each associated with lower odds of OAG, whereas fruit and egg intake were not. Neither dietary lutein intake nor consumption of lutein-rich food were associated with IOP or OCT structural measures. Conclusions Total dietary lutein intake was not significantly associated with OAG prevalence, whereas higher vegetable and nut intakes were associated with lower odds of OAG. These findings support examining total dietary and source-specific lutein intake alongside consumption of the lutein-rich foods.

items.title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
items.abstract: Objective To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis. Methods This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality. Results In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9). Conclusion Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

items.title: Neuroprotective effects of ropinirole against nicotine- and ethanol-induced cognitive impairment, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurodegenerative alterations in rats.
items.abstract: Background Adolescence is a critical period of brain development during which exposure to addictive substances may adversely affect cognitive function and neuronal plasticity. Combined nicotine and ethanol exposure may contribute to persistent cognitive impairment through disturbances in oxidative balance, inflammatory signaling, and hippocampal function. However, the potential effects of pharmacological interventions targeting these alterations after exposure remain insufficiently characterized. Given the previously reported neuroprotective properties of ropinirole, this study investigated whether post-exposure treatment with this dopamine D2/D3 receptor agonist could attenuate cognitive deficits and associated hippocampal biochemical alterations in rats subjected to adolescent nicotine-ethanol co-exposure. Methods Male Wistar rats were exposed to nicotine (2 mg/kg/day, intraperitoneally) and ethanol (20% v/v in drinking water) during adolescence (postnatal days 21-48). Following the exposure period, animals received oral ropinirole at doses of 5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for three weeks. Spatial learning and memory and recognition memory were assessed using the Morris water maze and novel object recognition tests, respectively. Hippocampal biochemical assessments included malondialdehyde (MDA), nitrite, total thiol content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and amyloid-β (Aβ). Results Nicotine-ethanol co-exposure significantly impaired spatial learning, memory retention, and recognition memory, accompanied by increased hippocampal MDA, nitrite, TNF-α, AChE activity, and Aβ levels, together with reduced antioxidant capacity, IL-10, and BDNF expression. Post-exposure ropinirole treatment improved performance in the behavioral tests and attenuated several of the associated biochemical alterations. The 20 mg/kg dose generally showed the most pronounced effects among the doses tested; however, a formal dose-response relationship was not established. Conclusion These findings suggest that ropinirole exerts neuroprotective effects against adolescent nicotine-ethanol-induced cognitive impairment through the modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, cholinergic dysfunction, neurotrophic signaling, and amyloid-related pathways. These results provide preliminary evidence supporting dopaminergic modulation as a potential strategy for mitigating substance-associated cognitive dysfunction, although further mechanistic and translational studies are necessary.

items.title: Glymphatic dysfunction in epilepsy: imaging assessment, comorbidities, pathophysiology, and emerging therapeutic perspectives.
items.abstract: Epilepsy is a prevalent neurological disorder driven by complex, multifactorial mechanisms, yet seizures remain uncontrolled in a substantial proportion of patients despite treatment. The glymphatic system, a brain-wide cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange pathway that facilitates metabolic waste clearance, has emerged as an important regulator of cerebral homeostasis. Accumulating experimental and neuroimaging evidence suggests that glymphatic-related processes may be involved in epileptogenesis and disease progression, although their precise roles remain to be established. This narrative review summarizes advances in the assessment of glymphatic-related processes and synthesizes findings across epilepsy subtypes. We examine how these findings relate to cognitive, sleep, and psychiatric comorbidities, as well as treatment outcomes. We interpret findings from complementary imaging approaches in their clinical context, considering epilepsy phenotype and disease course alongside accompanying white matter and network changes. This synthesis highlights the potential clinical significance of these findings and the limitations of current evidence while distinguishing observed associations from proposed mechanisms. We further discuss emerging therapeutic strategies as hypotheses for testing and outline considerations for initial proof-of-concept studies. Because most clinical studies rely on indirect imaging markers and include small patient cohorts, causal relationships and the clinical utility of these markers remain uncertain. Future studies combining standardized multimodal imaging, experimental models, and prospective clinical cohorts are needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and establish the clinical value of glymphatic-related findings in epilepsy.

items.title: Cerebellar structural and electrophysiological alterations associated with neuropathic pain in mice.
items.abstract: The cerebellum is increasingly implicated in pain, yet direct electrophysiology in neuropathy is scarce. We tested whether sciatic nerve chronic constriction injury (CCI) alters cerebellar dynamics and structure. Adult male mice underwent CCI, von Frey testing, structural MRI, spontaneous LFP recordings in lobules IV-V, and spontaneous/evoked single-unit recordings under anesthesia. CCI produced rapid, persistent mechanical hypersensitivity. Deformation-based morphometry (DBM) revealed regional volumetric alterations including localized contractions in the IV-V cerebellar lobules. Spontaneous LFPs showed reduced absolute δ/θ power, with unchanged relative (normalized) power, while β/γ were unchanged. Multi-unit activity in CCI mice exhibited higher firing rates, shorter inter-spike intervals, and larger spike amplitudes. Peripheral stimulation evoked larger responses in CCI. Neuropathic pain is associated with structural remodeling, suppressed spontaneous slow-band cerebellar activity and enhanced unit/evoked responsiveness, which we interpret, as a working hypothesis, as a low-synchrony/high-gain operating regime. These structural and electrophysiological changes are candidate signatures that motivate future mechanistic and causal studies of cerebellar involvement in neuropathic pain.

items.title: Sexual Experience Modulates Conditioned Preference for Morphine in Female Long-Evans Rats.
items.abstract: Sexually experienced female rats, compared to naïve rats, return to the male more quickly after receiving sexual stimulations, spend more time with the male, and display more proceptive behaviors during paced mating. Additionally, rewarding effects of mating are greater in sexually experienced relative to naïve female rats. A number of findings led to the hypothesis that experienced-induced neuroplasticity in the endogenous opioid system may be responsible for sexual experience changes in display of paced mating behavior and mating-induced reward. To test whether reward mediated by the opioid system differed between sexually experienced and naïve female rats, we asked whether rats would exhibit a conditioned object preference (COP) for 0.5, 1, or 2 mg/kg morphine. Ovariectomized, Long-Evans female rats were primed with estradiol benzoate and progesterone and either exposed to an empty paced mating chamber for 15 min (Naïve) or received a 15-intromission test of paced mating behavior (Experienced) on four separate occasions before undergoing the COP procedure for morphine. We predicted that sexual experience would lead to a sensitized opioid system reflected by conditioned preference for lower doses of morphine in experienced vs. naïve rats. Instead, we found that naïve female rats exhibited a conditioned object preference for all three doses of morphine, whereas experienced female rats exhibited a conditioned object preference only for 2 mg/kg morphine. In addition to illustrating that the opioid system is altered by sexual experience, these findings provide insight into the involvement of endogenous opioids in experience-enhanced paced mating behavior.

items.title: The World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement: 2026 Update.
items.abstract: Background In the 5 years since the publication of the original ADHD International Consensus Statement, a great deal of new evidence has emerged. This updated consensus statement reflects the current state of the science with respect to ADHD, with a goal of reducing misconceptions and stigma around the disorder. Methods Studies eligible for inclusion were published between January 1, 2021 and July 1, 2025 and were either: 1) large cohort studies of 2000 or more participants, or 2) meta-analyses of at least 5 studies or 2000 participants in which publication bias was considered. Eligible studies were summarized and consolidated by theme. Manuscript contents were reviewed and approved by 118 authors from 29 countries and 6 continents. Results Two hundred and fifty-two empirically-supported statements were generated from these studies, offering readers an up-to-date understanding of the most robust findings in the areas of prevalence, how genes and environmental factors shape ADHD, psychiatric and somatic comorbidities, cognitive and neurological differences among individuals with ADHD, functional outcomes, and treatments for the disorder. Conclusions Many of the conclusions of the original Consensus Statement are supported, but this update adds important nuance to some findings as a result of more recent evidence. It also highlights a few areas in which the balance of findings has shifted in the last 5 years, providing a transparent overview of the current scientific state of the field.

items.title: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
items.abstract: Chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction provide distinct settings in which inflammatory responses and persistent vulnerability may intersect. Evidence for specific cytokine, synaptic, and microglial mechanisms differs across these conditions and does not establish a single comorbidity mechanism. We examine whether circadian context influences the formation or later expression of neuroimmune memory. Circadian regulation of inflammatory responses and innate immune memory each have experimental support, while their coupling in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved. Human BCG vaccination studies provide a peripheral timing-and-training precedent, which cannot be assumed to operate in the brain. We distinguish immune memory from ongoing inflammation, neuronal chromatin regulation, and sustained symptoms, and separate cell-autonomous microglial timing from rhythmic environmental inputs. The framework generates distinct tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal. A convincing test requires a resolved first challenge, control of initial inflammatory exposure and recall phase, and cell-resolved molecular measurements coupled to altered secondary-response function. Failure to reverse an established imprint would not exclude a role for timing during its formation. Perioperative studies offer a defined exposure but must distinguish delirium from longer-term cognitive decline. This evidence-calibrated hypothesis specifies what must be demonstrated before circadian interventions can be linked to prevention or modification of neuroimmune memory.

items.title: A Metabolite-Centered Framework for Microbiota-Gut-Brain Communication Linking Constrained Signaling to Behavior and Stress Physiology.
items.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis links gut microbial activity with host neurophysiology and behavior, but its mechanistic interpretation remains fragmented across individual metabolites, biological compartments, and experimental systems. Here, we propose a metabolite-centered conceptual framework that organizes current evidence according to the constraints that determine whether microbial metabolic activity is translated into host effects, including metabolite production and host transformation, bioavailability and barrier access, host sensing, cross-system integration, and ultimately phenotype. Using short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan metabolic pathways, bile acids, neurotransmitter-related compounds, and emerging microbial signals as representative examples, we synthesize evidence for receptor-mediated, metabolic, neuroimmune, neuroendocrine, and barrier-dependent mechanisms. We further distinguish microbiota-level from metabolite-specific causality and preclinical from human evidence across stress reactivity, affective and stress-coping responses, social interaction, learning and memory, feeding, and sleep/circadian regulation. Finally, we evaluate the translational potential of metabolite-targeted interventions and biomarkers while highlighting unresolved challenges related to source attribution, bioavailability, species translation, and causal inference. Rather than providing another catalogue of microbial metabolites, this Review presents a mechanistic framework that links microbial metabolism to neural and behavioral outcomes while identifying the evidence needed to advance toward reproducible and clinically relevant applications.

items.title: Molecular basis of behavioral and cognitive changes induced by neurotropic viruses.
items.abstract: Neurotropic viruses induce behavioral and cognitive alterations through diverse molecular and cellular mechanisms that extend beyond simple neuronal damage. Comparative analysis of rabies virus (RABV), pseudorabies virus (PRV), Borna disease virus (BoDV-1), SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus (NiV), West Nile virus (WNV) and Herpes Simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) reveals distinct pathogenic strategies targeting specific neural circuits. While neuroinflammation characterized by microglial activation, astrocytic responses, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production contributes significantly to synaptic and network dysfunction in WNV and NiV infections, other mechanisms predominate in different pathogens. RABV selectively disrupts cholinergic, serotonergic, and glutamate/GABAergic pathways while preserving neuronal integrity to facilitate transmission, whereas BoDV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 induce dopaminergic and serotonergic dysfunctions through persistent immune activation and endothelial damage. Additionally, systemic factors such as the gut-brain axis and microbiome alterations, particularly evident in SARS-CoV-2 infection, modulate neurotransmitter metabolism and neuroimmune responses. Considering the lack of even diffuse neuronal loss observed during infection, behavioral changes may arise more from selective, circuit-dependent vulnerabilities, involving specific disruptions to emotion, cognition, and motor control networks. To provide a clear review of the knowledge regarding how targeted neuronal population alterations translate into behavioral phenotypes, we here integrate molecular, cellular, and systems-level insights across these seven neurotropic viruses used as models, with the aim of identifying common pathways linking infection to behavioral changes and cognitive dysfunction. Understanding these discrete mechanisms ranging from acute synaptic manipulation to long-lasting neuroimmune dysregulation is essential for developing therapeutic strategies that address both the infectious agent and the specific neural networks mediating acute disturbances and long-term neurological sequelae.

items.title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest.
items.abstract: Objectives Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images. Methods Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy. Results Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort. Conclusion In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

items.title: Principles of large-scale cortical organization across species: network properties and hierarchical gradients.
items.abstract: Here we address the question of fundamental organizational principles of cortex at its largest scale, as informed by increasingly coherent findings coming from comparative studies from rodents to primates. At such a scale, inter-areal network properties, hierarchy and gradients across cortex become such principles. The specific arrangement of the network architecture evolves as a function of brain size. It follows a deeper, common principle ensured by the physical embeddedness of the brain and characterized by an Exponential Distance Rule. Anatomical hierarchy, based on laminar projection patterns, deepens with network size and sparsity, and thus opens the structural possibility for enhanced function segregation, areal differentiation and specialization. Such changes may give rise to a series of large-scale gradients that can be used to define each area's specific functional and dynamical properties. Extrapolated to the human brain, such properties could facilitate translational research and help better understand brain disorders.

items.title: Working memory capacity moderates stress-related drinking in alcohol use disorder: An intensive one-year ecological assessment study.
items.abstract: Background Stress is a trigger for alcohol consumption, with working memory capacity (WMC) proposed as a protective factor. While several laboratory-based and cross-sectional studies point toward an interaction between WMC, stress, and alcohol consumption, ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) are needed to establish this relationship in real-life contexts, where alcohol consumption and stress experiences actually take place. Methods In this one-year longitudinal EMA study, we collected data from a gamified, smartphone-based WMC task (every 4 weeks) and EMAs of stress and alcohol consumption (every two days) from n=603 participants diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD). We then integrated this data with structural brain imaging data to explore the neural correlates of the hypothesized moderating effect of WMC. Results As preregistered, we found that WMC moderated the within-subject association between stress and alcohol consumption. Participants with low WMC, but not participants with high WMC, consumed more alcohol in more stressful compared to less stressful months. In further analysis, within-subject fluctuations in WMC also moderated the within-subject association between stress and drinking. Although effects were in the expected direction, the moderating effect of WMC was not mediated by neural correlates of interest (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and insula). Conclusions We provide first real-life evidence that greater WMC might increase resilience to stress-related drinking in individuals with AUD. This advances our neurocognitive understanding of individual susceptibility to stress-related drinking, which could inform the development of future, personalized interventions.

items.title: Do Bibliometric and Scientometric Studies in Medical Research Require Library Science Experts for Peer Review? Evidence from 118,484 Publications.
items.abstract: Background Bibliometric research is expanding in health sciences, highlighting the need for methodological expertise in peer review. The importance of Library and Information Science (LIS) expertise was highlighted in an international advocacy letter by leaders (presidents and national managers) of four major health library associations from Canada, Europe, the USA and Australia. Objective To assess bibliometric research trends and journal representation in medical and health sciences and explore the role of LIS specialists in methodological peer review. Methods Scopus was used as the primary data source. Three complementary searches employed bibliometric-, scientometric- and citation-related terms across title-abstract-keyword, abstract-only and title-only fields. A separate title-based search covered eight Scopus subject areas: Medicine, Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology, Psychology, Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics, Nursing, Health Professions, Immunology and Microbiology, and Neuroscience. Annual publication trends and journal distributions were examined descriptively. Results The three search approaches identified 118,484, 93,544 and 54,790 records, respectively. From 2000 to 2025, annual output increased from 315 to 18,343 in title-abstract-keyword searches, 161 to 16,012 in abstract searches, and 78 to 9,955 in title searches. The medical and health-related search identified 19,750 publications, including 12,901 (65.3%) published during 2020-2025. Annual output rose from 711 in 2020 to 3,819 in 2025. Eighty-five journals published at least 25 relevant records, led by Medicine (740), Frontiers in Oncology (329), Asian Journal of Surgery (311) and Frontiers in Medicine (310). Conclusion The growth of bibliometric research warrants specialised methodological review involving LIS specialists and experienced bibliometric researchers.

items.title: Clinical recommendations on monitoring and management of bone health in adults with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and transition to adult care: A national Delphi consensus study.
items.abstract: Poor bone health and low-trauma fractures are common in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), reflecting the combined effects of progressive muscle weakness, reduced mechanical loading, delayed puberty and/or hypogonadism, and long-term glucocorticoid exposure. Although paediatric bone health guidance in DMD is well established, adult-specific recommendations remain limited, particularly for individuals who enter adult services having received many years of bisphosphonate therapy during childhood or adolescence. We developed national expert consensus recommendations for the monitoring and management of bone health in adults with DMD, with particular emphasis on transition from paediatric to adult care. Recommendations were informed by review of the literature, a clinician survey, input from adults with DMD and carers, and discussion within a multidisciplinary expert group. A modified Delphi process was undertaken, with 16 clinicians voting on draft statements using a 9-point agreement scale; consensus was defined as at least 80% of participants scoring 7-9. Thirteen evidence-informed expert consensus clinical recommendations were agreed, covering fracture risk assessment, DXA and vertebral fracture monitoring, vitamin D and gonadal status, indications for specialist bone review, initiation and review of osteoporosis therapy, management of possible treatment failure, and structured review of long-term therapy during transition. The recommendations emphasise individualised decision-making, recognising the technical challenges of imaging, limited adult DMD-specific evidence, cumulative treatment burden, and the functional impact of fractures in this population. These consensus recommendations provide a practical framework to support adult neuromuscular and bone clinicians managing bone health in a rare, high-risk and increasingly adult DMD population.

items.title: Persistent autism-like behaviors and multilevel neurobiological abnormalities following prenatal valproic acid exposure in rats.
items.abstract: Prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure is widely used to model autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the persistence of its behavioral effects and the accompanying multilevel neurobiological abnormalities remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated behavioral, histological, morphological, electrophysiological, molecular, metabolomic, and epigenomic analyses to characterize the long-term effects of prenatal VPA exposure in rats from early postnatal life through adulthood. Prenatal VPA exposure caused delayed early development and persistent ASD-like phenotypes, including repetitive behaviors, impaired social interaction, anxiety-like behavior, reduced exploration, and cognitive deficits. These behavioral abnormalities were accompanied by neuronal and glial alterations and reduced dendritic complexity and spine density in the medial prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, as well as reduced excitatory and inhibitory synaptic inputs and decreased expression of key synaptic proteins in the medial prefrontal cortex. Multi-omics profiling further identified candidate metabolic alterations involving membrane lipid remodeling, neuromodulatory metabolism, and inflammatory lipid signaling, alongside bidirectional, locus-specific DNA methylation changes enriched in neurodevelopmental and synaptic pathways. Together, these findings show that prenatal VPA exposure produces persistent ASD-like phenotypes accompanied by multilevel cellular, structural, synaptic, metabolic, and epigenetic abnormalities. This work provides an integrated framework for understanding the long-term consequences of prenatal VPA exposure and supports the VPA model as a valuable platform for investigating mechanisms underlying ASD.

items.title: Whole-genome phylogenomics and synteny support a single origin of body-plan asymmetry in flatfishes.
items.abstract: Flatfishes exhibit the most extreme body asymmetry among vertebrates. During metamorphosis, one eye migrates across the dorsal midline of the skull, producing an adult that lies and swims on one side with both eyes on the upper side. Whether this body plan evolved once or repeatedly has been debated for over a century, with important implications for the evolution of the underlying developmental program. A recent genome-wide study supported multiple origins by placing Psettodes, the earliest-diverging flatfish, among symmetric relatives in Carangaria, the group that also includes billfishes, jacks, mahi-mahi, and barracudas. Later work traced that result to base-composition artifacts and inadequate substitution models. Here, we revisit the question using whole-genome phylogenomic and synteny data from 17 fish species. We add three new chromosome-level genome assemblies, including the first for Psettodes. Coalescent and other analyses of nucleotide data strongly support a single origin, with Psettodes placed as sister to other flatfishes. Microsynteny, measured from conserved gene-order blocks, supports the same result, whereas macrosynteny, based on chromosome-scale rearrangements, provides limited and reference-dependent support. This pattern likely reflects the different rates at which these changes accumulate. Gene-order rearrangements were frequent enough to resolve the short internodes of the rapid post-Cretaceous radiation of Carangaria, whereas chromosome-scale rearrangements accumulated too slowly to provide meaningful resolution. Together with shared developmental mechanisms and extensive fossil evidence, our results support a single origin of flatfish asymmetry, with gene order providing evidence independent of nucleotide substitution.

items.title: Cerebrospinal fluid lipidome in central nervous system infections: a study of diagnostic accuracy.
items.abstract: Diagnosing central nervous system (CNS) infections can be challenging when no pathogen is detected, emphasising the need for new diagnostics. We assessed the diagnostic accuracy of lipids in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for diagnosing CNS infections. Episodes were derived from four prospective community-acquired CNS infection cohorts. Three Dutch cohorts were used for the discovery and internal validation. An independent Danish cohort was used for external validation. All studies included adults with confirmed or suspected CNS infections who underwent a diagnostic lumbar puncture. Lipidomics, the index test, was conducted on CSF using liquid chromatography high resolution mass spectrometry. Microbiologically confirmed diagnoses were the reference standard. In total, 229 episodes were included in the discovery cohort. A CNS infection occurred in 81/229 (35%) episodes and consisted of bacterial meningitis in 39 (17%), viral meningoencephalitis in 31 (14%) and other CNS infections in 11 (5%). We analysed 626 lipid species across 33 classes and identified a distinct profile for bacterial meningitis. Elevated Hex2Cer [d] showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for bacterial meningitis: area under the curve (AUC) = 0·98 (95% CI 0·97-1·00) when compared to all other diagnoses and AUC = 0·98 (95% CI 0·96-1·00) when compared to viral meningoencephalitis. Among episodes with CSF leucocytes between 5 and 1000 cells/mm3, Hex2Cer [d] remained the best predictor. These findings were supported by the internal and external validation cohorts. Lipid alterations in CSF, particularly Hex2Cer [d], have high diagnostic accuracy for bacterial meningitis, highlighting their potential as a diagnostic biomarker. items.title: Circulating angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers for cerebral edema and infarcts in women with eclampsia or severe preeclampsia.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether circulating concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers are associated with cerebral edema and infarcts in women with eclampsia or preeclampsia with severe features. This prospective observational study included 45 women with eclampsia and 20 women with preeclampsia between April 2018 to November 2019. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed to assess cerebral edema and infarcts. Plasma samples were collected at inclusion and analyzed for concentrations of neurofilament light (NfL), tau, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), placental growth factor (PlGF), soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1 (sFlt-1), and soluble endoglin (sEng). Concentrations were compared between women with or without cerebral edema and infarcts. Main outcome measures MRI findings of cerebral edema and infarcts. Among women with eclampsia, concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers did not differ according to the presence of cerebral edema or infarcts on MRI. In women with preeclampsia and cerebral edema (n = 4), concentrations of sFlt-1, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, and sEng were higher than in women without edema (n = 16), with adjusted fold changes (95% CI) of 4.21 (2.42-7.33), 6.10 (1.42-26.20), and 1.68 (1.10-2.56), respectively. The single woman with preeclampsia and cerebral infarcts had markedly elevated concentrations of several cerebral and angiogenic biomarkers. Concentrations of angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers were not associated with the presence of cerebral edema or infarcts in women with eclampsia. Among women with preeclampsia, higher concentrations of several angiogenic and cerebral biomarkers were observed in women with cerebral edema or infarcts, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts.

items.title: Cognitive training mitigates the detrimental effect of interference on working memory.
items.abstract: Working memory (WM) is essential for maintaining task-relevant information in dynamic environments, yet its efficiency is often compromised by external interference. While cognitive training has been proposed as a method to enhance WM function, evidence for far transfer - particularly to interference-laden, real-world tasks - remains limited. In this longitudinal study, we evaluated whether a three-month, multi-domain cognitive training program could improve WM performance under interference among 127 corporate professionals. Participants were randomly assigned to either an immediate training group or a waitlist group and completed a novel Working Memory with External Interference (WMEI) task before and after training. A subsample of 95 individuals completed 2- and 4-month follow-up sessions as well. The WMEI assessed participants' ability to retrieve rule-based information following distracting interference, mimicking high-load workplace scenarios. Analyses revealed no significant changes in retrieval accuracy, but improvement in retrieval latency post-training. Difference-in-differences modeling provided evidence consistent with a genuine training effect, above and beyond practice or time-related factors, though the contribution of non-linear practice effects cannot be fully excluded. Exploratory analyses suggested that improvements may have been more pronounced in female participants. These findings suggest that cognitive training can enhance the efficiency - but not the accuracy - of WM retrieval under interference, supporting a more nuanced view of transfer effects. By employing ecologically valid tasks, this study advances our understanding of how cognitive interventions can foster functional gains in high-demand professional contexts.

items.title: Repeated Online Surveillance of Stress and Stress Management Effectiveness in Australian Adults (FocUS-R): Mixed Methods Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Trials of stress management interventions have shown modest and inconsistent effects. Emerging evidence suggests that structural constraints may limit the real-world effectiveness of behavioral strategies, yet this process has rarely been examined empirically. Population-level tools for monitoring stress and stress management processes over time remain limited. This study aimed to develop and pilot a mixed methods surveillance platform for repeated measurement of stress and stress management effectiveness in real-world contexts and to assess its feasibility, validity, and ability to detect equity-relevant patterns. Adults living in Australia completed baseline assessments including sociodemographics, perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale, 10-item version), psychological flexibility (Multidimensional Psychological Flexibility Inventory), social resources, and health measures. Participants then completed brief fortnightly surveillance surveys for up to 12 months, comprising 0 to 10 Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) ratings of stress and perceived stress management effectiveness, a stress-related symptom checklist, and open-ended reporting of stressors and coping strategies. We assessed feasibility, convergent validity of early VAS indicators, and preliminary equity patterning. Seventy-seven participants completed baseline measures, and 1195 fortnightly check-ins were recorded as of June 2025. Early VAS stress demonstrated strong convergent validity with baseline perceived stress and stress symptoms. Despite the pilot recruitment skewing toward higher socioeconomic status, clear gradients were observed in both stress and stress management. Lower-income participants reported higher stress, lower perceived stress management, and fewer good stress management check-ins. Psychological flexibility was positively associated with stress management overall, but showed weaker associations among lower-income participants. Brief, repeated stress surveillance is feasible and can generate equity-informative signals. Pilot findings support a model in which adaptive skills are widely available, but their effective expression is shaped by structural conditions. The FocUS-R (Focus on Understanding Stress, Resilience, and Adaptability) platform may provide a scalable approach for monitoring population stress processes and identifying contexts where structural constraints may limit the effectiveness of behavioral strategies.

items.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats.
items.abstract: The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. This framework revealed that the decoded latent neural states closely tracked behavior. Furthermore, during alcohol-reinforced sessions, neural and behavioral measures of drinking or non-drinking states were strongly aligned in both strains. However, after alcohol devaluation, this alignment diverged in P rats but remained consistent in Wistars. The inability of P rats to acquire stable neural states following devaluation suggests impaired formation of latent states as a neural mechanism of ARD, offering insights into the cognitive vulnerabilities that may sustain AUD.

items.title: Hierarchical data-driven dynamical surrogate models of social decision-making.
items.abstract: Social decision making is inherently complex, shaped by dynamic trust building, biases, and adaptive strategies. Yet in laboratory settings, its study is often constrained by small datasets that nonetheless encode rich and sophisticated cognitive processes. This scarcity has historically limited modeling approaches to hand-tailored frameworks that embed strong priors about the underlying mechanisms. Recent advances in data-driven modeling of latent dynamical processes provide an alternative, extracting generative models directly from behavioral data without restrictive assumptions. Building on these methods, we derive hierarchical digital surrogates from sparse, non-Gaussian investment sequences in repeated trust games. Our approach proceeds in three stages. First, we demonstrate that, despite the limited data, the inferred models can accurately predict future investments and outperform theory-driven reinforcement-learning and Bayesian cognitive models, establishing predictive validity and providing a solid baseline for subsequent mechanistic analyses. Second, we analyze the latent dynamics of these models and show that they capture mechanistic structure in how investments and choice uncertainty are organized in state space and how social versus non-social cues are represented, in a way that parallels patterns observed directly in the empirical behavior. Third, we exploit the generative nature of the hierarchical digital surrogates to run in-silico experiments beyond the original data, such as probing how specific cues steer participants into trusting or mistrusting states and simulating responses to novel, unobserved cue-outcome combinations and trustee strategies. Together, this work demonstrates how generative digital surrogates open a new path toward mechanistic, data-driven accounts of social interaction dynamics that both reproduce observed behavior and support hypothesis generation in virtual environments.

items.title: Changes in air pollution-avoidance behaviour and blood pressure following an AirHealth behavioural intervention among adults in Nigeria: a quasi-experimental study.
items.abstract: This study assessed changes in air pollution-avoidance behaviour and blood pressure (BP) following exposure to a novel co-created AirHealth behavioural intervention among apparently healthy community members in Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pre and postintervention study was conducted among 607 apparently healthy highly exposed adults in Ibadan, Nigeria. Baseline assessment included air pollution-avoidance behaviour, assessed using an 11-item Capacity, Opportunity, and Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) framework, and SBP and DBP, measured following a standardised procedure. The 12-week AirHealth intervention comprised a video documentary and a community-led educational session. Postintervention assessments were conducted to measure changes in COM-B scores and SBP/DBP as 'unimproved' versus 'improved' behaviour and BP, respectively. A paired t-test and linear mixed-effects model were used to evaluate the differences, while a multivariate regression model was used to determine the predictors of unimproved behaviour and BP. At baseline, the mean SBP and DBP were 130.3 ± 30.6 and 76.6 ± 16.8 mmHg, respectively. Following the AirHealth intervention, there was a significant reduction in mean SBP (4.58 mmHg, 95% confidence interval: 1.43-7.74), while the reduction in mean DBP was not significant. Multivariate analysis showed that unimproved behaviour (aOR 2.87; 95% CI: 1.87-3.80) was an independent predictor of unimproved BP among the apparently healthy population. The AirHealth intervention was associated with improved air pollution-avoidance behaviour and reduced SBP among apparently healthy adults in Nigeria. These findings suggest that behavioural strategies targeting air pollution exposure may have potential for improving air pollution-avoidance practices and BP at the population level.

items.title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause.
items.abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman's lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing "estrogen protection hypothesis," which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

items.title: Functional connectivity profile of the amygdala subfields associates with emotional well-being in aging.
items.abstract: Amygdala-related functional connectivity (FC) plays a crucial role in human emotion, cognition, and mental well-being. The amygdala is a highly heterogeneous structure, with subregions that have both distinct and overlapping functions. However, the connectivity patterns of different amygdala subregions, and how these associations vary with age, remain poorly understood. Functional MRI data were analyzed from 68 younger adults and 66 older adults during movie watching in a 7-T MRI scanner. Partial least squares (PLS) analysis was used to identify latent variables capturing variance associated with age-related differences in the FC patterns of three amygdala subregions: the basolateral (BLA), centromedial (CMA), and superficial (SFA) nuclei. In addition, covariance between behavioral measures, including emotional resilience and cognitive function, and FC of these subregions were examined. We further explored correspondence with large-scale brain networks, the associated cognitive processes in Neurosynth, and the spatial distributions of neurotransmitter receptors of the identified connectivity patterns of the BLA, CMA, and SFA. Multivariate analyses revealed that functional connectivity patterns of amygdala subregions related to emotional resilience largely overlapped across widespread brain regions; however, their associations differed by age. During negative movie viewing, stronger coupling of amygdala subregions with the cortex were associated with higher emotional resilience in older adults but lower emotional resilience in younger adults. Associations with cognitive function were weaker and less consistent across subregions. The identified connectivity patterns were linked to the salience, control, and default mode networks and showed spatial correspondence with mGluR5 and 5-HT6 receptor distributions. These findings highlight age-dependent reorganization of amygdala-related networks that support emotional resilience and provide novel insights into the functional connectivity patterns associated with emotional well-being in younger and older adults.

items.title: Interactions Between Cancer and the Nervous System: a Review of Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Cancer Neuroscience.
items.abstract: The emerging field of cancer neuroscience investigates how neural activity shapes tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. Recent research aims to define the bidirectional communication between neurons, glial cells, and tumor cells, and to clarify how neural signals influence the tumor microenvironment (TME). Neuronal activity promotes glioma growth via paracrine mediators such as neuroligin-3 (NLGN3), BDNF, TSP-1 and IGF-1, activating PI3K-mTOR signaling and supporting tumor proliferation. Cancer cells also exploit glutamatergic synapses, with AMPA and NMDA receptor activity driving survival and invasion, suggesting opportunities for repurposing antiseizure drugs such as perampanel. Ionic signaling through K⁺ and Ca²⁺ channels further facilitate tumor-neuron coupling. Beyond gliomas, sympathetic and parasympathetic inputs, as well as chronic stress-induced HPA axis activation, modulate angiogenesis, immune evasion, and metastasis. Neural regulation of cancer encompasses neurotrophic signaling, neurotransmitter pathways, ion channel activity, and stress-mediated neuroendocrine responses, collectively shaping tumor biology and revealing novel therapeutic targets.

items.title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for improving apraxia in corticobasal syndrome (CBS): an interventional pilot study.
items.abstract: Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder. We investigated, whether CBS is associated with a GABA deficiency in the cerebral cortex, whether inhibitory repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) affects cortical GABA+/Cr levels, and whether this improves apraxia. In this bicentric, open-label intervention study, we performed 20 daily sessions of inhibitory rTMS, applied over the clinically more affected parietal cortex. Over a period of 6 months, we examined 18 patients using the Apraxia DATE Testscore Version and, in 15 of these patients, measured cortical GABA+/Cr concentrations in the parietal cortex using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS). The secondary endpoints included motor and cognitive performance before and after the intervention. The Intervention revealed an improvement in the DATE Pseudoword subtest (p = 0.025). For the DATE Finger (F) subtest, the analyses showed a significant improvement from pre-intervention to 4 weeks post-intervention (p = < 0.001). Cognitive performance revealed an improvement for the Wordlist Recall in the CERAD-plus battery that remained significant also for the follow-up period (all p < 0.002). The baseline MRS measurements showed a significant deficiency of GABA+/Cr in the parietal cortex on the clinically more severely affected side (p < 0.05) and, post-intervention, a significant increase in GABA+/Cr concentration (p < 0.05). Pearson correlation indicated a marginally significant positive correlation in the DATE-Pseudoword subtest and parietal GABA+/Cr concentration (r = 0.632, p = 0.05). Inhibitory rTMS applied to the clinically more affected parietal cortex in severely affected CBS patients resulted in significant improvements across two apraxia subtests, an improvement of a pre-existing parietal GABA+/Cr deficiency and enhanced cognitive performance.

items.title: Global trade dynamics in captive-bred and wild-sourced reptiles.
items.abstract: Reptiles are among the most intensively harvested and globally traded vertebrates. Driven by their growing global demand and accelerating biodiversity loss, captive breeding has emerged as a key strategy to supply markets while alleviating harvesting pressure on wild populations. Despite hundreds of species being farmed across the world, the effectiveness of this approach remains contested, as a large proportion of reptile species continue to be threatened by trade. Based on global reptile trade reported to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) from 1991 to 2024, we quantified the similarities and differences in scale and network structures of captive-bred and wild-sourced reptile trade and examined the dynamic interactions between these two trade sources. Captive-bred trade accounted for over one-third of total reptile trade volume, involving fewer species (630) than those sourced from the wild (664). Captive-bred expansion was correlated with decreasing wild-sourced trade share and volume, suggesting an immediate restructuring of market composition and a lagged reduction in wild harvesting pressure over time; a 1% increase in previous-year captive-bred supply was linked to a 0.071% decline in current-year wild-sourced trade. The intensity and direction of these trade dynamics reflected both direct socioeconomic factors and a preference-mediated indirect association, with 46 engaged countries/territories identified as wild-sourced oriented and only 12 as captive-bred oriented in both their importing and exporting. Thus, captive breeding could mitigate, albeit to a low extent, the risk of wild overexploitation, with this potential strengthening where demographic, economic, and institutional factors jointly favor substitution across trading roles.
