items.title: Experimental forest gaps increase beetle diversity via abundance-mediated effects.
items.abstract: Forest gaps increase the heterogeneity and energy availability in a forest stand as they are accompanied by higher canopy openness and, under natural conditions, the occurrence of larger quantities of deadwood. Therefore, open-land and deadwood-dependent species may colonise gaps, potentially explaining the frequently reported higher local species diversity of gaps compared to closed forests. Higher energy availability in forest gaps could also increase species abundance, and subsequently diversity, via a 'more individuals' mechanism. However, to disentangle the responses of species diversity to forest gaps with and without deadwood enrichment, experimental approaches are needed. We sampled beetles, one of the most diverse taxa in forests, in a large-scale, full-factorial and well-replicated experiment at 26 sites in three regions of Germany (treatments: Control, Deadwood, Gap, Gap + Deadwood). We tested for changes in abundance, observed and standardised diversity, the community weighted means of body size and the share of forest and open-land specialist beetles in response to experimental gap creation and deadwood enrichment. Total beetle abundance and diversity were higher in gaps than in closed forests. However, in line with a 'more individuals' mechanism, the effect on diversity was mediated by increases in abundance. Once diversity was standardised by sample coverage, treatment effects on diversity vanished. We found that beetle communities in forest gaps consisted of on average larger species than in closed forests. The share of individuals from forest-specialist beetles was lower in the Gap than in the Deadwood and Gap + Deadwood treatments. However, the higher share of open-land specialist beetles in forest gaps compared to closed forests was negligible. We show that forest gaps are inhabited by larger-bodied and more diverse beetle communities, which could be due to enhanced resource availability and higher activity rates resulting from more favourable microclimatic conditions. A higher species abundance mediated the positive effect of forest gaps on beetle diversity. Our results furthermore highlight that disentangling responses of biodiversity to changing habitat conditions inherently depends on full-factorial experiments.

items.title: Barriers and Facilitators of Food Access and Food Availability in One Rural Alaska Community.
items.abstract: Rural communities comprise 20% of the United States, with many residents facing reduced food access and availability. Research on food security in Alaska is limited, and in many communities nonexistent. The goal of this study is to determine barriers and facilitators of food access and availability in the rural community of Ketchikan, Alaska. A retrospective cross-sectional study ascertained barriers and facilitators using a survey advertised via flyers, social media, and tables at a grocery store. A total of 108 Ketchikan residents were surveyed. The most commonly reported barriers were limited in-store availability of eggs, milk, cheese, and yogurt, fruits and vegetables, shipping delays, and food expenses. The commonly reported facilitators were traditional foods and food sharing with others. These findings point to food cost and traditional food access, for future interventions to improve food access and availability in rural Alaska communities.

items.title: Identification of novel bean bioindicator genotypes and biomarker traits for tropospheric ozone biomonitoring.
items.abstract: Elevated ozone (O 3 ) in the troposphere reduces crop productivity. Although the physiological responses of common bean genotypes to O 3 vary substantially, we understand inadequately the underlying drivers of this variation. Bioindicators connect O 3 pollution with its impact on plants through a standardised approach, which assesses symptoms. In this study, 15 bean genotypes, i.e. 3 genotypes known as O 3 bioindicators (S156, R123, Pinto), 10 Greek landraces, one commercially available cultivar, and one Greek runner bean landrace were exposed to charcoal-filtered air (CF) or 150 ppb O 3 (eO 3 ) over 7 days for 8 h day⁻ 1 , representative of documented Mediterranean ozone episodes. Physiological performance was assessed in primary and trifoliate leaves across three independent experimental runs. Exposure to eO 3 significantly reduced leaf greenness and pigment content in most genotypes, while gas exchange responses showed genotype-dependent variation. Primary leaves generally showed greater injury than trifoliate leaves, although the within-genotype differences were insignificant. Multivariate analyses distinguished tolerant genotypes such as CO, ZK, AS, and CH from more sensitive ones such as PP, T, ZC, and PY. Overall, the Greek landraces broadened the O 3 -sensitivity range beyond that set by the standard bioindicators S156, R123 and Pinto, highlighting their value for biomonitoring programs and breeding for O 3 resilience.

items.title: Correlative Microstructural and Elemental Analysis of Sika Deer Feces Using Resin-Embedded Cross-Sectional Polishing and SEM-EDS.
items.abstract: Traditional methods for investigating the diets of wild animals often depend on conventional approaches, including optical microscopy, and involve processing steps such as the washing and sieving fecal residues, which may alter or disperse the residues' original spatial configuration and compromise the preservation of detailed residue structures. Furthermore, DNA-based analyses generally require the disruption of fecal samples during sample processing, making it difficult to preserve the original morphology. Conversely, using resin-embedding techniques, conventional to electron microscopy, avoids this limitation, preserving the original shape and spatial configuration of fecal specimens and enabling a comprehensive analysis of fecal residues. To investigate the potential applicability of this approach to wildlife dietary analysis, we combined resin-embedded cross-sectional polishing and scanning electron microscopy for biological samples (bioCP-SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) to examine the morphology and elemental composition of fecal residues. As a model case, we analyzed fecal samples from sika deer (Cervus nippon) collected in Akaya, a mountainous area in Gunma Prefecture, and Nara Park, where deer routinely consume sika-senbei (deer crackers) as supplementary food. The results demonstrated that bioCP-SEM combined with EDS enabled the characterization of fecal residues while retaining information regarding their original shape and spatial configuration. Differences in the morphological and elemental characteristics of fecal residues were also found between two sites. This approach may complement conventional analytical methods and expand the range of information available for wildlife dietary analysis. When integrated with other analytical methods, it may contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of wildlife ecology and management.

items.title: Earlier spring advances phenology and reduces fitness in solitary bees (Osmia spp.) and plants without disrupting plant-pollinator synchrony.
items.abstract: Climate change affects the timing of seasonal events, potentially impacting plant-pollinator interactions through phenological mismatches. This study examined the simultaneous phenological responses of two species of solitary bees (Osmia bicornis and Osmia cornuta) and six herbaceous perennial plants to different spring onset timings. Using semi-controlled greenhouse experiments, we simulated earlier and later spring onsets at two locations in Germany (Freising and Greifswald). We monitored phenological timing and measured thermal requirements (Growing Degree Hours) for flowering and insect emergence, and fitness-related traits such as insect weight and flower size. Our results show that an earlier spring onset advanced the phenological events of both plants and bees compared to a later spring onset. However, there was no phenological mismatch in either spring onset timing treatment, as the dates of bee emergence and plant flowering remained close together. Notably, the earlier spring onset significantly increased the thermal requirements for pollinator emergence compared to the later spring onset, while no such difference was observed for plants across treatments. This suggests potential differences in the progression of dormancy and diapause in plants and insects, respectively. Lastly, the earlier spring onset led to greater weight loss in bees and species-specific variations in flower size. These results suggest that even when bees track floral phenology, they experience increased physiological stress, which could lower pollination efficiency and contribute to long-term population declines.

items.title: Density functional theory study on interfacial interactions and multifunctional regulation mechanisms of lignin-PBAT composite systems.
items.abstract: Interfacial interactions and multifunctional regulation mechanisms of lignin-polybutylene adipate-co-terephthalate (PBAT) composites were investigated via density functional theory (DFT) using simplified dimer models. Lignin spontaneously binds to PBAT in an enthalpy-driven manner, where electrostatic assembly, multi-site weak interactions and orbital hyperconjugation jointly stabilize the interface, with moderate-strength hydrogen bonds playing a critical role. A donor-acceptor charge-transfer system is formed, in which HOMO localizes on lignin and LUMO resides on PBAT. The narrowed HOMO-LUMO gap induces ultraviolet absorption redshift, while elevated hole reorganization energy restrains long-range charge migration. Lignin exerts multi-modal modulation on PBAT: steric hindrance and hydrogen-bond polarization produce competing effects on ester-bond hydrolysis; radical scavenging combined with UV absorption enhances UV-resistance; gas-phase radical quenching and condensed-phase suppression of thermal decomposition endow the system with potential flame-retardant capability. This work reveals microscopic mechanisms at the electronic-structure level. Nevertheless, static gas-phase dimer models cannot reflect condensed-phase conditions, and the proposed mechanisms need further verification by molecular dynamics, transition-state calculations and experiments.

items.title: Magnitudes of carbon sequestration offsets by CH<sub>4</sub> emission in restored Kandelia obovata mangrove ecosystems in a subtropical estuary.
items.abstract: Mangrove forests can absorb and store atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) over long timescales within their soils and vegetation. However, soil organic carbon in mangrove ecosystems can be mineralized and released to the atmosphere as methane (CH 4 ), a greenhouse gas with a much higher global warming potential than CO 2 . As a result, CH 4 emissions can partially offset net ecosystem CO 2 uptake. In this study, we quantified the annual plant biomass carbon increment, sediment carbon burial, and temporal variations of CH 4 emissions from three interfaces-sediment-atmosphere, water-atmosphere, and plant-atmosphere in the restored Kandelia obovata mangrove forest in the Minjiang River estuary, China. CH 4 fluxes at the sediment-atmosphere interface were 2.5 times higher than those at the water-atmosphere interface, and ebullition was the dominant CH 4 emissions pathway at the water-atmosphere interface. The annual mean CH 4 flux from the restored K. obovata mangrove forest ecosystem was 2.19±0.22 mg·m -2 h -1 . Over the annual scale, the relative surface elevation of the restored mangrove forest increased by 32.7± 2.16 mm. The ecosystem carbon sink rate was 4384.5±622.4 g CO 2 -eq m -2 a -1 . CH 4 emission offset 10.5% of the net carbon fixation of mangrove vegetation and 26.0% of the sediment carbon burial rate. Our findings indicate that although CH 4 emissions partially offset net carbon sequestration capacity of restored mangrove forests, restored mangrove stands still function as substantial net greenhouse gas sinks over a 100-year time horizon. Protecting and restoring mangrove carbon stocks is therefore an important component of global climate change mitigation strategies.

items.title: Atomic coordination engineering of MXene for electronic confinement-enabled sustained charge delivery toward PMS-mediated organic micropollutant abatement.
items.abstract: Developing robust single-atom catalysts to eliminate organic contaminants represents a trending research hotspot for advanced oxidation-based wastewater purification. A cobalt, nitrogen, and sulfur co-modified MXene composite labeled Co-N,S/MXene was fabricated through a combined hydrothermal reaction and low-temperature reduction strategy. The core objective was to trigger the activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) to achieve rapid sulfamethoxazole (SMX) elimination. Under the optimized reaction parameters (initial aqueous pH of 7.0, catalyst loading of 0.3 g·L -1 and 0.6 mM PMS), the Co-N,S/MXene-triggered PMS oxidation system achieves near-complete elimination of 20 mg·L -1 sulfamethoxazole within a 43 min reaction time. The density functional theory (DFT) examination unveiled that the PMS molecule adsorbs onto the cobalt single-atom site in a bidentate configuration through its O1 and O2 atoms. Concurrently, the Co monatomic center donates 0.521 electrons to the antibonding orbitals of PMS, thereby facilitating cleavage of the O-O bond. Notably, the system achieved efficient removal of SMX (96.8%) and exhibited low cobalt ion (Co 2+ ) leaching (23.27 μg·L -1 ) over a continuous operation period of 1500 min. Overall, this study uncovers, at the atomic level, a non-radical electron-transfer mechanism underlying single-site PMS activation, offering a rational and effective strategy for designing MXene-based single-atom catalysts as well as advancing their applicability to the oxidative degradation of organic contaminants.

items.title: Interpretable multi-label learning enables complete-site screening of remediation technologies from historical engineering cases.
items.abstract: Selecting remediation technologies for contaminated sites is a systems-level decision involving contaminant mixtures, risk intensity, spatial extent, medium properties and management constraints. Current data-driven studies focus on contaminant mapping, risk identification or single-process performance, lacking whole-site multi-technology screening. Here we examined whether pre-selection information from historical engineering projects could retrieve documented remediation functions. We curated 168 soil and 105 groundwater remediation projects from traceable Chinese engineering records as complete-site samples, using pre-selection information as predictors and historically implemented technologies including seven soil and four groundwater functional classes as multilabel outcomes. For soil, seven statistical and machine-learning approaches were evaluated under identical multilabel-stratified fivefold validation with inner-fold hyperparameter tuning and benchmarked against a feature-free historical-frequency comparator. Out-of-fold SHAP attribution, incremental information-set analysis and contamination-complexity-dependent Top-k recovery were subsequently used. All seven achieved higher Macro-AP than the historical-frequency comparator, with Random Forest achieving 0.594 versus 0.276; mean historical-technology coverage increased from 39.8% at Top-1 to 61.8% at Top-2 and 76.4% at Top-3, while exploratory groundwater validation yielded a Macro-AP of 0.668 versus 0.419. SHAP attribution showed that medium/hydrogeology and contaminant composition contributed 29.3% and 25.8%, respectively, while the other three information groups together contributed 44.9%. Historical technology portfolios broadened systematically with contamination complexity, increasing from 1.29 functional classes at single-contaminant sites to 2.34 at organic-inorganic co-contaminated sites, while Top-3 completely recovered the historical technology set for 58.9% of soil sites. Candidate width therefore emerges as a site-dependent screening variable, while ranked candidates still require technology-specific evaluation of feasibility, process compatibility, residual risk and implementation constraints before scheme development. By converting fragmented historical remediation practice into auditable complete-site evidence, this framework establishes a reproducible interface between data-driven inference and engineering judgment for transparent decision support in complex contaminated-site management.

items.title: Abundant microbial taxa diversity and key functional gene abundance are more strongly associated with soil multifunctionality than network complexity in northern drylands of China.
items.abstract: The relative importance of abundant- and rare-taxon diversity, microbial network complexity, and functional-gene abundance in explaining soil multifunctionality (SMF) along dryland aridity gradients remains unclear. Here, we combined a large-scale field survey across northern China's drylands with high-throughput sequencing and quantitative PCR to assess aridity-related changes in these attributes and their associations with SMF. We found that increasing aridity was associated with declines in abundant-taxon diversity across archaea, bacteria, and fungi, fungal rare-taxon diversity, and the abundance of most functional genes. In contrast, bacterial and fungal subnetwork complexity increased, whereas archaeal subnetwork complexity and the diversity of rare archaeal and bacterial taxa showed no clear aridity-related trends. Abundant-taxon diversity showed stronger positive associations with SMF than rare-taxon diversity, with explanatory contributions 2.42, 9.00, and 2.71 times those of rare-taxon diversity for archaea, bacteria, and fungi, respectively. In addition, network complexity was not significantly associated with SMF. Hierarchical partitioning showed that abundant-taxon diversity explained the largest fraction of SMF variation among the microbial attributes (21.13%), followed by key functional-gene abundance (14.30%), network complexity (6.23%), and rare-taxon diversity (1.60%). These findings reveal contrasting aridity-related patterns in the diversity of abundant and rare taxa, network topology, and functional potential across microbial domains, and highlight abundant-taxon diversity and measured functional-gene abundance as the microbial properties most closely associated with dryland SMF.

items.title: Biochar facilitates the recovery of seagrass meadows under antibiotic stress by alleviating microbial community disruption.
items.abstract: Seagrass meadows serve as crucial coastal ecosystems, supporting key ecological roles such as habitat formation, sediment stabilization, and carbon storage. Despite their ecological importance, these ecosystems are undergoing severe degradation driven by climate change and escalating human activities. Antibiotics, increasingly identified as persistent contaminants in coastal environments, pose emerging ecological threats, yet their impacts on seagrass physiology and associated microbial communities remain poorly understood. In this study, a microcosm-based simulation was conducted to assess the responses of the seagrass Thalassia hemprichii holobiont to four frequently detected antibiotics and to appraise the restorative efficacy of biochar. Results indicated that chloramphenicol and high-dose tetracycline significantly altered the composition of rhizosphere microbial assemblages (P < 0.05). As an adaptive response to antibiotic stress, seagrass enriched beneficial bacterial taxa, including Flavobacteriaceae, which may help alleviate stress and reorganize microbial networks. Biochar addition partially restored microbial diversity and promoted the recovery of microbial community composition. These effects may be linked to changes in rhizosphere carbon dynamics and organic matter-antibiotic interactions, potentially affecting antibiotic availability, although DOC and antibiotic concentrations were not directly measured. Biochar may alleviate antibiotic-associated stress in seagrass ecosystems, but its ecological benefits may be offset by trade-offs in nutrient availability. These findings highlight the ecological risks of antibiotic exposure and suggest that biochar may be a promising remediation strategy for supporting seagrass ecosystem recovery.

items.title: Impact of Climatic and Environmental Conditions on Prehospital Emergency Medical Dispatches in Germany: Protocol for an Exploratory, Population-Based Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background Extreme temperatures and other climatic stressors are increasingly affecting population health, even in temperate regions such as Germany. Previous studies have demonstrated associations between extreme heat, cold temperatures, and health indicators, including emergency department visits and mortality. However, most analyses rely on coarse meteorological data and hospital-based outcomes, limiting insights into fine-scale spatial variability and prehospital emergency responses. Prehospital emergency medical dispatches (PHEMD) data offer a unique opportunity to capture acute, real-time health effects of climatic and environmental conditions at high temporal resolution. Objective This study examines the association between climatic and environmental conditions and PHEMD use in 2 metropolitan regions in northern Germany. It will assess nonlinear temperature-response relationships, temporal lags, spatial and subgroup variation, and the added value of high-resolution vs station-based exposure assignment. Methods This is an exploratory, retrospective, population-based observational study using anonymized PHEMD data from the metropolitan regions of Hanover and Brunswick and their surrounding rural areas. PHEMD records will be linked to meteorological measurements and high-resolution urban microclimate data. Associations between climatic conditions and PHEMD use will be analyzed using quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag nonlinear model structures. The main temporal analyses will use daily mean temperature and lags of 0 to 6 days, with longer lag periods of up to 14 days examined for cold-related effects. Models will account for temporal trends, seasonality, weekdays, public holidays, and, where appropriate, air pollution. Geographic information system-based maps will visualize the spatial distribution of effects. Results Study funding began in July 2025. As of November 2026, acquisition and harmonization of emergency medical service and meteorological data are ongoing. The study dataset will include data through December 2030, with the final data export planned thereafter. All analyses are expected to be completed and the resulting manuscripts submitted for publication by May 2031. Conclusions This study uses high-resolution environmental data and PHEMD records to examine climate-related emergency medical demand in northern Germany. By linking microclimate information with dispatch data, it aims to improve the understanding of spatial and temporal patterns beyond conventional approaches. The findings may support more targeted heat-health preparedness, improve emergency service planning, and inform local climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
items.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating "late-small" and "early-large" epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

items.title: Perceived age-friendliness in multiethnic and multigenerational Klang Valley, Malaysia: An extended WHO Age-Friendly Cities assessment.
items.abstract: Malaysia's transition towards an ageing society underscores the need for context-sensitive tools to assess urban age-friendliness, particularly in the multiethnic cities of the Global South. This quantitative cross-sectional study adapted and extended the World Health Organization's Age-Friendly Cities framework by incorporating additional domains on technology and financial situation to assess perceived neighbourhood age-friendliness across six local authorities in Klang Valley, Malaysia. Incorporating a multigenerational perspective, the study captured perceptions from diverse age and ethnic populations. A bilingual self-administered questionnaire consisting of 15 socio-demographic items and 75 closed-ended age-friendly indicators measured on a 5-point Likert scale was administered to 511 community-dwelling adults aged 18 years and above. The instrument underwent expert review, content validity assessment, and pilot testing prior to implementation. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, one-sample t-tests, independent samples t-tests, and one-way ANOVA. The overall age-friendly score (AFI) indicated that Klang Valley was generally age-friendly, with scores significantly above the neutral midpoint of the 5-point scale (M = 3.36, p < .001). The technology and respect and social inclusion domains recorded the highest mean scores (both M = 3.77, p < .001), while civic participation and employment was the only domain scoring significantly below the midpoint (M = 2.81, p < .001). Significant spatial differences were observed across local authorities for AFI and nine domains (p < .05), with Putrajaya, the master-planned administrative capital consistently reporting the highest scores. Ethnic differences were significant for AFI and eight domains (p < .05). In contrast, age-group differences were largely non-significant except for technology, where young adult respondents reported higher satisfaction than older adult respondents (p < .001). The findings suggest that perceived age-friendliness in Klang Valley varies more clearly by spatial and ethnic contexts than by chronological age. This study provides a multidomain empirical benchmark of urban age-friendliness in Malaysia from a person-environment fit perspective. It highlights the importance of inclusive, multigenerational, and digitally responsive urban planning strategies.

items.title: Beyond generalizations: Understanding adolescent social networks in American Indian communities.
items.abstract: American Indian (AI) adolescents experience disproportionately high rates of substance use, yet the role of substance use and other individual characteristics in friendship network formation within AI-majority reservation schools remains understudied. Most existing research on adolescent networks derives from racially heterogeneous school settings, where substance use is often linked to friendship formation and popularity. This study examines the structural and relational foundations of friendship networks among AI adolescents in their unique cultural context. Using social network data from 9th and 10th-grade students (N = 247) across three schools on a Northern Plains reservation, we employed exponential random graph models (ERGMs) to analyze factors shaping friendship ties. Models assessed endogenous structural processes (reciprocity, transitivity, degree effects) and actor-level characteristics, including demographic factors, substance use (alcohol, tobacco, marijuana), depression, and AI identity. Results indicated that universal structural mechanisms (reciprocity, transitivity) and demographic homophily (gender, grade, sexual orientation) were primary drivers of friendship. However, unlike what is often observed in studies of other adolescent populations, substance use showed no consistent association with sending ties or receiving ties. Similarly, depression and AI identity were not substantively associated with friendship formation. These findings reveal a distinct relational ecology within AI-majority reservation schools, where peer ties are organized around structural and demographic commonalities rather than risky behaviors. These findings challenge assumptions underpinning many network-based prevention programs and underscore the critical need for theories and interventions that are culturally and contextually grounded in the lived experiences of AI youth.

items.title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants.
items.abstract: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

items.title: Enhanced methane production from lignite by bacterial pretreatment: mechanistic insights from multi‑technique analysis of Bacillus cereus and Lelliottia amnigena.
items.abstract: Microbial pretreatment is a promising strategy to enhance biogenic methane production from low-rank coal, but the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Hydrolytic and fermentative microorganisms can degrade complex lignite-derived organic matter into simpler compounds, providing substrates for methanogenic archaea and thereby facilitating methane production. This study investigated the effects of pretreating lignite with two bacterial isolates, Bacillus cereus and Lelliottia amnigena, on subsequent anaerobic methane production. The cumulative methane yield, enzyme activities, dissolved organic matter transformation, lignite structural changes, and microbial community metabolism were systematically evaluated using GC‑MS, 3D‑EEM fluorescence spectroscopy, FTIR, XPS, XRD, and metagenomic analysis. Pretreatment of lignite with B. cereus increased methane yield by 128% (370.25 µmol/g) and that with L. amnigena by 104% (331.12 µmol/g) compared to untreated lignite, while also shortening the lag phase. The B. cereus treatment group showed higher lignin peroxidase (22.12 U/L), lipase (15.12 U/L), and amylase (653.22 U/L) activities, promoting depolymerization of aromatic and aliphatic structures, as evidenced by increased hydroxyl groups, alkane accumulation, and decreased ester content. Pretreatment enriched the fermentative bacterium Petrimonas (up to 32.37%) and upregulated key genes involved in glycolysis (e.g., K03841), aromatic degradation (e.g., K14731), fatty acid β‑oxidation (e.g., K00197), and methanogenesis (e.g., methyl‑coenzyme M reductase). These integrated physicochemical and microbiological modifications enhanced substrate bioavailability and established an efficient metabolic chain from lignite depolymerization to methane generation. The superior performance of B. cereus over L. amnigena was attributed to its stronger lignolytic activity. This work provides a multi‑technique mechanistic insight into microbial pretreatment of lignite and offers a basis for strain selection and process optimization for enhanced lignite biogasification.

items.title: The offloading paradox: reminders improve prospective memory target detection but impair output monitoring.
items.abstract: Event-based prospective memory (PM) refers to the use of environmental cues (e.g., medication bottle) to trigger retrieval of delayed intentions (e.g., taking medication). Evidence suggests that offloading PM demands onto external sources (e.g., Google Calendar) can improve intention fulfilment. However, previous research has focused on how offloading influences performance when a cue is encountered only once. To simulate repeated encounters, participants memorised a list of words to which they were to respond the first time they were encountered during an ongoing task. Critically, on the second presentation they were instructed to make a different keypress if they remembered responding to that same word previously. Reminders displayed the words at the top of the screen, whereas the no-reminder condition showed a row of Xs. The results indicated that both repetition (Exp. 1 and 2) and omission (Exp. 2) errors were higher with reminders than without. These errors persisted even when intention retrieval was made more elaborative by having participants type the PM response (Exp. 2). These findings suggest that cognitive offloading through reminders can improve target detection while also altering the evidence individuals use to determine whether a prior action has been completed.

items.title: Moral courage in nursing interns: Latent profile and network analysis.
items.abstract: IntroductionMoral courage is important during clinical training, yet studies based primarily on aggregate scores may overlook individual heterogeneity among nursing interns. Combining Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) with network analysis may help identify latent differences in moral courage levels and examine profile-specific relationships among associated factors.AimTo identify latent profiles of moral courage among nursing interns and examine profile-specific network relationships and centrality patterns among associated factors.Research DesignA cross-sectional study.MethodsUsing convenience sampling, an online survey was conducted between October 2025 and January 2026 among 1,325 nursing interns undertaking clinical internships at seven hospitals in Hunan, Hubei, and Shandong provinces, China. Participants were voluntarily recruited through online channels. The electronic questionnaire collected sociodemographic information and included the Nurses' Moral Courage Scale, Nursing Professional Values Scale-Revised, Jefferson Scale of Empathy for Health Professionals, and Nursing Students' Professional Identity Scale. LPA was used to identify latent profiles characterized by different levels of moral courage, followed by network analysis to examine relationships among study variables and centrality patterns within each profile.Ethical ConsiderationsThis study was reviewed and approved by the Research Ethics Committee of Jishou University (JSDX-2025-0065). Before participant recruitment, permission to distribute the questionnaire was also obtained from the nursing administration departments of the relevant hospitals.FindingsA total of 1,325 nursing interns were included. LPA identified three moral courage profiles: low (8.53%), moderate (63.77%), and high (27.70%). The profiles primarily reflected graded differences in the overall level of moral courage rather than qualitatively distinct response patterns. Network analysis revealed profile-specific centrality patterns. Nursing Professional Values showed the highest Strength centrality in the low moral courage profile, Nurses' Professional Identity in the moderate profile, and Preference for Nursing Major in the high profile.ConclusionThis study identified three latent profiles of moral courage among nursing interns, characterized by low, moderate, and high levels of moral courage. Network analysis further revealed profile-specific centrality patterns, with Nursing Professional Values, Nurses' Professional Identity, and Preference for Nursing Major showing the highest centrality in the low, moderate, and high moral courage profiles, respectively. These findings contribute to a better understanding of factors associated with different levels of moral courage among nursing interns and may inform the development and future testing of tailored educational and supportive strategies. Given the cross-sectional design of this study, causal inferences cannot be made, and longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to further validate these findings.

items.title: Childhood competence, adverse childhood experiences, and sociocultural context: Understanding resilience processes from childhood to young adulthood.
items.abstract: Childhood competencies in mental health, social, and academic domains could support (or promote) low levels of stress later in life. These competencies could also protect those highly exposed to ACEs from experiencing elevated perceived stress (PS). Participants (N = 2,004, ages 5-17 at Waves 1-3; ages 15-29 at Wave 4) were from the Boricua Youth Study, a sample of Puerto Rican children recruited from the South Bronx, New York, and the metropolitan area in San Juan and Caguas, Puerto Rico. The current study examined longitudinal patterns of childhood competence (stable, unstable, not reaching) across three domains (mental health, social adjustment, and academic achievement) in relation to PS in young adulthood. We also investigated the role of childhood competencies as a protective factor, buffering the association between ACEs and PS. We explored whether associations varied across two sociocultural contexts with varying levels of ACEs (South Bronx vs. Puerto Rico). Childhood mental health competence, in relation to never reaching competence, was the only type of competence that promoted (b = -1.72, p < .001) lower PS in young adulthood. Childhood mental health competence also modified the association between ACEs and PS among those recruited in the South Bronx (F (2, 776) = 4.45, p = .01), such that among those with stable childhood mental health competence, higher ACEs were associated with more PS (b = 0.56, SE = 0.22, p = .01) while the same was not observed in the other two trajectories (Unstable: b = 0.44, SE = 0.23, p = .053; Not reaching competence: b = -0.59, SE = 0.33, p = .08). Experiencing competence in mental health during childhood may alleviate PS in young adulthood. For those growing up in a sociocultural context where adversities are frequent experiences and who have stable levels of mental health competence, ACEs were related to high PS in young adulthood.

items.title: The impact of sexual abuse on the receipt of dental care: A systematic review.
items.abstract: The aim of this review is to systematically examine and synthesise the published literature on the relationship between a history of sexual abuse (SA) and oral health, including access to dental care, oral health outcomes, dental anxiety and experiences of dental treatment. A structured search was conducted, including all study types, published manuscripts between 2011 and 2024 across five databases. A total of 17 articles that met the criteria were identified. Quantitative and qualitative findings were analysed separately and then integrated to identify overarching themes. Three core themes were generated from the data: dental anxiety and the avoidance of care, difficulties during treatment experience and physical and social impacts. The qualitative studies were judged to be of high quality using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme criteria. In contrast, only three of the nine quantitative studies were considered of high quality, with the remaining judged to be of moderate quality. A history of SA was associated with difficulties in accessing dental care, negative treatment experiences and adverse oral health outcomes. There is clear evidence of a significant relationship between a history of SA and a range of oral health challenges. These findings highlight the need to better support affected individuals, using trauma-informed approaches.

items.title: When AI Performs, What Remains? An Integrative Review of Generative AI and Cognitive Capital in Individuals and Organizations.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering knowledge work, and its short-term productivity benefits are increasingly documented. Less is known about what happens, over time, to the knowledge, skills, and judgment that remain in people and organizations. This integrative narrative review addresses that question through the construct of cognitive capital: the accumulated, renewable, and depletable stock of knowledge, cognitive, and metacognitive capabilities, and practices that enable an individual or an organization to learn, interpret information, exercise judgment, solve problems, and adapt. We distinguish individual and organizational cognitive capital from the capability of the human-AI system, so that gains in joint performance and losses in human capability can be observed at the same time. Drawing on experimental, field, and conceptual work, we propose four mechanisms through which interaction with AI affects cognitive capital: substitution of practice, scaffolding and feedback, metacognitive calibration, and organizational aggregation. Seven principles summarize the current evidence, including that assisted performance differs from retained competence, that the same technology can support or displace learning depending on design and use, and that individual gains can coexist with reduced collective diversity. For each mechanism, we derive testable propositions, and we discuss five design levers for organizations as proposals to be validated rather than established practice. We conclude that cognitive capital offers a multilevel frame for governing AI adoption and outline a research agenda centered on longitudinal, multilevel measurement.

items.title: Effectiveness, acceptability, and completeness of intervention reporting of psychological interventions for people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment: a mixed-methods systematic review.
items.abstract: Background People living with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) commonly experience difficulties with mental health and psychological well-being. Given the dyadic interdependence of well-being, these difficulties may also affect informal caregivers. However, access to psychological interventions remains limited for people living with dementia. Our overall aim was to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of the current research evidence for psychological interventions intended to improve mental health and psychological well-being in people living with dementia or MCI. Methods We systematically searched electronic databases ASSIA, CENTRAL, CINAHL, EMBASE, MEDLINE and PsycINFO for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and identified qualitative studies associated with eligible RCTs via hand searching. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, assessed full-texts, and completed quality appraisal. Quantitative studies with sufficient data were included in a meta-analysis, and qualitative studies were synthesized using framework analysis. A convergent mixed-methods design was adopted to integrate quantitative and qualitative results in the discussion. Results We included 15 quantitative studies in the review (n = 1,742 people living with dementia or MCI). Our meta-analysis showed a small-to-moderate effect size favoring the intervention for depressive symptoms in people living with dementia or MCI (n = 11 studies; Hedges' g = -0.36 [95% CI = -0.61 to -0.11] p .05). It was not appropriate to conduct a meta-analysis for other outcomes associated with mental health and psychological well-being in people living with dementia, MCI, or their caregivers due to insufficient data. We included six qualitative studies related to the included quantitative studies. In our meta-synthesis (n = 6 studies), we identified factors associated with intervention acceptability corresponding to six of the seven Theoretical Framework of Acceptability constructs. Completeness of intervention reporting was inadequate across studies. Conclusion Higher-quality RCTs with larger sample sizes, improved intervention reporting, and methodological rigor are needed to strengthen the evidence base for psychological interventions for people living with dementia or MCI, and their caregivers. Further research should explore intervention acceptability from the perspectives of key interest-holders. Prospero registration number CRD42023400514.

items.title: Risk and Maintenance Factors for Future Onset and Persistence of Binge-Eating and Purging Symptoms: A Prospective Study of the Gut Microbiome.
items.abstract: Background Eating disorders are severe, disabling, and costly mental disorders. Existing evidence on the gut microbiome in eating disorders is derived primarily from cross-sectional studies. This study aimed to apply a longitudinal grouping analysis to examine gut microbial factors that predict future onset and persistence of binge-eating and purging symptoms, two subtypes of eating disorder symptoms (EDSs). Method Participants from a prospective cohort (baseline N = 908; follow-up N = 407) were classified as non-afflicted controls (n = 29/26 [binge-eating/purging]; reported no EDSs at either time point), developers (n = 35/28; reported EDSs at follow-up only), maintainers (n = 20/40; reported EDSs at both time points), or remitters (n = 17/38; reported EDSs at baseline only). Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing, we examined group differences in microbial diversity (alpha and beta diversity), microbial features (at the level of phylum, genus and species), and functional pathways to identify risk factors and maintenance factors. Results Reduced abundance of Actinobacteria, several Proteobacteria genera (e.g., Oleiphilus, Oecophyllibacter, and Novosphingopyxis), and multiple species from Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria, and Firmicutes predicted future onset of binge eating. Lower abundance of Roseburia predicted future onset of purging. Elevated abundance of specific genera or species belonging to Proteobacteria, Deferribacteres, and Cyanobacteria, as well as functional pathways enriched in terpenoid and polyketide metabolism predicted future persistence of binge eating. Conclusions The evidence that reduced abundance of multiple species (especially from Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria, and Firmicutes) predicted future binge-eating onset, and that reduced Roseburia abundance predicted future purging onset, extends prior findings. The evidence that elevated abundance of specific Proteobacteria, Deferribacteres, and Cyanobacteria taxa predicted future binge eating persistence is novel.

items.title: Age at Menarche, Temperament, and Eating Disorder Severity Across Diagnostic Subtypes: A Transdiagnostic Investigation in a Large Clinical Sample.
items.abstract: Objective This study examined the timing of age at menarche relative to eating disorder (ED) onset across ED subtypes and tested whether temperamental traits moderated the link between pubertal timing and ED severity. Method The study comprised 3127 treatment-seeking women diagnosed with anorexia nervosa (AN), bulimia nervosa (BN), binge-eating disorder (BED), atypical AN, purging disorder (PD), and unspecified feeding or eating disorder (UFED). Age at current ED onset and age at menarche were assessed at intake using a semi-structured interview. ED symptom severity was measured using the Eating Disorder Inventory (EDI-2), and temperament and character were evaluated using the Temperament and Character Inventory-Revised (TCI-R). Results Participants, on average, reported ED onset at 19.7 years (SD = 7.85) and menarche at 12.47 years (SD = 1.61). ED diagnostic groups differed in both age at menarche and the interval between menarche and ED onset: BED was characterized by the earliest age of menarche and the longest gap of 12.4 years, whereas AN showed the latest age of menarche. Women whose age of menarche occurred after ED onset had significantly greater ED severity than those whose age of menarche preceded the ED onset. High harm avoidance and low self-directedness were consistently associated with greater ED severity, but temperament did not moderate the relationship between age of menarche and ED severity. Conclusion Age of menarche is a clinically meaningful marker that varies across ED subtypes and is independently associated with ED severity, supporting its routine consideration in assessment and formulation.

items.title: Age and sex differences in questionnaire-based indicators of motivational anhedonia, consummatory anhedonia, and negative affect among colorectal cancer survivors.
items.abstract: Purpose Depression is common among colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors and may involve heterogeneous symptom domains. We examined age- and sex-related differences in indicators of motivational anhedonia, consummatory anhedonia, and negative affect during survivorship and compared them with a frequency-matched normative population. Methods Data were obtained from 471 CRC survivors in the population-based PROCORE study. Indicators were assessed 12 and 24 months after diagnosis. Linear mixed-effects models examined associations of age, sex, and their interaction over time. A frequency-matched normative sample (n = 260) served as a comparison group. Results Overall symptom levels were comparable between CRC survivors and normative participants, except for higher HADS-D scores among survivors at 24 months. Significant Age × Sex interactions were observed for all three indicators. Motivational and consummatory anhedonia indicators increased with age among men but not women, whereas emotional functioning improved with age among women but not men, indicating more negative affect among younger women. Direct Group × Age × Sex tests showed differences for emotional functioning at both assessments and for the consummatory anhedonia indicator at 24 months, but not for motivational anhedonia. Motivational anhedonia increased over time among women of mean age; the other indicators did not change significantly. Conclusions Age and sex were associated with different patterns across depression-related symptom indicators. Replication is needed, particularly among younger CRC survivors and survivors with clinically significant depressive symptoms. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Symptom-level assessment may help characterize heterogeneity in psychological adjustment after CRC, although further research is needed before informing screening or care.

items.title: Exploiting the dynamics of gaze to modulate the evaluation of risky prospects.
items.abstract: Two incentivized experiments (N = 217) examined how visual attention contributes to the construction of risk preference. Using a staircase procedure in which participants' choices were titrated to an indifference point between a sure and risky prospect, we find that a gaze-contingent prompt procedure can influence participants' risk appetite. Our findings show that, on average, a sure offer of 100 points would be viewed as equivalent to a 50% chance of 266 points when gaze is biased toward the risky option, versus a 50% chance of 283 points when biased toward the safe option. Further aspects of our results and procedure confirm that participants genuinely evaluated risk and reward values, with the influence of the gaze-contingent prompt superimposed on this unfolding process of preference construction. Together our results reinforce the importance of last-fixations for driving preference and as such appear inconsistent with mechanistic accounts that rely solely on 'mere exposure' or 'gaze cascades', since such accounts see the relationship between gaze and choice as mediated by differences in total dwell time - which was not a pattern supported by our data. By contrast, the current findings could be accommodated by sequential sampling models that propose faster accumulation of evidence for attended options.

items.title: Fetal hemoglobin fraction: a potential predictor of late-onset sepsis in very preterm infants.
items.abstract: Late onset sepsis (LOS) is included between the so-called oxidative stress-related diseases in preterm infants. Increasing evidence supports a protective role of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) against oxidative stress. We hypothesized that HbF blood fractions measured during the first weeks of life may be associated with the risk of developing LOS. We carried out a retrospective observational study on 166 preterm infants with gestational age <30 weeks. The primary endpoint of our study was the comparison of HbF fraction values between infants who developed LOS and those who did not during the first week of life. Fifty-six (34%) infants had LOS at the mean age of 14±8 and 22±15 days of life. Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life (HbF14) to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF14 decreased (OR 0.974, 95% CI 0.956-0.992; P=0.004) the risk of LOS. In ROC analysis, HbF14 showed moderate discriminative ability in predicting LOS, with an AUC of 0.676 and 95% CI 0.593-0.758. Lower HbF fractions during the first weeks of life were associated with an increased risk of LOS, with HbF14 emerging as an independent protective factor. These findings confirm the role of HbF in modulating susceptibility to oxidative stress-related complications in this vulnerable population and the importance of maintaining its levels high. • Low fetal hemoglobin (HbF) fractions are associated with increased risk of oxidative stress-related complications of prematurity. Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is included among oxidative stress-related diseases. • Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF fraction at 14 days of life is associated with decreased risk of LOS.

items.title: Ultrasound localization microscopy reveals region-specific cerebrovascular responses to exercise in aged mice.
items.abstract: Abstract Aging is widely recognized to impair cerebrovascular structure and function, potentially compromising the vascular environment that supports hippocampal plasticity and adult neurogenesis. Whether exercise can reverse these age-related changes in vivo and what vascular mechanisms underlie such effects remain unclear. Ultrasound localization microscopy is one of the most powerful tools for addressing this question by enabling in vivo, super-resolution mapping of microvascular architecture and blood-flow dynamics across both cortical and deep brain regions. Therefore, this study used localization microscopy to reveal the region-specific cerebrovascular responses in aged mice after exercise. We used ultrasound localization microscopy to compare cerebrovascular structure and hemodynamics among young control mice, aged sedentary mice, and aged mice subjected to 4 weeks of treadmill exercise. We further integrated regional summary measurements and features using principal component analysis and an L2-regularized logistic-regression-based aging axis trained exclusively on young and aged sedentary controls, and found that exercise-trained aged mice shifted 74% toward the young vascular phenotype along the control-defined axis, driven primarily by hippocampal flow, radius, and velocity. Our findings show that 4 weeks of treadmill exercise partially shifted the aged cerebrovascular phenotype toward a younger state in a region-dependent manner, with the structural and hemodynamic responses occurring in the hippocampal and subcortical regions. This framework separates exercise-responsive from exercise-resistant components of cerebrovascular aging.

items.title: Human perception of curved space.
items.abstract: We all perceive our immediate surroundings in a decidedly Euclidean way. But is our local Euclidean model hardwired? items.title: Cardiovascular Reactivity to Peer Rejection Moderates the Impact of Early Life Stress on Body Mass Index in Adolescent Girls: A Cluster Analysis Approach.
items.abstract: Early life stress is linked to poor cardiometabolic outcomes including obesity. Blunted physiological stress reactivity, which may be adaptive in adverse contexts, has also been associated with obesity. The present study examines whether cardiovascular reactivity (CVR) serves as a biological susceptibility factor that moderates the longitudinal association between early life stress and body mass index (BMI) in female adolescents. Participants were 80 female adolescents (Mage= 13.3 years). Participants completed the Psychosocial Schedule to assess cumulative early life stress. The Yale Interpersonal Stressor-Child paradigm was executed to assess systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and heart rate (HR) during acute stress exposure. K-means clustering identified CVR patterns based on reactivity from baseline to the stressor. Height and weight were measured at baseline and twelve months later to derive BMI-for-age. Two CVR clusters were identified: high CVR (n=31; MΔSBP=15.0mmHg, MΔDBP=8.21mmHg, MΔHR=7.05 bpm) and low CVR (n= 49; MΔSBP=4.70mmHg, MΔDBP=3.58mmHg, MΔHR=0.94 bpm). CVR moderated the association between early life stress and BMI-for-age at 12-month follow-up, controlling for pubertal status, socioeconomic status, depression, and race/ethnicity (B(SE) =-4.61 (1.71), p =.009). Higher early life stress predicted higher BMI-for-age among adolescents with low CVR (B(SE)=3.53 (1.39), p=.01) but not among those with high CVR. Early life stress was associated with higher BMI-for-age only among adolescents with blunted CVR, suggesting reduced stress reactivity as a potential physiological risk pathway for obesity among adolescent females.

items.title: Cognitive capacity in subjective cognitive decline: Insights from electrophysiological markers and dual-task performance.
items.abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) refers to self-reported cognitive deficits in the absence of objective cognitive impairment. Evidence suggests that neural changes may precede performance declines, highlighting the potential of electroencephalography (EEG) to detect early cognitive declines. Electrophysiological markers and changes in cognitive and motor performance were examined during dual-task performance to better understand the neural mechanisms underlying SCD. Older adults with (n=20) and without (n=20) SCD performed a working memory and finger tapping task simultaneously (i.e., dual task) and alone (i.e., single cognitive or motor). Linear mixed models were used to assess task and group effects for behavioural performance and EEG measures, including mean amplitude and power spectral density, in frontal, central, and parietal regions of interest (ROI). P2 and P3b mean amplitude were smaller during the dual task compared to single cognitive task. Additionally, the SCD group exhibited higher theta power overall and higher alpha power in each task and ROI compared to the non-SCD group. Higher power was observed during the dual task compared to single tasks except in the alpha band where the opposite was observed. Cognitive and motor performance decreased between single and dual tasks, and slower finger tapping speed was observed in the SCD compared to the non-SCD group. Neural and performance findings support the capacity sharing model of attention and may reflect the use of compensatory mechanisms in the SCD group. Electrophysiological changes may precede objective cognitive deficits and have the potential to complement existing approaches to characterizing SCD but must be examined longitudinally.

items.title: Cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity in healthy humans during and after face immersion are moderated by water temperature and apnea.
items.abstract: The interaction between cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity during face immersion remains poorly understood, yet it is critical for identifying potential autonomic conflict. This study sought to disentangle the individual and synergistic contributions of breathing mode (apnea vs. snorkel breathing) and water temperature (10°C vs. 30°C) on heart rate, cardiac vagal (RMSSD), and cardiac sympathetic (PEP) indices before, during, and after exposure. In a randomized within-subjects design, 52 healthy adults completed five 30-second conditions: 1) apnea in an empty bowl, 2) apnea in cold water, 3) apnea in warm water, 4) snorkel breathing in cold water, and 5) snorkel breathing in warm water. Heart rate, RMSSD, and PEP were measured for 30 seconds before, during and after each condition. Significant bradycardia occurred in all five conditions. Apnea in an empty bowl resulted in the smallest bradycardia and a decrease in RMSSD. While cold-water apnea caused the strongest bradycardia, snorkel breathing in cold water elicited the largest RMSSD increase. PEP remained stable throughout all conditions and time points. These results demonstrate that face immersion triggers stimulus-dependent autonomic pathways. The observed decoupling of heart rate and RMSSD during apnea questions the validity of RMSSD as an index of cardiac vagal activity during breath-holding. The stability of PEP is consistent with predominantly cardiac parasympathetic involvement in diving bradycardia. These findings highlight limitations of RMSSD interpretation during apnea and emphasize the necessity of accounting for breathing modality in autonomic assessments. Applied interventions using cold-water face immersion under safe conditions are encouraged.

items.title: Dynamics of Daily Stress and Negative Affect Intensity in Early Adolescence: A DSEM Analysis of Cognitive Reappraisal, Physical Activity, and Trait Resilience.
items.abstract: Early adolescents exhibit heightened emotional reactivity to daily stress (defined here as the subjective intensity of the most bothersome daily hassle). However, the daily factors associated with variation in this reactivity in naturalistic settings remain inadequately understood. Specifically, cognitive reappraisal and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were examined as daily state-level moderators, alongside trait resilience as a stable dispositional moderator. To explicitly test both within-person and cross-level moderating effects, this study utilized a 21-day daily diary design to track 120 junior high school students (yielding 1,965 valid daily observations). Variables were assessed using brief self-reports, including a Visual Analogue Scale for negative affect intensity and categorical assessments for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). Bayesian dynamic structural equation modeling (DSEM) was employed to disentangle within-person fluctuations from between-person traits while accounting for the carry-over effects of previous-day negative affect. Daily stress significantly and positively predicted same-day negative affect intensity (b = 2.95, 95% CI [2.63, 3.27]). Crucially, DSEM revealed that engaging in same-day cognitive reappraisal (b = -1.62, 95% CI [-1.97, -1.27]) or MVPA (b = -2.38, 95% CI [-2.69, -2.08]) was associated with a significantly weaker daily stress-affect intensity link at the within-person level. Furthermore, trait resilience significantly moderated this association at the cross-level (b = -1.20, 95% CI [-1.76, -0.63]), with a weaker stress-negative affect association at higher resilience. These findings identify cognitive reappraisal, MVPA, and trait resilience as moderators of the daily stress-negative affect association in early adolescence.

items.title: Mapping the shared genetic architecture between anorexia nervosa and metabolomic biomarkers.
items.abstract: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) has the highest mortality rate of any psychiatric disorder yet lacks effective treatments. While recent genomic efforts have reframed AN as a metabo-psychiatric condition that overlaps with cardiometabolic traits, AN's relationship to circulating metabolomic markers remains unknown. We examined shared genetic architecture between AN and 249 metabolomic biomarkers, and compared profiles with related mental health, anthropometric and cardiometabolic traits. Genetic and biological overlap was assessed with global genetic correlations, conjunctional false discovery rate, bivariate Gaussian mixture modeling, and gene set enrichment analysis across body tissues. We also explored putative causal relationships between AN, body mass index (BMI), and metabolomic biomarkers. Significant genetic correlations emerged between AN and 142 metabolomic biomarkers, which were opposite in direction to cardiometabolic traits such as BMI and type 2 diabetes (rs<-0.94), and stronger than correlations with anxiety. Shared variants between AN and metabolomic biomarkers, particularly lipid-based metabolites, exhibited a mixture of positive and negative effects. These were mapped to genes involved in lipid-related cell signals, developmental growth, and inflammation, and were widely expressed in the brain, most internal organs and female reproductive organs. Bidirectional associations between AN and metabolomic biomarkers were found to act through their respective influence on BMI. These findings reveal a complex, bidirectional mixture of positive and negative genetic relationships between AN and systemic metabolism, which would be obscured by examination of broader cardiometabolic traits. Uncovering specific shared lipid and developmental pathways provides a genetically-anchored mechanistic understanding of the illness, while highlighting promising metabolomic targets for weight restoration approaches.

items.title: Mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction This systematic review aimed to assess prevalence and characteristics of mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with seven neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions, to compare these to normative populations, and identify associated factors. Material and Methods Using a PRISMA compliant protocol (PROSPERO CRD42023443731), studies on congenital diaphragmatic hernia(CDH), esophageal atresia(EA), abdominal wall defects (AWD: gastroschisis/omphalocele), anorectal malformations (ARM), Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) and surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) were identified through searches in MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library (inception-November 2025) A random-effects meta-analysis of prevalence was conducted, with heterogeneity assessed using I². Significance level was p<0.05. Results Forty-seven studies (published 1991-2025) with 1786 children (median sample size 28, range 10-157) were included: CDH (n=10), EA (n=11), AWD (n=9), NEC (n=2), ARM (n=17), and HSCR (n=5). Most studies originated from Europe (n=31). Mental health and behavioral difficulties were more frequently reported than in norms, in CDH (7/8 studies), EA (6/7 studies), and ARM (4/6 studies). Meta-analysis showed elevated difficulties in 25,7% (Child Behavior Check List; I²=59.6) and 17.8% (Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire; I²=65.3). The prevalence of autism ranged from 10-23% (CDH, AWD) and ADHD from 0-20% (CDH, AWD, NEC, ARM, HSCR). Across studies, methodological quality was generally 'fair' to 'poor'. Clinical and family-related factors were significantly associated with outcomes (p<0.05). Conclusions Children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions risk mental health and behavioral difficulties. Current research leaves room for improvement of study quality. Multidisciplinary follow-up care is warranted, and its effects should be evaluated.

items.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials investigating cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia in stroke and traumatic brain injury populations.
items.abstract: Insomnia is highly prevalent following stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), and can contribute to challenges with mood, psychological functioning and quality of life. Emerging evidence supports the efficacy of cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for those who have experienced stroke or TBI, however a broader review incorporating sleep and mood-related outcomes has not yet been conducted. A systematic literature search was performed on Scopus, PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO databases. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2.0 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses calculating pooled effect sizes were performed, alongside assessment of heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses. Nine randomised controlled trials were included, with seven contributing to the primary meta-analysis. CBT-I was associated with lower insomnia disorder severity on the ISI (MD = -3.07, 95% CI [-4.46; -1.67], p = 0.0037) and lower sleep disturbance on the PSQI (MD = -1.81, 95% CI [-2.82; -0.80], p = 0.0058). Secondary analyses demonstrated a small, significant effect on anxiety symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.30, 95% CI [-0.49; -0.12], p = 0.0106), and a small-moderate non-significant effect on depressive symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.36, 95% CI [-0.84; 0.12], p = 0.1146). CBT-I appears a promising intervention for improving insomnia after stroke or TBI, with additional modest benefits for depression and anxiety.

items.title: Dramatised Reading Workshops for Older Adults With Neurocognitive Disorders: A Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Theatre workshops for older adults have proliferated over the last ten years and have become a field of study in psychology. These workshops include dramatised reading, which has positive effects on mood, behaviour and social relationships in older adults who do not live from neurocognitive disorders. However, no study has explored the effects of these workshops on older adults with neurocognitive disorders. The aim of this pilot study was to investigate the effects of participation in dramatised reading workshops on older adults with neurocognitive disorders. Ten women aged 70 to 95 with moderate neurocognitive disorder (MMSE score: M = 18.2, SD = 3.49) took part in dramatised reading workshops over 6 months. Participants self-assessed their feelings of loneliness, self-efficacy, quality of life, well-being and life satisfaction. Assessments were made before and after participation in the workshops. The results show positive effects on well-being (W = 0.00; p = 0.006), quality of life (W = 3.5; p = 0.017), anxiety-depressive symptoms (W = 34.5; p = 0.025) and feelings of loneliness (W = 53; p = 0.011). These results suggest that participation in dramatised reading workshops may have beneficial effects on general mood, quality of life, well-being and feelings of loneliness in older adults with neurocognitive disorders.

items.title: A theory of generalized vector coding and subicular function.
items.abstract: Neural information processing is inextricably linked to the selectivity of individual neurons, as described by their receptive fields. Far from the sensory periphery, neural representations are the result of substantial upstream processing, mixed with internally generated information. Low-dimensional spatial codes in the hippocampal formation offer a handle on understanding these representations. The subiculum, a key but comparatively understudied hippocampal area, exhibits numerous, seemingly unrelated neural codes. Neurons like boundary vector cells, corner cells, or axis-tuned cells are named after the environmental features that appear to drive them, but a common account for their neuronal selectivity is lacking. Here, we propose Disco, a theory explaining subicular functions and related neural codes in other areas. Given the continuous flow of experience, subicular activity can be understood as signaling discontinuities in that flow, coded in a vector base. Geometric discontinuities drive responses to walls, drops, objects, holes, corners, and curved surfaces. The generality of Disco enables predictions for 3D environments, natural scenes, and mixed-modality coding. Discontinuities are not identical to the concept of boundaries (abstract or spatial), as illustrated by non-spatial discontinuities in behavioral state. These yield axis coding in the model (activity along parallel maze arms). Finally, tracking population activity signals event boundaries as discontinuities in neural space. The emergence of diverse neural activity suggests that discontinuity coding may serve as a key principle in the subiculum and related brain areas supporting (spatial) memory and navigation.

items.title: Physical Activity in Daily Life and Mental Health: Investigating Aerobic Intensity and Strength Training.
items.abstract: The current study examined the relationships between different types of physical activity and mental health in daily life. Participants (24 adults, 71% females) completed physical activity and mental health surveys across seven months, contributing a total of 129 observations. Total physical activity as well as light, moderate, and vigorous aerobic activity and muscle-strengthening activity were assessed. Mental health was evaluated as depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, positive affect, and negative affect. Mixed-effects regression models using total physical activity and types of physical activity to estimate associations with mental health were completed. Higher overall physical activity scores were associated with lower depressive symptoms and higher positive affect. Moderate aerobic activity scores were associated with lower depressive symptoms and stress as well as higher positive affect but were not associated with improvements in anxiety or negative affect. These results indicate a possible correlation between increased physical activity and improved mental health as indicated by depressive symptoms, stress, and positive affect. Given the prevalence of inactive lifestyles in many societies, physical activity is a modifiable lifestyle change that may help promote mental health.

items.title: Attention to faces and voices predicts internalizing problems in a community sample of toddlers: A new measure & novel predictors.
items.abstract: Heightened internalizing problems predict negative outcomes, including anxiety and depression. However, few studies have characterized whether foundational child behaviors, such as attention, predict internalizing outcomes. We recently demonstrated that three foundational "multisensory attention skills" (e.g., maintaining and shifting/disengaging attention, matching synchronous sights and sounds) predict a variety of socioemotional, language, and cognitive outcomes. Here, we investigated whether these multisensory attention skills predict emerging internalizing problems. A community sample of 36-month-olds (N = 84) participating in a longitudinal study received the novel Multisensory Attention Assessment Protocol to assess the three multisensory attention skills to faces and voices. Parents completed the Infant-Toddler Social and Emotional Assessment to assess internalizing problems. Results from structural equation modeling indicated that better multisensory attention skills, particularly better synchrony detection and matching of faces and voices, predicted lower levels of internalizing problems. Findings also demonstrated a pathway from basic to higher-order attention skills: faster shifting to look to faces predicted longer attention maintenance to faces, which predicted greater face-voice matching, which in turn, predicted lower levels of internalizing problems. Findings identify basic, early developing attention skills to non-threatening audiovisual social stimulation as novel predictors of internalizing problems in early childhood.

items.title: Child protection case management and adolescent mental health in humanitarian contexts: A mixed-methods study in Colombia and Nigeria.
items.abstract: Adolescents in humanitarian contexts are vulnerable to emotional distress, violence and trauma. Child protection case management (CM) is a primary response service for children in these contexts. To evaluate the association between CM and adolescents' wellbeing and mental health, and to explore the pathways through which CM supports these outcomes, including the role of the caseworker-adolescent relationship. Adolescents aged 13 to 17 in Norte de Santander, Colombia (N = 90) and Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, Nigeria (N = 99). Both contexts are socially and politically unstable, hosting large numbers of refugees and internally displaced populations. Using a pre-post, single-arm mixed-methods design, the assessed wellbeing (WHO-5) and emotional distress (PHQ-A) as primary outcomes, and safety, basic needs, agency, relationships, and empathy as intermediary outcomes. Fixed-effects regression models were estimated using baseline and endline data to assess change in primary outcomes. A parallel mediation analysis was implemented with intermediary outcomes as mediator variables between caseworkers' empathy and adolescent wellbeing using PROCESS framework, combined with qualitative interviews with adolescents analyzed using axial analysis. Participation in CM was associated with a significant increase in adolescents' wellbeing (WHO-5: β = 2.71, p < 0.001) and reduced emotional distress (PHQ-A: β = -3.45, p < 0.001) at endline, alongside self-reported improvements in family and peer relationships, safety, and agency. Higher perceived caseworker empathy was associated with increased wellbeing directly, and indirectly through enhanced feelings of safety (p < 0.01) and peer relationships (p < 0.05). CM contributes to adolescent mental health in humanitarian contexts. An empathetic relationship between caseworkers and adolescents is a key CM pathway.
