items.title: Identifying the metacommunity scale reconciles deterministic and stochastic assembly in a natural mainland–island microbial system
items.abstract: Disentangling the deterministic and stochastic processes that shape microbial communities remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. The framework proposed by Vellend---selection, drift, dispersal and speciation---offers a natural conceptual scaffold, but testing these processes in natural communities is technically demanding, and analyses are often narrowed to a single process, which can lead to seemingly contradictory conclusions. Here we illustrate the promise and the pitfalls of a comprehensive application of this framework by re-analysing a temporally resolved dataset of microbial communities inhabiting water-filled tree-holes at the base of a single beech tree, a natural mainland--island system for which both neutral assembly and strong selection have been reported. We show that these views are compatible once unsupervised compositional clustering is used to identify the scale at which assembly processes should be tested. Treating each compositional cluster as a set of local communities that receive immigrants from a distinct metacommunity, we applied neutral, phylogenetic and null-model tests of selection and dispersal, metagenomic prediction and association inference. Selection operated chiefly as environmental filtering at the metacommunity level, associated with tree-hole size and shape, whereas local communities were statistically indistinguishable from stochastic assembly. Variable selection and dispersal limitation acted between metacommunities, whereas homogenizing dispersal prevailed within them. Association networks recapitulated metacommunity structure, indicating that co-occurrence largely reflects shared environment rather than interactions. In summary, performing some analyses while excluding others leads to misleading conclusions: comprehensive analyses and identifying the intrinsic scale in which selection may operate are needed to move beyond the deterministic--stochastic dichotomy.

items.title: Major Limitations on the Use of the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology Land Cover Map to Interpret Habitat Partitioning at the Holy Loch, Argyll, Scotland
items.abstract: This short communication critiques the uncritical reliance on the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) Land Cover Map for fine-scale habitat analysis, using the head of the Holy Loch, Argyll, Scotland, as a case study. Ground-truthing reveals nine major categorical and spectral deviations—including misclassified algal mats, wild radish, and complex estuarine dynamics. By highlighting these severe remote sensing artifacts in a paraglacially inherited, dynamic system, this paper establishes a foundational methodological baseline for upcoming companion studies detailing the fully mapped vegetation, structural investigations, and historical-geology of the Holy Loch

items.title: Out of the cradle: secondary expansion from a source lake is associated with loss of morphological distinctiveness in endemic Kamchatkan charrs (Salvelinus).
items.abstract: The contribution of postglacial adaptive radiations to regional freshwater fish biodiversity remains debated. To test whether such radiations can give rise to new populations in neighboring ecosystems, we reconstructed the evolutionary history of the endemic Salvelinus malma assemblage of Lake Kronotskoe (Kamchatka). We traced the dispersal of endemic lineages from the lake into adjacent basins and quantified morphological divergence between lacustrine charrs and their derived populations. Using SNPs from SLAF-seq loci, we analyzed phylogeny, genetic differentiation, contemporary hybridization and historical gene flow among eleven charr groups, and complemented these analyses with morphometric comparisons. Our results indicate that the lacustrine-addfluvial predatory and benthivorous lineages of the Lake Kronotskoe basin colonized small peripheral waterbodies via temporary riverbed connections during the Holocene. These lineages also continue to disperse downstream from the lake, which is isolated by rapids, and hybridize with anadromous S. malma. These migrations have given rise to three new isolated populations and one hybrid anadromous population. Morphological evolution in the derived populations was independent of their phylogenetic history and converged on a generalized morphology typical of pelagic or riverine fish. Thus, postglacial expansion of adaptive morphs from the source lake enhances regional diversity, while migrants can rapidly lose ancestral adaptive traits in new habitats.

items.title: Persistence revisited: Partitioning rather than media-specific reactivity dominates persistence in the environment.
items.abstract: Current regulation identifies environmentally persistent chemicals often using thresholds defined for single-media half-lives. This approach ignores the large and even dominating impact of multimedia partitioning on the (bio)availability of compounds that undergo degradation, and accordingly may underestimate the chemical lifetimes by orders of magnitude. This is demonstrated through comparing chemical half-lives in water with overall persistence (Pov) in terms of environmental lifetimes calculated through a steady-state multimedia mass-balance model. While Pov depends on the entrance compartment, Stroebe's τE, the temporal-remote-state expected environmental lifetime, is less sensitive to the initial entry compartment. Thus, τE appears most suited for the prediction of chemical persistence. In this study, a stepwise Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis showed that only four chemical properties, log values of Kow (hydrophobicity), kdeg,w and kdeg,a (degradation rate constants in water and air, respectively), and Pv (vapour pressure), are sufficient to estimate τE. But this analysis also showed non-linear error patterns despite overall good statistics, unraveling peculiarities of the non-linear log-log dependence of τE on compound properties. A machine-learning k nearest neighbors (kNN) regression model operating in the property space yields even more accurate and linear results. Application to existing data sets demonstrates the usefulness of this approach. In particular, it shows that the reduction of bioavailability due to multimedia partitioning may cause compounds classified as "readily biodegradable" to be identified as persistent when they have sufficiently high hydrophobicity (e.g. phenanthrene with log Kow = 4.5: lifetime > 30 years). The developed tools (SimpleRisk4REACH enabling τE calculation through Stroebe's mathematical procedure; kNN regression model for τE prediction) are made available to the public.

items.title: Evolutionary rewiring of the Drosophila melanogaster accessory gland by the RNA-binding protein gene, Marf1.
items.abstract: Gene expression evolution can take several forms, including changes in isoform usage, transcript abundance, and patterns of tissue- or cell type-specific expression. Using comparative and population-level transcriptomic analyses in the melanogaster subgroup of Drosophila, we previously documented the gain of Marf1 expression in the main cells of the D. melanogaster accessory gland, which produces most of the seminal fluid proteins in the species. Marf1, an RNA-binding protein, is ovary biased in the female and accessory gland biased in the male. It is required for female fertility, but its potential male functions are unknown. We investigated the possible male function of this gene using genetic, genomic, transcriptomic, and organismal analyses. We found that despite its very young expression phenotype in the male accessory gland, Marf1 has become integrated into the accessory gland gene regulatory network. We also found that its novel accessory gland expression is correlated with a fixed transposon fragment that is also associated with species-specific open chromatin in the accessory gland. Because Marf1 is located in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, which is riddled with repetitive DNA and characterized by low recombination rates and strong effects of linked selection, we hypothesize that novel accessory gland expression of this gene was deleterious and an incidental effect of centromeric hitchhiking effects, followed by compensation and integration of this gene into a novel gene regulatory network in the D. melanogaster accessory gland.

items.title: Accelerating plastic pollution mitigation in Vietnam: A circular economy policy and implementation roadmap.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution poses significant environmental and public health risks in Vietnam, driven by rising consumption and inadequate waste management. As one of the leading contributors to marine plastic leakage, the country faces challenges linked to linear economic practices and weak recycling systems. This study applies a structured narrative review protocol to synthesize evidence from policy, scientific, and institutional sources in the manuscript corpus. The analysis examines circular economy strategies and evaluates them using a comparative prioritization framework based on impact potential, implementation feasibility, and time-to-effect. The article identifies high-priority interventions for Vietnam (extended producer responsibility enforcement, source segregation, and reuse systems), highlights major barriers (fragmented governance, informal-system exclusion, and weak data systems), and proposes an actionable research and policy agenda for the transition to a circular plastics economy.

items.title: The politics of stasis and change: The motivational roots of conservatism in party platforms and citizens' own words
items.abstract: A central question in political psychology concerns the motivational roots of ideological differences between left and right. A common approach explains right-wing thinking as reflecting heightened sensitivity to threat and a motivation to protect the status quo. We argue that this approach rests on an incomplete model of goals, which overlooks the motive to conserve. Building on the ternary goal model, we examine whether the right is better characterized by maintenance (sustaining a valued present) than by protection (responding to threats). Using a multilingual classifier validated on human-rated statements, we measured goals in a top-down manner, in 892 party platforms from 11 countries, and bottom-up, in the goals spontaneously reported by 2,333 citizens in six countries and in citizens’ support for platform statements that differed in goal orientation. Top-down, right-wing parties were more maintenance-oriented than left-wing parties, and in recent decades less progress-oriented. Protection orientation did not differ by side but was higher in opposition and at the ideological margins. Bottom-up, citizens showed a similar pattern. Progress orientation was strongest on the left. Maintenance orientation followed a curve that peaked among moderate conservatives. Its linear rise with conservatism was suppressed by institutional trust, which was lower on the right. In support ratings, progress-oriented statements appealed more to the left and maintenance-oriented statements more to the right, whereas protection-oriented statements favored neither. The left–right divide thus sets two constructive aims – to progress and to maintain – against each other, while protection marks those in opposition and at the margins.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Specialized Behavioral Psychology-Based Training in Reducing Cyberloafing among Perioperative Nurses
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Cyberloafing, defined as the non-work-related use of the Internet during working hours, can negatively impact the productivity of perioperative nurses and patient safety. The high psychological stress and the need for sustained concentration in surgical environments underscore the importance of targeted interventions to reduce this behavior. Behavioral psychology-based training, by strengthening self-control and time management skills, is one of the novel approaches in this field. Aim: To evaluate the effectiveness of specialized behavioral psychology-based training in reducing various cyberloafing behaviors among perioperative nurses in educational–therapeutic hospitals in Ilam Province. Methods: This quasi-experimental study with a pre-test–post-test control group design was conducted in 2025 on 40 perioperative nurses (20 in the experimental group and 20 in the control group) selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the standard Cyberloafing Questionnaire, which includes four subscales: “personal messaging/email,” “social networks,” “online shopping and financial activities,” and “online entertainment/multimedia.” The Cronbach’s alpha of the Persian version was 0.87. The intervention consisted of four 90-minute behavioral psychology-based training sessions over two weeks for the experimental group. Data were analyzed using paired t-test, independent t-test, and Cohen’s d effect size (α = 0.05). Results: In the experimental group, the mean total cyberloafing score decreased from 38.5 ± 6.7 to 29.1 ± 5.4 (t = 9.21, p Conclusion: Specialized behavioral psychology-based training significantly reduces cyberloafing behaviors among perioperative nurses across multiple dimensions and can contribute to improved occupational focus and enhanced patient safety. It is recommended that such training be incorporated into the professional development programs of healthcare centers, particularly in high-stress environments.

items.title: Leading System Transformation Through a Quality Standard Development Process for the Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions Sector.
items.abstract: Quality standards can improve service quality, accountability, and equity. Their development in Community-based Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions (CYMHA) settings requires sector-specific guidance and processes. Few standards are tailored to Ontario's CYMHA sector, and research on developing such standards remains scarce. This article presents the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Knowledge Institute on Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions (KI) Standard Development Process (SDP) for quality standards in the CYMHA sector. Drawing on experience developing standards and reviewing other approaches, the KI formalized a methodology that foregrounds collaboration with youth, families, service providers, and system leaders. The process follows four phases-scoping, drafting, mobilizing, and maintaining-and integrates implementation science, evaluation, and meaningful engagement. This article details the SDP development and pilot. It highlights the value of a replicable, evidence-informed approach and multi-partner collaboration in developing relevant, meaningful, standards and achieving system-wide implementation.

items.title: Seasonal Symptoms Are Related to Rumination and Habitual Negative Thinking.
items.abstract: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a mood disorder with a seasonal pattern that emerges usually in the winter and remits in summer. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the role of rumination and habits of negative thinking as vulnerability factors in elevated sensitivity to seasons and the potential change of these factors over seasons. A total of 185 participants completed a digital survey about seasonal patterns (SPAQ), ruminative response style (RRS), habits of negative thinking (HINT), and symptoms of depression (PHQ-9); 169 participated in a mood induction task, and 133 were followed up longitudinally with assessments in summer and winter. SPAQ scores correlated significantly with PHQ-9 scores, RRS scores, and HINT scores (all p < 0.001). Participants with a SAD diagnosis and elevated seasonal symptoms differed significantly on these scales from people with low seasonal symptoms. Longitudinal analysis revealed that only participants with a SAD diagnosis showed significant increases in their depression scores from summer to winter, while group differences on all other scales did not change significantly across seasons. In a mood induction task, we found baseline differences in mood and rumination, but no increased propensity of experiencing sad mood or state rumination among individuals with a SAD diagnosis or elevated seasonal symptoms as compared to participants with low levels of seasonal symptoms. Psychological factors such as rumination and its habitual features might be present all year round as a trait-like cognitive vulnerability, contributing to the development of seasonal symptoms and SAD.

items.title: Stability and change in loneliness among older Europeans: a trait-state-occasion analysis of SHARE data.
items.abstract: Background Loneliness in later life is a prevalent psychological experience that reflects both stable individual differences and changing social circumstances, yet little is known about the relative contribution of these components over time. The aims are: a) to partition the variance of loneliness into trait vs. occasion (state); and b) to accommodate covariates related to social contact (received and given help). Method Data comes from three waves of the Survey of Health, Aging and Retirement in Europe. Loneliness was measured with UCLA-R Scale. Results The trait component accounted for approximately 60% of the latent variance, whereas the occasion component accounted for approximately 40%. The TSO model was extended to include covariates. Received help was positively associated with trait-like loneliness, whereas given help was negatively associated with it. Associations with occasion-specific components were generally weaker and mostly non-significant, with two statistically significant exceptions. Conclusions Most of the loneliness seems to be trait-like. The time-varying loneliness was smaller in size, but relevant. Helping exchanges were more consistently associated with the stable component of loneliness than with occasion-specific variability.

items.title: Implementing LGBTQ+ Inclusive Mental Health Care Into Practice: Barriers and Facilitators in an Australian Local Health Network.
items.abstract: Mapping implicit barriers to and facilitators of care in ways that are sensitive to LGBTQ+ people's needs within health systems is key to improving LGBTQ+ mental health care. We conducted such a mapping within an Australian local health network's mental health services ("the Network"). Ethnographic fieldwork (in which we captured researcher impressions of the service-sites and the views of staff), was analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. To help us more effectively evidence and target findings specific to actors within different levels of the Network, we further broke down themes and subthemes using the five domains of the i-PARIHS framework- Innovation, Recipients, Local Context, Organisational Context , and the Outer Context . Two primary themes were developed: 1) affective responses to the intended change, including resistance to change, embarrassment about current inadequate practices , and a desire for change ; and 2) facilitators of pathways to change, including means of leveraging existing resources, contextual safety signals , and participants voicing a call for knowing what to do . The findings suggest clear barriers to improving LGBTQ+ inclusivity alongside goodwill to support change. Our findings and novel usage of the i-PARIHS framework show promising applicability to other LGBTQ+ mental health-care equity settings.

items.title: Comparing multivariate cognitive change in unimpaired older adults to those with questionable impairment or mild dementia: a NACC study.
items.abstract: Introduction We explored how frequently unimpaired older adults show declines across multiple cognitive measures and examined the extent to which their rates of multivariate cognitive change compared to older adults with questionable impairment or mild dementia. Method Two-year change scores were calculated for 1208 participants in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) database. The number of declines in performance falling below the 5 th percentile in the natural distribution of change scores (the total change count) among the unimpaired participants ( n = 742) was compared to those with questionable impairment ( n = 389) and those with mild dementia ( n = 77). Results Only 9.9% of the cognitively unimpaired participants obtained two or more significant declines in performance, compared to 27.5% of the questionably impaired participants and 49.4% of those with mild dementia. The total change count demonstrated significant discriminative ability for distinguishing between cognitively unimpaired participants and those with questionable impairment (AUC = .621) or mild dementia (AUC = .759). The threshold of two or more declines maintained high specificity (90.1%) for identifying atypical cognitive decline. In a multinomial logistic regression, a change count of two or more was a robust predictor of both questionable impairment (OR = 3.47) and mild dementia (OR = 8.55), beyond the effects of demographic covariates (age, gender, education, race/ethnicity). Conclusions Less than one tenth of cognitively unimpaired older adults show two or more significant declines in their performance on 13 measures from the NACC UDS 3.0 neuropsychological test battery. Individuals who exhibit two or more significant declines in their raw scores across this battery are likely experiencing atypical cognitive decline. Establishing longitudinal base rates of cognitive change across a test battery offers a viable, empirically grounded approach to identifying progression along the dementia continuum.

items.title: "Woven into the fabric of life": young adults' normalisation of stress in contemporary Aotearoa.
items.abstract: Objective This research explored 'lay' or everyday sense-making of young adults in Aotearoa New Zealand around stress. Stress has become a widely understood and commonly experienced phenomenon, with associated physical and mental health consequences. Contemporary understandings around stress are produced by and within context. Currently Aotearoa is dominated by neoliberal ideology, and an acceptance of 'hustle culture', with social media and digital technology increasingly embedded in daily life. Methods and measures We generated data using nine focus groups (online and in person), with 29 young adults (mean age 27), recruited through a range of strategies. Most participants identified as Pākehā or NZ European (20), two as Indian, and the remaining each identified as different ethnicities, including one as Māori. Taking a critical, social constructionist approach, we used reflexive thematic analysis to develop patterns in how stress is made sense of by young adults. Results: The analysis we report here focuses on the normalisation of stress. This analytic interpretation was conveyed through four themes: the pervasiveness of stress; (modern) life is stressful; but stress is the way you win; and stress as poison, and as medicine. Conclusions Stress was framed as a normal, natural, and universal experience, accepted as part of everyday life, and even desirable within the neoliberal contemporary context.

items.title: Correcting misconceptions and shaping preferences about energy with reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Addressing the climate crisis requires citizens to make informed choices about sustainable energy policy, yet public debates are often shaped by inaccurate beliefs about the environmental and health impacts of different energy sources. Misconceptions about key features of energy sources, such as their greenhouse gas emissions, mortality rates, and contribution to electricity production, are particularly dangerous for this debate, as they risk systematically distorting public support for effective decarbonisation strategies. Here we investigate whether a brief reinforcement‑based intervention can correct such misconceptions and influence societal investment preferences. Across seven countries, we reveal systematic misbeliefs, such as overestimating the emissions and mortality of nuclear power and under‑estimating the mortality of biomass, which were corrected by our intervention across all features and countries. Furthermore, correcting beliefs led to shifts in preferences towards objectively cleaner and safer energy mixes, and these changes were consistent across countries. Follow‑up assessments indicated that most of our intervention’s effects were detectable after 14 weeks. These results demonstrate a three‑step actionable pathway, from behavioural feedback, through belief correction, to preference change, and suggest that short, reinforcement‑based interventions could be a scalable tool for improving public decision‑making in climate policy and other domains where misconceptions pollute the debate.

items.title: Do Traffic Congestion Indicators Improve PM2.5 Forecasting? Evidence from Machine Learning Models in Kampala
items.abstract: Abstract Air pollution remains a major environmental and public health challenge in Kampala, Uganda, where PM 2.5 concentrations frequently exceed World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines values. Although traffic emissions are widely recognized as contributors to urban air pollution, limited empirical evidence exists on whether traffic-congestion indicators improve PM 2.5 forecasting beyond information provided by meteorological and temporal variables. This study evaluated the predictive contribution of traffic-congestion indicators to PM 2.5 using machine learning models. PM 2.5 , temperature, and humidity observations were obtained from the AirQo monitoring network, while traffic data were collected along the Jinja Road transport using the Google Routes API. After preprocessing and temporal synchronization, a dataset consisting of 696 hourly observations was used to implement Random Forest and HistGradientBoosting forecasting models. Environmental baseline models were compared with traffic-enhanced models incorporating mean speed, travel duration, and Traffic Performance Index (TPI). Model performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the coefficient of determination (R 2 ). Results showed that the best environmental baseline model, HistGradientBoosting, achieved superior performance (MAE = 15.28, RMSE = 21.40, R 2 = 0.5752) compared with the best traffic-enhanced model (MAE = 23.16, RMSE = 31.70, R 2 = 0.4753). Correlation and feature-importance analysis further indicated that traffic-congestion indicators exhibited weak relationships with PM2.5 concentrations and contributed substantially to less predictive information than temporal and meteorological variables. An additional analysis incorporating lagged PM 2.5 variables achieved the highest explanatory performance (R 2 = 0.6245), highlighting the importance of historical pollution measurements in forecasting future PM 2.5 concentrations. The findings suggest that, within the study context, corridor-level congestion indicators provided limited incremental forecasting value, while temporal patterns, meteorological conditions, and historical PM 2.5 measurements were more influential predictors. The study contributes empirical evidence for evaluating predictor relevance in machine-learning based air-quality forecasting and provides insights for the design of efficient forecasting systems in rapidly urbanizing cities.

items.title: Towards real-time wastewater pollution tracking: Evaluating the performance of instrumentation-based wastewater pollution proxies in an urban estuary
items.abstract: Abstract Wastewater pollution poses risks to both ecosystem and public health via the introduction of pathogens, excessive nutrients, and chemicals of emerging concern to the aquatic environment. Typical monitoring to alert the public of elevated fecal bacteria levels and potential wastewater pollution relies on discrete water samples and 24-hr culturing of indicator bacteria, which leads to alerts being posted no earlier than 1–2 days after pollution impacts. Discrete sampling can also miss acute wastewater impacts from storms or spills. Therefore, there is interest in real-time proxies to provide earlier public alerts and track wastewater pollution inputs to water bodies at a finer time scale. Emerging proxies include real-time monitoring of dissolved organic fluorescence, particularly tracking fluorescence wavelengths similar to optical brighteners (a component of laundry detergent) and tryptophan (an amino acid) that have been demonstrated to be enriched in wastewater. In this study, we examined the ability of in situ, real-time-capable sensors to predict wastewater-associated fecal indicator bacteria concentrations in the Ala Wai Harbor, Honolulu, HI. A fluorometer measuring “optical brightener” fluorescence and “tryptophan” fluorescence was deployed alongside an existing long-term monitoring sensor package measuring temperature, salinity, turbidity, and chlorophyll-a fluorescence. Discrete bottle samples were analyzed for fecal indicator bacteria, sucralose (a conservative wastewater tracer), nutrients, and 3-D scans of fluorescent dissolved organic matter. A positive correlation was observed between culture-based counts of the fecal indicator bacteria Enterococcus spp. and sucralose, which is found only in human waste, indicating consistent wastewater contamination in the Ala Wai Harbor. Dissolved fluorescence measurements in the wavelengths associated with optical brighteners were found to be the best instrumentation-based predictor of Enterococcus spp. concentrations, alone or in combination with other parameters (R 2 = 0.71–0.72). The best-specified categorical models to predict Enterococcus spp. exceedances of the Hawaiʻi state threshold of 130 colony forming units (CFU) /100 mL included both optical brightener fluorescence and salinity with > 95% sensitivity and ~ 75% specificity. The addition of the optical brightener fluorescence channel doubled the explained variance in fecal indicator bacteria by real-time sensors when compared to the existing suite of temperature, salinity, and turbidity (R 2 =0.36–0.38). Our results demonstrate that real-time measurements of optical brightener fluorescence could provide instantaneous warnings of wastewater spills and elevated fecal bacteria levels in waterways at risk of wastewater pollution, and this data stream could be integrated into existing outflow plume models and forecasts to provide better real-time estimates of water safety for ocean users in the surrounding marine areas.

items.title: Researching adaptations in equitable, diverse, and inclusive co-design practice during and beyond the pandemic: innovations in a design research realist synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, public health requirements for physical distancing and restrictions on physical gathering significantly altered how co-design could be conducted in health care contexts, especially negatively affecting projects engaging individuals from marginalized communities. Rapid adaptations were made with varied levels of success. A conventional strategy for understanding these adaptations would have been a review of published literature. However, few detailed accounts had been published at the time, and many co-designers were still actively exploring how to adapt their methods. Objectives This research investigated co-design practices to learn what adaptations were successful in engaging marginalized communities, what adaptations might be applied in other contexts, and what might be sustained post-pandemic. Design The overall research design was a realist synthesis, focusing on what works, for whom, and in what circumstances. An initial framework of co-design principles that contribute to equitable, diverse and inclusive (EDI) participation was developed to structure the analysis of adaptations that were made. However, with changes still underway and many adaptations not published, innovations to realist methods were necessary. In addition to a literature scan, design research approaches (workshops, interviews, a Community of Practice, webinars, a Winter School, and conference presentations) were used to generate data and validate findings iteratively. Setting and participants The data collection and analysis took place mostly online. Design researchers, health researchers and design practitioners from three continents were engaged in the various activities over time. Results Adding design research approaches to the realist synthesis identified many adaptations that would otherwise not have been recorded or noticed. Substantively, there were significant numbers of successful adaptations aligned with four initial EDI principles, and three additional categories of adaptations were identified. Conclusions Adapting realist methods to include design research approaches can be fruitful, especially when the evidence and experience under investigation are actively in development. Many of the adaptations that were made during the pandemic can potentially be carried into post-pandemic co-design practice, increasing opportunities for engagement with individuals from marginalized communities. Disseminating these findings in ways that are useable by co-designers is the next step in this research.

items.title: Catalysing system reforms in Pakistan’s Healthcare and Health Professions Education: National Stakeholder priorities for strengthening policy and system Governance
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Pakistan has broadened its medical and dental education sphere, yet apprehensions last about undergraduates’ competence, impact of regulation, international acknowledgment of qualifications and retention of the health workforce. This study explored multi stakeholder perspectives on training capacity, quality of education, governance, regulation and acknowledgment of health professions education in Pakistan, and identified prime reforms. Methodology: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using hybrid focus group discussion held on 4 August 2026 as part of national Health and Education Summit Pakistan (HESP) 2026. Fourteen purposively sampled stakeholders participated in discussion guided by 16 semi structured questions. Data were analysed using Framework Method, and Health Policy Triangle was applied as an interpretive lens. Results Nine themes were identified across three domains. Educational quality and competence : undefined and unenforced competency standards; deficits in clinical training infrastructure; faculty development and continuous quality improvement; and cautious, purpose-specific integration of artificial intelligence. Governance, regulation and recognition : fragmented, input-oriented governance; private-sector representation and public–private imbalance; and international recognition and global alignment. Workforce and equity : equity in workforce planning; and workforce sustainability, security and dignity. Participants identified main barrier to reform is not in an absence of policy but in weak implementation, input based accreditation and poor coordination among regulatory bodies. Conclusion Stakeholders called for a shift from input based to outcome-based accreditation built on a nationally agreed definition of competence, a shared inter agency governance platform, documented clinical supervision and simulation, and workforce protection measures.

items.title: Identification and Characterization of Linear B-Cell Epitopes in Plasmodium falciparum MSP9 Protein for Potential Application in Malaria Serodiagnosis
items.abstract: Background: Malaria remains a major global public health problem, causing millions of cases and thousands of deaths each year. Without an effective antimalarial vaccine, diagnosis remains a key strategy for disease control. However, false-negative results due to the emergence of P. falciparum populations with deletions in the Pfhrp2/3 genes may compromise case management. Thus, this study aimed to identify and characterize linear B-cell epitopes of the MSP9 protein to evaluate new targets for developing high-precision biotechnological tools for malaria diagnosis. Methods: We mapped MSP9 epitopes using a peptide microarray strategy, followed by epitope screening with bioinformatics tools and ELISA validation. Results: We identified 31 MSP9 epitopes through SPOT synthesis, 16 of which were in regions exhibiting low structural or chemical similarity to homologous proteins from other Plasmodium species. ELISA analysis revealed that the peptides PfMSP9/IgG/23, PfMSP9/IgG/27, and PfMSP9/IgG/30 exhibited sensitivities of 44.81%, 87.23%, and 46.81%, and specificities of 81.82%, 95.74%, and 89.74%, respectively. Conclusions: Our findings indicate that the PfMSP9/IgG/27 peptide, owing to its high sensitivity and specificity, enabled the differentiation of individuals infected with P. falciparum from those infected with P. vivax. Despite the low sensitivity of the other peptides, their high specificity allowed us to differentiate between the two organisms. We believe that using additional MSP9 epitopes and applying the same approach to other P. falciparum proteins will make it possible to develop a chimeric antigen for serological diagnosis of malaria.

items.title: Novel wounded porcine skin ex vivo methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection models.
items.abstract: Chronic wounds are a growing challenge in clinical practice and can be associated with infection by antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. With increasing demand for pathophysiology research and therapeutic technology development, biologically relevant platforms like infected swine skin explants are used; however, explants are not typically studied in conjunction with normal microbiota, which recapitulates the clinical scenario. The current study generated 1- and 8-cm diameter wounded swine skin explants from shaved, sanitized swine skin harvested immediately after euthanasia. Tissue morphology was evaluated over 9 days using a custom histological grading scale and growth dynamics of skin microbiota monitored. Explant viability decreased after 3 days in association with a peak in normal microbiota of varying diversity. Stable co-colonization of wound beds with clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates alongside microbiota over 3 days was demonstrated. In summary, the presented 1- and 8-cm explant models maintain normal microbiota and are suitable for microbiome and/or wound infection treatment or prevention studies.

items.title: Sarcopenia Beyond the Clinic: A Community-Based Pilot Screening Study Among Elderly Kuwaitis.
items.abstract: Objective This pilot study screened community-dwelling elderly Kuwaitis for sarcopenia using Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 criteria to inform public health strategy. Material and methods In this unfunded cross-sectional pilot study, 61 Kuwaiti nationals aged ≥60 years were recruited in Al Asimah Governorate. Handgrip strength and physical performance (Short Physical Performance Battery [SPPB]) were assessed in all participants. Possible sarcopenia was defined as low handgrip strength or impaired physical performance; screen-positive participants underwent multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) to confirm sarcopenia by muscle mass. Groups were compared with chi-square/Fisher's exact and t-/Mann-Whitney tests; 95% confidence intervals (CI) used the Wilson score method. Results Possible sarcopenia was identified in 33 of 61 participants (54.1%, CI 41.7-66.0%), rising from 21.4% (CI 7.6-47.6%) at 60-69 years to 90.9% (CI 72.2-97.5%) at ≥80 years (p Conclusion This pilot study provides the first community-based evidence of a high possible-sarcopenia burden among elderly Kuwaitis, with muscle-mass confirmation in nearly one-third of screen-positive cases and marked age and gender gradients. These findings warrant a larger, nationally representative validation study and support two-step sarcopenia screening in routine geriatric care. .

items.title: Cancer Incidence and Mortality Patterns in Central Asia in 2022 and an Assessment of the Future Burden in 2045.
items.abstract: Central Asia is undergoing rapid epidemiological transition, yet internationally comparable assessments of cancer profiles in the constituent countries (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan) remain limited. We aimed to describe patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across the region and to project the future cancer burden through 2045. Cancer incidence and mortality estimates in 2022 were obtained for the five countries from IARC's GLOBOCAN database. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were compared by country, sex and cancer type. The future cancer burden was projected by applying age-specific cancer rates to population projections, assuming stable rates over time. In 2022, an estimated 92,665 new cancer cases and 56,110 cancer deaths occurred across Central Asia. Kazakhstan had the highest overall incidence and mortality rates, whereas the lowest rates across most major cancer sites were consistently estimated for Tajikistan. Breast cancer was the most common cancer among women, and lung cancer among men. The regional cancer profile was characterised by the coexistence of infection-related cancers alongside those linked to socioeconomic transition. Assuming stable rates, the annual number of new cancer cases is projected to increase by approximately 65%, reaching 152,000 by 2045, while cancer deaths are projected to increase by 73% to nearly 97,000 deaths. Cancer patterns in Central Asia suggest that regional cancer control planning should be nuanced to reflect each country's profile and resources, balancing prevention of infection-related cancers with early detection and effective management of common cancers associated with ongoing socioeconomic transitions.

items.title: Climate change anxiety and insomnia in nursing students: implications for health promotion?
items.abstract: Background Climate change is not only an environmental crisis but also an emerging mental health concern. This study investigated the relationship between climate change anxiety and insomnia severity among nursing students in the Mediterranean Region of Turkey. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 512 participants between December 2024 and January 2025. Data were collected using the Descriptive Information Form, the Climate Change Anxiety Scale (CCAS), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Results The mean CCAS score was 1.63 ± 0.69 and the mean ISI score was 13.20 ± 4.18. Correlation analysis revealed a moderate positive relationship between climate change anxiety and insomnia severity ( r = 0.372, p Conclusions Climate change anxiety is associated with increased insomnia severity among nursing students, highlighting the mental health implications of climate-related psychological stress. Health promotion initiatives within universities should incorporate resilience-building, sleep hygiene education, and mental health support to address climate-related anxiety. Further longitudinal and multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings and guide effective public health interventions.

items.title: A Blessing in Disguise: The Long-Term Effects of Childhood Exposure to the Boll Weevil on Old-Age Male Longevity.
items.abstract: The infamous agricultural pest, the boll weevil, spread across southern US counties between 1892 and 1920. It had devastating impacts on cotton production, a highly child-labor-intensive crop. This study examines how the arrival of the boll weevil and the subsequent reductions in child labor affect later-life mortality outcomes. Using Social Security Administration death records linked with the 1940 census, we document that the staggered spread of the boll weevil improved the longevity of exposed male children. Full exposure to the boll weevil is associated with an intent-to-treat effect of 1-3 months of higher longevity. We show that the estimated effects are robust across a wide array of specifications, are not driven by sociodemographic and socioeconomic compositional change in the final sample, and are not associated with pre-existing trends in the outcome. Further, we find larger impacts among Blacks, children of lower educated mothers, whose fathers work in the farming industry, and those born in high cotton intensity counties. Moreover, the effects appear to be substantially larger among children in states with less restrictive child labor policies, implying the role of these policies in reducing the adverse effects of child labor in the absence of the boll weevil in cotton production counties. Affected children are more likely to migrate, and their destination counties are more likely to be urban and have higher socioeconomic scores. The 1940 census suggests that the exposed children attain higher levels of education and have higher socioeconomic scores. We discuss the policy implications of these results in relation to child labor and school attendance policies in developing countries.

items.title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models.
items.abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

items.title: The Long-term cognitive and mental health impacts of pandemic-induced social isolation: a trajectory analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives The COVID-19 pandemic imposed social deprivation on older adults, offering a natural experiment to test trajectories of cognitive vulnerability and psychological resilience. Guided by a Dual-Pathway Framework, we investigated how pandemic-era community-based social participation trajectories predicted 2022 cognitive and mental health outcomes, and whether childhood adversity (CA) moderated these effects. Methods We analyzed nationally representative longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Study, with final analytic samples of 2,457 for depressive symptoms and 1,679 for cognitive function. Survey-weighted multivariable regressions using baseline-adjusted change scores evaluated how 2016-2020 social participation trajectories (Consistently Isolated, Pandemic Drop-off, Consistently Engaged, Pandemic Initiators) predicted changes in cognitive function and depressive symptoms from 2016 to 2022. Models adjusted for 2016 baselines, sociodemographic disadvantages, and physical health constraints, while testing moderation by cumulative CA. Results Compared with Consistently Engaged peers, the Pandemic Drop-off cohort showed significant cognitive decline by 2022, resembling the Consistently Isolated. This drop-off did not predict worsened long-term depressive symptoms. CA independently predicted poorer mental health. Binary models showed no moderation, while continuous sensitivity analyses suggested a potential protective interaction between late-life social initiation and cumulative early-life trauma for cognitive preservation. Pandemic Initiators preserved cognitive function comparable to consistently engaged adults. Discussion Findings support the Dual-Pathway Framework: the aging mind demonstrates emotional adaptation, whereas the aging brain may show accelerated aging after abrupt community-level social deprivation. Social participation may be important for cognitive health. Mitigating post-pandemic cognitive decline may require treating social isolation as a clinical vital sign and supporting social prescribing.

items.title: Nurse Practitioner Practice in Nurse-Managed Health Clinics: A Cross-Sectional 6-State Study.
items.abstract: Nurse-managed health clinics (NMHCs) are settings in which the rapidly growing workforce of nurse practitioners (NPs) can serve as the main providers of primary care services. Depending on state requirements, NMHCs may operate with little or no physician involvement. If NMHCs promote NP recruitment and retention, they may help address critical primary care shortages in underserved areas. Assessing this potential requires evidence on the practice characteristics, practice patterns, work environments, and job outcomes for NPs practicing in NMHCs. To examine these factors, we compared NPs practicing in NMHCs ( n = 48) to NPs practicing in clinics not identified as NMHCs ( n = 1196) using data from a 6-state study. NPs in NMHCs had greater independent practice support (3.81 vs. 3.46; p p p p = .0033), performance feedback (0.47 vs. 0.62; p = .0150), and after-hours care (0.28 vs. 0.42; p = .0330). We found comparable rates of burnout, job dissatisfaction, and likelihood of leaving the job among NPs in NMHCs and other settings ( p > .05). NPs in NMHCs spent more time performing leadership (4.0 hr vs. 1.9 hr; p = .0026) and quality improvement activities (3.5 hr vs. 1.9 hr, p = .0231). Findings suggest that NPs in NMHCs experience favorable work environments and comparable job outcomes, while engaging in leadership and quality improvement activities. Lower structural capabilities in these settings may be related to their smaller size. Thus, NMHCs may support primary care NP recruitment and retention in underserved areas.

items.title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference.
items.abstract: When meeting new individuals or known individuals in new circumstances, we intuitively map out their relationships-not merely through direct experience, but by inferring new connections on the basis of prior relational knowledge. How such relational knowledge is represented and used in the brain remains a long-standing question in cognitive neuroscience. Here, using a behavioural task and computational modelling, we show that participants (N = 36) leveraged existing knowledge of relational structures to infer new relationships, facilitating adaptation in changing environments. Whole-brain neuroimaging identified consistent representations of relational structure in the hippocampus. To investigate the causal link between hippocampal representations and inference, we used neural network simulations to predict the behavioural effects of disrupting such representations. Consistent with this prediction, transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the human hippocampus (N = 20), transiently modulating its activity, disrupted structure-based inference (P < 0.001, Cohen's d = -0.89, 95% confidence interval -1.41 to -0.36), providing empirical evidence for a causal role of hippocampus in relational-structure learning and structure-based inference.

items.title: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation - from gene discovery to therapeutic strategies.
items.abstract: Precision therapeutics are emerging for various neurological disorders, most notably single-gene disorders. Development of breakthrough treatments typically requires insight into the earliest pathogenic changes, which enables intervention before irreversible damage to cell function has occurred. At the extreme, presymptomatic gene therapy could subvert entire disease processes. The neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders exemplify progress from Mendelian disease gene discovery to the era of precision neurotherapeutics. These disorders highlight the opportunities and challenges in developing precision therapeutics for single-gene neurological disorders. In this Review, we discuss the most common NBIA disorders to highlight how the study of genetic disorders can provide insight into basic neuroscience and the brain's regional vulnerability. We discuss in detail the biology of pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN), which underscores the complex and poorly understood biochemistry of this apparently simple inborn error of vitamin metabolism, and also forges a path for novel interventions. The progress in understanding of and therapeutic development for PKAN exemplifies the beginning of a rise in breakthrough therapies for genetic neurological disorders.

items.title: Selective and spatially biased activity remodeling following adult-onset sensory loss.
items.abstract: Cross-modal brain plasticity after sensory loss allows an organism to utilize the remaining senses to guide behavior. Two distinct mechanisms support such adaptation: cross-modal recruitment and compensatory plasticity. Cross-modal recruitment refers to the deprived sensory areas gaining responsiveness to the spared senses, while compensatory plasticity indicates enhanced functionality of the spared sensory areas. Widespread synaptic and circuit-level plasticity has been reported to support such cross-modal plasticity. Here we combined whole-brain clearing, light-sheet imaging, and activity labeling using a cFosTRAP2 mouse line to examine the spatial distribution of highly active cells across brain areas following acute sensory manipulations in adult mice of both sexes. Adult-onset vision loss led to an initial decrease in the density of activity-labeled cells in visual areas, including the primary visual cortex (V1), and a parallel increase in the spared primary auditory (A1) and somatosensory barrel (S1BF) cortices. V1 and some higher-order visual areas (HVAs), but not the visual thalamus, exhibited a partial rebound in activity after a week of vision loss. The activity rebound in visual cortices and the enhanced activity observed in A1 were spatially biased. Passively exposing adult-onset blind mice to sound did not further alter activity levels, except for a decrease in the claustrum. Conversely, adult-onset deafening significantly reduced the activity-labeled cell density in auditory and auditory-related areas without clear signs of compensatory plasticity in the spared areas. Our results indicate that adult cross-modal plasticity is largely observed in sensory cortices with rather specific within-area spatial bias, suggesting selective functional adaptations. Significance Statement This study examined the spatial profile of how the adult brain adapts when one sense is lost. In mice, vision loss caused brain activity to drop in visual areas followed by partial recovery over time, suggesting gradual recruitment of these areas by non-visual information. In parallel, the brain areas for hearing and touch became more active, a sign of compensation. Activity changes were not widespread but limited mainly to sensory areas with some local spatial bias. In contrast, the same duration of hearing loss produced much less evidence of compensation in the spared sensory areas. These findings suggest that the adult brain can reorganize after sensory loss, but this adaptation is selective and region-specific, implying targeted functional compensation.

items.title: RAI1 loss produces cell type-specific transcriptomic, circuit, and behavioural consequences across mPFC GABAergic interneuron subtypes.
items.abstract: Haploinsufficiency of RAI1 ( retinoic acid-induced 1 ) causes Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, maladaptive behaviours, and social deficits. RAI1 is a transcriptional regulator broadly expressed across multiple brain cell types, yet the cell type-specific transcriptional consequences of Rai1 haploinsufficiency remain unknown. Behavioural experiments used mice of both sexes. Our spatial transcriptomic assays in Rai1 +/- mice identified dysregulated genes across isocortical cell types, with synaptic organization and activity-dependent programs affected in a subtype-specific manner among GABAergic interneurons. To explore RAI1 function in these cells, we conditionally deleted Rai1 from parvalbumin (PV), somatostatin (SST), and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) interneurons. In the social dominance tube test, PV- and SST-specific Rai1 loss reduced winning rates, whereas VIP-specific loss increased winning. Rai1 ⁺/⁻ mice showed social competition-induced PV/VIP cFos activation in the medial-prefrontal cortex. Overall mPFC cFos activity was increased in VIP mutants but was decreased in PV and SST mutants. Monosynaptic rabies tracing revealed RAI1-dependent, subtype-specific remodeling of long-range inputs onto mPFC interneurons. Chemogenetic inhibition of Rai1 -deficient mPFC PV or VIP interneurons normalized the social competition phenotypes. Together, our findings reveal that Rai1 haploinsufficiency induces cell-type-specific transcriptional and anatomical reorganization of prefrontal interneurons, which bidirectionally biases social behaviour output and is acutely reversible by targeted activity modulation. By resolving how a broadly expressed gene produces divergent consequences across interneuron classes, our work clarifies the cellular origins of social deficits in SMS and points to subtype-selective interneuron modulation as a therapeutic strategy i SMS and GABAergic disorders. Significance statement Social behavioural deficits are a prominent feature of SMS, a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of the transcriptional regulator RAI1 GABAergic interneuron subtypes in the medial prefrontal cortex are critical for social behaviour, but the transcriptional programs governing their functional development and maturation are largely unknown. Here we show that Rai1 loss causes subtype-specific transcriptomic and anatomical input reorganization, and altered Fos activity in PV, SST, and VIP interneurons, culminating in divergent social competitive outcomes. The net social deficit likely arises from competing cell-type-specific perturbations. Notably, acute modulation of interneuron activity normalizes social behaviour, highlighting a potential therapeutic opportunity. Our findings emphasize the need for subtype-specific interventions and provide a cell-type-resolved framework for understanding GABAergic dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: A dorsoventral gradient of synaptic dynamics across columns of the midbrain periaqueductal gray.
items.abstract: The midbrain periaqueductal gray (PAG) is an evolutionarily conserved, highly interconnected brain region that coordinates diverse physiological and behavioral responses essential for survival, including pain modulation, autonomic and cardiovascular regulation, and defensive responses to threat. The PAG is anatomically and functionally subdivided into longitudinal columns that generate divergent behavioral and physiological responses. However, little is known about how distinct synaptic properties of neurons in each column support column-specific information processing. To address this gap, we made whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings from unlabeled neurons in the ventrolateral (vl), lateral (l), and dorsomedial (dm) columns of PAG in adult male and female C57BL/6J mice. Our results demonstrate that many features of synaptic processing are conserved across columns, including the relative balance of synaptic inhibition/excitation as well as stable paired pulse ratios across a wide range of interstimulus intervals. Despite these commonalities, high frequency stimulation revealed significant cross-column differences in synaptic integration mechanisms. Specifically, phasic EPSC amplitudes remained stable in the vlPAG and, to a lesser extent, the lPAG. In stark contrast, high frequency stimulation resulted in pronounced temporal summation in the dmPAG, due to, in part, slower EPSC kinetics. This profile resulted in the generation of an envelope/slow current during high-frequency trains which counteracted more pronounced phasic EPSC depression observed in the dmPAG. Together, these results identify column-specific strategies to preserve excitatory signal transfer across the PAG, providing a synaptic basis for how distinct columns process information to support their specialized functional roles. eNeuro Assessment The study investigates synaptic properties of periaqueductal grey (PAG) neurons in distinct divisions. The authors report convincing data for division-specific synaptic dynamics. The experiments are rigorously designed, the data are of high quality, and the statistical power and analyses are appropriate. The results provide important information about region-specific response properties within the PAG and have implication for the interpretation of the contribution of this circuit to behavior.

items.title: Nature, Nurture, and Early Childhood Development: Emerging Evidence and Opportunities for Pediatrics.
items.abstract: Early childhood represents a unique window of biological vulnerability and developmental opportunity 1 . Brain plasticity during the first years of life suggests that environmental exposures and relational experiences may exert profound and lasting effects on cognitive, emotional, and physical health throughout the lifespan 2,3 . Within the framework of contemporary developmental neuroscience, pediatric research has increasingly focused on how physical surroundings, particularly green spaces and natural environments, interact with socio-emotional experiences to shape early developmental trajectories. A major research initiative recently announced in Europe, by the Royal Foundation Centre for Early Childhood 4 , brings this intersection to the forefront. This commentary authored by members of the working group on Social Pediatrics of the European Pediatric Association, Union of National Pediatric Societies and Associations (EPA-UNEPSA), briefly explores current evidence across environmental psychology and pediatric developmental research, reporting recent parental survey data, with the aim to highlight the opportunities and methodological challenges this initiative may present for social and preventive pediatrics.

items.title: Beta 1 -adrenergic receptor regulation of VMN growth hormone-releasing hormone neuron lactate, estrogen, and counterregulatory transmitter receptor gene expression in male versus female rats.
items.abstract: The metabolic-sensitive hindbrain transmitter norepinephrine (NE) controls ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus (VMN) growth hormone-releasing hormone (Ghrh)/steroidogenic factor-1 (SF1) neuron counterregulatory neurotransmission via beta1-adrenergic receptor signaling. Ghrh neurons assimilate nutrient, hormone, and neurochemical cues that affect counterregulation. Current research employed in vivo ADRβ1 gene silencing technology to examine whether NE imposes sex-specific regulation of VMN Ghrh neuron receptivity to these stimuli during eu- and/or hypoglycemia. VMN ADRβ1 gene knockdown respectively up- or down-regulated Ghrh neuron GPR81 lactate receptor gene expression in vehicle- versus insulin-injected male rats, yet this mRNA was decreased (euglycemia) or unaffected (hypoglycemia) in females. Gene silencing suppressed estrogen receptor (ER)-alpha, ER-beta, and G protein-coupled ER-1 (GPER) transcripts in euglycemic females but negatively only a subset of these mRNAs in males. β1-AR knockdown did not modify ER gene expression in insulin-treated female rats but inhibited GPER transcripts in hypoglycemic males. Eu- and hypoglycemic animals of each sex exhibited down-regulated Ghrh neuron gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A receptor mRNA after VMN ADRβ1 siRNA pretreatment, whereas gene silencing correspondingly decreased or increased GABA-B receptor subunit-2 transcripts in hypoglycemic males versus females. ADRβ1 gene knockdown caused opposite changes in guanylate cyclase-1 soluble subunit alpha2 mRNA in vehicle- versus insulin-treated males but down-regulated this mRNA in females. Results suggest that sex-dimorphic β1-AR control of VMNdm Ghrh/SF-1 neuron transmission may involve regulation of cell sensitivity to convergent extrinsic stimuli that influence neural regulation of glucose homeostasis. Data moreover disclose that the direction of receptor control of distinctive receptor genes is glucose status-dependent.

items.title: Acupuncture alleviates post-stroke depression by inhibiting proline-driven ferroptosis in hippocampal neurons.
items.abstract: Background Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a prevalent stroke complication with scarce therapeutic interventions. Acupuncture has shown clinical efficacy in PSD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates whether acupuncture alleviates PSD by regulating proline metabolism-mediated ferroptosis. Methods We generated a rat PSD model via common carotid artery ligation coupled with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Acupuncture at GV20, GV26, GV24, and GV14 was administered for four weeks. Behavioral tests, TTC and Nissl staining, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, amino acid metabolomics, and hippocampal neuron cultures with proline intervention were performed. Results Acupuncture robustly rescued depression-like phenotypes and mitigated hippocampal neuronal injury in PSD rats. Acupuncture decreased serum levels of iron ions, malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), increased glutathione (GSH), and reversed the aberrant expression of ferroptosis-related proteins (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, TFR1) in the hippocampus. Amino acid metabolomics revealed elevated serum proline in PSD rats, which was normalized by acupuncture. Exogenous proline administration aggravated depressive behaviors and hippocampal ferroptosis. In cultured hippocampal neurons, high-dose proline directly induced ferroptosis and reduced cell viability. Conclusion Acupuncture ameliorates PSD by inhibiting hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis through regulation of proline metabolism, revealing a novel mechanism for acupuncture treatment.

items.title: From Variability to Synchrony: Non-linear Development of Auditory Neural Responses During the First Year of Life.
items.abstract: In humans, the first year of life is characterized by rapid developmental changes, including substantial brain maturation. As a result, neural responses to auditory stimuli undergo marked changes during this period. In this study, we followed 69 infants across their first year of life and recorded high-density electroencephalography (hdEEG) at 2 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum. Infants were presented with pure beep tones to examine the development of neural responses to auditory stimulation. We analyzed event-related potentials (ERPs), inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC), and event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) responses to the beep tones and controlled for arousal state during stimulus presentation. We found that with increasing age, neural responses became more pronounced and showed reduced trial-to-trial variability. Phase synchronization increased from 2 weeks to later developmental stages in a broad low-frequency range (0.5 Hz to 13.6 Hz), indicating improved temporal alignment of brain responses over time. However, phase synchronization decreased from 6 to 12 months, suggesting a developmental transition towards more differentiated brain activity. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that auditory maturation during the first year of life follows a non-linear trajectory driven by dynamic changes in neural synchronization, reflecting the progressive refinement of functional neural circuits. Our results thus provide a critical benchmark for understanding the neural dynamics underlying sensory development during this period.

items.title: Neuropathic pain: Opportunities and challenges for immune-based therapeutics.
items.abstract: Neuropathic pain develops as a result of a lesion or a disease affecting the somatosensory nervous system and is associated with substantial disability, poor quality of life, and high health care costs. Current management is dominated by neuron-focused interventions that provide modest benefits and are often poorly tolerated. Accumulating evidence from experimental and clinical research implicates neuroimmune mechanisms in the development and persistence of neuropathic pain, yet their clinical relevance and therapeutic potential remain uncertain. In this review, we outline the latest clinical evidence on the contribution of immune processes to neuropathic pain and review interventions that act on neuroimmune mechanisms, including novel neuroimmunomodulation therapies. Focusing on human data, we outline key challenges and future directions for the field, including establishing whether observed neuroimmune changes cause neuropathic pain, designing trials that are explicitly equipped to investigate heterogeneity in treatment effects, and testing novel interventions.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between maltreatment, bullying victimization and externalizing problems in children and adolescents: Evidence from Brazilian High Risk Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background Empirical evidence consistently demonstrates elevated rates of maltreatment and bullying victimization among children and adolescents with externalizing problems. However, most research has been conducted in high-income countries (HICs), with limited understanding of these developmental processes in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Objective To examine longitudinal associations between maltreatment, bullying victimization, and externalizing problems in an LMIC context. Participants and setting Participants were 2511 children and adolescents (aged 6-18 years) from the Brazilian High-Risk Cohort Study. Methods Caregiver reports were used to assess study variables across three waves. A Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM) was applied to data from T1 (mean age = 10.20, SD = 1.90), T2 (mean age = 13.50, SD = 1.92), and T3 (mean age = 16.58, SD = 1.03). Results At the within-person level, both maltreatment at T1 (β = 0.08, p = .024) and bullying victimization at T1 (β = 0.08, p = .016) were associated with externalizing problems at T2. Maltreatment at T2 was positively associated with externalizing problems at T3 in males (β = 0.14, p = .031), and negatively associated in females (β = -0.26, p = .003). Conclusions Our study highlights longitudinal associations between maltreatment, bullying victimization, and externalizing problems, which vary between sexes and developmental stages. These findings underscore the importance of prioritizing child and adolescent mental health in Brazil. More broadly, the results highlight the need for research in other LMICs to identify both global and context-specific mechanisms underlying the development of externalizing problems.

items.title: Cross-Domain Transfer of Depression Voice Biomarkers Depends on the Outcome Instrument: Leakage-Controlled Cross-Sectional Evaluation Study.
items.abstract: Voice-based depression screening is commercializing rapidly, yet whether voice biomarkers generalize across clinical settings is largely untested. Generalization is usually framed as a question about populations, but it is also a question about the outcome instrument a model is scored against, an effect confounded with other between-study differences in the literature. We tested whether depression voice biomarkers transfer between perinatal and general-psychiatric speech in both directions under strict leakage control and whether transfer depends on the screening instrument. In a cross-sectional, online US study, 390 pregnant participants at a mean of 22 (SD 1) weeks' gestation (analytical sample n=316) participated in 446 sessions; each participant provided 4 voice recordings and completed the modified 8-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8) and modified 9-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (mEPDS-9). We extracted 375 acoustic descriptors and 330-dimensional Population Dynamics Foundation Model community-health embeddings. Discrimination area under the curve (AUC) was assessed under leakage-controlled cross-validation, with feature and classifier selection inside training folds only and a permutation negative-control harness, across a prespecified grid of 4 speech tasks×4 outcome definitions. The prenatal-trained model was applied to 2 general-psychiatric corpora (Distress Analysis Interview Corpus-Wizard-of-Oz, n=189; Extended Distress Analysis Interview Corpus, n=219) under pure held-out inference, and the open-source Kintsugi Depression/Anxiety Model (DAM), trained on 35,000 individuals, was applied to all 3 cohorts without refitting, with Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity control. In the prenatal cohort, the preregistered outcome was at chance (AUC 0.494, 95% CI 0.431-0.560); no cell in the 16-cell grid survived adjustment under either modeling paradigm. The prenatal-trained model did not transfer to either general-psychiatric corpus (AUCs 0.505 and 0.478). Reverse transfer depended on the screening instrument. The DAM reached an AUC of 0.706 to 0.708 on general-psychiatric speech. In the same participants, it performed at chance against the PHQ-8 (AUC 0.510, 95% CI 0.411-0.609) but discriminated against the mEPDS-9 (AUC 0.645, 95% CI 0.541-0.744), a paired difference of 0.135 (95% CI 0.019-0.248; unadjusted post hoc P=0.02). Exploratory item-level analysis suggests a mechanism: the DAM tracked affective-distress items (crying r=0.26, sadness r=0.21, and overwhelmed r=0.20) but not somatic PHQ-8 items; only crying survived adjustment across 17 tests. Transfer varied by elicitation task (pregnancy narrative 0.653, 95% CI 0.550-0.753; open-ended speech 0.597, 95% CI 0.486-0.699; scripted reading 0.544, 95% CI 0.434-0.651), though these were not formally compared. Cross-domain comparison showed a compound shift: population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument differed together, while only the instrument could be varied on its own. Whether a depression voice biomarker transfers may depend not only on the population but also on whether the outcome instrument captures what the model can detect. Validation should state the population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument together; a tool validated against one instrument should not be assumed to work against another.

items.title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins.
items.abstract: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5' GGGGCC 3' sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR20) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR20. We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR-iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR20-induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR50, we found PR50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR50 or GR50 expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.

items.title: Astrocyte-associated water channel changes following buprenorphine administration in a rat model of diffuse traumatic brain injury.
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a significant concern, with millions sustaining a TBI each year. The vast majority are categorized as mild, in which diffuse pathologies are the hallmark and multiple cell types are affected, including astrocytes. Buprenorphine (bup), a semi-synthetic opioid, is a common human and veterinary analgesic. Previous studies from our group showed that a single dose of slow-release bup administered acutely following TBI alters astrocyte morphology at 1 day and 4 weeks post-injury in a region-specific manner. The current study expands on these findings by examining how four major astrocyte-associated proteins, GFAP, SWELL1/LRRC8A, TRPM4, and AQP4, are affected by such a dose of bup. Adult male rats received either a sham or TBI via a central fluid percussion injury model, followed by saline or bup 15 min following injury. Protein quantification at 1 day and 4 weeks post-injury revealed region- and time-dependent effects of acute bup administration. At 4 weeks following TBI, bup treatment was associated with reduced cortical SWELL1 and TRPM4, and reduced hippocampal and thalamic AQP4 expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that a single post-injury dose of bup can alter the regional expression of major astrocyte-associated proteins beyond the acute phase following diffuse TBI.
