items.title: Survival following 14% Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia: cerebral malaria and anaemic heart failure in a Nigerian toddler.
items.abstract: Malaria remains a leading cause of mortality amongst children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. Complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria frequently presents with multiple life-threatening sequelae, including cerebral malaria, profound anaemia, and hyperparasitaemia. Although parasite densities exceeding 10% are independently associated with high mortality, achieving full recovery in a young child presenting with simultaneous extreme parasitaemia, deep coma, and severe malarial anaemia remains exceptionally noteworthy. We report the case of a 20-month-old male from Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria, who presented with a five-day history of fever, cough, and diarrhoea, progressing to unconsciousness. Clinical examination revealed a Blantyre Coma Scale of 2/5, profound pallor, tachycardia (158 bpm), and tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory investigations confirmed an extreme 14% P. falciparum parasitaemia and a life-threatening packed cell volume of 8%. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis ruled out bacterial meningitis though an elevated protein level (71 mg/dL) supported the diagnosis of cerebral malaria. The patient was stabilised in the cardiac position to optimise venous return and alleviate signs of incipient heart failure, and was initiated on a multi-modal therapeutic regimen. Antimalarial therapy was commenced with intravenous artesunate (3 mg/kg), supported by two sessions of sedimented red blood cell transfusions and empiric IV Ceftriaxone. By the fourth day of treatment, the child regained full consciousness and was transitioned to oral artemether-lumefantrine. The patient was discharged in a stable condition on day seven with a recovered packed cell volume of 35%. This case highlights the critical importance of the "24-h window" in treating severe malaria. The successful outcome confirms the efficacy of intravenous artesunate and the necessity of aggressive supportive care-including blood transfusion-in managing the severe triad of hyperparasitaemia, cerebral sequestration, and severe anaemia in paediatric patients within endemic regions. This report emphasises the need for public health initiatives that educate caregivers on the early recognition of malaria symptoms to facilitate prompt care. Furthermore, it reaffirms that urgent microscopic evaluation remains the gold standard for the immediate diagnosis of hyperparasitaemic cases in resource-limited settings.

items.title: "I can definitely relate to that": leveraging peers with lived experience as interviewers in qualitative perinatal substance use research.
items.abstract: Peer interviewers are increasingly used in qualitative research to strengthen data collection, particularly when working with historically marginalized communities to foster trust and potentially elicit richer narratives. Yet the specific techniques by which peers shape the collection and quality of interview data remain underexplored. This study aims to examine how trained peer interviewers influenced the interview process across two perinatal substance use research studies. We conducted a secondary analysis of qualitative interview data from two U.S. studies (2021-2025) in which peer interviewers completed forty semi-structured interviews with pregnant, postpartum, and parenting people of color with a history of substance use disorder. Research coordinators independently reviewed all transcripts to identify exchanges where interviewer-interviewee dialogue included moments of rapport-building, emotional resonance, or personal reflection. Using a reflexive thematic analysis framework, we developed and refined a codebook, applied it across all excerpts, and integrated peer interviewer reflections to finalize themes. Three overarching themes appeared regarding the techniques peer interviewers used. First, peer interviewers built rapport and connection by referencing shared identities and experiences, using colloquial language, and pausing to check in on participant comfort. Second, peer interviewers used both empathetic validation (drawing on personal experience) and sympathetic validation (offering affirmation without explicit disclosure) to affirm participants' experiences or encourage deeper reflection. Third, peer interviewers proactively disclosed aspects of their identity either to clarify interview questions or to prompt more detailed participant responses, with personal disclosures frequently facilitating richer answers to questions. By describing specific interviewer techniques, specifically validation, disclosure, and rapport-building, we identified concrete, actionable guidance for future qualitative research teams seeking to integrate peer interviewers. These findings support the expansion of community-based participatory models that center lived experience and underscore the need for peer interviewer training programs that explicitly cultivate and reinforce these practices.

items.title: Designing a Locally Adapted Kader Educational Program to Improve Social Support for Women with Metastatic Breast Cancer in Indonesia.
items.abstract: The community-based program in Indonesia was established in 1970s through community health volunteer system, called Kader. Many efforts have been made to increase Kader's capacity for cancer care, yet existing programs are often short-term and unstructured, and they do not address the unique needs of people living with cancer. Despite the increasing number of people living with cancer, cadres' knowledge and confidence in supporting women with breast cancer in the community are low. This paper, part of the COMMUNICATED (community care for metastatic breast cancer), aimed to strengthen social support for women with breast cancer through Kader education. It describes the program development and some components of the first action phase. The program development involved three stages: (1) defining five competencies and introducing the term Kader TATAK (Tangguh dan Tanggap Kanker, Resilience and Responsive to Cancer) to strengthen role identity; (2) developing training program and materials; and (3) designing recruitment strategies and multisectoral collaboration. The first stage of action phase involved training facilitators and nurses buddies. It was followed by Kader training using a flipped learning approach. A total of 112 Kader from Yogyakarta and Bali participated. Kader's knowledge increased from 7.27 (SD = 1.81) to 8.89 (SD = 1.27) of 10 (Z = -7.19, p < 0.001), and self-confidence scores from 54.51 (SD = 14.82) to 66.06 (SD = 13.19) out of 85 (Z=-7.35, p < 0.001). The findings suggest that the program has potential to prepare Kader to provide social support for women with breast cancer in community settings. Further evaluation is needed to assess feasibility, transferability, and scalability across diverse settings.

items.title: Mental health care utilization among young black sexual minority men living with HIV at Ryan-white funded HIV care centers in Atlanta, Georgia.
items.abstract: Young Black sexual minority men (YB-SMM) living with HIV experience disproportionate mental health burdens, exacerbated by systemic inequities, stigma and structural determinants. Despite high rates of mental health symptoms, mental health service utilization remains low. We examined factors associated with mental health service utilization among YB-SMM receiving HIV care. We conducted a cross-sectional survey among 100 YB-SMM living with HIV recruited from two Ryan White-funded HIV clinics in a large Southeastern U.S. city. Participants completed validated measures assessing mental health care utilization, psychosocial factors and demographics. Logistic regression analyses examined associations with lifetime mental health provider use, desire for services in the past year and provider referral. Participants had a mean age of 25 years; 78% identified as gay, 49% experienced housing instability and 50% reported a history of incarceration. Overall, 51% had ever seen a mental health provider, 53% wanted mental health services in the past year; 40% received a provider referral; however, only 22% of the total sample attended a visit following referral. Lower income was associated with greater mental health service utilization among multiple outcomes. Greater non-organizational religious activity was associated with lifetime mental health provider use, depressive symptoms were associated with desire for services and higher trust in physicians was associated with provider referral. Mental health service interest was common, while provider and mental health service attendance were reported by fewer participants. Future work should examine how referral practices, provider availability and other service-level barriers influence mental health care engagement among YB-SMM living with HIV.

items.title: Barriers and Inequities in Access to Obstetric Analgesia during Labour: Implications for Latin America from a Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Equitable access to evidence-based pain relief during labour is a fundamental component of respectful maternity care. However, women in Latin America continue to face structural, sociocultural and health system barriers that limit access to desired pain management options. Evidence gaps remain in several countries. A scoping review was conducted following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Five electronic databases were searched for English and Spanish language publications from January 2010 to May 2026, complemented by snowball searching. The 2010 threshold was selected to capture contemporary health system reforms, with one earlier landmark study included by exception. Studies addressing access to obstetric analgesia in Latin America and conceptually relevant international evidence were included. Twenty-two studies were included. Evidence consistently identified that access to obstetric analgesia is conditioned by sociocultural, institutional, structural, and economic factors. Major barriers included shortages of trained personnel, socioeconomic inequalities, linguistic and cultural barriers, discrimination, and limited access to information. Across studies, women's childbirth experiences were strongly influenced by autonomy, respectful care, and participation in decision-making. Improving equitable access to labour pain relief requires policies that strengthen health system capacity, ensure informed choice, and promote respectful maternity care. Region-specific research is needed to inform equitable maternal health policies across Latin America.

items.title: Environmental Exposures and Diagnosed Dyslipidemia Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China.
items.abstract: Dyslipidemia is shaped not only by biological aging but also by historically structured social and environmental conditions experienced across cohorts and periods. Rapid urbanization, environmental degradation, and population aging in China provide a critical context for examining how life-course processes intersect with contemporary exposures to influence dyslipidemia risk. Drawing on Age-Period-Cohort (APC) analysis, this study investigated how age, birth cohort, and period-specific environmental conditions jointly structured dyslipidemia among middle-aged and older adults. Individual-level data were drawn from five waves (2011-2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). City-level environmental characteristics were compiled from the Google Earth Engine and China City Statistical Yearbook to construct measures of physical and social environments. Multilevel models incorporating APC specifications were used to estimate age, period, and cohort effects, and to assess associations between environmental exposures and the risk of dyslipidemia. Results reveal a nonlinear age pattern, with dyslipidemia risk peaking in the mid-50 s before declining in later life. Period effects indicate rising prevalence across survey waves, consistent with broader nutritional, behavioral, and diagnostic transitions. Cohort disparities were observed: later-born cohorts exhibited substantially lower risk than earlier-born cohorts (born in 1949 and earlier). Environmental exposures further structured these inequalities. Summer land-surface temperature showed a U-shaped association with dyslipidemia, while winter temperatures demonstrated inverted U-shaped relationships. Air pollutants were positively associated with risk in largely monotonic patterns. Importantly, cohort-stratified analyses revealed greater environmental susceptibility among earlier-born cohorts, suggesting cumulative disadvantage across the life course. These findings demonstrate how early-life conditions interact with contemporary environmental stressors to produce intergenerational disparities in cardiometabolic health. Integrating life-course perspectives with environmental governance may be essential for reducing chronic disease burdens in rapidly aging and ecologically transforming societies.

items.title: The impact of structured care versus usual care on service uptake and distress among distressed callers to a cancer telephone support service: outcomes of the START stepped wedge trial.
items.abstract: Up to 45% of people with a cancer diagnosis and 44% of caregivers experience distress. Evidence-based guidelines recommend psychosocial screening with structured referrals in all settings. To identify whether the implementation of a co-designed distress screening and structured referral intervention at Cancer Information and Support (CIS) telephone services resulted in increased referral uptake and reduced distress for people with cancer and caregivers versus those receiving usual care. As part of the stepped wedge trial, caller distress was measured using the Distress Thermometer (DT) and Generalised Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28) and uptake of referrals offered by the CIS were recorded. Referral uptake and GHQ-28 scores were assessed using generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) with fixed effects for the intervention period and structured care. Subgroup analyses were also performed to assess the difference between caller type (patients vs caregivers) and previous mental health treatment. This study of 2348 patients and caregivers found insufficient evidence to support increased referral uptake or decreased distress in the structured care group, or a relationship between referral uptake or distress by caller type (patient/caregiver) (p > .05 for adjusted ORs in each comparison). Although the structured care model did not improve referral uptake or distress, these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to a lack of intervention fidelity. Recommendations for improving intervention fidelity and future co-design research strategies are discussed.

items.title: Child emotional competence: a conceptual organizing framework and parent-report measure of emotion reasoning, emotion stability, emotion regulation, and empathy
items.abstract: Introduction Emotional competence (EC) plays a vital role in children's development, well-being, and mental health outcomes. However, the field lacks consensus on definitions and measurement approaches, leading to inconsistencies and limitations in understanding and assessing EC. Methods This paper presents a conceptual organizing framework for EC that integrates and clarifies the various components of emotional functioning. Additionally, a new measure, the Emotional Competence Inventory for Children (ECIC), was developed and validated to assess EC among children ages 3–12 years based on the proposed framework. The study involved two separate samples ( N = 695) recruited through Amazon's Mechanical Turk. Data analysis included exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance testing, and assessments of reliability and validity. Results Results supported the four components of EC: Emotion Reasoning, Emotion Stability, Emotion Regulation, and Empathy. Subscales of Emotion Reasoning and Emotion Stability were identified, providing nuanced insights into emotional development. The ECIC demonstrated promising psychometric properties, including evidence of measurement invariance across several demographic groups, although full scalar invariance was not established across all groups. The unique associations of ECIC scales/subscales shed light on their differential associations with child health outcomes, aiding precision-medicine approaches and intervention efforts. Discussion The validated ECIC measure offers an important tool for assessing EC and informing future personalized treatment research and assessment strategies. This conceptual organizing framework and accompanying measure contribute to advancing our understanding of EC, supporting children's emotional development, and promoting their overall well-being. Future research should further validate and refine the framework while investigating its applicability in diverse populations and treatment settings.

items.title: The role of scale in public goods problems: from pandemics to climate change
items.abstract: Climate change is a global emergency, as was the COVID-19 pandemic. But our collective response to COVID-19 was much stronger than our response to climate change, to date. Why is that the case? We hypothesize that one reason for the contrasting response in these two systems is their differing scales: not just spatial localization and temporal scale but also personal efficacy, which quantifies how much an intervention directly benefits the individual who adopts it. We introduce a framework that captures regimes of containment, mitigation, and failure to control in social-ecological public goods problems. As parameters governing these three scales are varied, it is possible to shift from a COVID-like system to a climate-like system. The framework replicates both inaction in the case of climate change mitigation, as well as the faster response that we exhibited to COVID-19. The model also exhibits abrupt transitions between regimes and oscillatory dynamics. Our cross-system comparison also suggests actionable ways that cooperation can be improved in large-scale public goods problems, like climate change. More broadly, we argue that considering scale and incorporating human-environment feedbacks are not just interesting special cases within non-cooperative game theory, but rather should be the starting point for the study of altruism and human cooperation.

items.title: Multi-timescale neural adaptation disturbances in major depression
items.abstract: Abstract Major depression is usually characterized in terms of momentary abnormalities, such as negative bias or emotional blunting, derived largely from paradigms that measure only the initial response to a stimulus. Yet depressive experience in daily life is repetitive and cumulative. Here we show that neural adaptation to repeated negative stimuli is altered in major depression and provides information beyond initial reactivity. Using a repeated negative-stimulus paradigm, we quantify adaptation at micro and macro timescales from electroencephalographic recordings in 28 patients with major depression and 34 healthy controls, measuring event-related potentials, frontal theta activity, and large-scale traveling-wave propagation. Relative to controls, patients with major depression show reduced micro-scale attenuation of the frontal late positive potential and theta activity, alongside macro-scale increases in the late positive potential and decreases in theta power. Within-participant decoding shows weaker First-versus-Second neural differentiation in major depression and lower recoverable repetition-state information. Thus, repeated exposure reveals neural dynamics beyond initial reactivity, particularly reduced rapid recalibration in major depression.

items.title: KARE-ing about civil discourse in higher education: a practical framework for cultivating the virtues to sustain it
items.abstract: Purpose Civil discourse, understood here as virtuous dialogue and deliberation across significant disagreement in ways that promote learning, mutual understanding and responsible judgment, is widely endorsed as important for democratic life and higher education. Yet faculty often lack practical tools for designing courses that cultivate the virtues required to sustain such engagement, especially when disagreements are morally, politically, religiously or identity-laden. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a developmentally grounded account of virtue formation, the article translates theory into a practical design heuristic organized around four components: Know, Act, Realign and Encourage (KARE). The framework is illustrated through a table of course-level practices focused on four virtues central to civil discourse and through two fictional, discipline-specific case studies. A faculty-facing worksheet is also introduced to support its application. Findings Because civil discourse requires students to listen, reason, speak and remain engaged amid disagreement, it depends on a constellation of virtues, such as intellectual humility, charitable listening, patience in discomfort, fair-mindedness and practical wisdom. The KARE framework helps instructors design repeated opportunities for students to learn, practice, reflect and sustain these virtues within routine course structures. Practical implications The KARE framework and worksheet provide faculty with a structured method for strengthening civil discourse through small, context-sensitive adjustments to existing courses. By supporting sustained engagement across deep differences, this work contributes to broader efforts to foster respectful dialogue and democratic participation in higher education. Originality/value This article contributes a civil discourse application of KARE, showing how an existing character-formation design tool can help faculty translate broad commitments to civil discourse into course-level practices.

items.title: Trait Mindfulness and Inhibitory Control in Young Adults: Exploring Sex Moderation and the Potential Mediating Role of Resting-State EEG
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to determine the association between five facets of trait mindfulness (TM) and inhibitory control (IC) and explore whether these associations were moderated by sex and mediated by resting-state electroencephalogram (rsEEG). Methods A total of 283 young adults (149 female, 134 male; 18 to 30 years old) completed the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire and a flanker task. A subsample ( n = 172) completed rsEEG to quantify power in theta and alpha bands defined using individual alpha peak frequency. Linear mixed-effects models examined the associations between TM and IC outcomes. Exploratory mediation analyses tested indirect effects of acting with awareness (AA), a TM facet reflecting attention to current actions, on incongruent-trial accuracy through rsEEG power. Results AA was positively associated with accuracy, with a stronger association for incongruent than congruent trials ( b = 0.19, 95% CI [0.08, 0.29]). The prespecified AA × Congruency interactions for RT and P3 amplitude were not significant. Exploratory analyses provided no evidence of sex moderation in the behavioral or P3 outcomes after false discovery rate correction, and none of the explored rsEEG indirect effects survived correction. Conclusions These findings suggest that the attentional component of TM may be particularly relevant to behavioural IC under conflict demands, without reliable evidence for sex-dependent or resting-state EEG pathways. Preregistration This study was not preregistered.

items.title: Statistical tests should inform behaviour in theory and practice
items.abstract: Objectives Statistical hypothesis testing cannot establish a hypothesis as certainly—or even approximately—true, but it is valuable in guiding behaviour as if it were true. To make decisions in theory and practice, statistical testing in psychology should weigh the Type I (α) and Type II (β) error probabilities according to their respective costs . Methods We outline costs and how to approach the α-β balance for six common decision-making questions: (1) Should a hypothesis be considered tentatively accepted? (2) Should a model or theory cover a newly proposed effect? (3) Should a new hypothesis be proposed? (4) Should a new intervention be introduced? (5) Are the psychometric properties of an instrument sufficient to use it? (6) Are the assumptions of a statistical method met so that it may be used? We give a worked example with real cost figures for question (4). Results We argue that parsimony—prioritizing low α over low β—often serves as a useful default stance in questions (1) to (5). This resembles the general preference for focusing on fewer, larger and more robust effects to allocate resources efficiently and to make scientific communication more reliable. Conclusions The parsimony default invites transparent counterarguments to override it, justifying a preference for small β. Examples include adding promising intervention components with little risk of adverse effects to well-established interventions. As with (6), statistical tests can sometimes introduce unnecessary errors when a sound decision can be made on substantive grounds alone, for example when setting up a model to test a given hypothesis.

items.title: Empowerment, delegation and vision awareness: motivational pathways to workplace creativity
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how employee empowerment and task delegation influence workplace creativity through harmonious and obsessive work passion, and whether organizational vision awareness (OVA) strengthens these motivational pathways in a public sector context. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 533 employees across two Namibian public sector ministries using stratified random sampling. Employee self-reports were matched with supervisor ratings of incremental and radical creativity to reduce common method bias. Structural equation modeling tested indirect and conditional relationships among empowerment, delegation, work passion and creativity. Findings Empowerment and task delegation are indirectly related to creativity through distinct forms of work passion. Harmonious passion predicts both incremental and radical creativity, whereas obsessive passion is primarily linked to incremental creativity. OVA strengthens selected motivational pathways, showing that shared vision enhances the effectiveness of leadership practices in fostering creativity. Originality/value This study demonstrates that empowerment and delegation operate through differentiated passion-based mechanisms rather than uniform effects. By distinguishing between incremental and radical creativity, it clarifies how motivational processes translate managerial practices into distinct creative outcomes. It further extends the literature by identifying OVA as a boundary condition and by providing evidence from an underexplored African public sector context.

items.title: Functions in neuroscience
items.abstract: This chapter examines the notion of "function" in neuroscience drawing primarily from human cognitive neuroscience. In it, I argue for three claims. First, philosophical theories of function such as etiological and causal role theories, can help clarify the meanings of "function" in neuroscience. Second, cognitive neuroscience has many notions of function operating within it; it exhibits what Garson calls "within-discipline" function pluralism. Lastly, some neuroscientific debates about the functions of brain regions conflate different notions of function to their detriment.

items.title: The Live Possibility Model of Disinformation: A Non-doxastic Account
items.abstract: Abstract In the philosophical literature, it is often assumed that disinformation leads to false beliefs. However, empirical work in the social sciences has established that much disinformation rather creates uncertainty. Taking seriously these empirical findings, I develop a non-doxastic theory of disinformation which I call the “live possibility model”. The core claim of my theory is that disinformation introduces live possibilities the victim cannot reject. Live possibilities are epistemic possibilities which are likely enough to be relevant for thought and action. When a live possibility is introduced, it forces a suspension of judgement. In the resulting context of uncertainty, the subject navigates by use of non-doxastic attitudes, such as hope, fear, faith, etc. Unlike most other philosophical accounts of disinformation, this model does not ascribe irrationality to disinformed subjects. Instead, it suggests that disinformation exploits processes of critical thinking. While there have been some other recent philosophical attempts to understand disinformation in terms of uncertainty—due to Blake-Turner, Harris, and Rini—I demonstrate how the live possibility model incorporates their insights while surpassing them theoretically.

items.title: Conservation taxonomy of the Cuban Parrot (Amazona leucocephala): variation in morphology and plumage
items.abstract: Abstract: Conservation taxonomy, the study of organismal classification to clarify conservation priorities, seeks to define species and subspecies limits. Allopatric populations, such as those present on islands, pose special challenges to identifying taxonomic boundaries which can be practically addressed using diagnostic criteria. Because some of the island populations of Cuban Parrot (Amazona leucocephala) are highly endangered, the five recognized subspecies need careful re-evaluation. We measured 18 morphological and plumage characters from 188 museum specimens representing the six extant and one extirpated island populations. We relied largely on discriminant function analyses (DFA) to assess diagnosability and to examine patterns of similarity among the populations. Most morphological characters indicated sexual dimorphism, with males 1-4% larger than females. The plumage characters, in contrast, demonstrated complete absence of sexual dichromatism. Stepwise discriminant analyses including all specimens and 14 characters revealed substantial differentiation among island groups, with 81.4% of individuals classified correctly to island. Pairwise comparisons among islands showed reciprocal discrimination > 80%, with the exception of Cuba / Cayman Brac (67%). None of the populations possessed a single diagnostic character. Although currently lumped into a single subspecies (A. l. bahamensis), each of the three Bahamas populations, including an extirpated population on Acklins Island, was equally distinct as the four other currently-recognized subspecies. Collectively, the evidence supports the view that all seven island populations, including the extirpated population, warrant subspecies status. We apply the name A. l. bahamensis to the extirpated Acklins population and propose the new names A. l. abacoensis for the Abaco Parrot and A. l. inaguaensis for the Inagua Parrot. The small and vulnerable populations on Abaco, Inagua, Isla de la Juventud, Cayman Brac, and Grand Cayman deserve special conservation status and should be treated as independent conservation units. Exemplary programs using these threatened populations as “flagship” taxa illustrate why recognizing the subspecies rank can greatly benefit conservation efforts by island nations. Keywords: conservation taxonomy, systematics, Cuban Parrot, Amazona leucocephala, morphology, plumage, new subspecies Resumen: Taxonomía conservacionista de la Cotorra Cubana (Amazona leucocephala): variación en la morfología y el plumaje- La taxonomía para la conservación, que es el estudio de la clasificación de los organismos para esclarecer las prioridades de conservación, busca definir los límites de las especies y subespecies. Las poblaciones alopátricas, como las presentes en las islas, plantean desafíos especiales para la identificación de los límites taxonómicos que pueden abordarse de forma práctica utilizando criterios de diagnóstico. Debido a que algunas de las poblaciones de Cotorra Cubana (Amazona leucocephala) están en grave peligro de extinción, las cinco subespecies reconocidas necesitan de una cuidadosa reevaluación. Se midieron 18 caracteres morfológicos y del plumaje de 188 especímenes de museo, que representan a las seis poblaciones existentes y a una población extirpada. Se basó en gran medida en análisis de función discriminante (DFA) para evaluar la capacidad de diagnóstico y examinar los patrones de similitud entre las poblaciones. La mayoría de los caracteres morfológicos indican dimorfismo sexual, siendo los machos 1-4% mayores que las hembras. Los caracteres del plumaje, en cambio, demostraron la ausencia completa de dicromatismo sexual. El análisis discriminante paso a paso, incluyendo todas las muestras y 14 caracteres, reveló diferencias sustanciales entre los grupos de las islas, con 81,4% de los individuos clasificados correctamente en relación con la isla. Las comparaciones por pares entre las islas mostraron la discriminación recíproca > 80%, con la excepción de Cuba / Cayman Brac (67%). Ninguna de las poblaciones tuvo un carácter de diagnóstico único. Aunque las tres poblaciones de Bahamas y la población extirpada de Acklins están incluidas en una sola subespecie (A. l. bahamensis), todas fueron igualmente diferentes, como ocurre con las restantes cuatro subespecies actualmente reconocidas. Colectivamente, las evidencias apoyan el punto de vista de que las siete poblaciones de diferentes islas, incluyendo la población extirpada, merecen el estado de subespecie. Le asignamos el nombre de A. l. bahamensis a la población extirpada de Acklins y proponemos los nuevos nombres de A. l. abacoensis para la cotorra de Abaco y A. l. inaguaensis para la cotorra de Inagua. Las poblaciones pequeñas y vulnerables de Abaco, Inagua, Isla de la Juventud, Caimán Brac y Gran Caimán, merecen un estatus especial de conservación y deben ser tratadas como unidades de conservación independientes. El uso de estos programas puede ser un ejemplo en el estudio de poblaciones amenazadas de especies banderas, ya que ilustra por qué el reconocimiento del rango de subespecies, puede beneficiar enormemente los esfuerzos conservacionistas en las naciones insulares. Palabras clave: Amazona leucocephala, Cotorra Cubana, morfología, nuevas subespecies, plumaje, sistemática, taxonomía para la conservación Résumé: Taxonomie et conservation de l’Amazone de Cuba (Amazona leucocephala): variation de la morphologie et du plumage- Taxonomie et conservation s’associent pour que l’étude de la classification des organismes permette de clarifier les priorités de conservation, en redéfinissant les limites séparant les espèces et les sous-espèces. Les populations allopatriques, telles que les populations insulaires, offrent des défis particuliers quant à l’identification de limites taxonomiques grâce à des critères de diagnostic. Certaines populations insulaires d’Amazone de Cuba (Amazona leucocephala) étant fortement menacées d’extinction, le statut des cinq sous-espèces actuellement reconnues doit être soigneusement ré-évalué. Nous avons mesuré 18 caractères morphologiques et de plumage, sur 188 spécimens de muséums, issus de 7 populations insulaires dont une éteinte localement. Nous nous sommes appuyés essentiellement sur des analyses discriminantes pour évaluer les possibilités de diagnostic et examiner des patrons de similitude entre populations. La plupart des caractères morphologiques présentaient un dimorphisme sexuel, les mâles étant de 1 à 4% plus grands que les femelles. Le plumage, en revanche, n’a montré aucun dichromatisme sexuel. Les analyses discriminantes pas à pas, concernant tous les spécimens et 14 caractères ont révélé des différences importantes entre les groupes d’îles, avec 81,4% des individus classés correctement par île. Les comparaisons par paires entre les îles ont montré une discrimination réciproque supérieure à 80%, à l’exception de Cuba / Cayman Brac (67%). Aucune des populations ne présentait un caractère de diagnostic unique. Bien qu’elles soient actuellement considérées comme appartenant à une seule sous-espèce (A. l. bahamensis), chacune des trois populations des Bahamas, y compris une population éteinte sur l’île Acklins, étaient toutes aussi distinctes que les quatre sous-espèces actuellement reconnues. Ainsi, ces résultats viennent soutenir l’hypothèse que les sept populations insulaires, y compris la population localement éteinte, justifient le statut de sous-espèce. Nous appliquons le nom de A. l. bahamensis à la population localement éteinte et nous proposons les nouveaux noms A. l. abacoensis pour l’Amazone Abaco et A. l. inaguaensis pour l’Amazone Inagua. Les populations d’Abaco, d’Inagua, de Isla de la Juventud, de Cayman Brac et de Grand Cayman sont petites et vulnérables. Elles méritent de ce fait un statut de conservation particulier et devraient être traitées comme des unités de conservation indépendantes. Des programmes exemplaires traitant ces populations menacées comme taxons «phares» démontrent en quoi la reconnaissance du rang de sous-espèce peut grandement bénéficier aux efforts de conservation des pays insulaires. items.title: Cross-feeding yields high-dimensional chaos and coexistence of species beyond exclusion principle
items.abstract: Abstract Cross-feeding mediated by leakage and uptake of chemicals is a key driver of microbial community diversity. We study a dynamical model in which species compete for metabolites leaked by others, with coupled dynamics of species populations and environmental chemical concentrations. The model allows diverse uptake and leakage network structures. Depending on the network structure, the system exhibits fixed points, limit cycles, low-dimensional chaos, and high-dimensional chaos. In the fixed-point and limit-cycle cases, coexistence is bounded by the number of exchangeable chemicals, consistent with the competitive exclusion principle. Low-dimensional chaos permits only a modest excess beyond this limit. By contrast, high-dimensional chaos supports persistent coexistence of many more species. In this regime, rank-abundance distributions are broader than exponential, resembling those observed in natural ecosystems. Population dynamics shows intermittent switching among quasi-stationary states, whereas chemical dynamics explores a high-dimensional state space. High-dimensional chaos arises robustly when the number of uptake metabolites moderately exceeds that of leaked metabolites. These results identify high-dimensional chaos with intermittent switching as a generic mechanism promoting coexistence beyond competitive-exclusion limits and suggest its relevance to maintaining highly diverse microbial communities sustained by leak-uptake cross-feeding.

items.title: A citywide metagenomic analysis reveals surface-specific microbiome and resistome patterns in outdoor urban environments across Liverpool, UK
items.abstract: Urbanization is rapidly increasing worldwide, with increasing attention focused on its consequences for human populations. Despite the importance of outdoor urban environments for biodiversity and human wellbeing, their microbial ecology remains poorly characterized, particularly in relation to emerging microbial threats including antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Where previous studies have targeted individual urban niches, we used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to assess microbial community composition and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) across five outdoor surface types at a citywide level: Touchpoints, Pathways, Soil, Refuse and Watersides. Microbial community composition differed significantly between surface types, with surface identity explaining 33.1% of variation, compared with 15.7% explained by council ward. Soil harboured the most compositionally distinct communities, whereas Touchpoints and Refuse showed greater overlap, with Pathways and Watersides occupying an intermediate position between the Touchpoint/Refuse and Soil communities. Touchpoints had significantly higher ARG abundance than Pathways, Soil and Watersides, with Refuse showing greater variability driven largely by a single high-abundance observation; following sensitivity analysis, Touchpoints were also significantly higher than Refuse. ARGs were rarely detected in Pathways, Watersides and Soil. These findings provide a citywide baseline showing that outdoor urban surfaces support distinct microbial communities and resistance profiles, with the strongest ARG signals observed on frequently contacted surfaces. This highlights the value of surface-specific metagenomic surveillance for characterizing the urban microbial and AMR landscape.

items.title: The Global Lakes Explorer: a basin-to-global scale data visualisation application for the assessment of nutrient emissions to lakes
items.abstract: Phosphorus and nitrogen are critical plant nutrients, essential for fertiliser production and global food security. However, poor management of anthropogenic nutrient cycles leads to losses associated with pollution of water bodies, driving eutrophication, biodiversity loss, and methane emissions. Addressing these interconnected challenges requires a sustainable, integrated, and, where possible, circular approach across the entire nutrient cycle. However, data on phosphorus and nitrogen emissions and impacts are fragmented across sectors and lack standardisation. Here, we introduce a new open-access web-based application: the “Global Lakes Explorer”, which harmonises phosphorus and nitrogen catchment export and emissions data alongside socio-economic and biodiversity risk factors spanning over 50 variables from multiple open data sources, covering more than 40,000 lake catchments worldwide. It enables users to visualise and download information on nutrient emissions across sectors, including agriculture, aquaculture, and wastewater, alongside socio-economic and environmental indicators. The app supports integrated governance on sustainable nutrient management in lake catchments by providing hindcasted emission data (1970–2015) in addition to future scenarios relating to shared socio-economic pathways (2015–2070) under various development projections. In this paper, we present several potential use cases for the app, including scenarios in which stakeholders can visualise and download forecasted nutrient emissions for their lake catchment of choice. We present ground-truthing analysis against phosphorus inputs from two lake catchments across natural and anthropogenic sources, in addition to model-to-model validation against total phosphorus estimations in the world’s 100 largest lakes. This open access tool is intended to help identify potential nutrient pollution risk areas, serve as a data source to support national governments in targeting efforts where they can have the greatest impact, and provide a tool that can help policymakers design informed, collaborative, and context-specific nutrient management strategies.

items.title: Experimental evolution of yeast reveals trade-offs between early and late stationary phase
items.abstract: Stationary phase in yeast and other microorganisms begins when a limiting nutrient in the environment is exhausted and cell division ceases. Most cells subsequently enter quiescence and then lose viability. However, even in spent media, metabolism continues, and the environment can change over time, causing the relative fitnesses of genotypes to differ over the course of stationary phase. For yeast, how such fitness varies and what genotypes might be favored at what points in stationary phase is largely unknown. In this work we experimentally evolve S. cerevisiae in batch culture, varying the time spent in stationary phase between growth cycles, and we isolate adaptive clones. We measure the relative fitness of these adaptive clones across a range of environments, characterized by different amounts of time in stationary phase and by two different carbon sources. By comparing the performance during a period of the growth cycle of a mutant to that of its ancestor, we can estimate the effects of each observed mutation on performance during various phases of the growth cycle. Here, we show that when an adaptive mutation emerges in growth cycles that include a stationary phase, its effect on stationary phase performance is largely independent of the type of carbon source provided. For the same group of mutants, mutational effects on performance in early stationary phase are negatively correlated with those effects in late stationary phase, suggesting a trade-off. We also show that increased intervals of stationary phase result in larger fitness effects of adaptive mutations and distinct routes of adaptation. Together, these results demonstrate that stationary phase consists of more than one distinct fitness-related phenotype, and that the phenotypes that allow for high performance in the first few days of stationary phase trade off with those that allow for high performance in later stationary phase.

items.title: Study on carbon sequestration and carbon neutrality spatial service scope in the Qinling Mountains of China
items.abstract: Quantifying the carbon sequestration capacity of the Qinling Mountains and delineating its carbon neutrality service scope are of great significance for rational territorial carbon management under China’s “dual carbon” strategy. Using vegetation net primary productivity from 2000 to 2022, this study estimated the net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and carbon absorption of the Qinling Mountains, estimated and spatially downscaled energy-related CO 2 emissions using nighttime-light data, analyzed the spatiotemporal characteristics of carbon neutrality, and delineated the carbon neutrality service scope based on a CO 2 diffusion framework. The main findings are as follows. (1) From 2000 to 2022, the net ecosystem productivity of the Qinling Mountains showed a fluctuating upward trend, with higher values in the west and lower values in the east. (2) Both carbon absorption and carbon emissions (in CO 2 -equivalent mass) exhibited significant fluctuating upward trends, whereas carbon sequestration increased without statistical significance. Carbon sequestration capacity differed markedly across regions: high- and medium-sequestration areas were concentrated in the western and central parts of the study area, while low- and negative-sequestration areas occurred mainly along its northern and eastern edges. (3) The carbon neutrality service radius ranged from 196.67 km to 262.84 km (mean 231.37 km), showing a statistically insignificant expanding trend, with the radiation range covering Gansu, Ningxia, Shanxi, Henan, Hubei, Chongqing and Sichuan. Following the mass‑conservation principle, this study theoretically quantifies the maximum spatial extent of forest carbon‑offsetting capacity instead of simulating actual atmospheric CO₂ transport and neutralization. Multi‑regional carbon‑flux observations will be adopted in future work to validate and refine the simulated service scope, offering solid cases and methodological support for spatial carbon governance of global mid‑latitude mountain ecotones. These results provide a spatially explicit basis for coordinating carbon neutrality actions between the Qinling Mountains and their surrounding regions.

items.title: Hidden in the desert: Community structure and temporal variation of scorpions (Arachnida: Scorpiones) in a protected area of Baja California Sur, Mexico
items.abstract: Scorpion community structure and population dynamics were evaluated over one year in the Cactus Sanctuary, Baja California Sur, Mexico, using six bimonthly sampling events. Four families, seven genera, and seven species were recorded, with Vaejovidae being the most species-rich. A total of 729 scorpions were collected, comprising 319 females, 222 males, and 188 juveniles in the study. The assemblage was numerically dominated by Centruroides exilicauda (Buthidae) and Maaykuyak vittatus (Vaejovidae), which together represented 79.3% of the specimens. Species richness was highest in August and February, whereas the total abundance peaked in October. Hill numbers indicated the highest diversity and evenness in June, whereas December showed lower effective diversity because of the uneven distribution of abundance among species. Multivariate analyses revealed temporal variations in community composition, which were potentially associated with seasonal changes in environmental conditions and species-specific activity patterns. Species accumulation and rarefaction analyses indicated that sampling effort adequately represented local species richness. Overall, the community was characterized by low species richness, numerical dominance by C. exilicauda and M. vittatus , and marked temporal variations in abundance and composition. These findings provide baseline information for understanding scorpion community dynamics in arid environments and support future ecological monitoring in the southern Baja California Peninsula.

items.title: PhaFoS: a global database of Phanerozoic foraminiferal size
items.abstract: Body size is a key phenotypic trait of living organisms, reflecting ecological function and individual metabolism. Evolutionary changes in body size also provide information on interactions between the organisms and their changing physical and biotic environments. Despite the utilitarian value of body size for understanding evolution and past environments, we lack a standardized, occurrence-based, Phanerozoic body size database for most groups of organisms, limiting large-scale studies of size evolution and size-environment interactions. Foraminifera are an ideal group to fill this data gap, given their abundant fossil record, extensive palaeogeographic distribution, and sensitivity to environmental changes. Here, we present PhaFoS, short for Pha nerozoic Fo raminifera S ize database. PhaFoS compiles 118 885 specimens, of which 103 121 from 963 published papers and the remaining 15 764 from our field colletions, representing 4167 genera and 34 256 species. Each record is linked to standardized and queryable metadata fields, including test volume (log 10 µm 3 ), taxonomy, stratigraphic age, and both modern and paleogeographic coordinates. This database can be used to quantify temporal and spatial patterns of foraminiferal body-size over the Phanerozoic, and to explore the body size relationships with environmental conditions and their changes. The data files described in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20777319 (Feng and Song, 2026).

items.title: Syntropic infrastructure for regenerative urban metabolic reorganization in an Atlantic island city
items.abstract: Urban climate vulnerability is increasingly associated with ecological fragmentation, thermal amplification, hydrological disruption, and declining ecosystem functionality across densely urbanized territories. This study proposes syntropic infrastructure as a regenerative urban framework capable of reorganizing ecological, hydrological, and thermal regulation processes through multiscalar spatial connectivity. Using Santa Cruz de Tenerife as a case study, the research integrates ecological connectivity metrics, land surface temperature (LST), soil organic carbon (SOC), hydrological runoff modeling, and socioecological accessibility indicators within a GIS-based spatial assessment framework standardized at 250 m grid resolution. Results revealed severe ecological fragmentation across the consolidated metropolitan matrix, with Probability of Connectivity values below 0.15 and Integral Index of Connectivity values below 0.10 throughout most coastal urban sectors. Thermal analyses identified persistent surface temperature anomalies ranging between +3 °C and +5 °C relative to peri-urban vegetated reference areas. Pearson correlation analyses demonstrated significant inverse relationships between SOC and LST ( r = −0.64, p < 0.01), while imperviousness intensity showed a strong positive association with thermal amplification ( r = 0.71, p < 0.01). Spatial autocorrelation analyses additionally confirmed significant clustering of thermal hotspots and degraded soils. The findings suggest that syntropic infrastructure may operate as a regenerative planning framework capable of increasing ecological connectivity, evapotranspirative cooling, hydrological retention, and socioecological resilience through integrated adaptive interventions in vulnerable coastal and island metropolitan systems.

items.title: From Bird Migration to Market Prices: How Will Offshore Wind Curtailment Affect Future Sustainable Electricity Systems?
items.abstract: Bird-related offshore wind curtailment is increasingly used to reduce collision risk during periods of intense bird migration, but its energy and electricity-market consequences depend strongly on when curtailment occurs. This study combines a historical analysis of Dutch Start/Stop events with a forward-looking electricity-market assessment. First, Start/Stop notifications between 2023 and 2026 are analysed using observed offshore wind conditions and aggregated offshore wind production to characterise the meteorological and generation conditions associated with individual events. The selected events occurred under markedly different wind conditions, with mean wind speeds during the notified periods ranging from approximately 5.0 to 10.5 m/s, indicating substantial variation in the wind-generation potential available during curtailment periods. Second, the EYE electricity-market model is used to assess the potential future electricity-system consequences of bird-related offshore wind curtailment under the National Drivers 2030 scenario. Sensitivity cases with offshore wind availability reduced by 40%, 60%, and 90% are compared with a reference case with full offshore wind availability. In the 2030 simulations, reduced offshore wind generation is compensated through changes in imports, dispatchable generation, storage, and other flexibility options. Daily-average market-clearing prices increase by approximately 2.0–5.0%, while larger price deviations are concentrated within the actual curtailment hours. The results demonstrate that the consequences of Start/Stop operation are both time-specific and resource-dependent, reflecting not only curtailment duration but also wind availability and electricity-system conditions during the affected hours. These scenario-specific results provide an assessment approach potentially relevant to other offshore wind regions with migration-related restrictions; the quantitative impacts depend on local wind, market and regulatory conditions. The findings can inform the integration of biodiversity protection into sustainable offshore wind and electricity-system development.

items.title: Marine Spatial Use Control, Blue Carbon, and Maritime Security in Indonesia: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Blue carbon ecosystems are increasingly central to climate mitigation, coastal resilience, and maritime governance, but their protection in Indonesia depends on how spatial plans are translated into effective implementation and control. This scoping review maps the relationship between marine spatial use control and mangrove and seagrass protection in Indonesia and interprets the implications for maritime security. Guided by JBI methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, searches of Scopus, Web of Science, GARUDA, and DOAJ, complemented by citation searching, yielded a final corpus of 39 studies. The evidence base is strongly asymmetrical: 29 studies focused on mangroves, whereas only three focused specifically on seagrasses; conclusions concerning seagrass governance are therefore exploratory and should not be generalized from the mangrove-dominated corpus. Regional Spatial Plans (RTRW) were the most frequently examined instrument type (12 studies), followed by coastal and small-island zoning plans (RZWP3K) and functional zoning (five each). The most commonly mapped primary evidence gaps concerned policy and governance (15 studies) and implementation and enforcement (12 studies). Only eight studies applied an explicit blue carbon framing. No formal critical appraisal of individual sources was undertaken, so these frequencies are interpreted as patterns in the reviewed literature rather than as estimates of national policy performance or causal effectiveness. Post-extraction interpretation using Bueger's maritime security framework indicated that the reviewed literature is most readily connected to the marine environment, human security, and economic development; except where security was explicitly discussed by source authors, these categories represent reviewer-applied interpretive pathways rather than direct security effects. Overall, the literature most consistently points to an implementation gap between spatial-plan design and effective control, including spatial conformity assessment, monitoring, institutional coordination, follow-up, and enforcement. Strengthening empirical evaluation of these functions, particularly for seagrasses and eastern Indonesia, is necessary before broader conclusions about blue carbon governance and maritime-security outcomes can be sustained.

items.title: Application of Environmental DNA Signatures for Detecting Rare Freshwater Species in Fragmented River Networks
items.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has become an innovative molecular technique for identifying rare and elusive species in freshwater ecosystems, especially in disconnected river systems where traditional identification methods are limited by sparse populations, habitat isolation, and reduced species mobility. The current research project assessed the utility of environmental DNA signatures to detect rare species in disconnected river ecosystems and their distribution patterns. The methodology involved collecting water samples from selected river sections and detecting genetic traces through molecular techniques and DNA sequencing. Special emphasis was placed on the role of hydrological connectivity, water flow, sediment interaction, and environmental conditions on eDNA detection and distribution patterns. This application of eDNA profiles offers the potential to increase species detection while avoiding disturbance to sensitive aquatic species. In addition, including habitat connectivity data in the molecular analysis enabled better understanding of rare-species distribution within fragmented freshwater ecosystems. Sampling location, environmental conditions, and DNA persistence were all crucial to interpreting detection results. Environmental DNA monitoring is an important complementary method for freshwater biodiversity assessments.

items.title: Seasonal Variation in Seagrass Epiphyte Communities and their Contribution to Coastal Primary Productivity
items.abstract: Seagrass ecosystems are significant coastal ecosystems where biodiversity, nutrient cycles, carbon sequestration, and primary production processes are carried out. Epiphytic communities living on seagrass leaves play a significant role in photosynthesis and ecological interactions in seagrass ecosystems. The biomass and productivity of epiphytic communities are influenced by seasonal changes in temperature, nutrients, penetration of light through water, and biological interactions. In the current study, seasonal variation in seagrass epiphytes is studied, and their contribution to coastal primary productivity is evaluated using simulation-based research method. Four seasons, namely pre-monsoon, monsoon, post-monsoon, and winter, were taken into consideration to study seasonal changes in environmental factors, biomass of epiphytes, and primary productivity. A simulated data set of 120 samples was constructed based on predetermined seasonal factors and variability of ecological factors. Mathematical models have been used to determine the biomass density, photosynthetic productivity, and relative importance of epiphytes in the overall ecosystem productivity. The simulations show that the biomass and productivity of the epiphytes are not consistent throughout the year; the post-monsoon season shows the greatest biomass and photosynthetic productivity. Availability of nutrients and underwater lighting influence the development of epiphytes, while environmental suitability influences their productivity dynamics. This leads to the creation of a mathematical base that explains the significance of epiphytes in relation to seagrasses ecologically and serves as a foundation for further research on coastal ecosystems productivity.

items.title: Pathways for high-quality development of marine ranching in the Beibu Gulf urban agglomeration
items.abstract: The transition of marine ranching from scale-oriented expansion toward high-quality development requires the simultaneous improvement of production efficiency, ecological sustainability, and farmed-animal welfare. However, increasing stocking intensity and technological investment may generate trade-offs among economic output, ecological carrying capacity, animal health, and long-term production sustainability. Existing studies have mainly examined ecological efficiency, resource and environmental carrying capacity, technological innovation, and industrial performance, while farmed aquatic animal welfare and its systemic interactions with ecological and socioeconomic outcomes remain insufficiently addressed. To fill this gap, this study introduces the One Welfare framework and constructs a One Welfare High-Quality Development Index (OWHI) integrating animal welfare, ecological environment, and economic and social development. Based on marine-ranching policy texts and development practices in the Beibu Gulf urban agglomeration, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) is employed to identify configurations associated with high-quality development, while System Dynamics (SD) is used to examine feedback mechanisms and the long-term effects of alternative policy combinations. The results reveal substantial conjunctural causation and equifinality, with no single condition constituting a necessary condition for high OWHI. Three major pathways are identified: technology-policy driven, ecology-market synergistic, and welfare-environment synergistic configurations. Smart technological empowerment and animal welfare management play important cross-path roles. Scenario simulations further show that isolated welfare, technological, or ecological interventions generate limited long-term improvements, whereas the coordinated integration of welfare standards, AI-enabled monitoring, IMTA, and cross-regional governance produces stronger and more persistent synergistic effects. These findings extend conventional ecological-economic-social assessments of marine ranching by explicitly incorporating animal welfare and provide a configurational and dynamic basis for improving marine ranching sustainability.

items.title: Mapping Ecological Connectivity among Isolated Freshwater Habitats Using Landscape-Based Spatial Analysis
items.abstract: Ponds, tanks, wetlands and small lakes are examples of freshwater ecosystems which house aquatic diversity. However, agriculture, urban development and drainage systems continue to cause fragmentation of these ecosystems. In this study, a spatial methodology based on a landscape approach that employs remote sensing, GIS, landscape metrics, least cost path analysis and graph theory was developed to map connectivity between isolated freshwater habitats in a 100 km² landscape. A total of 24 patches amounting to 3.84% of the total landscape were mapped, while 58.33% were found to be isolated. There were nine least cost corridors and habitat patches H03 and H10 were identified as important corridors. An ecosystem restoration scenario increased the Probability of Connectivity from 18.60% to 31.40%. The framework supports corridor restoration and conservation prioritization.

items.title: From forest edges to disciplinary boundaries: ecological patterns and structural analogy
items.abstract: Introduction Ecological boundaries separate habitats, whereas disciplinary boundaries can separate ways of understanding them. Whether empirical ecological patterns can provide a basis for structural analogy across disciplinary boundaries remains poorly understood. Methods We investigated soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities, enzyme activities, and soil fauna along edge-to-interior gradients at six forest sites spanning an urbanization gradient in Xiamen, China. In parallel, 150 participants from non-ecological professional backgrounds participated in structured field engagement. Cross-disciplinary analogies were assessed through open-ended responses, and their structural depth was evaluated using ordinal logistic regression. Results Microbial diversity, biomass, enzyme activities, and soil-faunal abundance generally increased from the urban core toward near-natural forests, whereas Proteobacteria relative abundance and bacterivorous nematode proportion declined. Ectomycorrhizal fungal relative abundance increased 7.74-fold across the urbanization gradient. Edge-to-interior contrasts were predominantly negative, although Proteobacteria exhibited significant edge enrichment (mean Edge Effect Index [EEI] = +0.191, p = 0.031), whereas available phosphorus showed a positive but non-significant mean EEI = +0.144, p = 0.062). Nematode community maturity showed an exploratory positive association between EEI and urbanization intensity (Spearman ρ = 0.829, n = 6). Following field engagement, 108 participants (72.0%) generated cross-disciplinary analogies, including 81 (54.0%) demonstrating intermediate or deep structural mapping. Longer observation duration was associated with greater analogy depth (odds ratio = 1.54 per 10-min increment, 95% confidence interval: 1.12–2.12; p = 0.007), whereas prior ecological knowledge and professional background showed no statistically detectable associations with depth. Discussion These findings reveal heterogeneous belowground ecological responses to urbanization and forest edges while demonstrating how measured ecological gradients can serve as a reference for cross-disciplinary structural reasoning. The observational design limits causal interpretation, but provides a basis for further investigation of ecological field engagement as a context for interdisciplinary understanding.

items.title: Priority gaps and governance mismatch in Andalusian olive and almond farming communities
items.abstract: Introduction Participatory sustainability assessments can reveal what farming communities value, but they rarely diagnose where those values are most acutely deteriorating or explain the structural forces behind such dynamics. In this study, we fill this gap by characterising the sustainability criteria of two Andalusian farming communities, ranked by importance and rated for their perceived trajectory (improving or deteriorating). We also recorded perceived causal influences on the trajectory of these criteria (actors and environmental or structural forces). From this, we identify “priority gaps,” i.e., criteria of high importance with a deteriorating perceived trajectory, as a basis for analysing causal mechanisms and governance responses. Methods The research is based on a three-week Photovoice process with 34 olive and almond farmers across two contrasting Andalusian regions. We analysed 57 farmer-defined criteria and 1,273 observations of causal influences. Results Four criteria were priority gaps in both regions. On three of them, generational succession, fair prices and agricultural policy, no group saw an improvement, pointing to structural failures that transcend local conditions and map onto unresolved challenges of the Common Agricultural Policy. Water protection, the fourth, divided the groups. Lock-in mapping revealed a governance mismatch. Taken together, negative influences on gap criteria concentrated at national-supranational and landscape-structural levels, while positive influences were most frequent at farm-household and community-cooperative levels. Adequate profitability was the single most important criterion in the intensive lowland site yet did not emerge at all in the diversified mountain site, suggesting that the two communities inhabit different lifeworld configurations. The men’s groups ranked generational succession, knowledge transmission, effort and dedication, and fair prices higher than the women’s groups did. The women’s groups ranked water protection and several criteria of care, health and recognition higher, and on average rated the perceived trajectory of fair prices lower, as the lowland women’s group did for profitability. Discussion The study shows that both priority-gap and lock-in mapping based on a participatory assessment can produce diagnostic evidence that aligns with accounts in the literature and thus offer a starting point for identifying areas for intervention, particularly in food-system governance, to address mismatches between governance levels.

items.title: Evaluating the Effects of Shoreline Modification on Nursery Habitat Quality in Tropical Estuaries
items.abstract: Tropical estuaries offer vital nursery habitats for young fishes and other aquatic organisms because of the presence of food, shelter, and appropriate water conditions, among others. Shoreline modifications caused by the urbanization process, coastal development, artificial embankments, and shoreline hardening may impact such ecological processes and decrease nursery habitat quality. The current research seeks to analyze how different shoreline modification conditions might influence nursery habitat quality in tropical estuaries using a simulation approach. A comparative evaluation framework was proposed using five ecological factors: abundance of juvenile fishes, species diversity, vegetation cover, habitat connectivity, and suitability of water quality. Four shoreline conditions were assessed: natural vegetated shorelines, moderately modified shorelines, highly armored shorelines, and living shorelines. Datasets have been created to analyze the distinctions in ecological functioning among the four scenarios. Based on the simulations, the natural and restored living shorelines have relatively higher nursery habitat quality when compared to highly armored shorelines. Vegetation cover and connectivity have high correlations with the habitat-quality index. It is suggested that shoreline modifications may impact nursery functioning through structural complexity, ecological connectivity, and environmental favorability. The developed conceptual framework can be used as a foundation for assessing the alternative shoreline management scenarios and prioritizing restoration in tropical estuarine ecosystems.

items.title: Cold atomic ensembles as quantum antennas for distributed networks of single-atom arrays
items.abstract: Single neutral atoms in optical tweezer arrays offer a promising platform for high-fidelity quantum computing at local nodes. Nonetheless, creating entanglement between remote nodes in a distributed quantum network remains challenging due to inherently weak atom-light coupling. Here, we design a distributed quantum network architecture in which cold atomic ensembles with strong atom-light interactions serve as quantum antennas, interfacing single-atom qubits with flying photons to enable high-efficiency atom-photon entanglement generation, analogous to the role of antennas in classical communication. Using realistic experimental parameters, we estimate an efficiency of for generating atom-photon entanglement, a probability of P_E % for generating atom-atom entanglement, and a remote entanglement generation rate of 16.9 kHz, which can be further improved through system optimization. This performance not only surpasses that of state-of-the-art cavity-based or high-numerical-aperture-lens-based architectures but also offers notable advantages in simplicity, tunability, and experimental accessibility. Our scheme also integrates a long-lived quantum memory, providing a storage advantage for quantum repeater design. By leveraging the complementary strengths of single-atom qubits for local operations and cold atomic ensembles for networking, this approach paves the way for scalable distributed quantum computing and sensing.

items.title: Low- T / | W | instabilities in differentially rotating neutron stars resembling merger remnants
items.abstract: We construct constant rest-mass sequences of equilibrium models of differentially rotating neutron stars which resemble binary neutron star post-merger remnants. For a more realistic description of the post-merger remnant, we impose that each model carries approximately 95% of the angular momentum that a binary system with the same total rest-mass has at the moment of merging, based on an empirical relation informed from neutron star merger simulations. We account for equation of state effects by employing two distinct microphysical descriptions for high density matter. We dynamically evolve the equilibrium models with a three-dimensional general relativistic hydrodynamics code that employs the conformal flatness approximation. We investigate the connection between the occurrence of the instability and the existence of corotation radii within the stellar configurations and determine the instability window for both equation of state sequences. The occurrence of low T/|W | instabilities leads to pronounced gravitational wave emission in the range 0.13 ⪅ β ⪅ 0.2, while models outside this range exhibit less pronounced features in the gravitational wave spectrum. The prominence of gravitational wave emission is primarily determined by β, while the equation of state seems to have a more minor effect. We present correlations between the strength of the gravitational wave emission associated with the instability and properties of the equilibrium models. Stellar configurations modelled by different equations of state display differences in the timescales over which the various dynamical features develop, as well as whether they exhibit a pronounced m = 1 deformation. Potential relations between the instability growth timescales and properties of the stellar models are studied.

items.title: Fast magnetosonic turbulence in two-dimensional relativistic plasmas
items.abstract: We present fully kinetic simulations of driven 2D turbulence in a relativistic plasma, designed for the first time to induce a fast magnetosonic cascade. As the driving strength increases, turbulence transitions from a weakly nonlinear wave-dominated regime to strongly nonlinear, compression-rich dynamics. Using spatiotemporal Fourier analysis, we identify fast modes consistent with the derived fluid-scale linear dispersion relation. We find that in the weakly nonlinear turbulence regime, the spatial power spectra have universal power-law scalings across different quantities in the inertial range. Our results demonstrate that fast-mode kinetic turbulence can persist as a wave-dominated cascade, without inevitably steepening into shocks. Our results are relevant for modeling of turbulence and shock statistics in high-energy astrophysical plasmas such as pulsar wind nebulae and jets.

items.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
items.abstract: Abstract Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax supernovae.

items.title: Unveiling the Dark Matter Nature with Reionization Relics
items.abstract: Abstract Dark matter constitutes roughly one-fourth of the Universe, yet its physical nature remains unknown. Warm dark matter (WDM), a class of dark matter candidates, has nonnegligible velocity dispersion that suppresses the formation of small-scale cosmic structures. Current constraints therefore rely mainly on small-scale probes such as the Ly α forest and Milky Way observations of satellite galaxies and stellar streams. We propose a novel large-scale probe based on long-lived “reionization relics”: because the thermal and dynamical evolution of the intergalactic medium depends on the local reionization redshift, patchy reionization imprints additional large-scale fluctuations in Ly α forest opacity and post-reionization H I traced by 21 cm intensity mapping. The strength of these imprints depends on WDM through both small-scale gas evolution and WDM-driven changes in the reionization history. For example, the Ly α (21 cm) power spectrum in 3 keV WDM differs from cold dark matter by ≃19% (≃19%) at k = 0.05 Mpc −1 at z = 4 ( z = 5.5) when reionization relics are included. Using Ly α forest with a covariance model designed to mimic the capabilities of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we forecast a constraint of m WDM > 5.0 keV (95%), which improves to m WDM > 7.1 keV when combined with 21 cm intensity-mapping observations from the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). The next-generation surveys can further strengthen the current best lower bounds from 9.7 to 39 keV.
