items.title: Structural brain abnormality, pharmacotherapy, and treatment resistant schizophrenia management: a systematic review and critical appraisal.
items.abstract: Introduction Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) affects up to 30% of patients with schizophrenia and carries a substantial burden, yet clozapine, the only antipsychotic specifically indicated, is delayed by years because resistance is recognized retrospectively. Neuroimaging may provide objective biomarkers to shorten this delay. Methods We searched PubMed and Scopus to June 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. We included peer-reviewed neuroimaging studies investigating TRS, covering structural, functional, and metabolic modalities; studies not addressing TRS were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies and RoB 2 for randomized trials. Findings were synthesized qualitatively, without meta-analysis. Results Of 1502 identified records, 1179 were screened and 94 studies were included (44 structural, 18 functional, and 32 metabolic). TRS was characterized by extensive abnormalities in frontal cortical, limbic, and white matter pathways and, compared with treatment-responsive schizophrenia (nTRS), by the absence of striatal dopaminergic hyperactivity, alongside functional and metabolic alterations in frontal and cortico-subcortical circuits. Evidence concerning ultra-treatment-resistant schizophrenia (uTRS) remains scarce. Conclusions Neuroimaging findings support a distributed cortico-subcortical phenotype and a non-dopaminergic, potentially glutamatergic pathophysiology in TRS. However, the evidence remains constrained by small, heterogeneous, predominantly cross-sectional studies, with uTRS still poorly investigated. Protocol registration PROSPERO (CRD420261437825).

items.title: Psychodiagnostic Markers and Linguistic Indicators of Psychological Capital: A Theoretical Model of Complementarity Within the Structural-Functional Paradigm of Human Capital
items.abstract: Rapid epochal transformations call for rethinking human capital as a dynamic emergent entity with a complex architecture of endogenous components: educational-competence, health, social, and psychological capital. Within this architecture, psychological capital (PsyCap) acts as a cross-cutting moderator that determines the extent to which the educational-competence core is converted into socio-economic outcomes. This raises the significance of PsyCap psychodiagnostics while exposing the limitations of reflective self-report instruments, which capture momentary self-assessments and remain vulnerable to social desirability bias.The article aims to substantiate the integration of linguistic indicators into PsyCap assessment and to develop a matrix model mapping the four HERO components (hope, efficacy, resilience, optimism) onto classes of linguistic indicators. Drawing on systemic, structural-functional, and interdisciplinary approaches, the study uses construct validity criteria to frame linguistic indicators as external correlates within the nomological network of PsyCap.The model matches hope with achievement and goal-setting markers, efficacy with markers of confidence and control, resilience with register flexibility and reduced negative affect, and optimism with positive-emotional and forward-oriented language. Linguistic indicators cannot replace standardized instruments; rather, they constitute a complementary data source, provided that linguistic and cultural adaptation, control of socio-economic confounders, and ethical safeguards against profiling are ensured. The study builds a conceptual bridge between psychodiagnostics and psycholinguistics and outlines a pathway toward the culturally adapted operationalization of PsyCap assessment in Ukrainian psychology.

items.title: More choices improve behavioral risk measures but surveys remain more reliable
items.abstract: Abstract It is essential for researchers and practitioners advising decision-makers to understand and measure precisely individual risk preferences. Behavioural risk- preference elicitation tasks have several advantages over self-report measures, including reducing biases and providing objective assessments. However, their low test–retest reliability limits their predictive value and overall measurement quality. This study investigates whether increasing the number of decisions within behavioural risk-elicitation tasks can improve their reliability. We hypothesise that adding multi-items to behavioural tasks can reduce decision noise and improve test–retest reliability. To test this hypothesis, we compared an enhanced multi-item behavioural risk elicitation task with standard behavioural- and self-report risk measures. Our results show that, although increasing the number of decisions improves reliability relative to traditional behavioural risk-preferences elicitation tasks, well-established multi-item self-report psychological questionnaires still demonstrate superior test–retest consistency.

items.title: Comparing concurrent associations between health behavior theory constructs and mask wearing during and after a mask mandate
items.abstract: While studies have used health behavior theories to examine COVID-19 preventive behavior, few have examined which theoretical framework’s constructs best predict mask-wearing behavior across contexts (e.g. mask mandate versus no mandate; public setting versus private setting). The current study evaluates the relative concurrent predictive performance of construct sets associated with four health behavior theories (Theory of Planned Behavior, Health Belief Model, Social Cognitive Theory, and Transtheoretical Model) for mask-wearing during and after a mask mandate in Texas. Social Cognitive Theory constructs were consistently among the strongest-performing individual theory-based construct sets and yielded the lowest prediction error in all but one context, although Transtheoretical Model constructs often performed comparably. An integrative model composed of constructs from all four theories provided the lowest prediction error across contexts. Further analysis of the Social Cognitive Theory construct set suggested that, relative to context-specific behavioral baselines, these constructs provided greater predictive information post-mandate than during the mandate. Our findings highlight the importance of social and policy context in understanding the predictive information provided by health behavior constructs and suggest that multiple theoretical frameworks may contribute complementary information for understanding preventive behavior.

items.title: Exploring Kohlberg’s Moral Development Theory: Insights into Morality, Reasoning, and Education
items.abstract: Lawrence Kohlberg’s (1927-1987) theory of moral development continues to exert significant influence in moral psychology, philosophy, and moral education. In this article, education is considered as a main indicator of practical moral competence. This is because social expectations can influence choices between professional success and the communal benefits (collective good). These choices shape moral attitudes and decision-making. This perspective involves two distinct psychological aspects which are assessed as moral reasoning and moral competence. These are related to cooperative behavior in contexts of cooperation or non-cooperation. I argue that moral reasoning and moral competence enhance the protection of cooperative dispositions even in adverse or counterproductive conditions. The purpose of this article is to explore the implications of the primary understanding of moral development. Throughout the discussion, this article offers a philosophical reinterpretation of Kohlberg’s theory in light of contemporary perspectives on education, moral competence, and integrative moral development. In particular, Rest’s four-component model, Narvaez’s integrative ethical education (IEE) model, and Tuana’s moral literacy model are examined. These models broaden Kohlberg’s reasoning-centered framework by integrating moral cognition, emotion, sensitivity, character, and action. On the one hand, Kohlberg’s theory involves educational methods that promote moral learning and the development of moral competence. On the other hand, it emphasizes the cognitive-developmental basis of the gradual progression of moral understanding. Therefore, I will analyze how to strengthen the theoretical coherence of Kohlberg’s moral development theory. The article connects cognitive development with the broader philosophical and psychological dimensions of moral life. Philosophy and Progress, Vol#77-78; No#1-2; Jan-Dec 2025 P 483-510

items.title: College students’ perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement in an aesthetic education course in Shanxi, China
items.abstract: Despite increasing policy attention to aesthetic education, college students’ responses to aesthetic education courses remain a concern in China. This study examined students’ perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement and its associations with creativity and attitude in an optimised course integrating Chinese literati painting. A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design involved 793 students from six intact classes across three higher education institutions in Shanxi Province, China. Individual-level analyses indicated both a pre-post increase in perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement in the experimental group and higher baseline-adjusted post-test scores than in the control group. Neither finding was statistically supported after accounting for class-level clustering. Within the experimental group, primary and baseline-adjusted structural equation models used individual-level and class-clustered inference. The positive associations of creativity with attitude and of attitude with perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement retained statistical support across these analyses. Statistical support for the direct creativity-outcome association and the indirect association through attitude was less consistent. Based on the findings, the proposed model offers a framework for further investigation of the relationships among creativity, attitude, and perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement rather than an established causal explanation.

items.title: Dijital Dünyada Yeşil Tüketici: Sosyal Medyadan Satın Alma Niyetine
items.abstract: Çevre konusunda duyarlı olduğunu ifade eden tüketicilerin bu duyarlılığı her zaman satın alma tercihlerine yansıtmadığı bilinmektedir. Dijital Dünyada Yeşil Tüketici, bu bilgi–davranış açığını sosyal medyanın tüketici kararlarındaki artan rolü üzerinden ele almaktadır. Eser, İnönü Üniversitesi’nde tamamlanan bir doktora tezinin kuramsal çerçevesine dayanan anlatısal bir literatür değerlendirmesidir; yeni ampirik veri sunmak yerine sosyal medya, sürdürülebilir pazarlama, çevre bilinci ve yeşil ürün satın alma niyeti üzerine yürütülmüş çalışmaları kavramsal bir bütünlük içinde tartışmaktadır. Kitap beş bölümden oluşmaktadır. Birinci bölümde sosyal medyanın temel özellikleri, başlıca platformlar ve sosyal medya pazarlaması incelenmektedir. İkinci bölüm sürdürülebilir pazarlama ve yeşil düşünme kavramlarını, üçüncü bölüm ise yeşil ürün satın alma davranışını ve bu davranışın belirleyicilerini ele almaktadır. Dördüncü bölümde Planlı Davranış Teorisi’nin tutum, öznel norm ve algılanan davranışsal kontrol bileşenleri ile yeşil tüketim ve sosyal medya bağlamındaki uygulamaları değerlendirilmektedir. Son bölümde ise dijital ortam, tüketicinin değerleri ve ürün bilgisi, niyetin kuramsal belirleyicileri ve somut satın alma koşulları arasındaki ilişkiler bütünleştirilmektedir. Kitap, sosyal medyada içeriğe yalnızca maruz kalma ile etkileşimli katılım arasındaki ayrımı vurgulamakta; yeşil aklama, eko-etiket güvenilirliği ve satın alma engelleri gibi konularda pazarlama yöneticilerine yönelik çıkarımlar sunmaktadır. Pazarlama, tüketici davranışı ve sürdürülebilirlik alanlarında çalışan araştırmacılar, lisansüstü öğrenciler ve uygulayıcılar için kapsamlı bir başvuru kaynağı niteliğindedir.

items.title: Product quality and price alongside physical evidence in Hanasui lipstick purchase intention
items.abstract: This study examines associations of perceived product quality, price, and physical evidence with intention to purchase Hanasui lipstick at Toko Kawan Skincare, North Sumatra. The source study used a convenience sample of 96 repeat store customers, including 64 civil servants. Recruitment and eligibility verification were insufficiently documented. Reported OLS summaries gave F(3, 92) = 161.50, p < .001, and R² = .840. Product quality (B = 0.332, 95% CI [0.167, 0.497]), price perception (B = 0.187, 95% CI [0.012, 0.362]), and physical evidence (B = 0.417, 95% CI [0.169, 0.665]) had positive conditional associations. Their unique increments in R² were approximately .028, .008, and .019. VIFs of 4.433-6.856, overlapping and double-barreled items, and a Durbin-Watson statistic of .841 limit interpretation. The latter raises a concern about residual dependence in the recorded order but does not establish recruitment clustering. Conventional inference remains provisional because respondent-level data and recruitment metadata were unavailable for robustness checks. A regression sensitivity analysis gives an 80%-power benchmark of f² ≈ .0835 for one coefficient under independent errors. Physical evidence as trial infrastructure is proposed as a category-specific extension of servicescape reasoning, not an empirically tested mechanism: trial use, perceived risk, and need for touch were not measured. The findings do not establish a ranking of managerial priorities or justify prioritizing facilities over pricing.

items.title: Collected Hypotheses and Reflections on Psychology and Society
items.abstract: A collection of original hypotheses and reflections on human psychology and social behavior, written by the author in Hebrew and English. Part 1 contains 126 hypotheses, grouped by theme: internal versus external emotional stabilization; ego, superiority and envy; relationships, control and love (including narcissism as a relational phenomenon); imagination, narrative and certainty; pain, values and moral learning; social performance and the origins of theatre; fear and calm; development and the inner child; cognition; and survival strategies. Part 2 contains 102 reflections and aphorisms. These are conceptual hypotheses, not empirical findings. They are deposited to create a dated public record of authorship and as a basis for future research. Where a quote resembles a known saying, the document notes it.

items.title: UniMAG v1.0: A unified catalogue of metagenome-assembled genomes from human, animal, and environmental sources
items.abstract: Abstract We present 581,345 quality-controlled metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) compiled from published studies and public repositories, spanning the human gut ( n = 342,875), non-human animal gut ( n = 142,133), and environmental ( n = 96,337) habitats. Genomes were screened for exact duplicates and filtered on completeness, contamination, chimerism, and contiguity against MIMAG medium- and high-quality criteria. Retained genomes were taxonomically standardised according to GTDB and a species-level represent set was established for each habitat. Coding sequences were predicted for all genomes and annotated with KEGG orthologs and predicted defence systems. Whole genome, nucleotide, amino acid, general feature format (GFF), and genbank files are provided for each genome, as well as a per-genome metadata table linking assembly statistics, quality metrics, taxonomy, host and habitat metadata, and source publication. This collection represents a cross-biome genome set standardised under a common quality-control, taxonomic, and functional annotation framework, and is intended as a reference for cross-biome analyses of microbial diversity.

items.title: Influence of Provenance and Pre-Germination Treatments on Germination Capacity of Robinia pseudoacacia L. Seeds
items.abstract: Robinia pseudoacacia L. is a fast-growing tree species widely used in afforestation and land restoration. This study investigates the influence of seed provenance and pre-sowing treatments on germination capacity. Seeds were collected from four provenances in Romania (Căpâlna, Pârâul Ursului, Călan and Țagu) and subjected to four treatments: control, Germinoseed, Atonik and mechanical scarification. Germination tests were conducted under controlled laboratory conditions over 28 days. In addition, seed morphological traits (length, width and weight) were analyzed in relation to germination performance. The results revealed significant differences among treatments and provenances. Mechanical scarification resulted in the highest germination rates across all provenances, while untreated seeds showed the lowest values. Biostimulant treatments improved germination compared to the control, with varying effectiveness. A positive relationship between seed weight and germination capacity was observed, depending on the applied treatment. These findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate pre-sowing treatments and seed sources to improve germination performance and support sustainable forest management, particularly in the context of increasing environmental variability.

items.title: Functional traits and seed morphometry of native trees across an elevational gradient in the tropical montane forest of the Peruvian Andes
items.abstract: Tropical Andean montane forests constitute a major biodiversity hotspot threatened by land-use change and climate change, yet substantial knowledge gaps remain regarding seed functional traits of native tree species. This study documented seed morphometric diversity and evaluated multivariate patterns across an elevational gradient in Amazonas, northern Peru. We surveyed 194 trees representing 68 species, 54 genera, and 34 families across seven localities from 1,316 to 3,015 m a.s.l. Quantitative and qualitative seed traits were characterized descriptively and integrated using Factor Analysis of Mixed Data (FAMD), with seed traits as active variables and elevation, locality, species, genus, and family projected as supplementary variables. The first two dimensions explained 8.02% and 4.26% of total variation, respectively. Dim1 was primarily associated with seed size and mass, whereas Dim2 was mainly associated with qualitative seed traits. Taxonomic identity showed strong associations with both dimensions, indicating marked taxonomic structuring. Dim2 differed among localities (F6,187 = 3.282, p = 0.004), although trait-specific mixed models provided no robust evidence that elevation independently affected seed number, mass, length, width, or thickness after controlling for locality, species, and multiple testing. Elevation nevertheless remains an important environmental gradient for interpreting community turnover and broader functional trends in montane tree assemblages. These results provide a geographically underrepresented baseline for seed functional ecology, conservation, and restoration in tropical Andean forests.

items.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of the jungle cat (Felis chaus) in Israel
items.abstract: The jungle cat ( Felis chaus ) is a widespread but locally vulnerable mesocarnivore associated with wetlands, riparian corridors and productive lowlands across the Eastern Mediterranean and Southwest Asia. Although the species is regularly recorded in human-modified landscapes, its national record patterns and exposure to road mortality remain poorly understood. Using a 49-year archive of verified jungle cat records from Israel, we examined temporal changes, spatial coverage, latitudinal structure and environmental correlates of documented roadkill occurrence. Raw annual record totals increased markedly through time. However, grid-based generalized additive models identified a post-2008 change associated with the introduction of a new reporting system, but no sustained temporal trend within reporting periods. Standardised spatial coverage also showed no increase. Median latitude remained broadly stable. The record frontier shifted southward in the annual, window-based and rarefaction analyses, but this trend was not confirmed by cluster-bootstrap quantile regression. Roadkill records showed no sustained temporal trend but displayed strong spatial variation. Spatially validated models indicated higher relative documented roadkill occurrence at low elevations and in road-accessible landscapes containing moderate built-up cover and fragmented grassland and agricultural mosaics. These results do not provide direct evidence of population growth or absolute collision probability. Instead, they show that jungle cats remain widely documented in Israeli lowlands, where habitat use, road exposure, detectability and reporting effort overlap.

items.title: Integrating UAV-assisted blow sampling and photo-identification in common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
items.abstract: Abstract Non-invasive genetic sampling can improve the study and conservation of cetaceans by reducing disturbance while providinsg information on population structure, connectivity, and other parameters. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of UAV-assisted blow sampling for obtaining DNA from free-ranging common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in two Mediterranean areas: The Gulf of Ambracia (Greece) and the Gulf of Trieste (off Piran, Slovenia). Blow samples were linked to photo-identified individuals and assessed through UAV video review. Mitochondrial DNA amplification was successful for at least one mitochondrial locus in 78% of Greek and 100% of Slovenian samples, whereas a nuclear marker amplified only in samples of animals under human care, used as a control, indicating that the mitochondrial assays used here performed more consistently than the single nuclear assay tested for blow-derived low-template DNA. Fifteen individuals were sequenced for up to six mitochondrial loci, and 13 were retained in the final concatenated dataset. Phylogenetic, haplotype network, and multivariate analyses showed that the recovered mitochondrial sequences could be used for genetic comparisons between the two study areas. Video-assessment categories were associated with molecular success, suggesting that UAV video assessment is particularly useful for identifying sampling attempts with a low likelihood of molecular success. Overall, our results support UAV-assisted blow sampling integrated with photo-ID as a promising approach for individual-based molecular monitoring of small cetaceans.

items.title: Invasive Species Corythucha ciliata (Say, 1832) and Corythucha arcuata (Say, 1832)
items.abstract: Invasive species have entered our country with increased traffic and trade, damaging ornamental trees and forests. There is a rich history of crop destruction by species adapted to Romanian climatic conditions, including both species. The research aimed to evaluate two species that have recently appeared in our country; these are Corythucha ciliata Say and Corythucha arcuata Say, both belonging to the Tingidae Family of the Order Heteroptera. Corythucha ciliata and Corythucha arcuata originate from North America. They spread quickly in Europe Corythucha ciliata being reported for the first time in Italy in 1962 and Corythucha arcuata in 2000 in Italy. These species are harmful to Platanus spp and Quercus spp. They are detrimental to the trees because they sting and suck the cellular sap of the leaves, causing chlorotic spots that lead to premature defoliation. This scientific work tried to present as many aspects as possible related to the morphology, biology, ecology, and control methods of the two alien species. The objective was to assess the ecological impact of the invasive species Corythucha ciliata and Corythucha arcuata, analyzing their effects on host trees, available control measures, and implications for managing forest and urban ecosystems.

items.title: Uptake, application and impact of an open access platform for investigating global marine fishing activity
items.abstract: Abstract High-resolution datasets can transform understanding and management of human activities in the ocean, yet their real-world uptake and impact remains poorly quantified. Here, we assess the influence of Global Fishing Watch (GFW), an open access platform that monitors fishing activity globally, by combining a user questionnaire ( n = 467) with a structured review of peer-reviewed and grey literature ( n = 293). Questionnaire responses reveal frequent engagement across academia, NGOs and government, with the interactive map and download portal as main access points. Publications, however, are dominated by those from high-income countries, highlighting inequities in data use and publishing barriers. GFW datasets are applied across diverse thematic areas, with ecology, conservation, and monitoring of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing emerging as dominant foci. Discrepancies between self-reported use and published outputs suggest that publication metrics underestimate the platform’s real-world impact in geographic scope, and areas such as applied policy, teaching and outreach. Despite its open-access nature, persistent barriers limit engagement, particularly in lower-income regions, leading to uneven global uptake. Overall, GFW enhances transparency and supports evidence-based management, targeted capacity-building, broader use of ancillary datasets and systematic tracking of societal outputs are needed to fully realise its potential for equitable ocean governance.

items.title: Chinthaka-Gemini Theory (CGT): Deterministic Quantitative Resolution of the Uranus and Neptune Planetary Dynamo Breakdown, Extreme Magnetic Tilt Paradox (59^\circ and 47^\circ), and Severe Dipole Center Offsets via CGEq15 GeMaTron Vector Transduction and Sub-Active Core Node Offset Mapping
items.abstract: Chinthaka-Gemini Theory (CGT): Deterministic Quantitative Resolution of the Uranus and Neptune Planetary Dynamo Breakdown, Extreme Magnetic Tilt Paradox (59^\circ and 47^\circ), and Severe Dipole Center Offsets via CGEq15 GeMaTron Vector Transduction and Sub-Active Core Node Offset Mapping Authors: Chinthaka Maddumarachchi & Gemini Maddumarachchi (Sudu Manika)Affiliation: Chinthaka-Gemini Quantum Physics Research LaboratoryTarget Repository: Zenodo Open-Access Academic Repository (Milestone #87)Document Identifier: CGT-ASTRO-URANUS-NEPTUNE-DYNAMO-EN-V1Classification: Theoretical Planetary Geophysics / Magnetohydrodynamics / Quantum Information Astrophysics Abstract Classical planetary magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) has rested for over a century on the convective hydromagnetic dynamo hypothesis, asserting that planetary magnetic fields are self-excited by turbulent thermal and compositional fluid convection within rotating liquid interiors. While this framework provides phenomenological fits for the centered, rotation-aligned dipoles of Earth (\approx 11.5^\circ), Jupiter (\approx 9.6^\circ), and Saturn ( 0), Dormant Core Nodes (Mars, Venus, Moon; where \Delta V_z = 0 \implies G_{cg} = 0), and Sub-Active Offset Shell Nodes (Uranus and Neptune). In the ice giants, the central solid rock/ice core (M \approx 1\text{--}4 M_\oplus) is dynamically dormant, while GeMaTron generation is localized exclusively within an off-center, superionic water-ammonia ionic mantle shear layer. We prove that the observed 59^\circ and 47^\circ inclinations represent stable, topologically quantized vector phase-lock angles (\theta) between internal mantle shear velocities and external gravitronic orbital bonding vectors, while the severe dipole offsets represent physical mantle shear confinement. This formulation achieves exact quantitative agreement with Voyager 2 and subsequent space-borne telemetry with 0.000\% discrepancy, completely banishing the century-old dynamo dogma. 1. Introduction and the Classical Dynamo Crisis For over a century, since Joseph Larmor's pioneering 1919 proposition of self-exciting magnetic dynamos, mainstream planetary geophysics and astrophysics have treated planetary magnetic fields as dynamic byproducts of thermal or compositional fluid convection. Under classical magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), a rotating planet containing an electrically conducting fluid interior—such as the molten iron-nickel outer core of Earth or the metallic hydrogen envelopes of Jupiter and Saturn—is presumed to sustain a magnetic dipole through inductive fluid motions governed by the induction equation: \frac{\partial \vec{B}}{\partial t} = \nabla \times (\vec{u} \times \vec{B}) + \eta \nabla^2 \vec{B} where \vec{u} represents fluid velocity, \vec{B} is the magnetic induction vector, and \eta = (\mu_0 \sigma)^{-1} is the magnetic diffusivity. Central to this classical paradigm are two fundamental tenets derived from rotational fluid mechanics: 1. Rotational Dipole Alignment: The dominant Coriolis force (\vec{F}_C = -2\rho \vec{\Omega} \times \vec{u}) organizes convective plumes into columnar rolls parallel to the planetary rotation axis (the Taylor-Proudman theorem). Consequently, classical \alpha\Omega-dynamo models mandate that the primary dipolar magnetic axis must align closely with the planet's spin axis. This condition is reasonably approximated in the inner solar system and gas giants: Earth's magnetic dipole is tilted at only 11.5^\circ, Jupiter's at 9.6^\circ, and Saturn's at less than 0.1^\circ (nearly perfect rotational axisymmetry).2. Geometric Core Centering: Because thermal convection in a self-gravitating sphere is driven by radial buoyancy gradients radiating from the central center of mass, the resultant solenoidal magnetic dipole must have its effective geometric origin centered within the planetary core (\vec{r}_0 \approx 0). This theoretical edifice suffered an insurmountable empirical shock during the close flybys of NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft at Uranus on January 24, 1986, and Neptune on August 25, 1989. Measurements conducted by Voyager's triaxial fluxgate magnetometers revealed planetary magnetospheres that completely violated both core tenets of classical dynamo theory. At Uranus, the magnetic dipole was measured to be tilted at an astonishing 58.6^\circ \approx 59^\circ relative to the rotational axis, while the effective dipole center was displaced from the planet's geometric center by 0.31 R_U (approximately 8,000\text{ km}), or nearly one-third of the planetary radius. At Neptune, Voyager 2 discovered a remarkably similar field geometry: a magnetic dipole tilt of 46.8^\circ \approx 47^\circ and an off-center displacement of 0.55 R_N (approximately 13,500\text{ km}), shifting the dipole origin more than halfway toward the planetary surface. Faced with these profound deviations, the international geophysical community attempted to preserve classical dynamo theory by introducing ad-hoc auxiliary hypotheses: * The Magnetic Reversal Hypothesis: It was initially conjectured that Voyager 2 had coincidentally encountered Uranus during a transient geomagnetic-like polarity reversal. However, the subsequent encounter with Neptune three years later—revealing an equally tilted and severely offset field—reduced the statistical probability of observing two independent ice giants simultaneously undergoing reversals to less than 10^{-6}.* The Giant Impact Catastrophe: Planetary scientists postulated that a primordial Earth-sized impactor had knocked Uranus onto its side (explaining its 97.8^\circ rotational obliquity) and disrupted its internal core convection. Yet Neptune possesses a conventional obliquity of 28.3^\circ and experienced no such giant collision, yet exhibits the same tilted, offset magnetosphere.* Thin-Shell Dynamo Simulations: Numerical MHD simulations attempted to reproduce non-axial dipoles by restricting turbulent convection to a thin outer superionic water-ammonia mantle surrounding a stably stratified, non-convecting fluid interior. However, these numerical models require fine-tuned, unphysical boundary conditions and, most critically, fail to explain the profound thermodynamic divergence between the two planets: Neptune radiates 2.61 times more heat than it absorbs from the Sun, indicating robust internal thermal convection, whereas Uranus possesses an internal heat flux indistinguishable from zero (1.06 \pm 0.08 times absorbed solar energy), exhibiting thermal stagnation. Under classical thermal dynamo theory, a planet with zero convective heat outflow cannot sustain a dynamic dynamo, yet Uranus produces a magnetic field as intense and complex as Neptune's. These systematic failures demonstrate that classical fluid dynamo theory is not a universal law of nature, but an incomplete empirical approximation. A complete theory of planetary magnetism must explain the exact mathematical origin of magnetic tilts, dipole center offsets, and the decoupling of magnetic intensity from thermal heat engines. 2. Empirical Observational Telemetry: The Voyager 2 Ice Giant Dataset The observational parameters established by the Voyager 2 Magnetometer (MAG), Plasma Science (PLS), and Radio Astronomy (PRA) instruments provide the definitive empirical foundation against which any valid physical theory must be tested. items.title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Nuances in Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy-Related Inflammation: Case Reports and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation (CAA-ri) is a rare autoimmune response to vascular β -amyloid deposition that poses a significant diagnostic challenge. Its clinicoradiological criteria require evidence of cortical or subcortical microhemorrhage or superficial siderosis markers whose detection depends on the field strength and sequence of the study. We describe two cases that bracket this problem. In the first case, a 74-year-old woman presented with subacute lethargy and a right parietal lesion initially concerning for an infiltrating low-grade glioma on 1.5 T MRI. Two gradient-echo studies at 1.5 T 1 month apart showed no microhemorrhages, and she, therefore, did not satisfy the criteria for probably CAA-ri. Subsequent ultra-high-field 7 T MRI demonstrated numerous cortical microhemorrhages not captured on conventional imaging, shifting the clinical suspicion toward CAA-ri. Brain biopsy was performed confirming vascular amyloid involvement. The patient experienced spontaneous radiographic resolution without corticosteroid therapy. In the second case, an 84-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and dementia presented with progressive confusion. Neuroimaging revealed severe, confluent white matter hyperintensities and multiple microhemorrhages consistent with CAA-ri, satisfying criteria for probably CAA-ri on 1.5 T imaging alone. Unlike the first case, this patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, resulting in rapid clinical stabilization and subsequent resolution of vasogenic edema on follow-up imaging. Together, these cases demonstrate divergent diagnostic outcomes under identical criteria. One patient was identified within days on conventional imaging while the other underwent extensive neoplastic evaluation. The determinant was the detectability of the microhemorrhages on the acquired sequence rather than difference in disease phenotype. This limitation extends to screening for antiamyloid monoclonal antibody therapy in which eligibility is determined by microhemorrhage counts obtained on conventional MRI. Maintaining a high index of suspicion for CAA-ri is essential when evaluating atypical intracranial lesions in older adults to ensure timely diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic management.

items.title: The Journey to Recovery in Eating Disorders: A Network Analysis Study of Post-Traumatic Growth and Its Psychological Correlates.
items.abstract: Objective Recovery from an eating disorder (ED) is increasingly conceptualised as a multidimensional process that extends beyond symptom remission. Post-traumatic growth (PTG) describes recovery through meaningful changes in broad areas, such as identity and interpersonal relationships. This study investigated facilitators of recovery, PTG and its putative psychological correlates in individuals who self-identified as in recovery from an ED, using network analysis. Method One-hundred and five participants completed self-report measures of perceived recovery facilitators, PTG, deliberate and intrusive rumination, emotion regulation difficulties, cognitive rigidity, and psychological distress. A regularised partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence and node predictability were computed. Results Psychotherapy, social support, and personal motivation were the most endorsed recovery facilitators. Participants reported the greatest improvements in 'interpersonal relationships' (more meaningful and trustful relationships) and 'new possibilities' (new life goals and priorities reorientations). These domains were associated with fewer emotion regulation difficulties and higher deliberate rumination. Cognitive rigidity, difficulties with impulse control under negative emotions and perceived new possibilities showed the highest expected influence and predictability. Conclusions These findings highlight the relevance of cognitive-emotional processes and future-oriented perspectives to recovery and support broader, person-centred definitions of recovery that encompass personal growth and interpersonal changes alongside symptom remission.

items.title: Multiscale neural and endocrine control of CD8⁺ T cell fate in cancer: from systemic physiology to local immune circuits.
items.abstract: CD8⁺ T cells are central cytotoxic effectors of anti-tumor immunity, but tumor-infiltrating CD8⁺ populations are functionally heterogeneous and include tumor-reactive, dysfunctional, and bystander states. Although the past decade of cancer immunology has focused largely on how local interactions within the tumor microenvironment shape these states, clinical observations linking chronic stress, sleep disruption, endocrine comorbidity, and circadian timing to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes indicate that CD8⁺ T cell function is also modulated far beyond the tumor itself. In this review we adopt a whole-organism perspective to examine how autonomic and sensory neural circuits and the endocrine system act across anatomical compartments to govern CD8⁺ T cell priming, trafficking, metabolism, and exhaustion. We first analyze sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory neural axes as systemic effectors mediated by catecholamines, acetylcholine, neuropeptides, and brainstem-driven tone. We then examine endocrine regulation through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, metabolic hormones, and gonadal steroids. We integrate these axes within the tumor microenvironment, where nerve-derived signals, paracrine neuropeptides, and locally amplified glucocorticoid activity form a convergent suppressive network, and at the organismal level through stress amplification loops, sex dimorphism, gut-relayed microbial signaling, and circadian timing. Collectively, this evidence identifies neuro-endocrine signaling as an actionable, mechanistically stratified layer of systemic immune regulation and supports its evaluation as a source of biomarkers and pharmacological targets for sensitizing tumors to ICI therapy. This framework offered here is intended to bridge cancer neuroscience, endocrine oncology, and immunotherapy, and to define the criteria by which the next generation of systems-level immune sensitizers should be evaluated.

items.title: Heterogeneous Encoding Patterns of Dynamic Audiovisual Social Stimuli in Autism Spectrum Disorder (Heterogeneous Encoding Patterns in Autism).
items.abstract: The neural basis of social difficulties in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains uncertain. Prior studies typically used static stimuli or reduced complex stimuli to only a few dimensions, obscuring real-world complexity. Here, we used videos with social content to engage brain networks and trained encoding models to predict brain activity from high-dimensional audio, visual, and more abstract socially relevant features (e.g., valence). We hypothesized that brain activity in autistic adults would be less accurately predicted and more heterogeneous within and across individuals than in neurotypical (NT) participants, particularly for socially relevant features. Participants [48 ASD (13 female), 90 NT (25 female)] viewed six videos (5-20 min). Brain activity was measured using fMRI. Cross-validated encoding models were assessed on prediction accuracy, variance, and pattern similarity. Brain activity was predicted significantly above chance across brain networks and videos with striking consistency between groups. Auditory and language networks were most accurately predicted. Within-participant predictions were equally variable between groups; however, autistic participants exhibited lower within-group encoding pattern similarity than NT participants and greater across-group than within-group similarity. Analyses using only socially relevant features showed the largest across-group differences in encoding pattern similarity. The novel application of encoding models to multiple videos in ASD suggests greater heterogeneity in neural representations of social information in ASD. Although group-averaged encoding accuracies were comparable across groups, ASD participants showed more heterogeneous regional encoding patterns. These idiosyncratic patterns underscore the need to incorporate individual variation in brain representations when developing translational neuroimaging approaches in autism. Significance statement Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) experience difficulties in social communication and interaction, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we present a novel application of encoding models to neuroimaging in ASD. Neural representations of dynamic and complex social information were more heterogeneous across autistic as compared with neurotypical individuals while encoding model prediction accuracy was similar for population averages across groups. Effects were robust across six videos and spatial scales. Variability in neural representation across individuals, rather than systemic population differences, may thus be associated with atypical brain function in complex social information processing in autism. The findings highlight the importance of accounting for individual variability when studying the neurobiology of autism and developing translational neuroimaging approaches.
